Damage from flash flooding occurred along County Road A3A. Debris and rubble were scattered across roadways and driveways with some vehicles trapped in the debris. Another video in the same area showed vehicles trapped in flash flooding in Rincon Montoso southwest of Rociada. Property damage for cabins and vehicles is an estimate.
A driveway a few miles south of Edgewood became flooded and impassable.
An arroyo that flows underneath I-40 just east of Wagon Wheel flooded and exceeded its banks with an observed water rise of 7 feet.

events.cz_name: MIDDLE RIO GRANDE VALLEY/ALBUQUERQUE METRO AREA
events.event_narrative: The Albuquerque Sunport measured a peak wind gust of 63 mph from east canyon winds.
The Little Burro WSMR mesonet measured a peak wind gust of 76 mph from east canyon winds.
Social media video shows a road washed out at intersection near E. Frontage Road and Bar D 4 Road near Santa Cruz south of Espanola. Road repair cost is an estimate.
The Fort Sumner Airport recorded a thunderstorm wind gust of 58 mph.

NM State Police reported a road closure on State Highway 434 due to flooding and runoff from the Hermits Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar flowing across the road. Road closure time estimated based on radar data.

Storms over the South Fork burn scar resulted in flash flooding in the Upper Canyon neighborhood including Johnson Road and Main Road requiring the closing of Main Road at Bridge 1. High flows in the Rio Ruidoso eventually flowed downstream resulting in water flowing across North Eagle Drive. Ruidoso Municipal Schools were put under a shelter in place notice while the flash flood warning was in effect.

The Albuquerque Fire Department rescued an injured man and a dog in 7 feet of water in an arroyo channel. A second man was spotted lifeless moving down the North Diversion Channel near Menaul Blvd. and eventually Osuna Road. His body was recovered in the North Valley outfall of the channel. Rainfall of 0.50 to 1.40 was reported upstream of the arroyo channel.
The Cannon AFB AWOS measured a peak thunderstorm wind gust caused by a downburst.

The Farmington Four Corners Regional Airport observed thunderstorm wind gusts peaking at 66 mph. These thunderstorm wind gusts produced thick blowing dust, power outages to 8,000 customers, and a down 69kV power line resulting in power outages around Aztec and surrounding areas. Power line damage cost is an estimate.
A wind gust of 69 mph from a thunderstorm downburst was observed at the Roswell Air Center.
A 59 mph wind gust was recorded at the Albuquerque International Sunport as an outflow boundary moved through the site.
Hail slightly larger than penny size accumulated up to 2 deep. Significant erosion. There were still piles of hail under downspouts 14 hours after the storm. Damage reported to home.

Locally heavy rainfall estimated to be near two inches per hour over the South Fork burn scar resulted in flash flooding along the Rio Ruidoso. Water over Bridge 2 on Main Road in Ruidoso was reported. Water over roadways was reported elsewhere in Ponderosa Heights, and near Alpine Village.

Locally heavy rainfall on the Salt burn scar resulted in flash flooding on secondary roads off U.S. Highway 70 and within the Cherokee Mobile Home Park. There were no reports of injuries, casualties or damage.
Brief heavy rainfall of 0.20 over the South Fork burn scar resulted in flash flooding and road closures over portions of Brady Canyon Road from South Oak Drive to Mechem Drive.

A fast moving storm developed over the South Fork burn scar, quickly moving east and producing 0.84 of rainfall over the McBride burn scar. Flash flooding was reported over roadways at University Dr. and Mechem Dr., Gavilan Canyon Rd. at several locations from Eagle Creek to east of Warrior Dr., and on Paradise Road. Debris was reported over the road at Prospect Rd. and Gavilan Canyon Road. While road closures were reported there were no reports of damage, injuries or casualties.
Intersection flooded and closed at East 3rd Street and Kilgore Avenue.

A trained spotter shared video of flood waters within the normally dry Rio Penasco well outside of banks overtopping a low water crossing. These flood waters were a response to an estimated three to six inches of rainfall over the prior two days over the nearby Sacramento Mountains.

Rainfall amounts superseding 0.60 inches resulted in burn scar flash flooding off the South Fork and McBride burn scars. Water over the road at Paradise Canyon Dr. and Hull Road resulted in a closure of the roadway. Water and debris was also reported over Friedenbloom Drive.

A video shared on social media showed a portion of Highway 2 south of Lake Arthur in southern Chaves County under six inches of water. Radar and gauge readings showed the likely period of flooding rains occurred in the morning from 8am to 9am MDT, while the reports were received later in the early afternoon when the heavier rain ended.

Heavy runoff within the Baker Arroyo jumped out and flooded west and south, impacting U.S. Highway 64, Christ the King Catholic Church, the Central Consolidated School District and the Chat and Chew restaurant. At least two homes were destroyed or made uninhabitable. Damage cost is an estimate.

Heavy runoff within the Salt Creek Wash overtopped a bridge along Farm Road or B.I.A. 364 and nearby homes. Vegetation overgrowth exacerbated these flood waters. Yellow Arroyo also flooded out over property, homes and nearby roadways from the same round of thunderstorms. Damage cost is an estimate.
A strong thunderstorm produced penny size hail at Sandia Park.
A severe thunderstorm produced quarter size hail near Sedillo.
Thunderstorms produced wind gusts as high as 70 mph in Placitas.
Thunderstorms produced a peak wind gust of 62 mph at the Mine mesonet on the White Sands Missile Range.

Flash flooding with debris over Via Sedillo road in the town of Sedillo between NM Highway 333 and Camino Verde Road. Flow at Tijeras Arroyo in Sedillo was at least 6 inches deep based on high water mark. Time estimated based on radar reflectivity.
A trained spotter reported flooding over the bridge crossing County Road A4A, just west of NM 94. Event time estimated based on radar reflectivity and time report occurred.
High wind gusts peaking at 77 mph and 61 mph were observed at the Little Burro and Tower 6 mesonet sites, respectively, on the White Sands Missile Range.

Law enforcement reported flooding on the north end of County Road A-1 in Sapello, NM. The Sapello Fire Department reported 2 foot deep water over the roadway. Event time estimated based on radar reflectivity and time report occurred.
Large 20 ft yucca shrub toppled in high winds near Inca Road NE & 10th Street NE in Rio Rancho.
Damage reported throughout Bandelier National Monument from significant flash flooding. All trails on the property were closed except for one within the official park boundaries.
Severe drought persisted across the southern portion of the zone.
Severe drought persisted across the far northwest portion of the zone.

events.event_narrative: The Albuquerque Sunport ASOS measured a peak wind gust of 59mph during a strong east canyon wind event well after convective thunderstorms had passed to the south.
Large sycamore tree limbs up to 2 inches in diameter were snapped near the Santa Fe Railyards.

Severe wind gusts from a storm heading directly toward Texline, TX blew through Clayton, NM, knocking out power for to an estimated 15 hours. Three power poles were reported down by the Southwestern Electric Cooperative.

The county Emergency Manager and Quay County Sun newspaper reported 10 commercial vehicles were blown over on I-40 due to severe thunderstorm wind gusts. This along with 7 other simultaneous crashes closed I-40 for several hours in both directions. Several people were taken to the local hospital in Tucumcari as emergency response from Logan, San Jon, Tucumcari and the Quay Fire District 2 responded to the incident.

Severe thunderstorm wind gusts blew of a community center roof, church doors and destroyed numerous outbuildings in Nara Visa as reported in Quay County Sun. A social media post showed a large section of a metal fence lofted into the air and draped over a toppled tree at Burns Ranch and a second large tree blown down.
The same severe thunderstorm wind gust that knocked at power at Clayton, NM also blew over a FEDEX semi-trailer along U.S. Highway 64/87 at mile marker 2 just west of the TX state line.
Quarter size hail fell at mile marker 232 along U.S. Highway 84 outside Ghost Ranch.

Severe thunderstorm wind gusts blew down a large tree branch at NM Highway 206 and Moreland Road, while also knocking out power in the area south of Portales to include the towns of Dora, Pep and Causey.
Fast flowing from a nearby culvert washed out a dirt road a few miles south of Chacon, within the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar. The location is estimated.
A storm chaser on social media reported 2 inch hail while driving along U.S. Highway 285 north of Roswell in Chaves County.

A tornado producing no damage touched down just northwest of Clines Corners between I-40 and U.S. Highway 285, travelling northeast. A survey revealed no apparent damage with an estimated width of 50 yards and path length of approximately one mile.
Severe drought conditions were removed from the southern portion of the zone.

A strong storm dropped penny size hail in central De Baca County west of Fort Sumner.
Quarter size hail was reported at the Burnt Well Guest Ranch from a severe thunderstorm.

A line of strong storms dropped penny size hail across Santa Fe.
A strong storm dropped penny size hail with accumulations of 2 to 3 inches.
A nearby severe thunderstorm produced a 60 mph wind gust at Melrose Air Force Range.
A severe storm dropped penny to quarter size hail east of Tucumcari stripping leaves off trees.

A severe storm dropped ping pong size hail in southwest Union County.

U.S. Highway 285 washed out at mile marker 137 and mile marker 151 due to heavy rainfall from thunderstorms. Additionally, NMDOT closed U.S. Highway 285 from mile marker 135 to 138 due to flash flooding. Flash flooding resulted in vehicles being stuck in several inches of water and multiple areas of the highway becoming impassable. An accident also occurred on the highway about 14 miles north of Roswell due to hydroplaning.

Heavy rain resulted in multiple low water crossings along County Road A19A being flooded with several inches of water. Additionally, parts of San Pablo Creek and Tecolote Creek overflowed its banks in the Mineral Hill area.
Two feet of water reported at the Burnt Well Guest Ranch where roadways near the ranch were flooded.

Historically bad flash flooding across Roswell, reported by numerous emergency officials and the public. Thunderstorms training over Roswell dumped an all-time one-day rainfall record of 5.78 at the Roswell Airport with numerous other public weather stations across town ranging from 4 to 9 inches. Major flooding was reported across the city and nearby low-lying areas south and west of town. Numerous vehicles were submerged in over 4 feet of water while several more were swept away. The Roswell Daily Record reported that as many as 500 rescues were carried out over the weekend during and after the flooding. Estimates have as many as 400 homes and 200 businesses facing significant damage. The Roswell Convention Center was hosting a UFO festival when flood waters up to 5 feet entered the building. Attendees were being rescued from the rooftop. Roswell's Spring River Zoo also suffered extensive damage including the loss of one donkey. Flood damage was also sustained to Roswell's Landfill and Wastewater Treatment Plant. All roads entering the city were closed by State Police. The city lost 4 fire trucks and 7 police patrol cars with numerous city facilities damaged. There is one confirmed direct fatality from drowning and one indirect fatality from a heart attack reported and there may have been more as many vehicles were swept away along the Spring River drainage.

Historically bad flash flooding across Roswell from storms dropping 4 to 9 inches across town, including an all-time one-day precipitation record of 5.78 at the Roswell airport caused major damage. This flooding was reported to have persisted through Monday October 21st. Damage and fatality information are recorded in the preceding flash flood entry.

A forecasted rise in the Pecos River at the ACME gauge just north of U.S. Highway 70 was to 13.2 feet, or to minor flood stage. The rise in the river ended up washing out the river gauge allowing for only an estimated gauge measurement. These floodwaters continued south along the Pecos River and were recorded at the Lake Arthur gauge.

Heavy rains resulting in the devastating flash flooding in Roswell swelled the Pecos River on October 20th, reaching the Lake Arthur gauge near the southern Chaves County line. River levels surpassed minor flood level at 20 feet at 17:30 MST, peaking at 20.34 feet at 7:30pm MST before receding below minor flood stage at 11:45pm MST that night.

The NM Department of Transportation reported river flooding along the Rio Felix south of Roswell overtopping and damaging the U.S. Highway 285 bridge, and overtopping  the NM State Highway 2 bridge just north of Hagerman closing both bridges. Flooding from heavy rains and poor drainage also extended over much of Dexter just north of Hagerman. Damage is an estimate. A Flood Warning was issued and repeatedly extended until local reports of the water receding came from local Emergency Management.
A 58 mph wind gust was observed at the Gallup Municipal Airport.
An estimated wind gust of 60 mph was observed at the Magdalena Ridge Observatory.
Peak wind gusts of up to 62 mph and peak sustained winds of up to 44 mph were observed at Clines Corners.

A high wind gust of 60 mph was observed at Hartley Ranch.
Peak wind gusts of up to 67 mph were observed at the Roswell Air Center.

Numerous road closures in the Roswell area due to blowing dust reported via NM DOT. Roads impacted from low visibility due to blowing dust included U.S. Highways 70, 285, and 380, NM State Highways 2, 246, 253, 254, 409, and the Roswell Relief Route between West Brasher Road and Sunset Avenue. Peak wind gusts of 60 mph were observed at the Roswell Air Center during this time.
A 58 mph wind gust was observed at the Las Vegas Municipal Airport.
Lots of hail up to quarter size covering the ground in Melrose.

U.S. Highway 285 and State Road 2 (Old Dexter Highway) in and around Dexter were impassible due to flood water moving across the respective roadways. Additionally, the neighborhood area near Ken Road west of U.S. Highway 285 was under 2 to 3 feet of water. Flooding also occurred in fields along U.S. Highway 285 at East Ottawa Road inundating the highway.

Video shows the water flowing over Bottomless Lakes Road north of Bottomless Lakes State Park. The road was closed due to being impassible from the floodwaters. Additionally, water was flowing across U.S. Highway 380 at mile marker 177 and at a rest stop next to the Mescalero Sands North Dune area.

A trained spotter reported bar ditches full of water from heavy rainfall, and State Highway 267 (Floyd Highway) had several places covered in 6 to 12 inches of water. However, the road still remained passable.
Water from Walnut Creek overflowed onto State Road 2, resulting in the closure of the roadway.

Flooding of crop fields and area highways across southern Chaves, between Midway and Lake Arthur, continued for the rest of the calendar day after the flash flooding ended. U.S. Highway 285 and State Road 2 remained closed during this time.

Numerous other damage was shown to outdoor equipment and materials, including their power supply. Little visible damage was received to the barn and home. Damage is an estimate.

events.event_narrative: Angel Fire Ski Resort observed 40 inches of snow. CoCoRaHS observers and SNOTEL sites generally observed between 1 to 2.5 feet of snow. State Highway 434 from mile marker 21 to 26 was closed due to snow drifts. In Rociada, video on social media showed cattle stuck in deep snow. Power outages and snow drifts lasted for a few days after the snow ended.
A CoCoRaHS observer in Arroyo Hondo observed 10.5 inches of snow. Elsewhere in the zone, generally 3 to 5 inches of snow was observed in Taos.
A CoCoRaHS observer at Abiquiu observed 12 inches of snow. Elsewhere in the zone, 8 inches of snow was observed at Abiquiu Reservoir and 3 to 6 inches of snow was observed at Espanola.

The heavy snow on November 6th caused down powerlines from San Ildenfonso to Gallisteo resulting in power outages for 5500 customers. Additionally, state offices were closed due to the heavy snow.

events.cz_name: MIDDLE RIO GRANDE VALLEY/ALBUQUERQUE METRO AREA
events.event_narrative: CoCoRaHS observers in Rio Rancho and Bernalillo observed 8 inches of snow. Generally, 3 to 8 inches of snow was observed on the west side of Albuquerque and 2 to 4 inches on the east side of Albuquerque and Belen. Isolated areas in Placitas observed 20 inches of snow. The heavy snow weighed down and broke tree limbs still containing foliage resulting in some power outages across the Albuquerque Metro. State government offices were closed November 8th due to the snow.

A CoCoRaHS observer measured 24 inches of snow near Golden north of Edgewood. Generally, 12 to 18 inches of snow was observed across the zone. Heavy snow and low visibility resulted in a massive backup on I-40 that stretched into this zone. Motorists were stuck for over 12 hours to as long as a day and half in the most severe cases. There were reports of vehicles running out of gas, with occupants needing food and water.

A CoCoRaHS observer just west-southwest of Estancia measured 28 inches of snow. Generally, 14 to 15 inches was observed in Moriarty and Estancia. Heavy snow and low visibility resulted in a massive backup on I-40 that stretched across this zone. Motorists were stuck for over 12 hours to as long as a day and half in the most severe cases.  There were reports of vehicles running out of gas, with occupants needing food and water.

A CoCoRaHS observer a few miles west of Vaughn measured 14 inches of snow. Heavy snow and low visibility resulted in a massive backup on I-40 that stretched across this zone including Clines Corners. Motorists were stuck for over 12 hours to as long as a day and half in the most severe cases. There were reports of vehicles running out of gas, with occupants needing food and water.
A trained spotter near Corona observed 18 inches of snow.

There were reports of traffic backups on State Road 48 (Alto Rd) between Ski Run Road and E. Challete the morning of November 7th.

events.cz_name: JOHNSON AND BARTLETT MESAS INCLUDING RATON PASS
events.event_narrative: The COOP observer in Capulin measured 26.1 inches of snow. Heavy blowing snow and near whiteout conditions at times resulted in the closure of I-25 at Raton Pass through the early morning hours of November 9th. Additionally, U.S. 64/87 through Capulin was shut down during this time.

A trained spotter in Cimmaron observed 26 inches of snow. Generally, 18 to 24 inches of snow was observed in the zone. Heavy snow and poor visibility resulted in the closure of I-25 in the zone and U.S. 56 at Springer through the zone from November 7th through the early morning hours of November 9th.

A CoCoRaHS observer in Las Vegas measured 31.7 inches of snow. This set a new 3 day snowfall record for the month of November in Las Vegas. Heavy snow, poor visibility and reports from law enforcement of semi-trucks stuck and stranded in the snow resulted in the closure of I-25 within the zone. Additionally, U.S. 84 was closed from Romeroville to Anton Chico at the San Miguel and Guadalupe County border during this time.

Twenty nine inches of snow was observed in far northern Union County near the Colorado border. Additionally, in Clayton and central Union County, around 19 to 22 inches of snow was observed. The 21.7 inches of snow observed in Clayton set a new 3 day snowfall record for the month of November and is the 2nd highest three day snowfall event. The Pasamonte COOP's 17 inch snowfall amount is that station's 2nd highest three-day total. A massive car pileup November 7th on U.S. 64/87 resulted in the closure of the highway. U.S. Highway 56 was closed as well due to the heavy snow and poor visibility. Local rancher rescued a stranded motorist on the highway and took them to a hospital in Clayton.
A trained spotter in Roy observed 24 inches of snow. Heavy snow and poor visibility resulted in the closure on State Highway 39 in the county.

A CoCoRaHS observer a few miles south of Mosquero observed 6.2 inches of snow. NM Roads reported severe driving conditions due to snow and blowing snow on State Highway 104 and 419 in the Trementina and Garita area on November 7th.

The emergency manager in Santa Rosa reported 8 inches of snow. Additionally, a trained spotter along I-40 in far northwest Guadalupe County reported 7 inches of snow. Heavy snow and blowing snow resulted in a massive traffic backup lasting at least 7 hours on the section of I-40 within the zone.

A trained spotter near Montoya in western Quay County reported 2.5 inches of snow. Poor road conditions from snow resulted in a long traffic backup on I-40 that stretched and started in the zone at mile marker 330, the western outskirts of Tucumcari.

events.cz_name: JOHNSON AND BARTLETT MESAS INCLUDING RATON PASS
events.event_narrative: Raton Pass NMDOT station reported blizzard conditions with blowing snow, wind gusts as high as 49 mph and visibility as low as 0.20 miles. I-25 at Raton Pass was closed during this time due to the blizzard conditions. Additionally, near blizzard conditions were observed for much of the day on November 7th.

Raton Crews Municipal Airport reported snow and blowing snow during the day November 7th resulting in near blizzard conditions. Wind gusts of up to 39 mph were briefly observed for less than three hours. Additionally, visibility dropped to less than 0.25 miles at times. These conditions resulted in the closure of I-25 and U.S. 56 in the zone during this time.

Las Vegas Municipal Airport reported visibility as low as 0.25 miles from snow and blowing snow along with wind gusts as high as 30 mph. Snow and blowing snow resulted in visibility below 0.25 miles and near blizzard conditions across other parts of the zone resulting in the closure of I-25 and U.S. 84 throughout the entire zone.

Whiteout conditions due to blowing snow along with snow drifts were observed across U.S. Highways 64/87, and U.S. Highway 56/412 beginning late Thursday morning. Wind gusts across western and central Union County from various mesonet stations and the Clayton Municipal Airpark ASOS peaked at around 40 mph during this time. Cars piled up behind a jack-knifed semi-truck between Clayton and Des Moines. The emergency manager estimated around 100 cars impacted and needing help getting turned around and off the road. The highway was closed and remained closed until all vehicles and drivers were cleared off after a couple of hours later. One stranded and injured motorist was rescued by a local rancher and taken from the scene to a nearby hospital.
The Mills Canyon RAWS station observed gusts of around 30 mph. These wind gusts along with snow and blowing snow caused lower visibility and severe driving conditions in the zone.

Heavy snow up to a foot caused power outages from San Ildefonso to Gallisteo and Santa Fe. State government offices were shutdown on November 7th. Unfortunately the cold resulted in two fatalities, one on the morning of the 7th and another on the morning of the 8th in Santa Fe. An unidentified male in his 50s was found Thursday outside Freedom Church on Cerrillos Road and Vegas Verdes Drive. Cody Lee Morales, 28, was found Friday morning near Cesar Chaves Elementary School on Jaguar Drive. The two deaths were determined to be from exposure to the cold, temperatures fell into the 20s each night.
Localized severe drought conditions returned to the far southeast portion of the zone due to a record warm October.

Severe drought conditions were mostly removed from the southern half of the zone due to a record amount of rainfall observed on October 19th. Roswell observed 5.78 inches of rain on October 19th setting a new all-time record for daily rainfall in the city.

Severe drought conditions returned to the far southern portion of the zone due to a record warm October. Heavy rainfall was observed just east of the zone over the Chaves County Plains during the second half of the month.

Severe drought conditions persisted across most of the zone due to a record warm October.  Heavy rainfall was observed just northeast of the zone over the Chaves County Plains during the second half of the month.

events.event_narrative: The Valencia County emergency management confirmed a wildfire burning within the bosque along the west side of the Rio Grande on Bureau of Indian Affairs land during the afternoon of April 17th. Strong and very dry southwesterly winds creating critical fire weather conditions allowed the fire to jump the Rio Grande River and into Bosque Farms just south of the Valencia and Bernalillo County line. Evacuations were ordered in Bosque Farms between Truchas Trail and Cottonwood Drive west of West Bosque Loop. The fire caused major damage to three homes with two of those being destroyed. There are no reports of injuries or fatalities. Damage is an estimate based on number of homes destroyed.

The Otero Wildfire was discovered in the late afternoon of April 27th just east of Socorro in the bosque along the Rio Grande River. As of April 29th, it had burned 405 acres, threatening no structures.

The Balsam Wildfire was discovered during a very dry and critical fire weather event on the evening of April 27th, in Grants, NM. Fire crews were able to keep the fire to just 3 to 5 acres, but it unfortunately burned through a residential area. The Grants Fire Chief reported 7 structures were impacted with 2 firemen injured. Damage is an estimate.

events.cz_name: MIDDLE RIO GRANDE VALLEY/ALBUQUERQUE METRO AREA
events.event_narrative: The Cotton fire was discovered in the afternoon of 6/21 while the Cotton II was discovered on the morning of 6/22 and determined to be human caused. Both quickly became combined into the Desert Willow Complex Fire on 6/22 burning in the bosque area on both sides of the Rio Grande north and south of Main Street Bridge in Los Lunas. Unfortunately, 11 structures were destroyed with 9 of them homes, and 4 other structures were damaged. Media reported 12 firefighters were treated for smoke and heat injuries while two firefighters were hospitalized. Evacuations were ordered for residences in the area, ending by the 23rd. The Cotton fire burned 95 acres while the Cotton II fire burned 145 acres, totaling 237 acres for the entire complex. Damage is an estimate based on the number of homes and structures destroyed.

The Buck Fire was discovered in an extremely remote area of Catron County near Pelona Mountain southwest of Magdalena, NM. The fire burned mainly through wilderness area on private land along and northwest of highway 163 reaching 57,736 acres by June 17th. No damage and destruction of property was reported.
The lightning caused Skyline Fire was discovered in the afternoon of June 21st just south of Hondo and U.S. Highway 380. The fire burned 127 acres on private land causing no damage to any structures.

events.event_narrative: An NWS Employee observed a cloud of blowing dust pushing west just east of the Albuquerque Sunport across the Rio Grande where visibility was clearing near zero and under one quarter statute mile.
A convectively induced outflow gust that funneled through the Tijeras Canyon reached a peak gust of 66 mph. No lightning was observed at the Sunport.
A convectively induced outflow gust that funneled through the Tijeras Canyon induced a severe wind gust of 59 mph. No lightning was observed at the Sunport.
A convectively induced outflow gust produced a severe wind gust of 61 mph. No lightning was observed at the airport.
Burn scar flash flooding off the Salt burn scar produced high water flows and culvert issues diverting water into the Cherokee Mobile home park that ran right up to people's homes.

Heavy rainfall over the Albuquerque metro area produced dangerous fast flows on the area arroyo system. Two swift water rescues were performed in the diversion channel along I-40 and the Snow Heights neighborhood. Additionally, a man was trapped and swept up among floodwaters in an arroyo near Carlisle and Menaul Boulevard. Crews searched the North Diversion Channel and nearby areas for at least an hour before deploying an airboat in a washout area at Roy Avenue and Fourth Street. The man was not found in the washout area. The individual is assumed to have been deceased.

Heavy rain exceeding 2 inches caused thick dirt and debris runoffs over roadways across western Rio Rancho which caused at least one road closure and debris removal efforts. During debris removal efforts around sunrise, road crews located a deceased male near the intersection of Northern Blvd. and Calor Rd. NW.
Overnight flood waters inundated a residence in Las Nutrias along NM 304. Flood waters also closed NM 304 at Las Nutrias Road, washing dirt onto the highway requiring debris removal later that day.
A video from a KOB viewer on social media showed large areas of water inundating farmland and nearby properties around El Cerro. Time and location are estimated.
Nickel to quarter size hail was observed at Sandia Park from a severe thunderstorm.
Penny to quarter size hail from a severe thunderstorm was observed a few miles east of Sandia Park.

Heavy rain from slow moving storms on the South Fork and McBride burn scars resulted in flash flooding on and downstream of the burn scars. Several roads along and crossing the Rio Ruidoso were closed due to the resultant flash flooding and debris flow in the river. This included Mechem Drive, Ebarb Drive at Main Road and West Redwood Road, Fern Trail at Terrance and Grindstone, Eagle Bridge on Eagle Road, Gavilan Bridge on Gavilan Canyon Road in Hollywood, Cree Meadows at Country Club and Heath, Robin Road, Hull Road, and Paradise Canyon Road. The floodwaters and debris flow washed away a vehicle on Porr Drive. No information was known on if any occupants were in the vehicle at the time. Another vehicle was stuck in flood waters at Apache Hills Drive and Grant Drive. Finally, 2 to 3 inches of water entered a home on Ash Drive.
A COOP observer in Capulin reported nickel size hail from a strong thunderstorm.

Heavy rain on the South Fork burn scar from slow moving thunderstorms during the early afternoon hours resulted in another round of flash flooding across roads and neighborhoods on and downstream of the burn scar. This resulted in Main Road at bridge 2 to become impassable, and the closure of Ebarb Drive and Porr Drive due to 3-6 inches of flowing water over the road. Additionally, the runoff and debris flow continued downstream on the Rio Ruidoso with the river overtopping the bridge at Gavilan Canyon Road just north of Sudderth Drive in Hollywood.

Another round of thunderstorms on the South Fork and McBride burn scars resulted in flash flooding and debris flows on and downstream of the burn during the evening hours. Water and debris were observed flowing near Flume Canyon Drive, Mecham and White Mountain Drive, Warren Tucker and White Mountain Drive, and on Gavilan Canyon Road at Eagle Creek Road and between Janet and Edwards Drive.
Severe thunderstorms in the area resulted in a peak wind gust of 64 mph at the Tower 6 mesonet station on the White Sands Missile Range.
Severe thunderstorms in the area resulted in a peak wind gust of 75 mph at the Little Burro mesonet station on the White Sands Missile Range.
Severe thunderstorms in the area resulted in a peak wind gust of 62 mph at the Phillips Hill mesonet station on the White Sands Missile Range.
Severe thunderstorms in the area resulted in a brief wind gust of 61 mph at the Pole 616 mesonet station on the White Sands Missile Range.
A severe thunderstorm resulted in a peak wind gust of 83 mph at the Chupadera RAWS on the White Sands Missile Range.
A weakening severe thunderstorm resulted in a peak wind gust of 61 mph at the Melrose Gunnery Range AWOS.
A trained spotter observed golf ball size hail from a severe thunderstorm.
A trained spotter estimated 60 mph wind gusts along with lots of blowing dust kicked up ahead of a severe thunderstorm. The blowing dust resulted in reduced visibility at his location.
The AWOS at Santa Rosa airport measured a 75 mph wind gust from outflow winds caused by a severe thunderstorm a few miles east of the site.
The Stallion WIT mesonet on the White Sands Missile Range measured a 65 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorm just south of the site.

A trained spotter's personal weather station just northwest of Logan and north of Ute Lake measured a 60 mph wind gust as outflow winds ahead of a line of severe thunderstorms moved through. The spotter lost power shortly after. Additionally, a mesonet and UPR station very close by near Logan and Ute Lake each measured a 59 mph wind gust.
The ASOS at Tucumcari Municipal Airport measured a 58 mph as outflow winds ahead of a line of severe thunderstorms moved through the site.
The West Texas mesonet station 2 miles southwest of Endee measured peak wind gusts of 77 mph as outflow winds ahead of a line of severe thunderstorms moved through the site.
A CoCoRaHS observer in Cedar Crest observed 2 inch hail from a severe thunderstorm.
A spotter observed nickel size hail accumulations of 6 to 8 inches deep from a severe thunderstorm. The hail resulted in widespread damage to vegetation, homes, and vehicles.
A CoCoRaHS observer a few miles east southeast of Sandia Park observed hail up to quarter size in diameter from a severe thunderstorm. The hail resulted in some minor leaf damage.
A spotter in Edgewood observed quarter to half dollar size hail from a severe thunderstorm.
The ASOS at the Albuquerque Sunport measured a 65 mph wind gust from nearby severe thunderstorms.

Heavy rain from slow moving severe thunderstorms resulted in severe flash flooding in the East Mountain communities of Cedar Crest, Tijeras and Sedillo. A 300 pound woodchipper was carried downstream on the normally dry Arroyo de San Antonio until becoming lodged in a tree. Video taken by a viewer in Tijeras and shared by a broadcast meteorologist shows Tijeras Arroyo flowing out of banks. A small tree was also moving downstream in the arroyo. Spotters also observed flood waters flowing down hillsides around Tijeras, Tablazon, and Zuzax with hail, rocks, mud, and debris covering parts of SR-333. Finally, low water crossings were completely flooded on secondary roads just east and south of the Zuzax exit at I-40.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms over the South Fork burn scar resulted in some minor water rises in the Rio Ruidoso with some water coming off the Upper Canyon and putting debris over Main Road by main bridge 2. Some debris on Cedar Creek Drive at Musket Ball Drive and near Mechem Drive resulted in a brief closure of the road to allow for crews to clean up the roadway.
The mesonet station at I-25 at Rowe measured a 58 mph wind gust from thunderstorms.

The Laguna Wildfire was a lightning started fire originally discovered June 25th and managed in an area of the Santa Fe National Forest roughly 25 miles west of Abiquiu. The fire was managed until a spot fire was discovered outside of the containment lines July 11th. A period of very dry and breezy conditions conducive to fire growth ensued during this time. The Laguna Fire quickly grew from 11,334 acres to 15,714 acres on July 16th, an increase of 4,380 acres before increased monsoonal moisture and rainfall helped fire suppression activities. The Gallina Ranch underwent evacuation orders and smoke impacts. The Vigil Ranch reported 75 of 120 total head of cattle missing after the fires at $5,000 per head. Cattle that was found had injuries to hooves and udders. Damage was based on this estimate.

Extremely heavy rainfall from slow moving thunderstorms resulted in catastrophic flash flooding and destructive debris flows on and downstream of the South Fork burn scar. Debris flows and a record rise on the Rio Ruidoso from 1.43 feet to 20.24 feet in approximately 30 minutes overtopped bridges and roads, pushed some houses off their foundations and down canyons and hillsides, forced power outages, and resulted in water and sewer services. These extremely high flows destroyed the horse racetrack at Ruidoso Downs. Swift water teams rescued 65 individuals from homes, RV trailers, vehicles and from flood waters and debris flows. Up to 150 families and 400 homes were believed to be impacted and damaged. Tragically, three deaths were reported, including two young children when flood waters and debris flows overwhelmed and destroyed their RV. The parents of these children ended up being hospitalized due to suffering serious injuries while trying to save their children from the floodwaters. Two family dogs were also lost in the floodwaters. A federal disaster declaration was issued by the president two days after the catastrophic flash flooding to help free up federal funds and assistance for recovery efforts.

The Turkeyfeather Wildfire was a lightning started fire in a very remote area of the Gila National Forest 22 miles southeast of Reserve, NM. Gusty and erratic winds from nearby thunderstorm activity allowed the fire to rapidly grow during the first week of July. The fire burned a total of 24,128 acres by July 16th before slowing down.
Heavy rain over the South Fork burn scar resulted in floodwaters overtopping Main Road Bridge 2. A swiftwater rescue was also conducted at Sleepy Hollow Bridge.
Quarter to ping pong ball size hail with accumulation of dime to nickel size hail on  roadways. Location estimated via radar.
Flash Flooding made Trigg Road impassable near the confluence of Conejo and Vallentine  Creeks with a concrete culvert becoming inundated and damaged. Location is  approximate.

Heavy rains over the South Fork and Salt burn scars near Ruidoso produced flash flooding. Water and debris overflowed U.S. Highway 70 at Sudderth Dr. and Ruidoso Downs, White Mountain Dr., Gavilan Canyon Rd. from Alto Cafe to Meander, and Alpine Village Road. The Cherokee Mobile Home village was evacuated with swiftwater rescues performed there, and at Big-O Tires and on Friedenbloom Drive. Damage is an estimate.
Heavy rains over the Laguna burn scar produced water and debris over a dirt road making it impassable.
Heavy rain over the Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar produced high flow in an arroyo feeding into Manuelitas Creek. This overflowed banks and splashed over the bridge on County Road A4A.

events.event_narrative: Extreme drought conditions persisted across the majority of the zone with an improvement to severe drought conditions on the far western portion of the zone.
Extreme drought conditions persisted across the southern half of the zone.
Extreme drought conditions persisted across the majority of the zone.

A trained spotter reported flooded streets with fast flowing water going over curbs in the town of Magdelena.
The Abbott COOP observer reported hail up to quarter size from a severe thunderstorm.

Heavy rain from slow moving thunderstorms resulted in mud and rockslides onto the Cochiti Golf Course and across the road at the entrance of the course.  Additionally, the golf cart barn got an inch or so of water in it. Property damage is an estimate.

Moderate to heavy rain on the Ruidoso area burn scars resulted in some flash flooding and debris across and downstream of the burn scars, especially along the Rio Ruidoso and Cedar Creek. Water was reported overtopping Cedar Creek Drive near Sam Tobias Campground, Mechem Drive at Brady Canyon Road, Gavilan Canyon Road north of Sudderth Drive (Highway 70) and Sudderth Drive itself in Hollywood. Some debris flow with a 3 foot wall of mud was also observed on Main Road at McDaniel Drive along with possible evidence of a landslide off Flume Ridge.

A slow-moving thunderstorm dropped an estimated 1 to 1.5 inches of rain in 20 minutes in the North Valley and Los Ranchos de Albuquerque neighborhood of Albuquerque. This resulted in flash flooding on the eastbound lanes of Paseo Del Norte at Rio Grande Blvd and on the westbound frontage road of Paseo Del Norte at Jefferson Street. Additionally, a post on social media reported flood waters entering a business on 4th Street in the Los Ranchos de Albuquerque neighborhood. Finally, a video on social media showed floodwaters in the individual's residence and the family sweeping out the floodwaters from the front entrance of the residence. Property damage cost for the business on 4th street and the residence in the North Valley neighborhood is an estimate.

Heavy rainfall fell over the South Fork burn scar near Ruidoso, with on gage measuring 2.14 inches. Flash flooding produced water over roadways and bridges along Cedar Creek at Mechem Drive, Cree Meadows Bridge and Drive, Innsbrook Drive, Starlite Road, White Mountain Drive, Gavilan Canyon Road, Warren Tucker Drive, Reese Drive, Musketball Drive, and Geneva Road. Three swift water rescues were conducted off Gunpowder Trail and Spring Canyon Road. A video was shared of what appears to be a mobile home washed away down Cedar Creek along Paradise Canyon Drive. The Rio Ruidoso crested to 12.68 feet in minor flood stage at 12:40pm MST, reaching out of its banks in numerous locations. Flash flooding impacted as far down Rio Ruidoso as the Ruidoso Downs Race Track.
Flash flooding was observed off the Salt burn scar out of Bear Canyon to areas near Elk Lodge along U.S. Highway 70.
A washed-out road stranded some personnel just west of Phillips Hill mesonet site (WSM30). It is unclear if folks were stranded all night or at the exact location of wash out.
Flash flooding over U.S. Highway 82 near Jay Powell Ranch with high flows out of banks along the Rio Penasco.
Emergency Management reported 6 inches of moving water over U.S. Highway 54 south of Carrizozo.
A likely virga induced thunderstorm wind gust of 73 mph was observed at the Gallup Airport.

Monsoon rains resulted in a mudslide along NM Highway 38 at mile marker 9 approximately 3 miles west of Red River. Both lanes were closed with no estimated time of return to service. Rainfall over a period of time this summer resulting in a gradual loosening of the hillside is the likely culprit of this mudslide. Damage cost is an estimate of cleanup.

Heavy rains over the South Fork and Salt burn scars in and around Ruidoso resulted in burn scar flash flooding. Flash flooding was reported along multiple portions of Cedar Creek and the Rio Ruidoso, including at Mechem Dr., Brady and Porr Roads, Country Club Road, Robin Road and River Trail, a bridge at Eagle Road, Gavilan Canyon Road, and along U.S. Highway 70 in Hollywood. Spring Canyon Road was washed out and made impassable. Fast moving water was reported over all roads in the Cherokee Village Mobile Home park where a confirmed gas leak was reported alongside a successful swift water rescue of an adult woman. An unknown number of other swift water rescues were conducted in Hollywood. Flash flooding overtopped the bridge on the access road to the Ruidoso Downs racetrack, and flooded the horse tunnel and Spaghetti Flats north and east of the racetrack. Damage is an estimate.

Heavy rains over the South Fork and Salt burn scars resulted in burn scar flash flooding in the Ruidoso area, including near schools. Flash flooding was reported in multiple areas along roads and highways including White Mountain Dr., Hull Rd., Mechem Dr., Paradise Canyon Dr. just north of Sudderth Dr., Perk Canyon Dr., and along Main Road. The access road to the Ruidoso Downs racetrack was once again overtopped. The Fire Department assisted in a swift water rescue of an occupied vehicle being pushed by flood waters. Damage is an estimate, and there are no reports of injuries or fatalities.
Heavy rains resulted in high water levels along the Rio Bonito and along Sandesta Dr., entering homes in the area. Damage is an estimate.
Deputy City Manager reported a collapsed sidewalk at the intersection of Corte de Princesa and Camino Consuela along the Arroyo de los Pinos in Sante Fe. Damage is an estimate.
Local news media shared a video from a viewer of a landspout just north of Rio Bravo Blvd. west of the Rio Grande. The time and location estimated based on video and radar.

Thunderstorms on the Ruidoso area burn scars resulted in flash flooding and debris flows on and downstream of the burn scars. Debris flow on Gavilan Canyon Road made the roadway impassible with a car containing an individual trapped in the debris. Thankfully, rescue crews were able to get the occupant out of the vehicle and debris flow.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms resulted in fast moving water flowing over U.S Highway 380 in Lincoln.
CoCoRaHS observer near Ocate reported hail between quarter to half dollar size from a severe thunderstorm.
A trained spotter and the county emergency manager reported water flowing over several roadways, including NM Highway 21 along with hail accumulating on the roads near Miami.
A peak wind gust of 68 mph was measured by the AWOS at the Santa Rosa Route 66 Airport. This wind gust resulted in a large tree to be blown over in the downtown area.
Heavy rain from severe thunderstorms resulted in five inches of water on 8th Street near Eddy Avenue and 6 inches of water on Park Lake Drive in Santa Rosa, NM.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms on the Salt burn scar resulted in flash flooding near U.S. Highway 70 and Dunagan Trail.
Hail up to golf ball size was observed along State Highway 562 13 miles northwest of Sedan.
Hail up to 2 inches in diameter was observed along County Road 64 just south of State Highway 562 10 miles northwest of Sedan.
A trained spotter 14 miles northwest of Sedan observed quarter size hail from a severe thunderstorm.
The Ziamet station in Hayden measured a 60 mph gust from a severe thunderstorm.
Hail up to ping pong balls caused broken windows, dents in cars, and resulted in the death of at least 27 birds a few miles north of Hayden.
A severe thunderstorm produced ping pong ball size hail along state highway 402 3 miles south of Amistad.
The Belen Regional Airport measured a severe wind gust of 61 mph from a non-thunderstorm convective dry downburst from virga showers in the area.

A trained spotter with the Philmont Scout Ranch shared reports and video of quarter to hen egg size hail pelting the grounds. Hail damaged trees, 60 vehicles, and tore through camping equipment such as unoccupied tents. Thankfully there were no reports of fatalities or injuries. Damage is an estimate.
A trained spotter in Maxwell, NM relayed reports from Facebook of half-dollar size hail from a severe thunderstorm just north of Maxwell passing over I-25.
The public and a trained spotter reported nickel to quarter size hail from a severe thunderstorm passing over Springer, NM.
A trained spotter reported 1.75 inch hail near the Raton Crews Airport.
A NMDOT mesonet weather station along I-40 measured a severe wind gust of 63 mph induced by a dry thunderstorm.

Heavy rainfall over the Blue 2 burn scar resulted in four reported locations of thick mud and debris washed out over the Bonito Lake Road up from Bonito Lake.

Heavy rainfall on the South Fork burn scar resulted in flash flooding and debris flow across roadways on and downstream of the burn scar. Debris flow was observed in multiple sections across Alpine Village Road, Cedar Creek Drive, Gavilan Canyon Road, Ash and Brady Canyon Road, White Mountain Drive at Mechem Drive and Geroge McCarthy Drive. This resulted in the closures of these roadways for a few hours in the mid to late afternoon. Finally, water in the Rio Ruidoso was observed overtopping the bridge at Gavilan Canyon Road just north of Sudderth Drive.
Brief heavy rainfall over the South Fork burn scar resulted in some flowing water and debris flow across Gavilan Canyon Road.
Broadcast media shared a viewer photo of a landspout tornado in Las Vegas New Mexico. Location and time are an estimate based on information provided from broadcast media.

The Middle Mesa Wildfire was started by lightning just west of Navajo Lake and 22 miles west of Dulce, NM. It quickly grew out of control on August 2nd, reaching a total size of 5,045 acres by August 10th. Impacts were limited to very remote areas of far northwestern NM in the Carson National Forest along Forest Road 218A.

The Vereda Blanca Fire was a lightning start along a mesa northeast of Mt. Taylor in the Mt. Taylor Ranger District, located right along the western edge of Sandoval County north of Marquez. The fire grew to a total of 1,307 acres by August 13th. There have been no reports of damages given its remote location.

Slow moving thunderstorms developed over the McBride burn scar back building east over the South Fork burn scar. Heavy rainfall rates first resulted in flash flooding on the McBride burn scar with debris flow resulting in the closure of Gavilan Canyon Road between Hull Road and Warrior Drive and Gavilan Canyon Road at Meander Drive. Debris flows and flash flooding then quickly occurred on the South Fork burn scar resulting in the closure of many roads including White Mountain Drive at Warren Tucker Drive, Alpine Village Road at University, Brady Canyon Road at Ponderosa Drive, Ash Drive, and Mechem Drive, Cree Meadows Drive, Sudderth Drive and Mechem Drive intersection, and Paradise Canyon Drive at Hull Road and Leon Farrar. The flash flooding and debris flows resulted in vehicles rushing down the road on Sunny Slope Drive and a water rescue of one male.

Repeated rounds of thunderstorms resulted in flash Flooding along NM Highway 518 just north of Cleveland. A trained spotter observed at least 8 places where small creeks along the Rio Mora were exceeding banks and flooding the highway. Flash flooding also resulted in extreme damage to NM Highway 434. The highway was closed for emergency repairs for 2 to 3 days and was reopened a few days later after installing five corrugated metal pipes and restoring the roadway with a temporary dirt surface.

Slow moving thunderstorms resulted in flash flooding and rushing water across NM Highway 117 near El Malpais National Monument. The highway was temporarily closed during this time until flood waters fully receded.
Heavy rainfall from a slow moving thunderstorm resulted in rushing floodwaters across State Highway 76 near Mile Marker 8 in Chimayo.
The Mills Canyon RAWS measured a 70 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorm.
The Union County emergency manager estimated 50 to 60 mph wind gusts at Clayton Lake State Park from a severe thunderstorm.
The ASOS at Clayton Municipal Airpark measured a 58 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorm.
Runoff from heavy rainfall on the Salt burn scar resulted in about 1 foot of rushing water flooding grassland at the base of Bear Canyon, according to video from the Ruidoso emergency manager.
Heavy rainfall from thunderstorms resulted in flash flooding on numerous streets in Portales. This included 18th Street which was flooded with 6 to 8 inches of water over the road.
Heavy rainfall from low moving thunderstorms washed-out Obsidian and Juniper Roads near State Highway 4 and 126.

State Road 2 was closed at the intersection with East Jackson Road due to flooding along the normally dry Walnut Arroyo. Based on photo provided, floodwaters looked to be about 1 foot deep and not moving.

A CoCoRaHS observer near Rowe observed a significant amount of penny to nickel size hail with a hail accumulation depth of over 2 inches. Some minor flooding was observed with a glacier like mass of ice and debris. The hail ended up destroying the observer's orchard, corn, and tomato crops.

Heavy rainfall from thunderstorms resulted in Dry Creek Road to County Road 84 near the Rio Pojoaque to become impassable due to water over the roadways. Additionally, the intersection at the end of NM 502 and Cities of Gold Road in Pojoaque became impassible due to 4 feet of water over the roadways.

A wet microburst from a severe thunderstorm resulted in an 81 mph wind gust at the Las Vegas Municipal Airport.

Heavy rainfall from slow moving thunderstorms resulted in water and debris from nearby drainages covering portions of I-25 between mile markers 248 and 249 near Algodones. The interstate was reduced to 1 lane with traffic backed up 4 miles in both directions for several hours during the evening. The Rail Runner tracks at mile marker 14 on Pan American Central Highway in Algodones was also flooded with debris over the railroad tracks and a bridge being washed out. This resulted in a 3 hour delay to allow for repairs to the railroad track and bridge. Northbound travelers were bussed from the stop on Highway 550 to the San Felipe station to continue their trip, while southbound travelers were bussed from the stop to the Highway 550 station.
A report obtained from social media shows pictures of hail up to golf ball size from a severe thunderstorm near Sugarite Canyon.
Ping pong to golf ball size hail was observed from a severe thunderstorm along U.S. Highway 64 and 87 on the northwest outskirts of Clayton.
A trained spotter between downtown Clayton and Clayton Municipal Airport observed half dollar size hail from a severe thunderstorm moving through the town.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms over the South Fork burn scar produced water and debris in Cedar Creek flowing over the bridge at Brady Canyon Road and Ponderosa Drive before moving across Mechem Drive at Brady Canyon Road, shutting down Mechem Drive. Water and debris in Cedar Creek continued downstream moving over the road at Cree Meadows and Country Club Drive and Paradise Canyon Drive at Starlite Road and Hull Road, closing these roads. Video from social media showed floodwaters and debris flows swiftly going around a house along the banks of the Rio Ruidoso at the first bridge on Main Road in the Upper Canyon neighborhood. The Rio Ruidoso was observed flowing over the bridge at Country Club Drive and Eagle Drive resulting in the closure of these two roadways. Finally, the floodwater and debris flow in the Rio Ruidoso overwhelmed culverts under the western part of the Ruidoso Downs racetrack eventually moving across the racetrack itself.
A trained spotter in Magdalena reported an estimated peak wind gust of about 60 mph from a severe thunderstorm.

The White Sands Missile Range mesonet station at Phillips Hill measured a peak wind gust of 62 mph from a severe thunderstorm. The station went offline 5 to 10 minutes later so the end time is estimated based on radar and surrounding observations.
The ASOS at the Roswell Air Center measured a 64 mph wind gust on the leading edge of a line of severe thunderstorms.
The RAWS station at Melrose Range observed a 69 mph wind gust on the leading edge of a line of severe thunderstorms.
The West Texas Mesonet station near Endee measured a 64 mph wind gust on the leading edge of a line of severe thunderstorms.

The Navajo Police Department reported on social media flash flooding from heavy rain through Coyote Canyon overtopping Navajo Route 9 between mile markers 7 and 14. Flash flooding closed the entrance to Nizhoni Housing and the highway. One vehicle appeared trapped in the floodwaters.
Reports on social media and by the NM DOT showed pictures of flash flooding over NM Highway 117 between mile markers 44 and 51.
Quarter size hail reported by a former NWS Employee.

A NWS Employee reported flash flooding stretching from San Pedro Creek at NM 14 where the creek was out of its banks. Numerous spots along NM 14 between Cedar Crest and the county line were flooded with rocks and debris over the road, with the worst of it at Ponderosa Park near Lantern Ridge. A USGS gage along the Tijeras Arroyo also observed a nine foot spike to 10 feet, coupled with a report of the arroyo overtopping Via Sedillo Road by two feet. The road was nearly impassible due to large rocks covering the roadway. Damage is an estimate.
Nickel to golf ball size hail reported near and just south of Los Lunas, NM.
Rainfall over the South Fork burn scar resulted in flash flooding that washed out a low water crossing along Maple Drive through Brady Canyon.

Repeated rounds of moderate to heavy rainfall resulted in standing water estimated up to a foot deep over an estimated one tenth of a mile stretch of highway along NM 13 at mile marker 29 approximately six miles west of U.S. Highway 285.

events.event_narrative: The Emergency Manager reported the start of the Unified Fire within the bosque area of the Rio Grande just southeast of Belen near the town of Madrone, NM. The fire quickly grew out of control in very dry and receptive fuels in the area thanks to persistent by modest southeasterly winds. Evacuations were ordered along Lagrima Road and Madrone Flyway road. Winds lessened during the evening of March 24th into the morning of March 25th as the fire grew to 300 total acres. The fire came under control March 25th with mop-up activities continuing a few days afterward. No damage to any structures, injuries, or fatalities were reported from this fire.

The Old 66 Wildfire was discovered mid-day March 27th, and quickly grew out of control north of I-40 near San Jon, NM. It burned quickly southward through grasslands crossing I-40 aided by strong northerly to northeasterly winds behind a strong cold front, growing to a final size of 4,111 acres. The fire came under control as winds subsided heading into March 28th. The fire caused a closure of NM 469 and Main Ave. in San Jon, NM. Emergency management reported the fire destroyed two structures, and that a wind farm that was threatened did not suffer any damage. No injuries or loss of life was reported. Damage is an estimate.

A steel building was destroyed and blown onto Interstate 40, six power poles were snapped, at least three water tanks were damaged beyond repair and a pumpkin shooter was damaged from sustained winds estimated at 55 to 70 mph with gusts of 90-100 mph. Corn stalks were also damaged in a large corn maze.

events.event_narrative: The Tusas Wildfire began along NM Highway 266 between mile markers 3 and 4 west of Sapello, NM. The fire grew northeastward into surrounding hills located in an area surrounded by but not included within the 2022 Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar. The fire grew in a critical fire weather environment April 23rd before coming under control April 24th, burning a total of 233 acres. No structures were reported destroyed or damaged.

The Riverside Fire began near Espanola, NM near the Santa Claran Hotel within the Santa Clara Pueblo. The fire grew to 44 acres destroying 5 structures, including one single-wide trailer, one home, one recreational vehicle, and two sheds. No injuries or fatalities were reported. Damage is an estimate.

The Sparks Wildfire was discovered in the afternoon of April 29th near NM Highway 156 in far western Quay County on private land. It quickly grew with reports of active running, spotting, and being wind-driven moving toward the east. While the fire was reported to have threatened multiple structures, there have been no reports of damage or destruction. The fire came under better control with slower creeping by April 29th.

The Crow Creek Wildfire was discovered in the afternoon of April 29th near NM Highway 445 north of Maxwell. The fire quickly grew to an estimated 1,200 acres making wind-driven runs north toward U.S. Highway 64, closing the highway between Colfax Tavern and Raton Municipal Airport. No structures were impacted.

The Hummingbird Wildfire was a lightning caused fire starting in a remote region of the Gila Wilderness, in Catron County. The wildfire was discovered during the afternoon of April 20th, growing within dead and downed trees within the old 2012 Whitewater-Baldy Fire burn scar, reaching 4,364 acres at month's end and continuing into May. An evacuation order was put in place for the Willow Creek Subdivision April 26th, lasting at least to the end of the month.
