Up to 6 inches of snow fell over parts of the Central High Plains.
A peak wind gust of 67 mph was also reported at 555pm MST. High winds (both sustained and peak gusts) were recorded at the Sierra Blanca Airport from around 600 am to 600 pm MST on the 23rd.

A peak wind gust to 76 mph was recorded at 414 am on the 26th. Sustained winds of 40 mph or greater and wind gusts of 58 mph or greater were recorded numerous times at the Sierra Blanca Airport between 11 am MST on the 25th through 3 pm MST on the 26th.
Up to four inches of snow fell over northern San Juan county.
While much of the area only received a few inches of snow, Chama reported around two feet of snow over the 2 day period.
Up to 5 inches of snow fell in the Farmington and Bloomfield areas.
Up to a foot of snow fell over the Northwest mountains, including around the Jemez mountains. Even higher totals were recorded at Snotel sites.
Up to a foot of snow fell over parts of the Sangre De Cristo mountains, with higher amounts at the ski areas and Snotel sites.
Up to 9 inches of snow fell over portions of the West Central Mountains, including around Gallup.
A peak wind gust of 66 mph was also recorded at 135pm MST.
A 42 year old male was found dead in his truck, apparently as a result of continued exposure to the cold.
High sustained winds 44 mph also at 0955 am. High winds were intermittently recorded through 100 pm.
Snowfall amounts ranged from four to 7 inches around Bloomfield, Farmington and Aztec.
Between two and six inches of snow accumulated across the zone.
Between four and eight inches of snow was common over the lower terrain, with over 16 inches of snow in many of the ski areas.
Two to six inches of snow was common over the West Central Mountains.
Two to four inches of snow accumulated over the lower elevations of the Upper Gila Region of the Southwest Mountains.
Report relayed by Channel 7 in Amarillo, TX.
Wind gust was measured by a Cannon Air Force Base runway sensor.
In addition to the 63 mph wind gust, sustained winds of up to 53 mph were also measured.
Public report of estimated 60 mph winds in downtown Clovis, relayed by Channel 7 in Amarillo, TX.
The thunderstorm wind gusts partially knocked over a windmill tower. A few branches were also downed from trees, with one branch knocking out the power.
A highway sign was blown off of its post and struck a vehicle.
Sustained wind speeds between 43 and 47 mph persisted for more than four hours at the Raton Crews Airport. The highest sustained wind speed of 47 mph was reported at both 5 and 7am.
The public reported high sustained winds estimated at 40 mph approximately 6 miles north of Springer at the Texaco Truck Stop.
The Raton Crews Airport reported wind gusts over 60 mph between 330am and 8am.  The peak wind gust of 69 mph was recorded at 7am.
The public reported an estimated wind gust of 60 mph 7 miles south of Raton. Winds were predominately out of the west.

The Clayton ASOS reported wind gusts between 62 and 64 mph for 30 minutes.  The peak wind gust of 64 mph occurred at 524pm, as the leading edge of the front went through. Sustained winds between 44 and 51 mph were also recorded during this time frame.
Wind gusts of 60 mph were estimated at the Northeast New Mexico Detention Facility in Clayton.
Peak wind gusts of at least 60 mph were reported six miles northwest of Rosebud.
Tucumcari ASOS reported a peak wind gust of 58 mph.  Sustained winds between 40 and 44 mph were also reported between 714 and 730pm.
On the north shore of Ute Lake, approximately one mile west of Logan, a weather station from Channel 7 in Amarillo reported a peak wind gust of 60 mph.

The ASOS at Cannon AFB gusted to 58 mph between 851 and 854pm. In addition, sustained winds between 40 and 45 mph occurred between 835 and 920pm.  Very similar observations were noted at the Clovis Airport AWOS, approximately three miles north-northwest of Texico. The public also reported sustained winds around 40 mph around 740pm near Grady.
Peak wind gusts between 59 mph and 61 mph were also recorded at the Las Vegas ASOS between 249 pm and 535 pm MST.
Peak wind gusts of 59 and 60 mph were also recorded at the Clines Corners ASOS between 236 pm and 334 pm MST.

A wind gusts of 62 mph was also reported in Wagon Mound at 1100 am MST. Wind gusts between 58 mph and 62 mph was recorded at the Las Vegas ASOS between 1127 am and 451 pm MST, while a sustained wind of 44 mph was recorded from 253 pm to 353 pm MST.

There were numerous reports of high winds at the Sierra Blanca Airport AWOS site. Sustained winds between 40 and 49 mph were recorded between|1055 am and 225 pm MST, while several gusts between 58 and 64 mph were recorded between 1035 am and 335 pm MST.
The Dora Mesonet site recorded numerous five minute observations of high sustained winds. Sustained wind speeds of 40 to 43 mph were recorded between 1000 am and 140 pm MST.
Up to eight inches of snow accumulated over the Sangre De Cristo mountains.
Two to six inches of snow fell over portions of the Northeast Highlands.
Five to seven inches of snow fell over southern Quay county.
The Gallup ASOS reported at 59 mph wind gust just prior to a cold frontal passage.  Areas of blowing dust were also noted on satellite imagery near the area.

The Las Vegas ASOS reported a peak wind gust of 70 mph at 330 am MST. However, wind gusts over 60 mph continued through approximately 530 am MST as the winds changed from a southerly to westerly direction due to the passage of a cold front.
A retired NWS Employee northeast of Quemado estimated wind gusts between 50 and 60mph between 430 and 930pm MST. Estimated sustained winds between 40 and 50mph were also reported.
The Las Vegas ASOS reported sustained winds over 40 mph between approximately 430 and 630am.  A peak sustained wind of 47 mph was reported at 453am MST.
The Bear Wallow RAWS site at 9953ft measured a 62 mph wind gust at 513pm MST as the cold front pushed through.
A retired NWS employee estimated 50 to 60 mph winds 7 miles northeast of Quemado.
An average of five inches of snow fell over the Upper Rio Grande valley.
Between two and seven inches of snow fell over mainly the eastern and northern portions of the zone.
Between six and twelve inches of snow fell over the Sangre De Cristo mountains, with higher amounts in the ski areas.
Two to seven inches of snow fell over the Northeast Highlands with drifts around two feet.
Around 6 inches of snow fell over Harding county with drifts of two to three feet.
Four to 15 inches of snow fell over the Far northeast Plains with drifts up to five feet.
Three to seven inches of snow fell over the Central High Plains.
Up to ten inches of snow was recorded around Conchas lake.
Five to 13 inches of snow blanketed Quay County with drifts around three feet.
Up to four inches of snow fell over eastern De Baca county.
Three inches of snow fell in northern Roosevelt county.
Three to five inches of snow fell across Curry county.

High peak wind gusts and high sustained winds developed shortly after midnight at the Sierra Blanca Airport and continued off and on through 900 am MST. The highest reported sustained wind speed of 51 mph was recorded at 116 am. Peak wind gusts of 63 mph were recorded at 1218 am, 61 mph at 116 am and 60 mph at 855 am.
Measured gust was recorded at KLVS. Sustained winds of 45 mph were also recorded at 553 am.

The Dora Mesonet measured sustained wind gusts equal to or exceeding 40 mph for approximately 3 hours. The highest sustained wind speed was 49 mph. A peak wind gust of 61 mph occurred at 310 pm MST. Strong winds caused the roof on the Portales Dream Center to peel off the sheet-metal roof around 100 pm MST.
Winds gusts equal to or exceeding 58 mph were recorded at Cannon Air Force Base between approximately 12 pm and 2 pm MST.  The peak wind gust of 62 mph occurred at 1255 pm.
Sustained wind speeds over 40 mph occurred at Cannon Air Force Base for over an hour. Visibilities were reduced to 3 miles in blowing dust.

A Gallup woman, Denise Caleb, was killed in her SUV on Interstate 40 due to icy roads and windy conditions. Her vehicle was heading east on I-40 near Gallup when she lost control and crossed the median and went into oncoming traffic. Her SUV was struck by a tractor-trailer.
A wind gust to 60 mph was also recorded at 353 pm MST.
A 58 mph gust was also recorded at 1536 pm MST and a sustained wind of 49 mph was recorded at 1555 pm MST.

Wind damage was reported eight miles south of Albuquerque at 1200 am MST. A 50 foot section of fence was blown over and gate hinges snapped. Golf carts were tossed around by the wind. A gust to 58 mph was recorded at the Double Eagle Airport at 1215 am MST. A wind gust to 65 mph was reported at the Isleta Pueblo, where a FEDEX truck traveling on Interstate 25 was blown off the road and another tractor trailor tipped over. There were numerous reports of shingles blown off the roofs of homes. Large trees were downed in Bosque Farms. Power to 5000 homes went out. A 40 foot tree was uprooted in the Five Points neighborhood and crushed a swing set.
A peak wind gust of 69 mph was also recorded at 1245 am MST, and sustained winds of 49 mph were recorded at 1244 am MST.
A gust to 58 mph was recorded at Cannon AFB at 1055 am MST.

A wind gust to 58 mph was reported three miles northwest of Texico. A 35 year old man was killed in Clovis when a gust of wind caught a door on a semitrailer and slammed the man into the loading dock wall. He suffered head injuries.
Intense winds knocked down 4 medium sized trees, broke a basketball backboard off its poll and blew several 2x10 pieces of lumber around and hit a car causing minor damage in the south valley.

Sustained winds between 35 and 40 knots were observed at the Clovis AWOS between 815am and 1015am MST. Cannon AFB ASOS had sustained winds between 35 and 39 knots and a wind gust of 50 knots between 755am and 1024pm MST.
A wind gust to 51 knots was recorded at 940am and 53 knots at 955am MST.
Sustained winds between 35 and 40 knots were recorded at the Dora Mesonet site from 725am to 310pm MST. A wind gust of 50 knots was recorded at 1115am MST.

Thundersnow resulted in significant snow amounts from Tesuque and Santa Fe to Cowles.  6 to 8 inches of snow was reported between Tesuque and Santa Fe which prompted Highway 285 to be closed for a time.  A spotter in Cowles, near 8700 feet, reported 14 inches of snow these storms.
Thundersnow resulted in a quick 6 to 8 inches of snowfall between Pojoaque and Tesuque which prompted Highway 285 to be closed for a time.
Between 2 and 5 inches of snow were reported from near Sandia Park to south of Tijeras.
Wind gusts between 50 and 52 knots were recorded between 216pm and 459pm MST. A sustained wind speed of 37 knots was also recorded between 255pm and 355pm MST.
High wind gusts toppled a billboard and ripped the roofs off of four buildings.

A roof was blown off the abandoned Club Cafe on Historic Route 66 in downtown Santa Rosa. Another roof was blown off a two story home. Several power poles and light posts were damaged or snapped in two. Damage occurred to 87 cars and the buildings at the Northside Auto Park.

Though many locations across the Northwest Mountains above 7500 feet only received between 3 and 7 inches of snow, similar amounts were also observed below 7500 feet.  Spotters in Los Alamos estimate around 5 inches of snow fell.

Widespread snows of 3 to 7 inches were reported across the Sangre De Cristo Mountains.  However, thundersnow resulted in localized heavy snowfall near Gascon, where a trained spotter reported 13 inches. In addition, 8 inches of snow was reported northwest of Taos by a CoCoRaHS observer.

The heaviest snow fell during the afternoon and evening hours of the 17th and it piled up quickly. Between 4 and 7 inches of snowfall was reported across the Sandia and Manzano Mountains.  Some totals include 7 inches 10 miles south of Tijeras, 5.5 inches 6 miles northeast of Cedar Crest and 4.5 inches 5 miles east-southeast of Sandia Park.

A CoCoRaHS observer reported 9.5 inches near El Porvenir, or about 8 miles northwest of Las Vegas. Thundersnow attributed to the high snowfall amounts in the northern appendage of the Central High Plains.
Shingles were blown off a roof of a mobile home in Algodones.
Golf ball size hail was reported along Pine Lodge Road or Highway 246 northwest of Roswell.  One citizen reported hail dents to their family vehicle.
Localized flash flooding reported 20 to 30 miles south of Shiprock on State Highway 491. Part of the road was washed out.
Heavy rain caused about four feet of mud to slide into an irrigation canal running along Navajo route 362. This forced water over route 362 and onto farm land and residents' homes.
Nickel size hail was reported at Buena Vista.
Hail accumulated to around 4 inches in depth.
Wind gusts of 52 knots reported 3 different times between 413pm and 420pm MST. A sustained wind of 41 knots was also recorded at 414pm MST.
Hail and strong winds knocked siding off of a home, broke house windows and piled up over one foot deep on Route 202, east of U.S. Highway 70. A funnel cloud was also reported to be in the area.
Quarter size hail was reported along Interstate 40 at Exit 267.
The hail damaged a lot of vegetation and piled up three inches deep.

A small dumpster was rolled over into a chain link fence by a local eddy or dust devil on the edge of an outflow boundary. Debris within the dumpster was spread out across the field of an elementary school.

Three major fires consumed around 44,000 acres of rangeland from May 20th into the 24th. The three fires were located north of Capitan, around Arabela and near Picacho. The most significant of these was the Fresquez 2 fire north of Capitan. It burned around 10,000 acres north of Highway 246/48 and six ranches suffered fire damage to various degrees. Burned pasture/grassland was the main fire damage as no structures were damaged. However, several cattle were killed in the blaze.
Showers produced a high wind gust from a dry microburst 8 miles north of Mountainair.
Showers produced a high wind gust from a dry microburst 2 miles southeast of Edgewood.
Showers produced a high wind gust from a dry microburst 6 miles northeast of Las Vegas.
Showers produced a high wind gust from a dry microburst 2 miles east northeast of Clayton.

High wind gusts were reported to the Emergency Manager on the evening of the 6th. These high winds were from showers that produced little rain but damaging downburst winds. Damage was reported between Edgewood and Moriarty, south of Interstate 40. A 60 foot mobile home was blown over onto a truck. A man inside the truck at the time was able to escape without injury. In addition, one-third of a tin roof was blown off a building and a storage shed was blown 100 yards.

Highway 380 was closed between mile markers 2 and 4 east of San Antonio due to water flowing over the roadway after over an estimated 2.5 inches of rain fell in less than 2 hours. Mud and rocks had to be cleared off the road before it was reopened. The flash flooding destroyed an 80 foot section of water supply line just east of the community of San Pedro.  This left residents of San Pedro temporarily without water. In addition, a low water crossing in the Bosquecito area was flooded which halted traffic for a few hours.
Heavy rains caused a flash flood along Highway 605 north-northeast of Milan. Two feet of water was running over the road which made the road impassible.
A gas station attendant reported customers were unable to hold their footing in the high wind gusts.
A wind gust to 60 mph was recorded at the SchoolNet site in House.
High winds between 700 and 730 pm MST ripped telephone polls in half and broke tree branches 8 to 12 inches in diameter. Electrical power was out for about 7 hours.
Spotters and law enforcement reported golfball size hail in Los Alamos for at least 5 minutes.
The hail dented automobiles and cracked wind shields.
The hail caused extensive damage to cars.
In addition to the hail, a grass fire was started from a lightning strike.
Winds were estimated between 50 and 60 mph with no damage reported.
A two foot diameter, 60 foot tall tree was blown down in the front of a police station. Winds were estimated at 60 to 70 mph.
An amateur radio operator estimated a 58 mph wind gust from a thunderstorm.
A peak wind gust of 69 mph lasted for 9 minutes. The highest two minute wind speed was 58 mph at 525 pm MST.
A schoolnet site recorded a wind gust to 58 mph.
There were large tree branches and power lines downed from high winds.
A spotter reported a wind gust to 68 mph near Highway 206.  Blowing dust reduced the visibility to near zero.
A high wind gust estimated at 60 mph reduced the visibility to a quarter of a mile in blowing dust.
Large tree branches were downed all along 18th street.
A roof was blown off a building and one wall collapsed at 109 W. 2nd St.
A wind shield was damaged on a vehicle.
There was extensive 0.75 inch hail with very heavy rain.
Multiple trees and power lines were knocked down from the strong wind gusts.
A trampoline was blown into power lines.
The tornado was observed about 8 miles north of Edgewood, was on the ground for about 6 minutes and moved slowly to the southeast.
There was two and one half feet of standing water at the intersection of Juan Tabo and Candelaria with cars stranded in the water.
The Rio Felix was flowing at a depth of ten feet and began to flood the area around Cherokee Road, three miles west of Hagerman.
Highway 249 east of Hagerman was closed with damage to the road due to water overflowing the Rio Felix.
Water overflowed Walnut Creek about 2 miles south of Lake Arthur, flooding a portion of State Road 2.
Heavy rain caused the normally dry Rio Felix to rise ten feet and flood Morgan road west of Hagerman.
Heavy rain caused the normally dry Rio Felix to rise 10 feet and flood Lincoln road west of Hagerman.
A cooperative observer reported that several tree limbs were downed around town including a large branch from a Cottonwood tree.
Several three to four inch tree branches were snapped off.
Eight to 10 inches of water was running over State Highway 456 between mile markers 16 and 30.  Cars were submerged in the water and mud and had to be pulled out near mile marker 25.
A microburst downed a mature tree at the intersection of Ladera and Unser.
There was lots of pea to dime size hail with a few up to the size of golf balls.
Large tree limbs were snapped off of trees.
The hail size ranged from peas to nickels.
Hail was mostly pea size, with a few quarter size.
An off-duty Air Force Base employee reported tree branches three to four inches in diameter were snapped off trees.
The security team at Los Alamos National Laboratory reported penny to nickel sized hail.
The hail was reported at the Bandelier National Monument.
Hail covered the ground.

Several pieces of metal were blown off storefront facade near 2nd and Main Street as well as up to 8 inch diameter tree limbs broken off trees within a few blocks of the courthouse.  This was reported by KRQE News Channel 13.
A tree fell on a mobile home, destroying its roof.
A spotter estimated a wind gust of at least 80 mph, with sustained winds around 55 mph.
A Schoolnet site reported high winds between 549 and 553 pm MST at Ute Lake. A peak wind gust of 60 mph was reported at 553 pm with sustained winds over 40 mph.
The Tucumcari ASOS reported wind gusts of 60 mph between 709 and 718 pm MST.
A mobile home, four miles east of Midway, was rolled over by strong winds.
A roof of a building sustained damage after being peeled back from damaging winds.
Flash flooding from Berrendo Creek created flows two to three feet deep over Brown Road.  People were stranded on top of their cars.
A SchoolNet site in House reported a 63 mph wind gust from the south-southwest.
The roof of a barn was torn off when gusty winds moved through the area.
The strong dust devil produced some damage, including ripping the metal siding off a hay barn, damaging a coral and knocking over a 5th wheel trailer.
A brief tornado, likely a landspout, occurred two miles south of the Highway 64 and 285 intersection.  The tornado tore the roof off a barn and ripped up some fencing.

Water was flowing rapidly down Corrales Road, as well as on Martin Luther King Blvd, between 7th and 21st Streets. The water level was at or above curb height. Significant debris covered several streets, especially on 21st Street. Curb high water was also flowing rapidly down 21st Street approaching Green Acres Park.
Hail between 0.88 inches and 1.75 inches was reported between 415pm and 430pm MST in Clovis. Some roof damage was reported, with leaves stripped off trees and damage to corn and tomato crops.
The hail lasted for 10 minutes and covered the ground.
Hail was reported on the south side of Clovis near U.S. Highways 70 and 60/84.
Several customers at the Texaco truck stop and a county sheriff estimated wind gusts around 60 mph.
A 58 mph wind gusts was reported at the SchoolNet site at Frost Ranch.
Heavy rain caused flooding on County Road 155, washing out culverts and parts of the road.
Hail was mostly pea size, but a few stones were the size of a golfball.
Hail was mostly golf ball size, however, a few stones were around two inches.
KVII-TV in Amarillo relayed a view report of penny size hail.
Pea to penny size hail lasted 35 minutes.  1.80 inches of rain also fell in the same time frame.
The Police Department confirmed golf ball size hail along Interstate 25.
Ping pong ball size hail was relayed via KVII in Amarillo from a viewer.
Report relayed through spotternetwork.org.
Several 1.75 inch to 3 inch hail stones were along State Highway 392.  Relayed by spotternetwork.org.
A trained spotter reported ping pong ball to golf ball size hail.
A member of the public lost a truck window at the intersection of State Highways 392 and 469.
A trained spotter estimated a 60 mph wind gust seven miles west of House.
KVII-TV in Amarillo relayed a 65 mph wind gust from their Schoolnet site at Frost Ranch along State Highway 93.
The Broadview Fire Department estimated a 60 mph wind gust.
Hail was reported along U.S. Highway 54 northeast of Tucumcari. Hail fog developed as a result of the amount of hail along the ground.  A wall cloud was also sighted with this storm.
Multiple reports of a tornado were received approximately 10 miles north of Roy.  No damage was reported.

A 24 year old man was critically injured when he was struck by lightning while riding his horse along a metal fence. The horse was killed. The man's hat had a four inch hole in it from the lightning strike.
Hail started with an accumulation of peas then grew in size up to quarters.
The nickel sized hail was soft and mushy.
Quarter size hail lasted 10 minutes and covered the ground.
A vehicle was washed away in an arroyo near the intersection of Second Canyon Road and Highway N11-49 (also called Navajo Service Route 11).
Four feet of water near the intersection of Mountain View Road and Highway 53 made the road impassible.
Heavy rain caused a vehicle to be washed away in an arroyo.  Law enforcement discovered the vehicle unoccupied with keys in the ignition.
Dirt roads were washed away by the heavy rainfall in the Timberlake Ranch subdivision.  Giant boulders blocked the roadways, preventing residents from making it home from the main roadway.
Highway 66 was closed for approximately one hour near Western Skies Road due to high water.

Four people in the North Diversion Channel under Interstate 25 at Montgomery Blvd. were swept downstream by swift moving water from a nearby thunderstorm that was producing heavy rain. Three men were able to pull themselves out of the Channel, but a fourth male, Brandon Clifford Jordan, was found dead the next day in the Channel at 2nd street and Alameda.
Harry Beggerly, 61, died near Quemado Lake from a lightning strike on the afternoon of August 30, while seeking shelter from the rain under a 30 foot tall tree.
A home was damaged from excess runoff from the Rio San Jose.
A vehicle was damaged on Interstate 25 from the one inch hail.
The Las Vegas ASOS reported a wind gust to 59 mph.
The Las Vegas ASOS reported a wind gust to 61 mph.
The Gallup ASOS reported a wind gust to 58 mph.
The Raton ASOS reported a peak wind gust of 58 mph.

Thunderstorms over northwest New Mexico during the early morning hours produced a cloud to ground lightning strike that hit the 96.1 FM KZRM Radio transmitter on Rabbit Peak, just west northwest of Chama. The station was off the air for at least three weeks.
The Clines Corners ASOS reported a peak wind gust of 58 mph.
Five telephone poles were snapped along Highway 70, about 4 miles west of Roswell.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: The Santa Fe Ski Area reported 9 inches of snow at mid slope.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Though widespread amounts of 5 inches were reported, heavier amounts were more localized.  However, 8 inches of snow was reported southeast of Eagle Nest.
Warning snow amounts were spotty across the area, however, 6 inches of snow was reported Lake Maloya, which is just below 7500 feet.
The top of the Sandia Peak Tramway at 10300 feet reported 12 inches of snow.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Snowfall amounts of 8 to 12 inches were common near Angel Fire and Eagle Nest.  The highest total of 12 inches was reported 12 miles south-southeast of Angel Fire at an elevation of 10080 feet.
The AWOS at Sierra Blanca Regional Airport reached a peak wind gust of 67 mph at 1035 pm MST.  However, wind gusts did exceed 60 mph between 955 and 1055 pm MST.

Multiple snowfall reports of 2 to 6 inches were received across the Northwest Plateau. Around 5 inches of snow fell in the Farmington area, while up to 7 inches of snow was reported approximately 10 miles north of Farmington.
Highest snow accumulations were found near the Colorado border just north of La Plata and Cedar Hill.  Up to 10.5 inches of snow was reported.
Three to 5.5 inches of snow was reported around the Gallup area.
Highest snowfall accumulations were near the Colorado border, including 8 inches at the Raton Port of Entry.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Just over 8 inches of snow was reported across portions of the west slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, including at the Sipapu Ski Area.
Up to 6 inches of snowfall was reported around Crownpoint.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: Over a foot of snow was reported at both Taos Ski Valley and Red River Ski Area.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: Over 8 inches of snow was reported at Ski Santa Fe.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Widespread snowfall amounts of 2 to 6 inches were reported across the east slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, though higher amounts were reported above 9000 feet. Over a foot of snow was reported at the Angel Fire Ski Resort.

Widespread snow amounts of 2 to 6 inches were reported across the lower elevations of the south central mountains. However, more than a foot of snow was reported across the higher elevations, including the Sierra Blanca SNOTEL and Apachi Ski Area.
Up to 6 inches of snow was reported near and north of Tres Piedras.
Snowfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches were common across the northwest highlands. The greatest snow totals were found just southwest of Cuba.
Snowfall totals ranging from 8 to 10 inches were reported by the Hopewell SNOTEL as well as members of the public across the higher elevations of the San Juan Mountains.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: Taos Ski Valley reported over a foot of snow across the ski basin. Up to 12 inches fell at the base, while 16 inches of snow fell at Kachina Peak.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: Elevations generally above 10000 feet received around 8 inches of snow, including the Santa Fe Ski area.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Over a foot of snow fell at the highest elevations, including at the Angel Fire Ski Resort.

Up to 15 inches of snow fell across the highest elevations of the south central mountains, including at the Sierra Blanca SNOTEL and at Ski Apache.  However, 9 inches of snow was also reported on the southwest side of Ruidoso, with somewhat lesser amounts elsewhere.

Jarrod Truesdale, a 26 year old man, was killed by a lightning strike in the parking lot of Rio Rancho High School before a fireworks show.  His wife, 26, was also struck and sustained serious injuries.  Their 4 kids, ranging from 18 months to 7 years in age, as well as the wife's 21 year old sister also sustained injuries.  The family was headed for their vehicle to seek shelter from the storm.

Up to 6 inches of snow fell west of the Interstate 25 corridor late on the 2nd into the morning hours of the 3rd.  Lesser amounts were reported along and east of the interstate.  Light snow lingered into the afternoon hours.
Widespread snow amounts of 5 to 6 inches were reported across the northeast highlands.  However, isolated higher amounts up to 9 inches were also reported.
Widespread snowfall amounts of 4 to 6 inches were reported, mainly across the western portion of the county.  However, an isolated amount of 8 inches was also reported.

Widespread snow amounts of 4 to 6 inches, mainly across the western portion of the county, were reported by both the CoCoRaHS network and locally trained spotters.  Very little area across the county received less than 3 inches.
Widespread amounts of 3 to 5 inches were noted across the county, including in Roswell.
Four to 6 inches of snow was common across eastern Lincoln County.  However, isolated higher amounts up to 8.5 inches were noted immediately east and northeast of the Capitan Mountains.
Around 4 inches of snow was reported in and north of Tres Piedras.

Up to 15 inches of snow fell across the highest elevations of the south central mountains, including at the Sierra Blanca SNOTEL and at Ski Apache.  However, 9 inches of snow was also reported on the southwest side of Ruidoso, with somewhat lesser amounts elsewhere.
Significant snow accumulations blanketed eastern Lincoln County.  The heaviest amounts were across southeast Lincoln County where up to 9 inches of snow was reported.
Significant snow accumulations blanketed southwest Chaves County.  Areas north and west of Dunken received up to 20 inches of snow.
Significant snow accumulations blanketed eastern Lincoln County.  The heaviest amounts were across southeast Lincoln County where up to 9 inches of snow was reported.
Significant snow accumulations blanketed southwest Chaves County.  Areas north and west of Dunken received up to 20 inches of snow.
Heaviest snow accumulations were reported generally above 6500 feet across the far northwest highlands.  The cooperative observer in Dulce recorded a total of 14 inches.

Widespread snow amounts of 2 inches or greater coated the northwest highlands.  The greatest amounts were near Lindrith, where 8 inches of snow was reported.  The heavy snow resulted in one fatality.  Jimmy Shendo, of Jemez Pueblo, was driving a Toyota truck southbound on U.S. 550 in southeast San Juan County, when he lost control and slid into the northbound lanes.  He was struck by an oncoming vehicle at mile marker 110.  Shendo, 59, was not wearing a seatbelt and was partially ejected from the truck.
Snow amounts of 2 to 6 inches were reported across the West Central Plateau.  The greatest amounts were found in McKinley County.

Over a foot of snow fell across portions of the West Central Mountains.  The hardest hit areas were near El Morro where up to 14 inches of snow was reported.  In addition, McGaffey picked up 8 inches of new snow.

The San Juan Mountains were the hardest hit area from this winter storm - particularly the west slopes. Widespread amounts of 10 to 20 inches were common, however, there were a few locales that received more.  Over 2 feet of snow was recorded at the Hopewell SNOTEL site, while almost 2 feet of snow was recorded at the Chamita SNOTEL.  The cooperative observer in Chama measured a total of 17.5 inches for the event.

Over a foot of snow was reported across the Jemez Mountains, including 12.5 inches northwest of La Cueva and around 22 inches at Pajarito Ski Area. Strong winds around Los Alamos resulted in downed power lines in the North Mesa and Barranca Mesa areas.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: In general, 8 to 16 inches of snow fell across the west slopes of the Sangre De Cristo Mountains.  Some reported amounts include 14 inches in Tererro and around 8 inches at Sipapu Ski Area.  The heavy snow resulted in one death in the Santa Fe Foothills.  Gail Patterson, a 57-year old woman from Dallas, TX was trying to flag down an oncoming vehicle after her own vehicle slid off Atalaya Hill Road, a narrow, steep grade road, into a drainage ditch.  The vehicle she was trying to flag down started to slide down the icy road, struck and killed her.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Up to one foot of snow was reported across the east slopes of the Sangre De Cristo Mountains. One foot of snow was reported at Sapello, Angel Fire Ski area and 7 miles north of Mora.  In addition, the cooperative observer in Eagle Nest reported 10 inches of snow.
Up to 18 inches of snow was reported around Tres Piedras.  The heaviest accumulations were above 7500 feet, however, lower elevations still received 3 to 6 inches of snow.
Much of the Lower Chama River Valley received between 2 and 6 inches of snowfall.  The heaviest accumulations fell northeast of Youngsville, between the Jemez and San Juan Mountains.
Above 6500 feet, between 3 and 6 inches of snow was reported.  Strong winds and ice knocked down power lines resulting in power outages to approximately 4800 customers.

The Interstate 25 corridor between Raton and Watrous picked up 3 to 5 inches of snowfall. Strong winds also created areas of blowing and drifting snow. Southbound Interstate 25 was closed for a few hours to prevent travelers from heading farther south toward Springer, where visibilities were worse.

Up to a foot of snow fell in blizzard conditions as winds topped out over 100 mph across the peaks of the southwest mountains.  The heaviest snowfall occurred in western Catron County near Luna, but the winds blew hard across the entire area.  The Magdalena Ridge Observatory at 10,600 feet recorded sustained winds between 80 and 120 mph with gusts to 135 mph before the instrument failed.  The wind gusts were literally picking people off their feet. Visibilities were near zero in blowing and drifting snow.

Light snow began falling the evening of the 7th, but the heavier snow came in the morning of the 8th as a strong cold front plowed from west to east.  Blizzard conditions were noted as visibilities dropped to near zero in blowing and drifting snow with winds gusting up to 78 mph.  Up to 8 inches of snow fell across the top of the Sandia Mountains.

Light snow began falling the evening of the 7th, but the heavier snow came in the morning of the 8th as a strong cold front plowed from west to east.  Blizzard conditions were noted for about 4 hours as visibilities dropped near one quarter of a mile in blowing and drifting snow with wind gusts estimated near 60 mph. Two to 4 inches of snow was reported across the Estancia Valley.

Light snow began falling the evening of the 7th, but the heavier snow came in the morning of the 8th as a strong cold front plowed from west to east.  Blizzard conditions were noted for about 4 hours as visibilities dropped near or below one quarter of a mile in blowing and drifting snow with wind gusts up to 65 mph. Two to 5 inches of snow was reported across the Central Highlands, with the heaviest amounts north of Interstate 40.

Light snow began falling the evening of the 7th, but the heavier snow came in the morning of the 8th as a strong cold front swept through the area.  Blizzard conditions developed as visibilities were significantly reduced in blowing and drifting snow with wind gusts up to 66 mph. Three to 6 inches of snow was reported across the area with locally higher amounts west of Interstate 25.
A sensor on the northern end of White Sands Missile Range, 15 miles east-southeast of San Antonio, recorded a peak wind gust of 61 mph at 1015 am.

The Chupadera RAWS site recorded wind gusts around 60 mph much of the morning through early afternoon.  The peak wind gust was 62 mph at 639am.  The high winds toppled trees in Spencer Park in Carrizozo and lifted at least two carport roofs from their bases. One of the carport roofs was deposited onto a fence, which was also damaged.
A White Sands Missile Range sensor, 35 miles southeast of San Antonio, recorded a peak wind gust of 61 mph at 515 am, and recorded multiple other gusts between 58 and 60 mph from 11 am to 1 pm.

Numerous gusts over 60 mph were recorded at Sierra Blanca airport.  The peak wind gust of 78 mph was reported at 1035 am.  Between 700 am and 800 am trees were downed from the high winds.  A few trees fell on and damaged two of the ski lifts at Ski Apache and one of the buildings at Ski Apache had roof damage.  The Ski area was closed on the 8th due to the high winds and on the 9th for clean up.  In addition, a 125-foot commercial tower on Buck Mountain was toppled by the high winds, causing radio station and other commercial outages.
A spotter northeast of Arabela reported estimated wind gusts in excess of 60 mph for much of the morning and early afternoon hours.
The Dunken RAWS site reported a peak wind gust of 61 mph at 709 am with other gusts to 58 mph later that morning.

The Roswell ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 61 mph at 1149 am, however, the strong winds affected the entire area. Not only were 4 power poles broken in Roswell and numerous power lines down, a semi-truck trailer was blown over while parked on the north side of Roswell.  The truck was blown into a utility box containing a 12,000 Volt power line. In addition, a roof was torn off an equipment shed approximately 16 miles west of Roswell.
A peak wind gust of 67 mph was recorded at Lake Sumner Village between 120 and 130 pm.

The West Texas Mesonet sensor near Dora recorded a peak wind gust of 63 mph at both 105 and 110 pm, though severe gusts were recorded frequently for over an hour. Other severe wind gusts between 59 and 61 mph were recorded at Melrose, Elida and Portales by Schoolnet and RAWS sites.

The Clovis AWOS recorded a peak wind gust of 66 mph at 135 pm.  In addition, the KCVS ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 60 mph and a Schoolnet site north of Clovis recorded a 62 mph wind gust. The strong wind toppled power lines and a power pole fell on the old Pizza Hut building on West Seventh Street.  Other damage included roof coverings from two garages blown off and a storage barn wall was blown down.

Two KVII Amarillo Schoolnet sites recorded peak wind gusts over 60 mph.  The Schoolnet site at Frost Ranch, approximately 9 miles east-northeast of Wheatland, recorded a 65 mph gust, while the Logan Schoolnet site recorded a 62 mph gust.   In addition, the Tucumcari ASOS measured a 62 mph wind gust.
Wind gusts near 60 mph were estimated across the county.
The cooperative observer at Conchas Dam estimated winds of 60 mph, which broke 8 inch diameter tree limbs across the area.
The Mills Canyon RAWS site recorded a peak wind gust of 59 mph at 205 pm.
The KSRR AWOS measured sustained winds above 40 mph for over an hour and a half.  The peak sustained wind speed was 53 mph.

A trampoline was picked up and carried 150 yards over a camp trail 1.5 miles west of Roswell.
Wind gusts were estimated near 60 mph. This high wind event began as a blizzard which began late on December 7th and ended at 11am on the 8th.

The KCQC measured sustained winds over 40 mph constantly between 11 am and 1245 pm.  The sustained winds peaked at 46 mph. This high wind event began as a blizzard which began late on December 7th and ended at 11am on the 8th.

KCQC measured extreme wind gusts constantly between 11 am and 1230 pm. The peak wind gust during this time was 62 mph. This high wind event began as a blizzard which began late on December 7th and ended at 11am on the 8th. The peak wind gust during the blizzard event was 66 mph.

Wind gusts were estimated near 65 mph at the top of Sandia Peak. This high wind event began as a blizzard which began late on December 7th and ended at 11am on the 8th.  The peak wind gust during the blizzard event was 78 mph.

Heavy snow blasted the Sandia and Manzano Mountains with several reports of between 6 and 14 inches of new snow.  Across the east mountains, where around 6 inches of snow was reported, Ken Garrison, a 77-year old man, died after trying to walk home in sub-freezing temperatures after a minor crash disabled his pickup truck. The truck likely slid off the road and was stuck in the snow around Highway 217 and Griego Road around 6 am on the 31st.  His body was found approximately 300 yards from the truck.
Local amounts of up to 12 inches of snow fell across the South Central Highlands.

Between 2 and 7 inches of snow fell across the Santa Fe Metro Area, with the heaviest amounts falling in the Santa Fe Foothills. Icy roads lead to a three-car crash 7 miles south of El Dorado on Highway 285 on the morning of the 23rd.  Kendall Kalstad, age 59, died when his Volkswagen Beetle was struck head-on by a car that slid on the ice at mile marker 282.  The man's car was then struck from behind by another vehicle that couldn't stop in time.  Three other people were also injured in the accident. The highway was closed for several hours after the crash.
Between 2 and 8 inches of snow fell across the Santa Fe Metro area.  The heaviest amounts were located in the Santa Fe foothills.

Though snow amounts were generally 2 inches or less, it was enough to create slick roads.  Luis Segovia-Cabrera, age 39, sustained massive head injuries after he lost control of his SUV and crossed the median on Interstate 40 near exit 96 and crashed into a commercial tractor-trailer head-on. It is suspected he was driving too fast for the conditions and slid on the ice.  Segovia-Cabrera died more than a month later after he was taken off of life support. Three other people sustained injuries from the crash.

An 88 year old woman was found dead 7 miles north of Crystal.  The woman insisted on visiting her sister at 4 am, but her vehicle got stuck in melting snow and mud. She tried to continue on foot, but was unsuccessful.  The woman's body was discovered several yards from her vehicle.

A family from California was headed east on I-40 when they hit a patch of ice around 930 am in Gallup. Their pickup truck slid into the westbound lanes where it struck a second pickup truck head on.  Martha R. Toscano, 45, died in the crash. Moreno G. Toscano, 51 and their 4 month old child, Emmuel as well as James T. Riley, 29, of Jamestown, NM sustained injuries.  Snow amounts across Gallup ranged from 1 to 2 inches.
