Widespread snow amounts of 5 to 8 inches were reported across the Santa Fe Metro Area.

The east slopes of the Sandia and Manzano Mountains was one of the hardest hit areas.  Some reports included 14 inches south of Golden, around a foot just northeast of Tajique and near 10 inches around Sedillo.
Areas west of a line from Moriarty to Willard received the most snow.  Reports between 6 and 10 inches were received.
Between 6 and 12 inches of snow was reported across the Central Highlands.
Five to six inches of snow was reported around Corona.
Between 2 and 6 inches of snow fell across the area.
Between 5 and 10 inches fell across the area.  The heaviest snow was reported west of Interstate 25.
Around 8 inches of snow fell near Anton Chico.  Elsewhere, between 1 and 4 inches of snow fell.

Approximately 1 to 3 inches of snow created slick and hazardous roadways across the West Central Plateau.  A man, age 60, was killed after losing control of his SUV on Interstate 40 near Gallup around 645 am MST.  His wife and grandchildren were also in the vehicle, but survived with only minor injuries.  Almost 30 crashes were reported, though no others resulted in injuries.

A 31 year old man was killed after he lost control of his vehicle and it rolled over an icy road near Tesuque. The man was headed south on County Road 73 toward US 84/285 when he slid of the roadway.  He was not wearing a seat belt and was partially ejected through the driver's side window.

Up to 7 inches of snow fell across the Chuska Mountains, however, it was the cold weather that claimed the life of a man near Rabbit Brush, New Mexico (just across the state line from Fort Defiance). He was walking back home after being dropped off along Navajo Route 12.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Up to nine inches of snow fell over the West Slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: Up to a foot of snow fell on the high terrain of the northern Sangre de Cristo Mountains.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: Over a foot of snow was common over the high terrain of the southern Sangre de Cristo Mountains.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Around of foot of snow was common along the East Slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains.
Between three and six inches of snow fell across the Lower Chama River Valley.
Between three and seven inches of snow fell across the Upper Rio Grande Valley.
Five to eight inches of snow was reported across the Santa Fe Metro Area.
Snowfall over the Sandia and Manzano Mountains averaged seven to 13 inches.
Three to eight inches of snow blanketed the Estancia Valley.
Three to six inches of snow fell across the Central Highlands.
Two to six inches of snow fell across the Northeast Highlands.
Three to seven inches of snow blanketed Guadalupe county, including around the Santa Rosa Lake State Park.
Two to four inches of new snow fell on De Baca County, including around Sumner Lake.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: Taos Ski Area picked up another foot of snow.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: Santa Fe SNOTEL as well as the Santa Fe Ski Area picked up between 12 and 14 inches of snow.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Eight to nine inches of snow fell around Angel Fire and Ute Park.
Eight to nine inches of snow fell across Raton Ridge and Johnson Mesa.  Snow drifts were reportedly 2 to 4 feet high.
Three to six inches of snow fell across the Far Northeast Highlands.
Four to seven inches of snow fell across Union County.  The highest amounts were noted across the southeast part of the county.
Up to four inches of snow fell across eastern Harding County.
Up to five inches of snow fell across eastern Quay County.
The Raton ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 58 mph from the north.
KSRR recorded sustained west-southwest winds above 40 mph for about six hours.  The peak sustained wind speed was 54 mph which occurred around the noon hour.
KSRR recorded severe wind gusts nearly continuously for approximately 7 hours.  The peak wind gust of 71 mph was measured at 215 pm MST.

The Roswell ASOS recorded sustained westerly winds above 40 mph for just over an hour. The peak sustained wind was 47 mph which occurred at 410 pm MST. The strong winds resulted in blowing dust which reduced visibility down to one mile at times.
Several White Sands Missile Range Mesonet sites recorded wind gusts to 59 mph.
The Cannon AFB ASOS recorded sustained winds over 40 mph for around 90 minutes.  The peak sustained wind of 49 mph occurred at 327 pm MST.  Visibility was reduced to 1 1/4 miles in blowing dust.
The Cannon AFB ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 63 mph at 252 pm MST.  Another wind gust to 59 mph was measured at 415 pm MST.

The Double Eagle Airport AWOS on the west side of the Albuquerque Metro Area recorded a peak wind gust of 59 mph.  Visibility was reduced down to 5 miles in blowing dust.  The strong winds collapsed a large tent sending a teenage boy to the hospital with minor injuries at the annual Pork and Brew in Rio Rancho.
Clines Corners blew up to 59 mph around 4 pm MST.
The West Texas Mesonet station near Dora recorded sustained winds over 40 mph for over 3 hours.  The max sustained wind was 45 mph which occurred around 2 pm MST.
The West Texas Mesonet station near Dora recorded a peak wind gust of 61 mph at 4 pm MST.  Another wind gust of 58 mph was measured at 7 pm.

The Dunken RAWS site recorded sustained westerly wind speeds over 40 mph for at least 2 hours.  The peak sustained wind was 43 mph. The strong and gusty winds pealed a metal roof off an old barn east of Elk.
The Dunken RAWS site recorded a peak wind gust of 68 mph at 409 pm MST, however, wind gusts over 58 mph were recorded for at least 4 hours.
The APRS Weather Net CWOP site in Lake Sumner Village recorded a 58 mph wind gust.
Local law enforcement officials around Estancia received wind gusts reports between 62 and 70 mph for much of the late morning and early afternoon. The strongest winds were reported just after noon.
The ASOS at Clines Corners recorded sustained wind speeds in excess of 40 mph for nearly 5 hours. The highest sustained wind speed was 47 mph which occurred around 10 am MST.
The ASOS at Clines Corners recorded wind gusts in excess of 58 mph for around 3 hours.  The peak wind gust of 67 mph occurred at 936 am MST.
Estimated wind gusts up to 60 mph were reported around Claunch.  The strong winds reduced visibility to around 1 mile in blowing dust.

The KSRR AWOS recorded sustained winds of 40 mph or greater for much of the morning and early afternoon. These winds were reported generally between 135 am MST and 355 am MST and then again between 915 am and 1215 pm MST. The highest sustained wind speed of 53 mph was recorded at 1115 am MST.

The KSRR AWOS recorded peak wind gusts over 58 mph for much of the morning and early afternoon. These winds were reported generally between 135 am MST and 355 am MST and then again between 915 am and 1215 pm MST, though a few gusts over 58 mph occurred in between those times. The highest peak wind gust of 69 mph was recorded at 1115 am MST.
The cooperative observer in Capulin estimated wind gusts up to 60 mph.  A 58 mph wind gust was also measured by a KVII Schoolnet site in Portales.
The Raton ASOS measured sustained winds over 40 mph for about a four hour period. The highest sustained wind of 48 mph was recorded around 2 pm MST.
The Raton ASOS measured severe gusts nearly continuously for three hours. The peak wind gust of 68 mph at 1236 pm MST.  A peak wind gust of 64 mph was also measured at Wagon Mound.
The Las Vegas ASOS sustained winds of 40 mph or greater for over 4 hours. The highest sustained winds of 44 mph occurred between 1 and 2 pm MST.
The Las Vegas ASOS recorded severe wind gusts off and on for around 6 hours. The peak wind gust of 63 mph occurred at 1226 pm MST.
The Clayton ASOS recorded sustained winds of 40 mph or greater for around four hours.  The highest sustained wind of 45 mph occurred just before 4 pm MST.
The Clayton ASOS recorded severe wind gusts during much of the early and mid afternoon hours.  Peak wind gusts of 64 mph occurred between 1250 pm and 121 pm MST.
Near Mills, wind gusts were estimated to 60 mph.
Near Conchas, wind gusts were estimated to 60 mph.
Law enforcement officials estimated wind gusts to 60 mph in Santa Rosa.
The Tucumcari ASOS recorded sustained winds of 40 mph or greater for around 2 hours.  The highest sustained wind of 43 mph was measured at 153 pm MST.

The Tucumcari ASOS measured a peak wind gust of 59 mph at 250 pm MST.  KVII's Frost Ranch Schoolnet site southwest of Glenrio recorded a 61 mph wind gust at 151 pm MST, while another Schoolnet site near Ute Lake recorded a 67 mph wind gust at 223 pm MST.
Severe wind gusts were measured for over 2 hours at KCVS. The peak wind gust of 60 mph was recorded at 139 pm MST.
KVII's Schoolnet site in Portales measured a peak wind gust of 60 mph at 1155am, though severe winds occurred much of the early afternoon.
The APRS Weather Net CWOP site near Lake Sumner recorded wind gusts up to 59 mph.
The Roswell ASOS measured wind gusts of 59 mph.
East of Arabela, estimated wind gusts up to 60 mph were reported.
A White Sands Missile Range Mesonet site southeast of San Antonio recorded a peak wind gust of 59 mph. The roof of the New Loma Stadium Cinema in Socorro was partially torn off from the high winds.
A peak wind gust of 58 mph was recorded at the Gallup ASOS at 223pm and 427pm MST.
Sustained winds of 40 mph were also recorded between 753 am and 853 am.
Sustained winds of 47 mph were also recorded between 853 am and 953 am.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS

events.event_narrative: Nickel sized hail was reported at 630pm MST and quickly grew to Quarter size hail and continued until 740pm MST. The hail covered the ground.

A peak wind gust of 71 mph also occurred at 135 pm MST. High wind gusts were recorded between 1023 am and 215 pm MST at speeds of 58 to 71 mph. High sustained winds of 51 mph occurred between 1153 am and 1253 pm MST.
High sustained winds of 40 to 44 mph were reported by the Clayton ASOS between 1055 am and 355 pm MST.
A peak wind gust of 58 mph was also recorded at 1230 pm MST. High sustained winds of 40 mph occurred between 1055 am and 1155 am MST.
Hail ranged from quarter to golf ball size and lasted from 525 pm to 535 pm MST.
Quarter size hail lasted for roughly 3 minutes.
KVII TV in Amarillo relayed a report of quarter size hail by a SchoolNet observer.
Rising water from the Rio Chamita resulted in flooding of yards, storage sheds and possibly a barn on the west side of Chama.  No homes were flooded.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS

events.event_narrative: The area around Fence Lake received between 4 and 10 inches of snow, with the greatest snow amounts reported just south of town.

There was also a sustained wind speed of 47 mph at the Smokey Bear Remote Automated Weather Station on the 28th from 900 pm to 1000 pm MST and a peak wind gust of 68 mph at 137am MST on the 29th at the Sierra Blanca airport.

The 99 mph wind was recorded at Sandia Peak at an elevation of 10,378 feet. Double Eagle Airport reported a peak wind gust of 62 mph at 1115 am MST and a sustained wind speed of 43 mph from 1115 am to 1215 pm. The Albuquerque Sunport recorded a peak wind gust of 63 mph at 451 pm and a sustained wind speed of 46 mph from 415 pm to 515 pm. Power lines were down near Central and Laguna Place in Albuquerque. A downed power line in southwest Albuquerque started a brush fire and minor damage to a house. Vinyl fabric on the north side of the upper wall of the University of New Mexico's indoor practice facility was ripped off from the winds.
A peak wind gust of 72 mph also occurred at the Sierra Blanca Airport at 655 am MST. A large tree limb fell on a trailer home on 2nd St. in Capitan.
A peak wind gust of 61 mph was also recorded at 1017 am MST.

The 74 mph wind gust occurred 6 miles north of Wagon Mound at 1017 am MST. The Las Vegas ASOS reported a peak wind gust of 69 mph at 1132 am and a sustained wind speed of 55 mph from 153 pm to 253 pm.
There was also a gust to 62 mph at the Bandelier National Monument at 1221 pm MST.

The Socorro Automated Weather Observing Station recorded a sustained wind speed of 41 mph from 1250 pm to 150 pm MST. Wind damage occurred in Veguita at 200 pm when several sheets of Pro-Panel roofing were blown off the roof of a trading post along highway 304. A travel trailer was blown over along Interstate 25, 1.5 miles of Socorro at 230 pm MST.
There was also a peak wind gust of 59 mph at the Tucumcari ASOS at 248 pm MST.

Wind gusts estimated to be around 60 mph overturned two semi-trucks along U.S. 84 in Guadalupe county.  Both trucks were empty, which made them more susceptible to the strong wind gusts.  Luckily, no one was injured.   These gusts also knocked down an awning at Travel Centers of America.  Debris from the awning smashed a vehicle's window.   Elsewhere around the county, streets were littered with shingles blown off of rooftops.
In addition to the high sustained winds, there was a peak wind gust of 61 mph at the Roswell ASOS at 410 pm MST.
A peak wind gust of 60 mph was also recorded at the Dunken RAWS at 309 pm MST.
Strong wind gusts blew the roofs off of two commercial greenhouses. The roofs were made of plastic sheeting and shade cloth. A seven foot windbreak structure was also snapped off at the ground.
An approximately 50 year old blue spruce was uprooted by strong winds on Alamosa Drive in the southwest part of Santa Fe. The tree was the tallest one in the entire neighborhood.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS

events.event_narrative: There was a peak wind gust of 62 mph recorded at the Las Vegas Airport ASOS at |151 pm MST.
The Sierra Blanca Airport AWOS also recorded a peak wind gust of 59 mph at 235 pm MST. The Smokey Bear RAWS recorded also recorded a peak wind gust of 59 mph at 200 pm MST.

The 70 mph wind gust occurred in Wagon Mound at 129 pm MST. A peak wind gust of 59 mph was recorded at the Raton Crews Airport at 139 pm MST, with a sustained wind of 44 mph between 153 and 253 pm MST.
The 61 mph wind gust at Gallup Airport was recorded at 256 pm MST, while a sustained wind of 40 mph was recorded between 153 and 253 pm MST.

A 65 mph gust was measured 3 miles southeast of Manzano at 822 am MST, meanwhile a measured wind gust of 63 mph was reported just southeast of Tajique shortly after 8 am MST.  Some minor street sign damage was noted in Edgewood, along with blowing dust reducing visibilities down to one-half mile.
Sustained winds over 40 mph were measured at the Clines Corners ASOS for over 3 hours.  Peak sustained winds of 51 mph was measured shortly before 9 am.
A peak wind gust of 68 mph was recorded at Clines Corners at 821 am MST, though gusts over 58 mph were noted for several hours.
Two power poles were blown down just northwest of Corona on Highway 42.
Wind gusts up to 63 mph were recorded at Sierra Blanca Regional Airport near Ruidoso.
Sustained winds of 43 mph were measured at the Raton Crews Airport.
Sustained winds up to 45 mph were measured at the Las Vegas ASOS.
Wind gusts up to 63 mph were measured at the Las Vegas ASOS.
An estimated 60 mph gust was reported near Hayden, while a measured gust to 59 mph was recorded just southeast of Gladstone.
Four inch tree limbs were blown down.
A mobile home had its roof blown off in Conchas due to the high winds.

A School Net site near Ute Lake recorded a peak wind gust of 71 mph at 1027 am MST.  Report was relayed by KVII television in Amarillo.  Additionally, the ASOS in Tucumcari recorded a peak wind gust of 63 mph at 1038 am MST. However, wind gust over 58 mph were recorded between 908 and 1101 am.  A few powerlines were downed northeast of Logan which started a small grass fire.  Fortunately, the fire was quickly put out.
Sustained winds of 40 mph were recorded at the Tucumcari ASOS between 908 am and noon MST.  The highest sustained winds of 52 mph were measured around 1030 am.
The Dunken RAWS site hit 60 mph at 1009 am, but also hit 59 mph at 1209 pm MST.
The West Texas Mesonet site near Dora recorded sustained winds above 40 mph nearly continuously between 925 and 1145 am MST.  Sustained winds peaked at 48 mph right as the strong winds started.

The West Texas Mesonet site near Dora recorded peak wind gusts of 60 mph at 1035 am, 61 mph at 1130 am, and 59 mph at 1125 am MST. The high winds caused extensive damage to power polls in Portales, along with a few downed trees and part of a roof was blown off a barn.

The Clovis AWOS recorded a peak wind gust of 63 mph at 955 am MST.  Meanwhile, the Cannon AFB ASOS recorded gusts over 58 mph between 944 and 1010 am, peaking at 59 mph.  Visibility was reduced to 2 miles in blowing dust.
The Cannon AFB ASOS recorded sustained winds above 40 mph for an hour.  The highest sustained wind speed recorded was 45 mph.
A trained spotter at Sumner Lake recorded a peak wind gust of 65 mph.  Visibility was reduced to 3 miles in blowing dust.
Hail fell near Highways 380 and 409.

Winds estimated around 85 mph uprooted at least a dozen mature pinon pine trees at 6340 feet in the northern Sacramento Mountains. In addition, a 500-gallon diesel tank that was estimated to be half full was lofted vertically and carried at least 150 yards, and an empty 53 foot box trailed was tipped on its side.  There was also minor damage to a horse/tack barn and a fire department truck.
Trees were downed along Forest Roads 376 and 126 blocking the roadway.  Pea size hail was also reported.
Along State Highway 13, a wind shield was broken out of one of the vehicles in the Vortex 2 armada.
Ping pong ball sized hail was reported by Vortex 2.
Ping pong ball sized hail started at 405 pm MST.  Hail decreased in size to quarters by 415 pm.
Golf ball sized hail started at 510 pm MST along Interstate 25.  Sized was reduced to dimes by 515 pm.
Hail last 10 minutes along Interstate 25.
Hail ranged from pea size to pennies.
Minor roof damage was reported.

Debris on Highway 56 was seen at mile post 93. Power lines were down, barbed wire fences and hay bales were all over.  In addition, a steel building from a feed lot was destroyed, a cow with a broken leg was observed on the road, and a semi truck was turned over on private property. The tornado crossed the New Mexico-Oklahoma state line approximately 8.7 miles southeast of Seneca and continued into neighboring Cimarron County, Oklahoma.
There was damage to agricultural equipment. A single wide mobile home that had tie down straps was completely destroyed and the undercarriage was carried approximately 40 yards. No injuries reported.
Two tornadoes were reported from the same parent supercell thunderstorm.  This is the second tornado with shorter track farther north.
Nickel to quarter size hail.
Relayed by Emergency Manager. Tornado briefly touched down in open rangeland. No damage reported.
Report relayed by Emergency Manager. Tornado briefly touched down approximately 0.25 mi west of NM/TX state line.
Hail was 2 to 3 inches deep along Interstate 25.  Several cars reported off the road.
Primarily one inch hail came down occasionally for 15 minutes.  However, a few stones were as large as golf balls.
Half dollar size hail from 345 pm to 355 pm.
Tree limbs were downed by the large hail.
Hail ranged from pea to quarter size.
Large tree limbs were downed from strong winds in the Dexter area.
One inch to 1.90 inch hail broke three windows out of a house.
A SchoolNet site north of Clovis reported a 59 mph wind gust.  Relayed by KVII in Amarillo.
The wind pushed a small Chevy truck, that was in neutral, 30 yards down a driveway.
The wind knocked down a large tree and destroyed a shed.
Several transformers and power lines were damaged from the high wind gusts.
Cars were stranded on Main Street and Highway 209 in Clovis.

The hailstorm left much of the Clovis area battered by hail up to the size of golf balls.  The majority of the damage occurred in the northeastern portion of the community.  Over 1600 home and auto claims were submitted to insurance companies.
Frost Ranch SchoolNet observation recorded a 62 mph wind gusts on a 34 foot tower.  Observation was relayed by KVII in Amarillo.
Multiple large tree branches were knocked down. A 12 inch diameter cottonwood tree was reduced to less than half its original height.
Damage to residence located just northwest of Amistad.
No reports of significant damage and no injuries.

The dry microburst winds severely damaged a large tank that was under construction on the Kirtland Air Force Base, which is at the eastern end of the Albuquerque Sunport. The tank was 85 feet in diameter and 48 feet tall, but did not have a roof, yet. Three trees were also uprooted at the VA hospital on Gibson Street.  Near this location, a portion of a fence was blown over onto neighboring vehicles.
State police reported zero visibility in rain and hail along Highway 285 at mile marker 141.
The Logan Fire Department reported localized flooding with a couple of intersections impassable.

Several reports of high winds across the Albuquerque Metro Area were reported as the east winds raced through the gaps of the central mountain chain.  In the Albuquerque Foothills, winds were estimated around 70 mph, which blew down a fence, broke numerous large branches, and uprooted at least two trees.  Roof shingle damage also occurred to numerous houses in the foothills. A 60 mph gust was measured just west of Placitas, and a 58 mph wind gust was recorded at the Albuquerque ASOS at 837 pm MST.
The hail accumulated to a depth of 3 inches and ranged in size from peas to nickels.
State Route 370 was impassable due to water covering much of the road between Clayton and Clayton Lake State Park, as several creeks overflowed their banks. Several motorists were stranded.
The hail lasted 15 minutes and accumulated four to five inches deep. The hail broke a car windshield.

A garage on Avalon Place flooded due to heavy rain.  Fortunately, flooding to the the interior of the house was avoided because mechanical pumps were brought in to mitigate the disaster.  Just north of this area, 2.32 inches of rain was reported in the Santa Fe Seton Village.  This rain fell in just over one hours time.

Heavy rains carried logs across a private roadway about one half mile downstream of the Tecolote Fire burn area, or about 1.5 miles north of Blue Haven Church Camp.  The road was impassable for a time due to the logs and high water.  The heavy rains also washed debris from the burn scar into Blue Creek, which doubled in size.
Lightning struck the satellite dish on top of a home southwest of Tesuque.  The current traveled down a PVC pipe into the house and blew out a 1 by 2 foot area of sheet rock.

The intersection of Los Pinos and Sunrise in La Cienega was not passable due to high water and the road was closed for a time.  A nearby arroyo had debris in it with fast moving water about 6 feet high.  A backhoe had been left in the arroyo somewhat downstream the previous day.  This piece of equipment was almost entirely enveloped in water and mud.
Multiple roads closed due to at least 10 inches of water flowing over the road.  This included the low water crossing at Dawn Trail and Arroyo Trail, and also at Turquoise Trail and County Road 45.
There was 18 inches of standing water on 18th St. in the southern portion of Portales.
Hail ranged from peas to nickels.

Heavy rains caused the Pecos River to overflow its banks from Ribera south to nearly Villanueva. One home in Ribera was moderately damaged and two others had minor damage. Route 3, which runs along the Pecos River, was mostly under water.  Three other roads were washed out in Ribera. Areas along and upstream from the Pecos received heavy rain, but so did many creeks and tributaries that flow into the river.  Roads along these secondary creeks sustained as much, if not more, damage than in the town of Ribera.  In Bernal, flooding creeks caused damage to County Roads B27 and B28A.  Only one lane remained open after the shoulders were washed away.  The flooding also washed out 300 feet of railway along the Burlington Northern Santa Fe Railroad near Bernal.  Further upstream, flash flooding along Tecolote Creek caused one bridge to collapse and damaged five low water crossings. The fast moving water was 12 feet outside of its banks.  Another low water crossing in Ojito Fritos along County Road A19A had standing water because culverts were blocked by debris.  Despite the mud and debris along the road, one lane was kept open.
A few portable buildings near Logan were overturned.
A large tree, 2.5-3 feet in diameter, was blown down near Broadview.
Hail was reported along U.S. Highway 380.
A large 4 foot diameter tree was knocked over by the strong wind gusts.

Several tree branches larger than 2 inches in diameter were broken off of trees from wind gusts estimated around 60 mph. In addition, high winds knocked the roof off of an abandoned single wide trailer, which fell onto the roof a neighboring house on Blue Canyon Dr.

A 2-year-old died after being left in a hot car for almost four hours at Southwestern Indian Polytechnic Institute.  By noon MST, the outside air temperature was 93 degrees which may have resulted in temperatures exceeding 135 degrees in the vehicle.
Water up to one foot deep covered Highway 285/60 between Encino and Vaughn from 530 pm to 600 pm MST.  Spotters reported large debris along the roadway, and significant fence line damage.
A large landslide washed out the dirt road leading to the Magdalena Ridge Observatory and Langmuir Laboratory for Atmospheric Research.
A SchoolNet site in the Pueblo Point subdivision recorded a 59 mph wind gust.  Report relayed by KVII in Amarillo.

Heavy rain eroded the smaller of two uranium tailing piles at the Homestead/Barrick Gold former mill site. A wall of water 80 to 100 yards wide flooded the four subdivisions. Ralph Card, Sundowner, Thunderbird and Malapais roads were flooded and several other roads in the area had high water.  Residents of the four subdivisions likened their front and back yards to lakes with water up to 18 inches deep.

Cox Canyon Bridge on County Road 2900 just southwest of Cedar Hill collapsed.  Officials say the bridge collapsed because water running down the canyon hit the bridge at an angle and the eddy it created, ripped out the structure's support.  The residents of about 100 homes were left stranded.
A large area of one foot deep water along Highway 267 between mile markers 6 and 8 made the road impassible.

Arroyo del Oso Golf Course at Osuna and Louisiana flooded. Lots of debris on course from Bear Canyon Arroyo. Ducks were actually swimming in standing water at hole number seven.  Intersection of San Francisco and Barstow also flooded with traffic stopped due to flowing water.
A large three to four foot diameter tree trunk was split apart at a height of eight feet off the ground as seen via webcam. Wind gust recorded by SchoolNet site, and relayed by KVII in Amarillo.
Weak satellite tornado captured on video that lasted for approximately 8 minutes. No injuries or significant damage reported.
A large cottonwood tree in southwest Albuquerque was uprooted due to the rain-softened ground. The tree blocked a street and tore up some sidewalk.
Large rocks were swept onto State Route 48, one mile south of Alto, by rushing water.

Six to 12 inches of water was on several roads northeast of Alto in the Rancho Ruidoso subdivision. Some of the worst hit roadways include County Road D003, Little Creek Road, and Little Creek Hills Road.  At least one house and one barn flooded, and several other homes in the area had minor damage.

A 16 year old boy was swept down the Embudo Arroyo by rapid flowing flood waters from near Juan Tabo and Candelaria to Carlisle and Interstate 40. This was a distance of five miles and the water was estimated to be flowing at 35 mph. The boy only received a few cuts and bruises.
At Ranchitos and Eubank, the shoulders of the roads were eroded with a foot of water covering the intersection.
Water accumulated on State Highway 41 with county roads along side the highway impassable.
There was running water, rocks and a mudslide over State Road 511 between mile markers 3 and 7. One vehicle hit the rocks which ruptured its fuel tank.

Significant amounts of water flowed over Thompson Bridge on Telstar Road in Church Rock which eventually caused the bridge to collapse. The bridge served as the only way in and out of the Church Rock community.  Other portions of this road were covered in up to 3 feet of mud.  Challenger Road, which leads up to the elementary school, was covered with up to 5 feet of mud.   Superman Canyon Road, Old Church Rock Coal Road and Becenti Trail were also washed out.
Six to eight inches of flowing water and mud impacted Main Street near Interstate 25.
A drainage ditch along N. Los Lentes Road backed up into one house, meanwhile water was overflowing a brick fence into a residents yard.

Three to four feet of water was reported near the intersection of Coors and Sage as well as Coors and Tower. Several vehicles were stuck. Knee deep water was approaching structures near Gonzales and 52nd Street.  Three feet of water was also reported at Coors and Bridge with roads closed.
Small boulders, rocks, and water washed over Highway 4.
Four trees washed into Kutz Canyon along with portion of a neighboring horse corral. Four feet of the embankment was eroded away.

Significant flooding plagued the Farmington area during the evening hours of August 1st.  More than 2.5 inches of rain fell in 3 hours, but most of the rain fell in about a 30 minute time frame.  Some of the hardest hit areas are described in the following paragraphs. ||The Webb Chevrolet-Toyota dealership and neighboring businesses along East Main Street between Gila St. and Hannon Dr. was described as a swamp.  Weeds and shrubs were wrapped around the tires of each truck as water, mud and debris flooded into the lot.  The force of the water moved one truck about six feet, and moved a nearby dumpster approximately 100 yards.  Also in this area, a man whose car got stuck at the intersection of Cliffside Dr. and East Main got trapped in shallow, quick moving water. The man was rescued by firefighters and was unharmed.||Near the intersection of Largo St. and Railroad St., water was estimated to be 6 to 12 inches deep at the height of the event.  Water damage was evident to at least two residences. ||An arroyo that crosses Hubbard St. near Peace Valley Road was flowing over the roadway. A high school senior attempted to drive through the waters, when her car was washed away.  Her car traveled approximately 80 yards down the arroyo before she was rescued.  She was unharmed, but her car was destroyed.  After the waters receded, it became evident that Peace Valley Road was partially eroded away beneath the pavement.||Due to a holding pond that overflowed, five homes around the Country Club suffered significant damage, including one basement that was completely filled with water. Most of these homes were filled with no less than 6 inches of water on the ground level, resulting in damage of carpet, tile and other objects or furniture that was on the floor. Landscaping was completely eroded away, and fence lines were downed.||A mudslide was also reported on County Road 3000 at mile marker 9.5.  The road was impassible until the mud was cleaned off the road.
An arroyo washed over the roadway at intersection of Highway 550 and County Road 7150.

After the Church Rock bridge at Telstar Road collapsed July 31st, a temporary bridge was put in place.  Just 2 days later, another bout of flash flooding resulted in the temporary bridge being washed out. A female flood victim had to be rescued the high waters in Church Rock.  She sustained only minor injuries. Other vehicles were flooded out in Church Rock as well. In addition, mud as deep as 5 feet plagued Challenger Road again. Superman Canyon Road, Old Church Rock Coal Road, and Becenti Trail were also washed out for the 2nd time in as many days.
Flash flooding resulted in mud and rocks, some as large as 10 inches in diameter, flowing across portions of Highway 4 between Jemez Pueblo and Jemez Springs.
The La Cueva fire station flooded and Twisted Juniper Road was washed out.
Navajo Route 134 was impassible due to high water at mile marker 22.
A White Sands Missile Range Mesonet site recorded a 69 mph wind gust at Stallion Army Airfield.
Heavy rain caused an awning at the Giant gas station to collapse and fall on three cars at the intersection of Sawmill Rd. and St. Francis Dr.
Cerrillos Rd. between St. Michael's Dr. and Camino Carlos Rey was flooded and impassable.
Large tree limbs blown down.
Bosquecito Road was closed due to high, fast moving water just north of U.S. Highway 380 near an arroyo crossing.

A 2-acre fire resulted in damage of the Cumbres and Toltec Scenic Railroad by the Lobato Trestle.  The fire, which was approximately 5 miles north-northeast of Chama near the Colorado border, destroyed the wooden ties that support the rail bed.  As a result, the railroad had to halt train operations through the area. The cause of the fire remains unknown, though arson and natural causes have been ruled out.
Due to flooding from Chavez Lake, 14th Street was closed between N. Edwards and N. Hull streets.

A couple driving home from dinner was caught in the swollen Santa Fe River at San Ysidro Crossing.  The couple attempted to drive through the flooded roadway, when the river surged and a tree came down changing the flow of the river.  Santa Fe fire department successfully rescued the couple who only sustained minor injuries.  At the time of the rescue, the water was up to the car windows.  After the rescue, the car floated and flipped over San Ysidro Falls, where later it was found to be totaled.
Wind gusts estimated near 50 mph damaged a 15,000 square foot tent at The Downs of Santa Fe which housed the flea market.
Highway 76 was closed due to flash flooding in the vicinity of La Puebla, southeast of Espanola.   Four to five feet of rock and silt was washed over the road.  Cars were washed into nearby arroyos.

Numerous road were closed or impassible in and near Roswell due to the heavy rains and flooding.  This includes Poe Street west from Southeast Main as well as Brown Road from Country Club to Pine Lodge.  Cars were also reported to have been floating down Highway 285 north of Roswell. Two feet of water ran over the highway between mile markers 136 and 138, leading the road to be closed. A couple of cars ended up in the ditch, with water up to their windshields.  Also along Pine Lodge Road near mile marker 59, three to four feet of water ran over the road where it crossed Salt Creek.  Cricket Creek as well as Spring and Hondo Rivers were running bank full.  Unofficial rainfall reports include near 5 inches near Berrendo Road and North Main, 3.5 inches near the Roswell High School on West Church Street, and 3.0 inches at the 2600 block of South Sunset. Hundreds of homes were without power.

Multiple roads were flooded across northern Roosevelt County, particularly around Floyd and Portales. One citizen attempted to drive through a low water crossing filled with three to four feet of water along Highway 267 near Floyd.  The car stalled, but was recovered.  18th Street in Portales was a particularly hard hit area.  Streets along 18th were impassible between Avenue D and Globe.  The intersection of Avenue I and 18th Street was impassible as well.  The cooperative observer in Portales measured 1.75 inches of rain.
County Road 1 was impassible as water was quickly running over the road and lapping up along the Tse Bonito bridge.  Though the bridge remains standing, the water tore off both sides of the bridge.

Nearly 2 inches of rain fell across portions of northwest Rio Rancho.  The intersection of Northern and Idalia was closed due to flash flooding.  Along Unser, though the road was not closed, it was impassible to several cars which got stuck in the high waters.  A sewer line was also damaged, which allowed sewage to flow into the Montoya's Arroyo.

Winds of 65 mph from a microburst uprooted several small dead trees, and downed a 10 inch diameter green elm tree which damaged parked vehicles.  In addition, several metal roof panels were ripped off an out building.  This located only received a few raindrops, but the spotter saw the storm to the northwest.
A five inch diameter tree limb was snapped off due to the strong winds.

A low water crossing along Quay Road 49 flooded out due to the heavy rains. This area only received about an inch of rain, however, areas upstream received nearly 4 inches, resulting in high water in all area creeks and streams.

A mobile home was overturned just south of U.S. 64 in Shiprock. The trailer had just moved to this location one month prior, and was not yet anchored down nor hooked up to any utilities. It sat atop it's wheels on one end and concrete blocks on another.  There was no mobile home skirt around the trailer to prevent wind from going underneath.  It appeared that the trailer rolled off the concrete blocks onto its side, and then again onto its roof. Two people were inside, but escaped without any major injuries.

One home was flooded approximately 9 miles north of Farmington on Highway 170. Heavy rainfall, combined with insufficient drainage along the highway, resulted in water flowing across the roadway and into the house. High water marks suggest the water was around 10 inches deep, which destroyed carpet and other objects on the floor.  Water continued to flow eastward along a one lane dirt road into a 5 acre, 12 foot deep pond, which was empty prior to the storm. The runoff filled the pond entirely.

Flash flooding occurred along CR4990. A damage survey found that several arroyos flow from the higher terrain to the south of the road northward into the San Juan River. Though radar indicates that the brunt of the precipitation fell to the south of the road, the road became impassible at several locations as there was evidence that a large swath of mud and water flowed across the road, underneath some nearby raised residences.  Since these homes were elevated, they did not receive any damage inside. The storm moved east-northeast near the intersection of CR4990 and CR4550, just south of Blanco, where there was some evidence that high waters flowed there recently.

As the east canyon wind came through the gaps of the central mountain chain during the early morning hours, a Davis weather station recorded a 64 mph wind gust at the mouth of Embudo Canyon at an elevation of 5925 feet.  Other gusts exceeding 58 mph were recorded for nearly a 3 hour period.

Multiple dirt roads were washed out in an area called Tramperos.  Vehicles were stuck in the mud and high water.  The Bartley RAWS near Gascon received over 2 inches of rain in less than 2 hours time.

Several dirt and gravel roads were washed out completely along the northern periphery of the Acoma Indian Reservation and points just north of Acomita.  Much of the damage occurred where arroyos crossed or neared the roadway. The greatest damage occurred  along Indian Service Roads 34, 345, 30 and 26 as well as Stock Yard Road. Water continued to spill over what was left of the roadways days later.  Minor damage was also noted on the Wastewater Treatment Facilities property.
Sweetwater, Iyanbito and Dakota Loop Roads were washed out due to flash flooding in Iyanbito for the second time in two days.
Sweetwater, Iyanbito, and Dakota Loop Roads in Iyanbito were washed out due to flash flooding.
South Chavez Road and Woodview Drive in Baca as well as Navajo Road in Thoreau were washed out.
Lori Drive just northeast of Bluewater Lake was washed out due to heavy rains.
South Chavez Road and Woodview Drive in Baca as well as Navajo Road in Thoreau were washed out due to heavy rains.
Flash flooding damaged Manuelito Canyon Road and nearby Manuelito Canyon.

Several roads were washed out around Gladstone. A house 8 miles south southeast of Gladstone had three feet of water in it and the owner had his Mercedes Benz car carried one quarter mile away by rapidly flowing water.

A 27-year old man was swept away by fast flowing water in the I-40 Channel.  The man was walking in the arroyo with his brother near I-40 and Louisiana, when a rush of water swept the man off his feet.  The man traveled west to the North Diversion Channel, then north to the Rio Grande River.  He was found dead along a sand bar in the Rio Grande River three days later near Coors Bypass. He traveled a total distance of 13 miles.  His brother made it out alive, without injury.
Roads were washed out 6 miles east of Rogers as 3.40 inches of rain fell in 2 hours and 50 minutes.  2.75 inches of rain was also reported 3 miles north-northeast of Causey.
Back yard was covered in hail.
Ground was about 50 percent covered in large hail.  The hail broke a skylight and damaged roof shingles.
Quarter size hail lasted for 10 minutes and broke skylights in the roof.

Golf ball sized hail accumulated 2 inches deep on the ground. Over 200 houses sustained significant damage including roof and window damage. Multiple vehicles were also dented and damaged by the large hail.
Three minutes of golf ball size hail followed by 15 minutes of pea size hail.
Hail shredded leaves off the trees.
Hail accumulated to a depth of 2 to 3 inches on the ground.
Spotter also reported 15 to 20 minutes of pea to half inch size hail.
Tree limbs greater than 2 inches in diameter were blown down.

Kewa Pueblo, formerly known as Santa Domingo Pueblo, received golf ball sized hail which accumulated six to eight inches deep. This caused several roofs on the Pueblo to cave in and weaken some walls. The combination of heavy rain and accumulated hail resulted in some roads being washed out.
Penny size hail was reported at both San Mateo and I-25 as well as Academy and Burlison.
Quarter size hail was reported near the intersection of Spain and Tramway in Albuquerque.
This is the Sandia Peak Tram observation.
Observed wind gusts were recorded between 61 and 64 mph for nearly 2 hours.  This is the strongest gust reported. Damage to an antenna was reported on the spotters property.
The observation was taken from a Weathernet site at the Vaughn Junior Senior High School.
Large tree limbs broke and large aspen trees fell and snapped power lines in and around Los Alamos as winds gusted to 58 mph.
The high wind gusts caused numerous trees and tree limbs to break and knock down power lines.
In addition to wind gusts over 58 mph, the Clayton ASOS measured 41 mph sustained winds for at least an hour behind a strong back door cold front.
The observer estimated wind gusts around 55 mph. An east bound semi truck was blown off the road, onto its side, by the strong winds 1.5 miles west of Capulin on U.S. Highway 64.
The Hopewell SNOTEL at 10,000 feet picked up about 8 inches of snow.  Around Chama, 4 to 6 inches was common.
Winds gusts over 50 knots were recorded at Sierra Blanca Regional Airport near Ruidoso intermittently for over 2 hours.  The highest wind gusts was 63 mph at 1035 am.
Sustained winds over 35 knots were recorded at Sierra Blanca Regional Airport near Ruidoso between 1015 and 1115 am.  The highest sustained wind was 48 mph.
The Las Vegas ASOS peaked at 58 mph.
Both the Hopewell and Chamita SNOTELS picked up about 8 inches of new snow.  The cooperative observer in Chama only picked up 4 inches of snow.

Though most of the far northwest highlands only received an inch or two of snow, the higher elevation locations picked up significantly higher amounts. The cooperative observer at Dulce reported 7 inches of fresh snow.
A cooperative observer measured a 60 mph wind gust 3 miles southeast of Manzano.
A SchoolNet site recorded a 74 mph wind gust at the high school in Cimarron.   Report relayed by KOB-TV.
The Clines Corners ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 59 mph.

The Las Vegas ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 62 mph, though was gusting over 58 mph for over 30 minutes.  These strong winds blew 2 solar panels off the roof of a house on Highway 84 between mile markers 100 and 101 southwest of Las Vegas.  Meanwhile, a roof was blown off a vacant house near K-Bob's restaurant and also a tree was blown over on Columbia Avenue which blocked the street for a time.  Power outages were abundant across the region.

SKYWARN spotters and several members of the general public filmed the tornado while looking north on Highway 246.  The tornado was also viewable from the town of Roswell.  This tornado primarily impacted the Salt Creek Basin for approximately nine minutes.  This EF-0 tornado had peak winds around 65 mph. No significant damage or injuries were reported.

SKYWARN spotters and emergency management officials noted a second tornado while looking north from Highway 246.  This tornado began just west of Highway 285 and north of Verbena Road. Peak winds were estimated around 65 mph. No significant damage or injuries were reported.

Around Tohajiillee, 6 to 7 inches of snow was reported. Just west of Grants, a man driving too fast for the wintry conditions on Interstate 40, loss control and veered off the highway.  The 65-year old man died when the vehicle struck lava rocks and overturned.
The higher elevations above Chama picked up 8 inches of new snow.
Ski sites and SNOTELS in the Jemez Mountains picked up between 8 and 12 inches of snow. The White Rock and Los Alamos areas received between 5 and 8 inches of snow.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Ski sites and SNOTELS on the west slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains received between 10 and 20 inches of fresh snow.  Other areas received up to 10 inches of snow.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: The Taos ski area picked up a foot of new snow, while SNOTELs in the area received up to 9 inches.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: Snow fell fast and furious across the southern Sangre de Cristo Mountains. The Santa Fe SNOTEL and the Santa Fe Ski area received between 15 and 16 inches of snow.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Though all of the east slopes received snow, the heaviest amounts were found in San Miguel County. 20 inches of snow fell at Mineral Hill.
Between 4 and 7 inches of snow fell around the Taos area.
The Espanola cooperative observer reported just over 4 inches of snow.

The Santa Fe Metro area was one of the hardest hit areas from this winter storm.  6 to 10 inches of snow was common in Santa Fe, however further south near Lamy, Madrid and Gallisteo, up to 22 inches of snow was measured. Interstate 25 was closed for a time from Santa Fe northward to Las Vegas due to treacherous driving conditions.

The west side of Albuquerque northeastward through Rio Rancho and Placitas were the hardest hit areas. 3 to 7 inches of snow quickly accumulated on roads and grassy surfaces.  The Albuquerque valley, northeast heights and foothills had less than an inch of snow.  Most of the precipitation in these areas stayed as rain.
Eight to 16 inches of snow was common over the Sandia Mountains, with many areas reporting around a foot exactly. However, Sandia Ski Area reported a whopping 28 inches of new snow.
Between 4 and 9 inches of snow fell across the Estancia Valley.
Four to 6 inches was common across the Central Highlands, however, areas closest to the Sangre de Cristo Mountains picked up significantly higher amounts.
Between 3 and 8 inches of snow fell across the northeast highlands.  The highest amounts fell southwest of Wagon Mound.

Easterly upslope flow contributed to significant snowfall accumulations around the Las Vegas area.  East of Interstate 25, 6 to 12 inches of snow was common, however, along and west of the interstate, up to 2 feet of snow fell.  Snow totals include 24 inches at Romeroville, 18 inches around Las Vegas, and 10 inches at Los Montoyas.  I-25 was closed for a time due to dangerous driving conditions.
Three to 5 inches of snow fell across Union County.
Around 4 inches of snow fell across Harding County.
Two to 6 inches of snow fell across eastern San Miguel County.
Northwestern portions of Guadalupe County received the bulk of the snow.  Around 8 inches fell in Anton Chico.
Areas near and just east of Dulce picked up just over 4 inches of snow.
Near and just southwest of Cuba, around 4 inches of new snow fell.

Southwest of Corona, around 5 inches of snow fell. The snow packed roads caused a passenger bus to lose control on U.S. 54 15 miles south of Corona at 745 am local time.  The bus collided with a cattle truck and overturned. The bus driver and 19 passengers were hospitalized, some with critical injuries.

A grass fire started 14 miles southwest of Elida during the afternoon of the 15th.  Strong winds flamed the fire as it scorched approximately 4500 acres of grass and wheat fields.  One barn was destroyed.  The cause of the fire is unknown.
Up to 10 inches of snow fell across the Northwest Plateau.  The highest snow amounts were near the Colorado border around Aztec and La Plata.
The Navajo Whiskey Creek SNOTEL picked up around 19 inches of fresh snow.

Over a foot and a half of snow fell across portions of the far northwest highlands. One foot was reported north of La Plata along the Colorado border, while 8 inches was reported at Navajo Dam.  Meanwhile, Dulce picked up close to 21 inches of snow.

Over a foot of snow fell across the northwest highlands, with the greatest amounts found near Cuba and Lindrith.  Snowfall accumulations include 5 inches at Torreon Navajo Mission, 8 inches near Cuba and 12.5 inches near Lindrith.
Up to a foot of snow fell across the west central plateau.  The highest amounts were around Fence Lake, meanwhile the Gallup area received 5 to 6 inches of snow.
The west central mountains received up to 16 inches of snow.
The San Francisco River Valley received up to 5 inches of snow.
Snowfall amounts of 12 to 18 inches were common across the San Juan Mountains.  Some snowfall reports include 14.5 inches at Chama, 18 inches at Tierra Amarilla, and 11 inches at El Vado.
Snowfall amounts over 8 inches were common across the Jemez Mountains.  Snowfall reports include 12 inches at Wolf Canyon and 20 inches at Pajarito Ski area.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: The Sipapu Ski area picked up around 15 inches of snow while areas near Tererro received around one foot. Areas east of Taos were also hit hard with heavy snow. A volunteer firefighter was killed just after 9 am on the 30th, when he lost control on an icy U.S. 64 around a sharp curve.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: Taos Ski Area picked up over a foot of snow, while the Red River Ski area picked up 10 inches.  Several of the SNOTELs in the area received over 8 inches of snow as well.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: Snowfall accumulations over 12 inches were common across the southern Sangre de Cristo Mountains.
CoCoRaHS observers around Taos picked up around 4 inches of snow.  Higher amounts are suspected near Tres Piedras.
Three to six inches of fresh snow were common across the lower Chama River Valley.  However, up to 11 inches of snow fell around Coyote.
Around 4 to 5 inches of snow fell in Santa Fe and the Santa Fe foothills.

The Mogollon and Luna areas were the hardest hit as winds blasted around 50 to 60 mph while around one foot of snow fell. The Mogollon RAWS site recorded a 58 mph wind gust between 713 and 813am on the 30th, which was approximately the same time as some of the heavier snow fall.

The Sierra Blanca SNOTEL picked up 16 inches of snow while Ski Apache received about 11 inches.  Winds gusting at 50 to 60 mph created dangerous blowing snow conditions with visibilities reduced under one half mile.
Winds gusted to 60 mph for over 30 minutes at the Tucumcari ASOS.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: A trained spotter in Sapello measured a 61 mph wind gust early in the morning, though the high winds continued through the afternoon hours.  Winds of at least 58 mph around Ute Park caused large cottonwood trees to blow down. 58 mph wind gusts were also recorded at the Angel Fire AWOS between 210pm and 330pm.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: The Angel Fire AWOS recorded a peak wind gust of 64 mph at 910am, but continued to gust over 58 mph through 1110am. An 8 to 10 inch diameter tree limb was downed just north of town.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Winds over 60 mph plagued the east slopes before snow began to fall. A measured wind gust of 63 mph was recorded at north-northwest of Rociada, meanwhile a cabin roof was blown off and large cottonwood trees were blown down along the Cimarron River near Ute Park.
The Smokey Bear RAWS recorded a wind gust of 70 mph between 6 and 7 pm, before the heavy snow began.
The Eight Mile Draw RAWS site recorded a 58 mph wind gust.
The Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility Transwestern Pump weather station 18 miles north-northeast of Encinoso recorded a 63 mph wind gust.
A 65 mph wind gust was recorded at Sumner Lake while a 59 mph wind gust was recorded at the Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility Fort Sumner weather station.
The Dunken RAWS site recorded a wind gust of 60 mph between 209 and 309pm.
A Native American man between 55 and 60 years old was found in a lot near the corner of Aztec Avenue and Patton Drive.
Four inches of snow fell around Crownpoint.
Approximately 4 to 5 inches of snow fell around Gallup.  Lesser amounts were noted farther south.
Between 3 and 7 inches of snow fell across the west central highlands.  Amounts included 4 inches at Grants and nearly 7 inches around Acoma.
Around 8 inches of snow fell near and in Magdalena.  Elsewhere, 3 to 6 inch amounts were common.
In Reserve, up to 6 inches of snow fell.
Snow amounts varied between 8 and 15 inches across the San Juan Mountains.  Chama received the greatest amount at 15 inches, though most of the SNOTELs in the area picked up between 8 and 10 inches.
The Vacas Locas SNOTEL picked up 8 inches of snow.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Over a foot of snow was reported at the Tres Ritos and Gallegos Peak SNOTELs as well as the Sipapu Ski Area.

events.event_narrative: Between 8 and 12 inches of snow fell across the northern Sangre de Cristo Mountains.

events.event_narrative: Between one and two feet of snow fell across the southern Sangre de Cristo Mountains.

Between 4 and 6 inches of snow fell around Taos.
Generally 3 to 4 inches of snow fell around the Santa Fe area, however, localized amounts up to 6 inches were reported.

On the east side of Albuquerque, 4 to 6 inches of snow was common.  West of Interstate 25, amounts were generally 1 to 2 inches.  Three to 6 inches was also common around Belen, Los Lunas and Bosque Farms.  Spotters also reported hearing thunder around Albuquerque.
Four to 6 inches of snow was common around Socorro, though further east, near Bingham, around 10 inches of snow was reported.
Eight to 13 inches of snow was common across the mountains, though locally higher amounts around Sandia Peak were reported.
About 9 inches of snow fell in Moriarty, though around 6 inches of snow was reported near Stanley.
Six to 8 inches of snow was common across the central highlands.

Between 7 and 13 inches of snow fell across the south central highlands. Along Highway 54, approximately 15 miles south of Corona, a family of four skidded off the road and landed upside down in a 30 foot deep ravine. Highway workers patrolling the area found and rescued the family.  The family sustained some injuries and showed early signs of hypothermia.
Approximately 5 inches of snow fell around Carrizozo.

Amounts varied significantly across the south central mountains.  However, around Alto and Ruidoso, more than a foot of snow was common. The highest elevations around Sierra Blanca received 18 inches or more.
Snow totals varied from 3 to 8 inches across the far northeast highlands, though the highest amounts were noted southwest of Wagon Mound.

The highest snow totals were generally along and west of Interstate 25 where 6 to 12 inches of snow was reported.  During the evening of the 31st, 3 to 4 inch snow rates existed at times around San Jose.
Up to 4 inches of snow fell around Clayton.
Up to 4 inches of snow fell in Harding County.
Up to 4 inches of snow fell in eastern San Miguel County.
Between 2 and 6 inches of snow fell across Guadalupe County, with the highest amounts across western portions of the county.
Between 3 and 10 inches of snow fell across eastern Lincoln County.  The highest amounts were several miles north of Encinoso.
About 6 inches of snow fell around Dunken.
Around 4 inches of snow fell around Crownpoint.  This event continued into February.
Between 4 and 5 inches of snow fell around Gallup, with lesser amounts further south.  This event continued into February.
Between 3 and 7 inches of snow fell across the west central highlands.  Amounts included 4 inches at Grants and nearly 7 inches around Acoma.  This event continued into February.
Around 8 inches of snow fell in and near Magdalena. Elsewhere, 3 to 6 inch amounts were common. This event continued into February.
In Reserve, up to 6 inches of snow fell. This event continued into February.

Snow amounts varied between 8 and 15 inches across the San Juan Mountains.  Chama received the greatest amount at 15 inches, though most of the SNOTELs in the area picked up between 8 and 10 inches. This event continued into February.
The Vacas Locas SNOTEL reported about 8 inches of snow. This event continued into February.

Up to 8  inches of snow fell across Union County, with the higher amounts around Grenville, Folsom and Capulin.
Up to 4 inches of snow fell around Clayton. This event continued into February.
Up to 4 inches of snow fell across Harding County. This event continued into February.
Up to 4 inches of snow fell across eastern San Miguel County. This event continued into February.
Up to 6 inches of snow fell across Quay County, with the highest amounts amounts around Ragland and San Jon.
Between 2 and 6 inches of snow fell across Guadalupe County, though the highest amounts were across western portions of the county. This event continued into February.

Up to 6 inches of snow fell across Curry county, with the highest amounts around Broadview and Grady. Zoo officials in Clovis reported that a giraffe slipped on the snow and ice and fell into a fence, sustaining a head injury, which was then followed by exposure to the cold weather.  Unfortunately, his injuries were too great and the giraffe had to be euthanized.
Between 3 and 10 inches of snow fell across eastern Lincoln County.  The highest amounts were noted several miles north of Encinoso. This event continued into February.
Around 6 inches of snow fell around Dunken. This event continued into February.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: The low temperature at Angel Fire plummeted to 35 degrees below zero.  Winds were generally calm, though brief winds of 5 mph or so dropped the wind chills around -50 degrees. An unofficial observation station in Eagle Nest reported a low temperature of -41 degrees.
The low temperature at Las Vegas dropped to 16 degrees below zero.  North winds of 10 to 15 mph dropped wind chills between -25 and-40 degrees through the early morning hours.
Up to 9 inches of snow fell over the higher elevations of the San Juan Mountains.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: An impressive 5 to 18 inches of snow fell across the East Slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains.
Snowfall ranged between 2 and 6 inches across the Upper Rio Grande Valley.
There were a few reports of 6 inches of snow across the Estancia Valley.
Two to 5 inches of snow was reported across the Central Highlands.
Up to 4 inches of snow fell over the Raton Ridge and Johnson Mesa.
Up to 7 inches of snow fell across the Far Northeast Highlands.
Up to 5 inches of snow fell across the Northeast Highlands.
Up to 4 inches of snow fell across Union County.
Up to 4 inches of snow fell across Guadalupe County.
The Albuquerque ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 77 mph.  Blowing dust reduced visibility below 2 miles for a time.
The Moriarty AWOS measured a peak wind gust of 64 mph.
The Santa Fe ASOS measured a peak wind gust of 62 mph.
A Los Alamos National Lab Mesonet station recorded a 59 mph wind gust approximately 6 miles west-southwest of San Ildefonso Pueblo.

The KSRR AWOS began reporting severe wind gusts during the early morning hours, however, severe gusts became more frequent during the late morning and afternoon hours. The highest wind gusts of 66 mph were recorded at 835 and 935 am, as well as at 155 pm.

In addition to the strong wind gusts, sustained winds over 40 mph plagued the Ruidoso area as well.  For a period in the afternoon, winds were sustained at 52 mph. Sustained winds over 40 mph were most consistent between 815 and 935am and again between 1235 and 315pm.
The Las Vegas ASOS recorded severe wind gusts of 58 and 59 mph several times during the four hour period.  The highest gust of 59 mph was recorded at 926 am.
The Columbia Scientific Balloon Facilities TransWestern Pump weather station north-northeast of Encinoso recorded a 60 mph wind gust.
The Magdalena Ridge Observatory local weather station recorded severe wind gusts for much of the day.  The peak wind gust of 92 mph was observed around 9am.
The Frost Ranch SchoolNet site recorded several wind gusts over 58 mph.  The peak gust of 60 mph was observed at 1211pm.  Report relayed by KVII Amarillo.
The West Texas Mesonet Station southwest of Dora recorded wind gusts up to 64 mph through the late morning and early afternoon.
The West Texas Mesonet Station southwest of Dora recorded sustained winds over 40 mph through the late morning and early afternoon.
The Roswell ASOS recorded wind gusts up to 63 mph.  Visibilities were reduced to near zero in blowing dust.
Winds were sustained over 40 mph at the KCVS ASOS as well as at KCVN for several hours during the late morning and early afternoon hours.
Wind gusts reached 62 mph at the KCVS ASOS while 61 mph gusts were noted at KCVN.  Severe gusts lasted for several hours at each site.
The APRS Weather Net site in Fort Sumner recorded gusts to 59 mph.

The Columbia Scientific Balloon Facilities Transwestern Pump Station north-northeast of Encinoso recorded wind gusts topping 58 mph for several hours.  The peak wind gust of 63 mph occurred around 1030 am.

A 47 year-old woman was found dead at a campsite in the vicinity of 6900 E. Main St. in Farmington. The woman was a transient who was living in a tent across from Memory Gardens.  The morning low temperature was -3 degrees in Farmington.

A 61 year-old man died of exposure in a wooded area near the intersection of Southside River Road and River View Lane in Farmington.  Morning low temperatures only dipped down to 31 degrees in Farmington.
A 69 year-old man from Fort Defiance was found in a wind swept field about 150 years east of North Ninth Street in Gallup.  The low temperature in Gallup that morning was only 9 degrees.
Areas east of Aztec and around Dulce picked up 4 inches of fresh snow.
Chama picked up 8 inches of new snow, however, the SNOTELS across the higher elevations of the San Juan Mountains picked up as much as a foot of new snow.
A wind gust of 59 mph was recorded at the Albuquerque Airport, around the time a large tree toppled onto the roof of a home near the airport.
For nearly six hours, the AWOS at Sierra Blanca Regional Airport reported gusts at or above 58 mph.  The peak gust of 70 mph occurred at 1215 pm.
The AWOS at Sierra Blanca Regional Airport reported sustained winds nearly continuously for 7 hours.  The highest sustained wind speed of 53 mph occurred around the noon hour.
The Gallup ASOS blew at over 58 mph for just over an hour.  The peak gust of 67 mph occurred at 422 pm.
Gusts over 58 mph were reported at the Clines Corners ASOS for around 3 hours.  The max gust of 61 mph was reported at 139 pm.
Sustained winds over 40 mph were reported at Clines Corners for four hours.  The maximum sustained wind was 46 mph around 1pm.
Sustained winds of 40 mph were reported at Las Vegas.
The Columbia Scientific Balloon Facilities Transwestern Pump Station north-northeast of Encinoso recorded a few wind gusts over 58 mph.  The strongest wind gust was 62 mph which occurred at 225 pm.
The Magdalena Ridge Observatory recorded a peak wind gust of 60 mph.
Wind gusts routinely reached 58 mph or greater between 1153 am and 453 pm MST. A peak wind gust of 65 mph was recorded at 1248 pm MST.
High winds occurred at the Sierra Blanca Airport between 1135 am and 535 pm MST. Highest sustained winds reached 46 mph at 1155 am MST.
Gallup reported a peak wind gust of 59 mph at 1253 pm MST.
The Magdalena Ridge Observatory reported wind gusts around 70 mph.

High winds occurred between 1230 pm and 350 pm MST around the Albuquerque Metro Area. The Double Eagle Airport reported a peak wind gust of 66 mph at 150 pm MST, with sustained winds of 55 mph between 1230 and 130 pm MST. The Albuquerque ASOS reported a peak wind gust of 60 mph at 200 pm and sustained winds of 43 mph from 200 pm to 300 pm MST. A peak wind gust of 60 mph was recorded at the top of the Tram at 100 pm MST.
High sustained winds occurred around Clines Corners between 1253 pm and 453 pm MST.
Eight power poles were snapped in two around Edgewood.
A person at the New Mexico Military Institute observed several 6 to 7 inch branches snapped off by strong winds.
A peak wind gust of 64 mph was recorded at 835 am MST.

The Clines Corners ASOS also reported a sustained wind of 49 mph from 1253 pm to 153 pm MST. Amateur radio reported a wind gust of 60 mph five miles west of Estancia. The Moriarty AWOS recorded a wind gust of 59 mph at 535 pm MST.
Television stations reported large trees knocked down and uprooted near the intersection of Roma and Tennessee streets.
The Emergency Manager for Socorro County called shortly after 400 pm MST to report a roof was blown off a house in the northeast part of Socorro and several trees were also down.
The Clines Corners ASOS recorded wind gusts over 58 mph periodically for around 2 hours.  The strongest gust was 61 mph at 922 am MST.
The Columbia Scientific Balloon Facilities Transwestern Pump Station north-northeast of Encinoso recorded a 61 mph wind gust.
KVII in Amarillo reported that the Elida SchoolNet site recorded a 60 mph wind gust.  In addition, the military site K4MR recorded a 58 mph wind gust.
Winds gusted up to 58 mph west of Estancia.
The Clines Corners ASOS measured sustained winds of 40 mph or greater for over an hour.
A mostly dry microburst resulted in winds of 60 mph for a period of 8 minutes at the Farmington ASOS.
As a mountain wave crashed onto the surface, the Clines Corners ASOS measured a 62 mph wind gust.
As a mountain wave crashed onto the surface, the Clines Corners ASOS recorded sustained winds over 40 mph.
Sandia Peak recorded a peak wind gust of 73 mph.
The Clayton ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 59 mph, which was likely due to a dry microburst.
The Hopewell SNOTEL at 10,000 feet picked up 12 inches of fresh snow.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: The Taos Powderhorn SNOTEL at 11,050 feet picked up 17 inches of fresh snow.
A peak wind gust of 58 mph was recorded at 853 am MST.
The KSRR AWOS near Ruidoso recorded a peak wind gust of 60 mph.
The Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility's Transwestern Pump Station north-northeast of Encinoso recorded a 58 mph wind gust.

The ASOS in Tucumcari recorded a peak wind gust of 58 mph.  Approximately 5 north-northwest of Tucumcari, two large cottonwood trees feel onto a home, injuring an elderly couple.  The home suffered severe damage. It's possible that the winds were stronger in this location, perhaps due to a dry microburst.
A 59 mph wind gust was measured 2 miles northwest of Sedillo.
The Clines Corners ASOS recorded sustained winds of 46 mph for approximately an hour.
The Clines Corners ASOS recorded peak wind gust of 60 mph.
The Clovis ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 60 mph.
A tractor trailor was blown over on Interstate 25 near Wagon Mound.
One large cottonwood tree was downed near the intersection of Lomas and Morris.
Strong and gusty winds resulted in damage to a Grants motel.  The roof of the motel as well as outdoor signage sustained most of the damage.
A peak wind gust of 64 was also recorded at the Las Vegas ASOS at 1243 pm MST.
A wind gust of 60 mph was estimated by a trained spotter near Conchas Dam.
Wind damage and power outages occurred on the Zuni Pueblo when a trampoline was blown into power lines.
The 74 mph peak wind gust was recorded at a schoolnet site.
The location of the high sustained winds was 6 miles WNW of Sandia Park.

The Sierra Blanca Airport reported a sustained wind of at least 44 mph for one solid hour. A peak wind gust of 67 mph was also recorded at 135 pm MST. Sustained winds |of 40 mph or greater and peak wind gusts of 58 mph or greater occurred nearly continuously between 1055 am and 255 pm MST.
The CSBF Transwestern Pump mesonet station reported a peak wind gust of 62 mph.
High wind gust of 62 mph reported at base of Sandia Tram.  A 59 mph wind gust was also measured at the mouth of Embudo Canyon.
Various snowfall amounts from spotters, CoCoRaHS, and SNOTEL data between 6 and 10 inches across the San Juan Mountains. El Rito reported 7.5 inches and Bateman SNOTEL 9.0 inches.
Various heavy snowfall amounts between 6 and 11 inches reported over the Jemez Mountains.  Wolf Canyon reported 11 inches and Vacas Locas SNOTEL 8 inches.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Various reports between 2 and 9 inches were reported from CoCoRaHS, spotters, SNOTELs, and the public. Black Lake received 9 inches and Gascon 7 inches.
Various snowfall amounts between 4 and 8 inches were reported from public and spotters. Wagon Mound received 8 inches of snowfall.
Various amounts between 1 and 6 inches were reported from public, law enforcement, and spotters. Trujillo received 4 inches of snowfall.
A small 50-acre fire near Alcalde, NM, named the Palm Fire, burned two abandoned structures.

Several media outlets as well as the Southwest Coordination Center reported that a grass fire erupted during the late morning hours of the 17th. A person traveling along Highway 267 had a blow out which caused sparks along the rim of the vehicle, igniting the fire.  The Tire Fire raced eastward from six miles south of Melrose eastward along the Curry/Roosevelt county line for approximately 20 miles as antecedent dry conditions and east winds of at least 20 mph fueled the fire. In all, 24,000 acres of land was scorched, much of it cattle grazing land, and three homes were destroyed.  No cattle were harmed, however, three firefighters were treated for minor burns and smoke inhalation.

A human-caused wildfire begun in Gavilan Canyon and quickly spread north and northeast as very strong winds fueled the fire. The White Fire crossed Highway 70 near Ruidoso Downs and continued to move toward Forest Service Road 120. Highway 70 between mile markers 265 and 271 was closed for a time. Much of the burned area consists of steep, rough and rocky terrain, which made it difficult to contain the fire.  In all, 10,384 acres were scorched, 5 homes and 7 outbuildings were destroyed and another 2 homes and 2 outbuildings were damaged.

A wildfire scorched a 7 mile long by 1/2 mile wide path from Curry Road H near Ned Houk Memorial Park to Curry Road D.  One home was damaged in the area of Curry Road G and 19.  In all, the wildfire burned 4000 acres. This wildfire continued to burn into March.

A wildfire scorched a 7 mile long by 1/2 mile wide path from Curry Road H near Ned Houk Memorial Park to Curry Road D.  One home was damaged in the area of Curry Road G and 19.  In all, the wildfire burned 4000 acres.
An amateur radio operator reported one third of his metal roof was blown off is home from a microburst at 425 Stephens St., two miles southwest of Hagerman.
The Magdalena Ridge Observatory recorded high wind gusts for several hours.  The peak wind gusts of 67 mph occurred between 9 and 11 am MST.

The Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility's Transwestern Pump Station northeast of Encinoso recorded a peak wind gust of 61 mph at 115 pm MST, though a 58 mph gust was recorded as early as 1130 am MST.
The Sierra Blanca AWOS as well as the Smokey Bear RAWS reported peak wind gusts of 63 mph.  Both also recorded high wind gusts for several hours.
The Santa Fe ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 60 mph, which was likely aided by microburst winds.
The Clines Corners ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 58 mph.
The ASOS at the Tucumcari Airport registered a peak wind gust of 58 mph during the midday hours.
The Clayton ASOS recorded sustained winds over 40 mph from 155 pm to 455 pm MST.
The Sierra Blanca AWOS recorded sustained winds between 40 and 46 mph from 1255 pm to 155 pm MST.
Hail was reported along Highway 236 near Bethel.
Spotter reported mostly pea sized hail, but a few stones were as large as a nickel.
State Police reported golf ball sized hail along Highway 70 at mile post 407. The hail broke the windshield of the police car.
Hagerman Police Department reported golf ball sized hail along State Road 249 east of Hagerman.
The cooperative observer in Capulin estimates a peak wind gust of 65 mph.  A few hailstones and one tenth of an inch of rain was also reported.
A spotter estimated a 60 mph wind gust in Sedan.
The Tucumcari ASOS recorded severe wind gusts for at least 10 minutes, with a peak gust of 74 mph at 635 pm MST.
The Logan SchoolNet Site recorded a thunderstorm wind gust of 61 mph.  Report relayed by KVII Amarillo.
A trained spotter estimated a 60 mph thunderstorm wind gust.

A heat burst struck Cannon Air Force Base as formerly severe thunderstorms decayed over the area.  Winds peaked at 90 mph, but winds greater than 58 mph persisted for over 30 minutes causing widespread damage.  These strong winds damaged roofs and broke limbs off trees. KCVS ASOS jumped from 71 to 78 degrees and the dewpoint dropped from 50 to 44 degrees. The nearby AWOS, KCVN, jumped from 73 to 81 degrees and the dewpoint dropped from 46 to 41 degrees.  KCVN, however, only gusted to 43 mph.

A heat burst struck the Clayton Airport during the early morning hours of the 4th.  The temperature jumped 14 degrees, from 63 to 77, and the dewpoint dropped 11 degrees, from 46 to 35. The wind peaked at 64 mph at 109 am MST.
The Las Vegas ASOS reached a peak wind gust of 58 mph.
One business lost some shingles in Grants, while several homes had minor roof damage from the strong wind gusts. A tent filled with fireworks was blown over as well.
Wind gusts were measured between 60 and 63 mph for 15 minutes.

This human caused wildfire, named the Miller Fire, began at the end of April and continued well into June, burning within the steep and rugged terrain of the Gila Wilderness.  Four, generally unused, trailers burned near the Gila Cliff Dwellings Visitor in May, but fortunately, all of the historic cabins were saved. 13 minor injuries occurred with the fire fighting efforts, which are also believed to have occurred in May.  In total, 88,835 acres burned, though less than half of this area was within Catron County.

This human caused wildfire, named the Miller Fire, began at the end of April and continued well into June, burning within the steep and rugged terrain of the Gila Wilderness. Four, generally unused, trailers burned near the Gila Cliff Dwellings Visitor Center in May, but fortunately, all of the historic cabins were saved. 13 minor injuries occurred with the fire fighting efforts, which are also believed to have occurred in May. In total, 88,835 acres burned, though less than half of this area was within Catron County.
