Four, generally unused, trailers burned near the Gila Cliff Dwellings Visitor in May, but fortunately, all of the historic cabins were saved. 13 minor injuries occurred with the fire fighting efforts, which are also believed to have occurred in May. In total, 88,835 acres burned, though less than half of this area was within Catron County.
This human caused fire burned 6159 acres just north of Interstate 40, north of Milagro.  This so-called Milagro Fire destroyed one outbuilding and damaged another.

This grass and timber fueled fire, named the Track Fire, started just north of Raton and burned along and between Bartlett and Horse Mesas, and on either side of the Interstate 25 corridor. I-25 was closed for approximately 3.5 days.  This fire was caused by engine exhaust particles, likely expelled by an TV on Burlington Northern Santa Fe Railway property.  The ATV rider trespassed  onto land owned by BNSF through access from nearby private property.  Evacuations were needed along the northside of Raton, Pine Valley Estates, and within Sugarite Canyon State Park and Yankee Canyon.  The Raton watershed sustained significant damage. In all, 27,792 acres burned, 19,962 of which was in New Mexico. In all, 8 residences and 11 outbuilding were destroyed.
A dry microburst produced a wind gust of 78 mph at the Clovis airport.
This human caused fire, named the Swallow Fire for starting on Swallow Drive, burned 10 acres of land in a wooded Ruidoso neighborhood.  Nine homes were lost to the blaze.

The Windy Fire originated 3 miles east of McAlister and quickly spread under very windy conditions along the Curry and Quay county line. One unoccupied residence was burned as was 6 outbuildings. In all, 32,143 acres were scorched.
A roof was blown off a home on the southwest side of Roswell.
An outflow boundary from a thunderstorm produced a wind gust of 63 mph at the Clayton Airport.
A 58 mph wind gust was recorded at Stallion Runway on White Sands Missile Range.
Outflow boundaries with winds exceeding 58 mph continuously impacted the Raton Crews Airport.

An unnamed arroyo feeding into the San Francisco River became flooded near the Luna Post Office.  The water was at least four feet high and washed away the porch steps of a nearby mobile home.  The headwaters of the arroyo are located northwest of town, within the Wallow Fire burn scar.

Heavy rains led to flooding in Allison Canyon along U.S. Highway 70 near mile marker 268.  Fortunately, residents in the River Ranch RV park along the canyon were evacuated prior to the high water reaching the ranch.  An estimated 4 to 6 feet of water flowed through the area.  Fortunately, the RV park did not sustain much damage.
Quarter size hail was reported along I-40.
Sustained winds of 43 knots were also noted.
The roof of a barn collapsed and killed an elderly man.
Several trees and large limbs were downed by strong wind gusts in Portales, along U.S. Highway 70.

events.event_narrative: The White Sands mesonet site at Phillips Hills recorded a 77 mph wind gust from a storm that rapidly intensified over the site after interacting with a gust front.

The 346 Fire, located 5 miles south of Belen in the Bosque, burned 262 acres over a five day period.  The fire destroyed 3 residences and 7 outbuildings, and also damaged another 3 residences and 7 outbuildings.
The Sierra Blanca Regional Airport near Ruidoso recorded a peak wind gust of 58 mph at 1255 pm MST.
The Las Vegas ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 58 mph.
The Clayton ASOS a peak wind gust of 61 mph at 355 pm MST.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: The Pacheco fire scorched 10,250 acres in all.  Though no buildings were damaged, 12 power poles burned during the event.  This power line fed both the Tesuque Peak NOAA weather radio transmitter as well as the Santa Fe Ski Basin. After some communication interruption, generators were installed to facilitate operations.  Total damage estimates will be entered at the end of the event.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: The Pacheco fire scorched 10,250 acres in all. Though no buildings were damaged, 12 power poles burned during the event. This power line fed both the Tesuque Peak NOAA weather radio transmitter as well as the Santa Fe Ski Basin. After some communication interruption, generators were installed to facilitate operations.

The Las Conchas wildfire damaged 80 homes, of which, 15 were primary residences.  The other 65 homes were seasonal.  Numerous outbuildings were also damaged or destroyed.  The fire prompted evacuations of Los Alamos National Labs, Bandelier National Monument, the City of Los Alamos, as well as numerous other campgrounds and homes within the burned area itself. The fire burned portions of the Santa Clara, Cochiti, San Ildefonso and Santa Domingo Pueblos as well as portions of Bandelier National Monument and the Valles Caldera National Preserve.  This fire burned on both sides of Highway 4, and up to Highway 501, causing both highways to be closed for a time. Some of this area was previously burned by the Cerro Grande Fire in 2000.  Fortunately, no member of the public or any emergency responders were seriously injured during the fire suppression efforts.

The Las Conchas wildfire damaged 80 homes, of which, 15 were primary residences. The other 65 homes were seasonal. Numerous outbuildings were also damaged or destroyed and 10 vehicles were completely destroyed. The fire prompted evacuations of Los Alamos National Labs, Bandelier National Monument, the city of Los Alamos, as well as numerous other campgrounds and homes within the burn area itself. The fire burned portions of the Santa Clara, Cochiti, San Ildefonso and Santa Domingo Indian Reservations as well as portions of Bandelier National Monument and the Valles Caldera National Preserve. Fortunately, no member of the public or any emergency responders were seriously injured during the fire suppression efforts.

events.event_narrative: Hail piled up between 12 and 17 inches over Johnson Mesa due to a stationary thunderstorm that persisted for approximately one hour.  Though some stones were as large as a quarter, much of the hail was smaller. Snow plows had to be called out to clear Highway 72.  Some motorists were stranded for nearly 6 hours.
Significant runoff transported considerable amounts of ash and debris from the Track Fire burn scar into Lake Maloya. All lakes and ponds in the Sugarite area were bankfull.
Rainfall rates of 2 inches in 30 minutes were reported in Folsom. Streets rapidly flooded including Highways 456 and 325. The runoff flooded some homes.
Water was approximately four feet deep over Highway 456 at the Dry Cimarron River Crossing approximately 10 miles east of Folsom. A few fences were washed out due to the high water.

Both Highway 4 and 501 were closed in the Jemez Mountains due to flooding.  Heavy rains on the Las Conchas burn scar caused significant runoff and debris flow over the roadways. At least a 50 yard stretch of debris several inches deep was noted along State Highway 501.  Both roads had to be cleared by the Highway Department before traffic was allowed to pass.

Heavy rain fell early in the afternoon across the White Fire burn scar. Fortunately only minor flooding ensued at the time. However, as another round of showers and thunderstorms moved over the burn scar in the evening, more significant flooding resulted.  Culverts that were built along a road near Seeping Springs that crossed Allison Canyon were already at capacity from the earlier rains.  The additional precipitation caused them to give way, which lead to rapid flows along Allison Canyon.  These waters reach the River Ranch RV Park along Highway 70.  The water was estimated to be three feet high, which topped the concrete barriers that were installed to protect the park.   Fortunately, the park did not sustain any damage.

Though the Rio Ruidoso was running high and fast downstream of Ruidoso Downs, the most significant flooding was within the town itself. Water approximately two feet deep flooded the intersection of Highlands and Joe Welch. An SUV attempted to cross the waters but was unsuccessful.  Flooding and debris from the White Fire burn scar was also noted along Highway 70.
The 66 mph thunderstorm wind gust was reported by the White Sands Missile Range Mesonet at Stallion Runway.
Tree limbs approximately four feet long and 3 inches in diameter were blown down.

A creek that parallels Dixon Apple Orchard overflowed with rushing water and debris. It likely did not rain at this location, rather heavy rains fell on the southern portion of the Las Conchas burn scar, and runoff quickly moved down the canyons. Radar estimated between one and two inches of rain fell.

The River Ranch RV Park northeast of Ruidoso along Highway 70 had to be evacuated due to flooding.   Water was flowing fast out of Gavilan Canyon and the Rio Ruidoso was out of its banks. In addition, Forest Service Roads 120 B and C were flooded and damaged.

A KVII Schoolnet site north of Clovis recorded winds from a wet microburst. Winds initially were from the north-northeast at 72 mph at 545 pm MST, then increased to 79 mph at 549 pm.  The wind direction switched to the south-southwest at 652 pm and a final gust of 64 mph occurred.

State Police in Raton reported rock and tree limb debris from the Track Fire burn scar on Interstate 25 from mile markers 455 to 459.  The northbound lanes were primarily impacted.  Much of the water and debris came from the mountains on the west side of the interstate.  Raton Creek also overflowed its banks on the north side of Raton.  The creek, which is 15 feet deep and cemented, had water spilling out up to 30 feet away from its banks.  The water came up to the porches on a half dozen homes, but fortunately did not cause any house damage.
Flash flooding occurred along Maloney Street between 1st and 6th streets.  Several of these intersections were closed as water was halfway up vehicles.  A few cars were stuck in the water.

Santa Fe police reported home evacuations near the intersection of Valmora Road and Serafina Street.  Water was reported to be two feet deep and 40 feet wide.  Two feet of water was also reported at the intersection of Rodeo Road and Old Pecos Trail.  Cars attempting to drive through the water stalled.  Two feet of water was also reported to have flooded a home at the Rainbow Vision Condominium Complex at I-25 and St. Francis Dr. Spotters in the area reported between 1 and 1.8 inches of rain in one hours time.

Emergency management reported the Rio Ruidoso out of its banks for a 6 to 10 mile stretch downstream of the White Fire burn scar.  High water levels in the canyons and arroyos on the east and south side of the burn scar flowed into the Rio Ruidoso, causing it to flood.  Debris from the burn area was piled up on the banks. Near mile marker 272.5 on Highway 70, portions of the Rio de Oso Trailer park was underwater.
Law enforcement official reported a roof blown off a home on the southwest side of Clayton.  Numerous fences were also blown down in this area.
A wildfire, caused by overheated vehicle brakes, forced temporary evacuations and burned one home before fire crews contained the blaze.  In all, 14.2 acres were burned along Old Las Vegas Highway.

An arroyo backed up and flooded a portion of Indian Service Route 27.  Five homes were flooded and evacuated. Further to the west, what was described as a waterfall was coming off the higher terrain surrounding the interstate. Water was flowing over the interstate and the frontage roads.  Each of these roads had to be shut down for a short time.
Water and debris flowed over Highway 501 after approximately one inch of rain fell over central portions of the Las Conchas burn scar.  The highway was temporarily closed.

After 1 to 1.5 inches of rain fell on the northern portion of the Las Conchas burn scar, flash flooding was reported in Santa Clara Canyon.   Four people that were working in the canyon had to be rescued by helicopter.
Highway 30 near Santa Clara Pueblo was temporarily closed due to flash flooding.

Major flash flooding ensued after an estimated 3 to 4 inches of rain fell across the southern portion of the Las Conchas burn scar.  Flooding in Frijoles Creek caused damage in and around Bandelier National Monument.  Two barrier walls around the Visitors Center were overtopped and the septic system lift station was inundated with water.  Major flooding was also reported in Peralta Canyon around Kasha Katuwe (Tent Rocks) National Monument.  Damage was reported to the access road as well as other local roads.  ||Along and downstream of Cochiti Canyon sustained the most damage from flood waters.  Flows were reported to be 8 to 10 feet high when they reached Dixon's Apple Orchard.  The flood waters damaged the owners personal residence, inundated the main storage facility with 10 feet of mud and debris, moved a semi truck approximately 200 yards and destroyed approximately 10 percent of the apple orchard.   The water also wiped out a 50 yard long 4 foot by 4 foot rock retaining wall that was built in 1942.

Flash flooding was reported in homes on Galisteo Street, within the Forest Circle Street and Calle Torreador subdivisions, Miguel Chaves Road and the Tuscany at St. Francis Apartments.  Street flooding was also reported on portions of Cerrillos, St. Francis Dr., and St. Michaels Road.

During the damage survey of the previous days flooding, abundant rain above Cochiti Canyon resulted in another, more devastating flood, to Dixon's Apple Orchard which was witness first hand by the NWS Albuquerque Warning Coordination Meteorologist. The force of the flow was estimated to be 3 times as that of the previous days flood.  At least 10 feet high, the width of the flood waters was approximately 100 yards wide. 20 to 40 percent more of the apple orchard was destroyed. Also, the main storage building that sustained damage in the previous days flood was wiped completely off its foundation.  The semi truck that moved 200 yards before, was washed downstream and ended up in the Cochiti Lake Reservoir in pieces.
There was considerable amounts of mud and rocks across New Mexico State Highways 4 and 502.
Hail size ranged from peas to quarters.
The hail occurred on the west side of Farmington.

events.event_narrative: The Baton Rouge Complex consisted of both the Baton Rouge wildfire and the Flying H wildfire which were started by lightning. In all, the fires burned 28,165 acres near the Chaves and Lincoln county line. Approximately 10 power poles, which fed a local ranch, were destroyed on the north side of the fire within Lincoln County.
A brief landspout formed underneath a developing updraft is southeast Albuquerque.  Though the landspout picked up some dust, no damage was noted.
Multiple wind gusts over 58 mph occurred at the Clayton ASOS.
Sustained winds over 40 mph occurred for several hours at the Clayton ASOS.
The Raton ASOS hit a peak wind gust of 67 mph at 134 pm MST, though gusts above 58 mph occurred for several hours.
The Raton ASOS recorded sustained winds over 40 mph for at least an hour.
The Las Vegas ASOS recorded a peak wind gust of 59 mph.
This report was relayed by KVII television in Amarillo.
Reported by KFDA Amarillo News storm chaser.

The KSRR AWOS reported sustained wind speeds over 40 mph for a period of 2 hours. The highest sustained wind speed was 55 mph which occurred at 735 am MST.
A spotter in Stanley reported a peak wind gust of 59 mph.
Winds gusts over 58 mph for at least 24 minutes at the Clines Corners ASOS.  The peak wind gust was 67 mph which occurred at 822 am MST.
The Raton Crews Airport ASOS recorded a 61 mph wind gust.

The Roswell ASOS recorded at 58 mph wind gust.

events.event_narrative: Though most areas received between 4 and 7 inches of snow, isolated locations received well more than that.  The cooperative observer in Eagle Nest reported a whopping 19 inches of snow with this storm.

Areas between Springer, Cimarron and Rayado were the hardest hit locations within the far northeast highlands. Between 4 and 8 inches of snow was common.  Eight inches was reported 6 miles east-southeast of Cimarron by a trained spotter.
As enhanced radar echoes moved over the KSKX AWOS, some mid level momentum was transported to the surface, resulting in an 82 mph wind gust.  No damage was reported by airport personnel.
The northern half of Union County received between 2 and 5 inches of snowfall.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: The Angel Fire AWOS measured wind gusts exceeding 58 mph for at least 40 minutes. The peak wind gust of 64 mph occurred at 1255 am MST.
A mountain wave crashed onto the Raton ASOS causing a gust to 62 mph.
The Clayton ASOS measured sustained winds of 40 mph for at least one hour.
The Clovis AWOS measured sustained winds of at least 40 mph for one hour.

Sustained winds between 40 and 55 mph and gusts between 60 and 90 mph were common across the Albuquerque Metro Area with numerous reports of roof damage, downed power lines, evaporative coolers blown off roofs, tree limbs snapped and trees toppled over. Over 2500 damage claims have been filed in and around the Albuquerque Metro area with damage in the millions. The winds also took on the University of New Mexico football practice facility, with damage noted to the south walls and roof. Also, the Valencia High School roof in Los Lunas was partially damaged from high winds.  This damage alone cost an estimated $15,000.

High winds caused damage for several hours across the lower Rio Grande Valley. Pro panel roofing was blown off the Chaves Community Center near the community of La Nutrias on Highway 304 around 2 pm LST. A bit later, a roof blew off a hay barn at the Black and White Dairy in Abeytas, NM west of mile marker 4 on Highway 116. Also, a mobile home on Wallner Road in the Ranchos de Veguita subdivision was blown apart and scattered approximately 300 feet from where it was sitting around 5 pm LST.  No one was home during the incident.  Around the same time, a mobile home was turned on its side near the Veguita Trading Post. Around 11 pm, a large tree was blown down across Highway 304 at mile marker 11.  Several other mobile homes were damaged in northern Socorro County by Able Wash due to the winds, and one fire engine was damaged east of Bernardo.  The strong winds caused sand in the area to pile up on area roadways.  Approximately one foot of sand was noted on the roads west of Bernardo.

Two commercial buildings, one home and two motels sustained roof damage from high winds around Grants. In addition, one business sustained minor roof damage in Milan.  Numerous trees were toppled and limbs were blown down.
A truck rolled over on U.S. Route 64/87 between Capulin and Raton due to high winds.
The cooperative observer in Dulce reported approximately 6 inches of snow.
Between 2 and 5 inches of snow was reported across the upper Rio Grande Valley.
Up to 5 inches of snow was reported across the lower Chama River Valley.
Up to 4 inches of snow was reported near the Bingham area.
The heavy snow band set up along the Manzano Mountains, dropping up to a foot of snow.
The heavy snow band stretched across the Estancia Valley dropping around 4 to 6 inches of snow, but localized areas received up to 10 inches.
Four to six inches of snow fell across the central highlands.
Six inches of snow fell in Claunch, while 6.5 inches of snow fell southeast of Corona.
Approximately 6 to 7 inches of snow fell around the Valley of Fires Recreation Area near Carrizozo.
The Sierra Blanca SNOTEL picked up around 11 inches of snow.  Lower elevations received between 4 and 7 inches.
Around 5 to 6 inches of snow fell around Las Vegas.
Parts of Union County were inundated with snow.  Southwestern portions of the county received between 8 and 12.5 inches of snow.  Further east, 3 to 5 inches of snow was common.
The western portions of Harding County received up to 10 inches of snow.
Four to six inches of snow was common across eastern San Miguel County.
Between 3 and 8 inches of snow was reported across Santa Rosa.
Up to 4 inches of snow fell across De Baca County.
The northeastern portion of Lincoln County received between 6 to 7 inches of snow.
Near Dulce, between 2 and 5 inches of snow was reported.
Heavy snow began once the front moved into the area. Amounts of 4 to 8 inches were common in and near Laguna Pueblo, while up to a foot of snow as reported around Alamo.
The heaviest snows were across the eastern portion of the southwest mountains.  Near Magdalena, up to 10 inches of snow was reported.
The southeast slopes of the San Juan Mountains received the most snowfall.  The Bateman SNOTEL picked up 10 inches of fresh snow.
Between 12 and 13 inches were reported across the Jemez Mountains by both the cooperative observer and the Pajarito Ski Area.

The lower Rio Grande Valley saw between 3 and 10.5 inches of snow. This caused portions of Interstate 25 to be shut down due to hazardous road conditions.  Two semi trucks jackknifed on the interstate at mile marker 140.
Widespread snowfall amounts of 8 to 14 inches were reported. 14 inches of snow was reported at both Manzano and Sandia Ski Area.

The second occurred approximately 3 miles east a half an hour later, taking the life of a 70 year-old man.  Both drivers lost control due to icy roadways.

events.event_narrative: Four inches of new snow fell around Chaco Canyon.  Areas near Farmington received less than an inch of snow.
Close to 4 inches of snow fell around Cuba while 4.5 inches of snow was reported east-southeast of Counselor.

Snow rapidly fell across the west central mountains during the overnight hours.  Near one foot of snow was reported around El Morro and Thoreau while even higher amounts were reported south of El Morro.

Snow rapidly piled up across the west central highlands, especially around Grants.  Grants picked up 15 inches of snow, while Cubero and Acoma Pueblo received 6 and 7 inches, respectively. The heavy wet snow caused 6 carports to collapse in Grants.  No injuries were reported.

Around 8 inches of snow fell in Los Alamos, but at the Pajarito Ski site, more than a foot of snow fell.  East slopes of the Jemez Mountains received more snow than western slopes, which generally picked up around 2 to 5 inches.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: The southern Sangre de Cristo Mountains started with the initial round of precipitation that came up from the south, then the east slopes received another round of heavy snow when the back door front backed up to the mountains. The Wesner Springs SNOTEL picked up 19 inches of snow while the Santa Fe Ski area received 10 inches.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: The Black Lake and Eagle Nest areas received 8 to 9 inches of snow, but the Angel Fire Ski area received approximately one foot.
Western portions of the lower Chama River Valley picked up the most snow, including around 4 inches at Canones and 8 inches at Coyote.
Approximately 3 to 4 inches of snow fell across the Santa Fe Metro area.
Between 4 and 7 inches of snow fell across eastern portions of Albuquerque, including the foothills.
Between 8 and 14 inches fell across the high peaks and the east slopes of the Sandia and Manzano Mountains.
Between 7 and 9 inches of snow fell across the Estancia Valley, including 7 inches at Stanley, 8 inches at Moriarty, and 9 inches at Estancia.

Eight inches of snow was reported 7 miles southeast of Clines Corners, while 11 inches of snow was reported 16 miles east of Clines Corners along Interstate 40. I-40 was shutdown until roads were safe for travel.
Between 4 and 6 inches of snow fell across the south central highlands, including 6 inches at Corona.

Approximately 8 inches of snow fell at the Raton Port of Entry, while nearly 11 inches of snow fell at Capulin.  Winds of 40 to 45 mph with gusts over 60 mph caused unbelievable blowing and drifting snow. Snow drifts over 4 feet were reported.

The Interstate 25 corridor was hit hard with nearly 15 inches of snow in Wagon Mound.  7 inches of snow was also reported around Abbott. The Raton ASOS measured a gust of 60 mph during the event. Sustained winds of 35 to 45 mph caused substantial blowing and drifting snow.  Snow drifts were over 4 feet.  A horse trailer going southbound overturned on Interstate 25 between Wagon Mound and Springer.  Three people were injured.
At least 4 to 5 inches of snow fell across the northeast highlands.

One to two feet of snow blanketed Union County. Approximately 18 inches of snow fell in Clayton, while 12 inches fell in Pasamonte. In far northern portions of the county, up to 24 inches of snow was reported.  Meanwhile, sustained winds of 35 to 45 mph with gusts over 60 mph caused unbelievable blowing and drifting snow. Snow drifts were reported to be 8 to 10 feet high in some locations.  Roads quickly took a turn for the worse, and left several travelers stranded. One family from Texas pulled over on U.S. Highway 56 near mile marker 48, east of Gladstone, due to the white-out conditions. However, snow continued to pile up on their vehicle.  The family was buried under the snow in their Yukon for 2 days before rescuers found them. Both parents had pneumonia, but their 5 year old daughter was fine.
Between 5 and 6 inches of snow was common across Harding County, with locally higher amounts. Due to the strong winds of 30 to 40 mph with higher gusts, snow drifts were 3 to 4 feet high.
Between 4 and 7 inches of snow fell across eastern San Miguel County.  Snow drifts were up to 3 feet high due to the strong and gusty winds.

Western portions of Guadalupe County received approximately one foot of snow, including around Vaughn.  Eastern portions of the county generally received around 6 inches.  The icy roads combined with blowing and drifting snow due to the strong winds, caused a single car rollover in Vaughn.  The lone occupant was killed.

Four to seven inches of snow fell across Quay County, including around 6 inches in Tucumcari.  The Tucumcari ASOS measured wind gusts of 40 to 45 mph with gusts to 60 mph, which resulted in significant blowing and drifting snow.

As 2 to 4 inches of snow fell across Curry County, roads quickly became icy. A driver of a Toyota sedan traveling on U.S. 60/84 four miles east of Melrose lost traction and slid head on into a pickup truck around 245 pm on the 19th. All four occupants of the sedan were killed, and both passengers of the pick up truck were sent to the hospital for non-life threatening injuries.
Northwest portions of De Baca County received the most snow.  Up to 9 inches of snow was reported in this area, while up to 4 inches was reported across eastern portions of the county.
Between 3 and 5 inches fell near and southwest of Cuba.
Near Fence Lake, approximately 6 inches of snow fell.
Snow fell fast across the east slopes of the west central mountains. 12 to 18 inches of snow was reported in these areas.

Snow fell fast across the west central highlands, including around Grants.  Between 10 and 12 inches of fresh snow fell at Grants, which was just under what this area had received in the previous storm just a few days earlier. Up to two feet of snow was reported from Laguna Pueblo southward toward Alamo, while 14 inches of snow was reported in Cubero.
The east slopes of the southwest mountains were blanketed with 8 to 24 inches of new snow.

The east slopes of the Jemez Mountains picked up more than a foot of new snow in some areas, including at Pajarito Ski Area, which received approximately 16 inches.  Near Los Alamos, 8 inches of snow was reported.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: The Wesner Springs SNOTEL picked up another 8 inches of snow.
Between 2 and 4 inches of snow fell across the area, though the heaviest amounts were near Cochiti Lake.

Strong east winds prevented much of the city of Albuquerque from receiving appreciable snow.  However, far western portions of the city, as well as portions of Rio Rancho, received 1 to 2 inches of snow. This small amount of snow wreaked havoc on roads in the area and numerous accidents were reported.  The heaviest snow was reported around Belen and west of Double Eagle Airport, where approximately 4 inches of snow fell.
Areas along and west of the Rio Grande were the hardest hit.  Between 9 and 12 inches of new snow was reported around Socorro, while 5 inches was reported near San Acacia.
Around 18 inches of snow fell across the Sandia and Manzano Mountains.  This amount was reported at the Sandia Ski Area, Sedillo, near Manzano and just east of Tijeras.
Snowfall amounts were highly variable across the Estancia Valley.  Around 4 inches of snow fell at Moriarty, but nearly 14 inches was reported at Estancia.
Around 5 inches of snow fell just southeast of Clines Corners, but nearly 8 inches of snow fell at Duran.
Approximately 5 inches of snow fell near Corona.
Between 12 and 16 inches of snow fell in and near Ruidoso, with over a foot and a half reported at Ski Apache.
Between 2 and 6 inches of snow fell across the northeast highlands.

Snow amounts varied from 2 to 4 inches across northern portions of the county, including at Portales, to 10 to 12 inches of snow across the southern portions of the county, including at Milnesand and Elida.
Southern portions of De Baca County received between 5 and 8 inches of snow, while northern portions of the county received between 3 and 4.
Between 9 and 12 inches of snow blanketed the Chaves County plains, including at Roswell, Hagerman and Elkins.
Six to 10 inches of snow fell across eastern Lincoln County.
Around 7 inches of snow fell northeast of Dunken, while about 16 inches of snow fell near Elk.

East canyon winds blew through the gaps of the Sandia and Manzano Mountains with gusts near 70 mph around the Albuquerque Foothills and 75 mph at the mouth of Embudo Canyon.  Because of the strong winds, these areas did not receive much snow.
A 4-year old girl died after her family's SUV lost traction on an icy Highway 209 north of Clovis and overturned. The girl's mother and sister suffered minor injuries.

The semi then hit another vehicle and pinned it against the median barrier where both caught fire, but the occupants escaped.  At the time of the accident, visibility was reduced to approximately 4 miles with a temperature of 19 degrees.

National Weather Service meteorologists surveyed tornado damage that originated in an open desert, native to only small juniper trees and cactus. Based on multiple eyewitness accounts, several photos and video, the landspout began as two dust devils merged. The circulation grew vertically and made connection with the parent thunderstorm as it moved east. Interestingly though, the parent storm moved southeast. The landspout moved over two stock tanks. One was blown back to the west approximately 20 feet and hit a steel fence that was dented. The other tank was blown approximately 0.75 miles to the east and was mangled and in pieces. The landspout crossed State Road 107 and increased in intensity. Numerous pinon and juniper trees as well as cholla cacti were uprooted and displaced between 20 and 100 feet. No homes or outbuildings were damaged or destroyed. Peak wind speed was estimated at 90 mph.

events.event_narrative: The hail resulted in damage to automobiles, including broken windshields.
A local COOP observer estimated a wind gust to near 60 mph.
Wind gust recorded at a RAWS site.
Wind gust was recorded at White Sands Missile Range- Oscura Range Camp site.

The Clayton Police Dept. relayed reports of a funnel cloud associated with a severe thunderstorm storm in the area.  A large funnel cloud was accompanied by several smaller funnel clouds. Rotation was not observed or evident on radar.

An amateur radio operator reported torrents of water along NM 3 with up to 4 feet of flowing water over the road.  Considerable hail and reduced visibilities also accompanied the storms. Difficult driving conditions due to heavy rain,  hail and near zero visibility were also reported along Interstate 40 in this area via NMDOT.
The Lincoln County Emergency Manager relayed a report from the Capitan Police Dept. Chief of a well-defined funnel cloud just north of Capitan.
An amateur radio operator reported quarter sized hail as well as downed power lines.

Nickel to golfball sized hail pounded the Santa Rosa area resulting in major damage. Partial roof collapses and broken skylights were common throughout the central and western portions of the community. Smaller hail accumulated to depths of up to two feet in areas. Snow plows were required to clear roads. Many local residents and motorists described the scene as snow in July.
A SKYWARN Spotter reported strong winds in association with a thunderstorm in the area along with quarter sized hail.
A SKYWARN Spotter relayed a report of windows that had been broken out in the Portales area from a severe storm the evening of the 3rd.

Residents were reported to be stranded in the Meadow Lake and El Cerro Mission areas east of Los Lunas due to flooding. Roads were completely covered with water and pumps were required for water removal. Some residents reported water several feet deep. Much of the impacted area has non-paved roads and runoff originated from heavy rains over the Manzano Mountains immediately to the east.
A SKYWARN Spotter relayed a report of automobile damage due to large hail just north of Santa Rosa. Hail sizes in this area ranged from nickel to golfball sized.

Bursum Rd - NM 159 was closed due to flooding and burn scar debris from mile marker 2-25. Per reports, Silver Creek flooded Mogollon and blew out Bursum Rd. in several locations near Mogollon. Whitewater Creek also flooded and brought down a significant amount of ash. The Catwalk was closed due to flooding as well. Rainfall amounts ranging from 0.50 to 1.40 inches were recorded from RAWS and HADS sites in the area.
Mesonet site recorded a 58mph wind gust as an isolated cell moved from NW to the SE across the area.

A trained spotter reported that heavy rains had washed out roads in his neighborhood. His neighbor called to relay that 3 inches of rain fell in an hour causing major flooding on roads. He later reported that the culvert into an arroyo could not handle the volume of water and washed out Deer Tank Rd. Deer Tank Rd. was impassable for much of the evening and next morning. Water on roads of 3ft deep and 50-60ft wide were reported (all dirt roads). Radar showed an isolated thunderstorm over the area that stayed in the general vicinity for over an hour. Highest reflectivity was 66dBz. Storm total precipitation estimates had numerous values greater than 3.5.

BAER team on the Tres Lagunas Burn Scar reported flooding in the area. Minor flooding was reported across NM 63 where sediment and small rocks were carried over a portion of the road between the Windy Bridge and Tererro areas in the Santa Fe National Forest. Major flooding was reported over Forest Road 122 a.k.a. Holy Ghost, which was impassable after large rocks were rolled over the road by flood waters. Storms developed and stayed over the burn location for close to an hour with light rain persisting another half hour and additional light rain about 6 hours later.

On July 4th, during a torrential storm, Engine 12 and Rescue 12 of the Albuquerque Fire Dept. were near the area of Eubank and Copper when they heard a very loud lightning strike. Approximately 60-90 seconds later, Engine 12 was dispatched to a residence where a tree had been struck.  Two individuals were injured including a pregnant woman who was two weeks away from her due date.  The 38- week pregnant female and her boyfriend were assessed, treated and transported to a local hospital. The woman underwent an emergency C-section. Days later, mom and dad along with their new baby girl were released from the hospital.

Emergency Manager relayed that Bonito Lake Rd. near Bonito Lake was washed out. Storm cell was stationary over area for nearly one and a half hours before it dissipated. Rain gauges across the burn scar area reported rainfall amounts ranging from 0.70-1.50 during this time. A car was washed off the road in flooding location with one occupant needing rescue.

The body of an adult female was recovered from an arroyo on the south side of Santa Fe during the late evening hours. Additionally, one to two feet of water was reported on some roads on the south side of Santa Fe.  Rainfall reports ranged from 0.50-1.41. Dry arroyos and streams in the area ran deep and fast well into the evening as a result of runoff from the storm. Arroyos were reported to be filled with about 8 feet of fast-moving water at the peak of the flooding.
Peak wind gust of 61 mph was recorded from a 10-meter White Sands Missile Range mission support tower in extreme southern Socorro County.

Heavy rain caused a major mudslide/debris flow near Bobcat Pass on NM 38 north of Eagle Nest. Several vehicles were directly impacted as rocks and sediment were washed onto the road blocking both lanes of traffic. A snow plow was used to clear debris and the road was reopened about an hour later.

The Santa Fe New Mexican reported that Pecos Canyon was hit hard by flash flooding. The flooding apparently occurred in the canyon above Brush Ranch River Lodge on NM 63. Large boulders along with sludge and debris were carried down the canyon. The flooding apparently came down three different ravines that are in the area, over topped sandbags and left about 4-5 feet of muddy water on the property. The Tres Lagunas burn scar is also in this area and the debris that affected this property came from the burnt trees and sludge from the fire. Crews worked the following day to remove debris with heavy equipment.

A local news station reported that heavy rains Friday night caused part of U.S. 491 to collapse creating a sinkhole. The rain was reported to have damaged a culvert that ran underneath the roadway leading to the collapse. U.S. 491 was closed in both directions between Sheep Springs and Naschitti for several days after the event.
Heavy rain on Albuquerque's West-side led to street flooding with some vehicles partially submerged on the side of roads.

The Santa Fe New Mexican ran story about lightning hitting a large cottonwood tree in the Santa Fe Plaza. The bolt hit the tree and sent branches flying into a nearby crowd of people that were gathered in downtown for weekend festivities. Newspaper reporting that at least one man was injured from flying debris while another had breathing problems for a short time.

Power outages as well as flooding in the basement at Los Alamos National Labs were reported. An isolated strong cell formed over the area and stayed generally stationary for 2 hours. Rainfall amounts over 1.5 were recorded at sites across LANL.

Morning rainfall that ranged from 1 to nearly 3 in some areas around the burn scar caused heavy flows in creeks in the area which in turn deposited debris on roads. Roads were closed until the Department of Transportation could clear them.

Local media reported that Unser Rd. was closed between St. Josephs and Vista Oriente due to flooding. Rainfall amounts of over one inch in 20 minutes were reported in the area. Power was out for approximately 10,000 customers in association with this storm.
Double Eagle ASOS on Albuquerque's west side reported a high wind gust. A truck and trailer were blown over on Interstate 40 near this site during this time frame.

Patchy to severe blowing dust kicked up along U.S. 70 along the Curry County / Roosevelt County line just south of Clovis. Visibility was estimated at 1/4 mile. An outflow boundary from activity in Texas moved into the affected area and continued to move southwest. A single storm cell developed in the area as well as this boundary passed through.

A trained spotter in association with KRTN Radio in Raton reported and showed photos of flooding near Maxwell, NM. Over 3 was reported to have fallen in parts of town with drainages running full. Irrigation ponds north of town were also filled with up to 12 of standing water in nearby agricultural fields. No flooding issues were reported on major roadways, but local unpaved roads were turned into creeks along with the fields as water collected in low spots. An initial isolated cell developed over the location around 12:30pm and after that training cells went over the location for the next couple hours. By 5:00pm, flooding had occurred throughout the area.

Embudo Canyon weather station near Indian School and Tramway recorded gusts from 55-61 mph during the evening hours. Storms were in the vicinity of an outflow boundary that passed across the location 30 to 45 minutes before this gust was recorded.

Flooding occurred in Hail Canyon along Forest Road 141 on the northern periphery of the Whitewater-Baldy burn scar. Rainfall amounts ranging from 0.25 - 0.75 were reported across the entirety of the burn scar. Pictures showed significant amounts of large rocks and sediment were deposited on this road. Crews had to plow road before it was passable.
Photos of a small funnel cloud over the Grants area were received from the public.
Power lines downed in a couple areas from Juan Tabo and Candelaria to Wyoming and Lomas.
Quarter hail at Montgomery and Moon.
Nickel hail at Spain and Eubank.
Quarter hail near Spain and Eubank.
Quarter hail near Montgomery and Moon.
Nickel size hail at University and Strand Loop.

Gold Mine Road was flooded and impassable for nearly 200 yards near Cerrillos. Major torrents of water raging in San Marcos Arroyo between Eldorado and NM 14 near Cerrillos were captured by local residents, many of whom described it as a rare sight.

A major mudslide off the hill behind property ended up a couple feet deep on the deck and patio. Unpaved driveway completely destroyed by flood waters. The arroyo that crossed the property along NM 14 was at least 40 feet wide and 10 feet deep.

A couple of man hole covers were blown out of roadway from flash flooding around Spain and Eubank.  Widespread flooded roadways were reported within this area.  Small sink hole developed at the intersection of Copper and Juan Tabo.
Large amounts of landscape debris washed across Wyoming at Carmel blocking northbound lanes of traffic.
Three to four feet of water standing in parking lot at Home Depot.

Highway 111 washed away along Rio Vallecitos. Vehicles parked at Ojo Caliente Mineral Springs Resort & Spa were among the damages and mudslides were reported along the hillsides near the resort. The RV and camping area was closed due to flooding.

Portion of highway 554 washed away in El Rito.  A home along highway 554 was impacted by the flood waters with damage reported to the kitchen.  Local print media reported that the skirt of a mobile home was washed away and a propane tank floated several hundred feet away from the home.

Flash flooding was observed over several roadways in Santa Clara Canyon including 601 and 602. Flash flood wave made it to the NM 30 bridge with no damage apparent.  However, significant damage occurred to several reservation roads, culverts, diversion structures, and trees through the canyon.  A storage building was engulfed in several feet of mud.  The Santa Clara Pueblo received a Presidential Disaster Declaration for this event.
Rainfall rate of nearly 6 inches per hour over the Deer Pond gage produced 2.74 inches of rain in less than 30 minutes.  This heavy rainfall produced a nearly 10 foot flood wave on Santa Clara Creek.
Entire roof covering exterior garden department collapsed at the Kmart on Montgomery and Eubank due to heavy rainfall.
Two large trees blown down at the FAA Air Route Traffic Control Center.
Culvert on forest service 105 destroyed due to fast flowing water, mud, and debris.  60ft wide torrent of water, mud, and debris also impacted Elk Valley Estates however no structures were lost.

Damage survey was a classic dry microburst event.  Unfortunately,  there were no direct measurements of wind speeds but the toolkit conservatively estimated wind speeds of 60-70 mph, based on the type of power pole,  orientation, etc. The winds were from the north-northwest and may have been accelerated by the terrain along the immediate west slopes of the Sandias. The damage area was extremely small at 1/2km or less bounded by Tramway on the east,  Montgomery on the north,  Comanche on the south,  and extended maybe 1/4 mile west of Tramway.
Wind gust to 59mph reported 2 miles east of Stanley.
WSMR site Phillips Hill reported peak wind gust to 77mph.

A car traveling east bound on Interstate 40 three miles east of Moriarty at mile marker 199 with 4 occupants was struck by lightning. One child and one adult were injured and treated at the scene. Car's electronics were destroyed and vehicle towed from scene.
A large tree was destroyed by a lightning strikes along highway 47.
State road 55 was closed due to flooding between mile markers 95 and 97.

Bland and Peralta Canyons flooded across low water crossings and was described as a flash flood situation by Cochiti Pueblo emergency management. Water came up to Cochiti highway but did not top it. Bandelier National Monument also received flooding Thursday night into Friday morning with mud and debris being deposited across parking lots and bridges in the area. The Monument had to stay closed Friday due to continued clean up efforts.
NM 313 closed due to flooding from Tramway to the southern end of Bernalillo.

One home flooded in Bernalillo and 3 to 4 homes flooded in El Llanito.  Mud and debris from the flood waters significantly impacted the area and clean up cost thousands of dollars beyond damage to structures.

Drainage ditch along Carolina Drive breached creating widespread flooding in Bernalillo.  Several nearby homes reported major flooding inside with one home taking up to 5 feet of water.  Mud and debris from the flooding was widespread near the breach.  Several cars were also reported flooded in the area.  Significant damage was also reported at Sandia Pueblo due to a damaged drainage ditch.

Torrential rainfall reported within the area from Paseo del Norte and Wyoming south to around San Antonio and Louisiana.  2.54 inches of rain was reported at La Cueva high school and 3.24 inches was reported near San Francisco and San Antonio.  Fire department reported lots of roadways with flooding however no flash flooding was directly observed. The North Diversion Channel at the Alameda Bridge reported at top 10 flow of 7,120cfs.
Penny size hail at Montgomery and Wyoming.
One to 1.5 feet of water reported flowing over the curb tops down Montgomery at Wyoming.

Trained Spotter relayed video of flooding beneath a prominent underpass in north Raton. A woman drove her car with 2 children into water and became submerged and had to be rescued by officials. Water was reported to be 11-12ft deep. Flooding occurred in an underpass where 2nd St. in north Raton crosses the railroad tracks. Spotter reported a total rainfall amount of 1.47 inches with 1.22 inches with the initial burst and an inch of that falling in 30 minutes. Raton Creek was reported to be 7-8ft deep.
Dime to nickel size hail reported with storm.

Emergency Manager reported that culverts were blown out along Sulphur Springs drainage in the Thompson Ridge burn scar area. Roads were impassable, as there were 3-4 culverts along the Sulphur Springs drainage that go under a 1.5 lane road. The culverts had been getting clogged with debris with previous flood events and this event the water and debris took out the road.
Large tree limbs downed with strong wind at Matthew and Rio Grande Rds.
Trees were snapped and uprooted at Wilson Park.
Trees snapped and uprooted at Indian School and University.

Albuquerque ASOS recorded a historical 89mph wind gust. Sustained wind speed at the time was 64mph. HAM radio antennae at the WFO bent from winds. Widespread tree and structural damage along with flooding resulted in over 1 million dollars in damages.

Wind damage reported to several concession stands within the Isotopes Stadium. Crews were covered by tarp as they attempted to cover the baseball field before the rains hit. They didn't bring tarp out fast enough and the wind hit with the tarp covering some employees who took shelter in the dugout.
Two feet of water reported at the Albuquerque Zoo.
Large tree limbs downed at the Albuquerque Zoo.
Recorded at the I-40 RAWS site located in west/southwest Albuquerque.
Several large tree limbs down in the Summit Park neighborhood.
Several large trees down in the area around Randolph and Yale Rds.
Six inches of water reported in the basement of an apartment building near Lead and Broadway.

Several vehicles submerged on Central Avenue under the railroad tracks. AMAFCA noted that at one point the Broadway Pump Station did not activate. This may have been due to a power failure. This caused some flooding at Broadway and Lomas. That water flowed south and taxed the storm drainage network to the south. The South Broadway Detention Basin may have overtopped. At Tingley Park (which is a surge pond) the ring and cover was knocked loose by the water in the storm drain but it is unclear whether or not the Alcalde and Barelas Pump Stations then failed.
Interstate 25 northbound closed from Rio Bravo to Gibson due to downed power lines along highway.
Interstate 25 southbound from the I25/I40 interchange south to Gibson closed due to downed power lines.
Water up to the doors of vehicles on Alameda westbound from Rio Grande Rd. to Coors. Report of a truck stuck in the water.

Southbound Coors closed from Irving to Paseo del Norte, one car stuck in water. AMAFCA official reported that a small private pond adjacent to the shopping center parking lot at Coors and Paseo overtopped. From the air, it looked like water flowed across Coors and then across the off ramp from westbound Paseo, then next to the pond at the northeast corner of Paseo and Coors. Some water made it up the emergency spillway and ran into the pond and then into the Corrales Main Canal, causing large erosions in the area.

Emergency Manager as well as local media reported that the entire city of Corrales was flooded due to heavy rains. Several businesses were flooded as well as numerous cars and neighborhoods. Many roads were also washed out. Trees were downed due to the wind and many traffic lights were out. Rainfall reports of up to nearly 3 inches of rain were reported in association with this storm. Residents were still cleaning up the damage throughout the following weekend.
Emergency Manager reported water in homes in Meadow Lake.
Emergency Manager reported water in homes in Los Lunas area.
Emergency Manager reported water in two homes in Belen near State Roads 47 and 309.
Broadway Rd. was flooded with mud and debris over the road just north of the Interstate 25.  An estimated 4ft of mud and debris was reported at this location.
Photos received by local district ranger showed flooding across the Whitewater-Baldy burn scar in Deer Park, Little Whitewater, and Whitewater Creeks.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Downed power lines ignited a wildfire along highway 63 near the vacation community of Tres Lagunas.  The wildfire spread quickly to 7,395 acres in the last 2 days of May.
A downed power line along Sulphur Creek Road ignited a wildfire that spread east into the Valles Caldera National Preserve.  The fire burned 653 acres at the last day of May.
The metal roof of the Socorro County annex building was partially peeled off and significantly damaged.
Fast flowing water and rocks over Forest Service Road 107 beneath Washington canyon to the west of Bonito Lake.

Dry Cimarron Creek at Folsom became a raging torrent of water with flows out of bank into nearby trees and meadows.  Photos from one section of the creek showed a large waterfall scouring out the creek bed and nearby creek banks.
State highway 406 between mile marker 18 and 19 is impassible.
Penny size hail 20 miles northeast of Des Moines.
Nickel size hail 2 miles north northwest of Hayden.
Nickel size hail 7 miles south southwest of Yates.
Roads washed over and impassible below canyons in the Loma Grande subdivision.
High flows reported over several low water crossings beneath Bland and Peralta Canyons.
A funnel cloud developed just to the southwest of White Rock.  A photo taken by Karl Maness showed a well developed funnel as viewed from the LANL Emergency Operations Center.
Damage reported to several trees, some fence, and sections of Ridge Road near Travecere Road from flash flooding on nearby Travecere Creek.

NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET

events.event_narrative: Quarter size hail reported at Ponil Campground.
Nickel size hail in Sedan.
NWS employee reported large hail at Frost Rd. and Highway 14 in Sandia Park.
Route 246 around mile post 14, half dollar size hail fell from probably 345 to 4PM.
Highway 14 and Frost Rd. in near Sandia Park.

Law enforcement officials reported that roads were closed in Onava due to flooding. Reports from broadcast media also indicated that the Interstate 25 frontage road was washed over between the Las Vegas Airport and the Onava exit. Extensive damage also occurred to guardrails and a bridge located on CR-23. The flooding appeared to be the result of heavy rainfall that fell within the Pecos Arroyo farther upstream where the first flooding event occurred.
Car washed off Riley Rd. when an arroyo overflowed between Routes 55 and 542. Vehicle dangled over the edge of arroyo and almost fell into the arroyo. Driver escaped safely.
Vehicle stuck in water. Driver tried to cross flooded road or low water crossing on Spangler Rd. between Routes 55 and 542. Needed police assistance.
Observer reported 4.50 inches of rain 2 miles east of Lingo.
Observer reported 3.50 inches of rain 2 miles south of Lingo.
Spotter reported 3.10 inches of rain 6 miles southeast of Pep.
Spotter reported 5.10 inches of rainfall 7 miles south southeast of Pep.

Spotter one-half mile west of Luna reported intense heavy rainfall with ditches around home overflowing. Reported they were trapped at home and unable to use road to leave. Power outage also reported.
Tucucmari ASOS reported a 64 mph wind gust at 1645 followed by a peak wind gust of 70 mph at 1646.
A funnel cloud was reported just north of Bluewater Lake near Mt. Taylor in the vicinity of two merging thunderstorm cells.
A ranger at the El Malpais National Monument reported funnel clouds near La Ventana arch.
NM 117 was closed just north of the El Malpais Visitor Center due to flash flooding.
Two inches of rain was reported during the afternoon with an additional one inch of rain during the night.

Two inches of rain was reported with afternoon storms with an additional inch during the evening and overnight hours. Non-paved roads in the area were all undercut and washed out with large boulders blocking portions of the roads.
Nickel size hail at the Santa Fe Opera.

Flash flooding in Vigil Canyon near Alma was reported by two rangers that were trapped and nearly carried away by flood waters. Flood debris was reported 15 feet in depth within the canyon. Some elk fences were destroyed and several mobile home trailers were briefly endangered.
Spotter reported pea to quarter size hail.
Trained spotter estimated a wind gust of 60 mph.

NWS employee from neighboring office was hiking in the area and employees from the Philmont Scout Ranch reported hail the size of golfballs associated with this storm. Numerous tree branches downed across the ranch property.
Law Enforcement reported nickel size hail.
