events.event_narrative: Downed power lines ignited a wildfire along highway 63 near the vacation community of Tres Lagunas. The wildfire spread from 7,395 acres at the end of May to just under 10,300 acres by June 12th.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: Downed power lines ignited a wildfire along highway 63 near the vacation community of Tres Lagunas. The wildfire spread from 7,395 acres at the end of May to just under 10,300 acres by June 12th.
Golf ball size hail reported west of Pleasant Hill.
Quarter size hail reported in NE Clovis.
Half dollar size hail reported in NE Clovis.
Hail size ranged from slightly larger than pea size to quarters.
Ping pong ball size hail reported on the east side of Clovis.
Widespread quarter size hail reported over the entire east-side of Clovis.
Ping pong ball size hail reported in downtown Clovis.
Quarter size hail reported in SW Clovis.
Golf ball size hail reported in NE Clovis.
Hail ranged in size from ping pong ball size to hen egg size.
Spotter reported rotation with a brief funnel cloud.
Brief funnel cloud observed by a trained spotter.

A downed power line along Sulphur Creek Road ignited a wildfire that spread east into the Valles Caldera National Preserve. The fire grew from 653 acres at the end of May to 23,937 acres on June 23rd.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Downed power lines ignited a wildfire along highway 63 near the vacation community of Tres Lagunas. The wildfire spread from 7,395 acres at the end of May to just under 10,300 acres by June 12th.  The fire did not experience any further growth through early July before being declared 100% contained on July 5th.  Extensive efforts have been put forth to mitigate the impacts from monsoon flooding.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: Downed power lines ignited a wildfire along highway 63 near the vacation community of Tres Lagunas. The wildfire spread from 7,395 acres at the end of May to just under 10,300 acres by June 12th.  The fire did not experience any further growth through early July before being declared 100% contained on July 5th.  Extensive efforts have been put forth to mitigate the impacts from monsoon flooding.

A downed power line along Sulphur Creek Road ignited a wildfire that spread east into the Valles Caldera National Preserve. The fire grew from 653 acres at the end of May to 23,937 acres on June 23rd.  No additional fire growth was reported in early July before 100% containment was declared on July 11th. Significant efforts have been put forth to mitigate the impacts of monsoon flooding.

Dry microburst impacted portions of Albuquerque metropolitan area.  ASOS measured peak winds between 40 and 55mph. Power lines were reported damaged near the Albuquerque Metropolitan Detention Center.
Nickel size hail reported from off duty NWS employee on Highway 285.
Retired NWS Meteorologist reported several funnel clouds with a storm 5 miles northwest of Taos.
Runoff exceeding bank full in Hyer Draw. Water running out of arroyo and across low spots on the southeast corner of spotters 10 acre plot of land.
Flooded low water crossings resulting in road closures near intersection of NM 344 and NM 472.
Fort Sumner Airport reported 64 mph peak wind gust.

Several homes were damaged by flood waters in the Albuquerque South Valley. The heavy rain began during the evening hours around 830pm and continued until close to 1030pm with rainfall amounts ranging from 0.50 to nearly 2.70.  The Albuquerque Metro Area Flood Control Authority reported that Amole Dam retained an estimated 400 acre-feet of storm-water, which was the first time the dam had nearly filled since it was built in the early 1990s. The Amole Dam is 2000 feet long, 700 feet wide, and 33 feet deep.

A flash flood resulted in the closure of Martinez Road due to high water and debris.  A resident observed water and debris flowing over the road about 100 yards wide. Rainfall reports from this area were near one inch in less than an hour.

Off duty NWS employee reported while traveling in northeast NM. Met with a highway patrol supervisor who gave information on a flash flood event that did considerable damage to sections of SR 419 just north of Trementina.  NMDOT was in the process of replacing two bridges (1/8 mile apart) that span arroyos in this area and had temporary detours in place.   The water took out a total of three 7 foot culverts that had been in place for over a decade and a local rancher said the water was 7-8 feet deep.   It scoured the pavement.

Sabinoso experienced a highly intense rainfall event that caused severe damage to CR-55-A. Runoff severely eroded the roadway including the complete removal of the sub-base and base course materials.  Cutting of drainage ditches was severe and left deep crevasses along the edge of the driving lanes that created a severe safety issue for motor vehicles.
Flooding reported around Portales High School.  Numerous sandbags and resources deployed to prevent significant residential flooding.
Broadcast media partner relayed report of hail ranging in size from marble to golf ball in association with a passing storm near Moriarty.  One half an inch of rain was also reported.
Four to 5 feet of water flowed over a bridge on County Road 5, which is locally known as Superman Canyon Road.

Flooding damaged residence and dining halls at Red Rock Care Center.  The combination of heavy rain and hail created a water damming situation that resulted in roof leaks and eventual slight inundation of portions of the facility.
Six inches of water flooded the ground floor of the McKinley County Juvenile Detention Center.
An infant left inside a hot car for over 2 hours during the afternoon was left in critical condition due to the heat. Temperatures around the city were in the upper 90's to low 100's.

Dry microburst impacted portions of the Albuquerque Foothills near Tramway Boulevard and Comanche NE.  A total of seven high-tension power poles were downed within a very small area immediately west of Tramway Blvd.
Bursum Road closed from near Mogollon east about 10 miles due to debris and flooding over the roadway.
Barn flooded and damaged by running water on Brannan Road about 1 mile west of New Mexico Highway 217.
Flood waters estimated 6 to 7 feet deep in Bachelor Draw that crosses Dinkle Road about 3 miles west of NM 344. A couple vehicles were stranded.
Intersection of Dinkle Road and Sunset Boulevard washed out.

Runoff resulted in flash flooding along Whitewater Creek with a report of ���a roaring��� sound near the Deer Park drainage channel. Black and silty water was reported along with considerable debris across NM 174. Up to 14 inches of water was flowing over the highway at the upper crossing just downstream of the Catwalk.
Heavy rainfall lead to ponding of water 6 to 8 inches deep along Interstate 40 east and west bound near McCartys.  Numerous accidents were reported in the area.

Widespread flash flooding was observed in Farmington.  Numerous crashes and stalled vehicles were stranded in flood waters.  Several flooded and damaged drainage systems along Peace Valley Road, Hubbard Road, East Navajo Street, Main Street, Butler Street, Apache Street, and San Juan Boulevard caused widespread flooding of parking lots, low lying areas, homes and businesses.  Mud, rocks, and debris flows were reported at Webb Chevrolet, KFC, Si Senors, Taco Bell, and Park-n-Sell.
A 50-yard section of NM 36 was washed over and partially destroyed from several feet of water, rocks, mud, and debris.

Tropical funnel cloud touched ground for a couple minutes near Shiprock.  Location and time determined from radar imagery and photos sent from print media and a NWS family relative.  No damage reported.

The initial round of intense rainfall on the 10th and 11th flooded numerous roadways and homes then subsequent heavy rainfall through the 15th created extreme flooding. County emergency management indicated a total of at least 16 roads were washed out and damaged severely across the county, including NM 408 and CR 91 between Escondida and Lemitar, and NM 1 between San Antonio and Luis Lopez. The Rio Puerco and Rio Grande rivers both flooded into nearby low lying areas and threatened nearby communities. A breach in a levee on the Rio Puerco flooded several homes and the community of San Francisco was evacuated.  The US 380 bridge east of San Antonio was overtopped. US 60 was closed at mile marker 166.
Water flooded several homes near San Antonio.  Several roads around San Antonio were still under water as of noon on the 12th and then finally cleaned up by around 630 pm on the 12th.
Franklin Street flooded and closed due to high water.  Other streets in western Socorro also flooded out from heavy rainfall.
State EOC Situation Report #2 on the 11th detailed numerous dirt and gravel roads across Valencia County were impassible and sandbags were requested due to heavy rainfall on the 10th.
State EOC Situation Report #2 on the 11th indicated NM 118 was closed on the 10th due to flood waters, mud, and debris over roadway.

Law enforcement and emergency management reported major flooding along El Rito Creek and at Power Dam.  NM 91 was closed between mile markers 0 and 9.  The El Rito Creek South Bridge was nearly topped.  Large chunks of concrete from Power Dam were destroyed.  A railroad bridge over El Rito Creek was compromised and engineers closed rail traffic to assess the bridge.  Extensive damage was done to nearby Park Lake Trail.  A bridge carrying a water line to Puerto de Luna was extensively damaged.  Low lying areas near Brush Dam were flooded in Puerto de Luna.  Extensive road damaged has occurred to city and county roads.

State EOC Situation Report #2 reported Blue Hole Road closed due to flooding.  The Santa Rosa golf course and a pump house flooded with extensive damage.  Entire golf course was under water. Flooding was also reported near the KSRR transmitter.
NM 419 closed from mile markers 0 to 47 due to flooding of roadway.

Roads became impassible and a vehicle was stranded near a ranch.  A barn and nearby building were flooded.  Flash flooding turned into areal flooding as rain continued and water remained over roadways through the following morning.  Low lying areas throughout the area ended up flooded.

Heavy rainfall that produced flash flooding continued overnight resulting in further flooding of roadways and low lying areas near Estancia.  A barn, nearby building, and numerous roadways were impassable through the morning of the 12th.
State EOC Situation Report #2 on the 11th indicated numerous low water crossings were flooded across Roswell with minor flooding in the city.  Water levels began receding by the afternoon.
Three feet of standing water in Portales along 1st and 2nd Streets from Avenue C to K.
Numerous roads flooded in downtown Portales.
Portions of NM 246 washed out between mile markers 36 and 61.

The Rio Hondo at Diamond A Ranch experienced its 5th highest crest of 29,500 cfs around 4am on the 11th. This led to the 2nd highest crest at Roswell of 1,920 cfs around 815pm on the 12th.  The US 70 relief route southwest of Roswell was flooded by the Rio Hondo as a result.  Cars were stranded and water rescued took place.

Several vehicles rescued along US 70 relief route due to Rio Hondo flooding. Water rescue also occurred along NM 246 near Berrendo Creek.  River Road was closed along the Pecos River and a small neighborhood was evacuated with 3 houses flooded.  A Red Cross shelter was opened and 2 people stayed overnight.
NM 294 closed due to flooding.

NM 85 and 90 were initially flooded with 5,000 cfs flow through the area on the 12th then extremely heavy rainfall created severe flooding through the 13th.  Numerous roads were flooded and partially destroyed.  Kasha-Katuwe Tent Rocks National Monument was isolated.  Evacuations took place in Cochiti Pueblo.
Water over roadways and several bridges along NM 502 and 30.  One car was stuck in the water.
Mudslide reported along NM 502 at Totavi gas station.  Power lines also downed in the area. Significant flooding along NM 30.

Worst flash flood event ever recorded at Bandelier National Monument as the creek near the visitor center crested to 11 feet at 830am.  Several points of infrastructure were damaged.  The entrance road to the park was undermined and nearly destroyed.

Northern Boulevard and 10th washed out by nearby arroyo.  Southern washed over with significant amounts of water as well.  Damage to roadway occurred near Hondo Avenue.  Unser and 10th also washed out due to high water from arroyo. 12 families evacuated homes due to high water in nearby arroyo.  Heavy flows in these arroyos led to flooding downstream into the Harvey Jones Canal in Corrales where the Harvey Jones Bridge was overtopped.

The Jemez River was out of its banks along NM 4 near San Ysidro damaging a major fiber line and water supply infrastructure.  Several homes were flooded with up to 3 feet of water.  NM 4 was also damaged.

Pecos River out of its banks below Acme with near record crest.  The crest of 21,800 cfs at 815pm on the 12th was the 3rd highest crest ever observed dating back to 1954.  The river remained above flood stage for several hours and above action stage for several days.  Farmlands flooded.  Evacuations took place along River Road.  NM 249 closed around 924am on the 13th between mile markers 2 and 5 per NM DOT.  The Pecos River at Lake Arthur reached action stage for several hours with a peak flow of 11,781 cfs (17.85 feet) at 1115am on the 13th. The combination of heavy rainfall and high flows along the river continued near action stage flows through the 17th.  8 to 15 homes were reported damaged from flooding between Dexter and Lake Arthur.  Numerous roads closed into Dexter.
NM 434 was closed from mile markers 17 to 24 due to flooding over roadway.  NM EOC Situation Report #6 indicated severe flooding throughout the county with numerous county roads washed out.

Major flooding observed along Gallina Creek near Las Vegas.  Evacuations ordered for areas along the  river from Montezuma east to Las Vegas.  A major breach occurred on the Storrie Lake Diversion Channel.  An estimated one year supply of water storage was lost for drinking water due to the breach.  A Red Cross shelter was established at Robertson High School.  An elderly couple was rescued overnight by the National Guard from the Pine Camp area. NM 283 was closed west of Las Vegas.  A sink hole was reported near the South Diversion River Crossing Catwalk with damage to waste water components.  A couple of homes and numerous vehicles and roadways were damaged.  A bridge on CR-A1 near Sapello was closed due to high water.  A total of 1,040 structures were damaged in this multi-day event.
The Pecos River breached its banks in Pecos Canyon.  NM 63 north of Pecos was closed due to flooding. A small creek behind residences rose fast and forced evacuations of nearby residences.

State EOC Situation Report #6 indicated heavy rainfall produced flooding around many areas of Tohajiilee, including a school, homes, roads, and the fire department.  One lane of Interstate 40 was closed due to a sink hole at the Tohajiilee exit.  An ICP was set up to assist with flooding situation.
All roads washed out in the community of Sile.  Road in Elk Run Estates washed out near La Cueva.  100 residences in La Cueva reported loss of telephone service.

State EOC Situation Report #10 indicated that initial flooding over the area became severe as the San Francisco Dam spillway was compromised.  Water Tank Dam was full and clogged.  Many village roads were damaged.  Approximately 40 occupants were sheltered at the San Felipe Elementary School.
State EOC Situation Report #7 and NM DOT indicated NM 68 was closed due to rockslides and debris flow over the roadway.
Intense rainfall caused evacuations due to high water in Crownpoint.  Longer duration rainfall after this event lead to widespread areal flooding through the 14th.

State EOC Situation Report #10 indicated heavy rainfall and flooding continued through the night on the 14th.  30 to 40 families were evacuated around Crownpoint as dams protecting Smith Lake and Old PHS were at risk of being compromised.  A shelter was established.

Heavy rainfall over the Rio Bonito watershed led to a 23 feet rise in Bonito Lake.  The lake rose from 22 feet below the spillway to 8 inches over the spillway.  Emergency operations were in place due to significant concerns regarding a breach of the spillway.  No breach occurred.  Eagle Creek was out of banks and flooded a nearby playground along NM 48.
A creek overflowed its banks into nearby ranch buildings northeast of Pietown.

State EOC Situation Reports detailed that 40 families were evacuated from Highland Meadow neighborhood due to flooding. A culvert 25' wide by 10' deep was completely destroyed and National Guard assisted recovery effort using mobile bridge. Another 20 families affected.  A total of 7 structures were damaged in the mult-day event.
NM 412 closed between Prewitt and Bluewater Lake. Debris reported over NM 612.
US 491 closed between Twin Lakes and Naschitti due to flooding.  CR 5 bridge closed in Superman Canyon due to flooding from arroyo.

Areal flooding developed after flash flooding with continued heavy rainfall. Twenty five to 30 homes were partially under water around Bluewater Village.  Milan endangered by flooding with 4 residents displaced to shelter.  The Grants West Centurlink box was flooded and cell phone services were temporarily out in the area.  CR 23A closed due to high water.  A total of 50 structures were damaged from this multi-day event.

State EOC Situation Reports detailed flooding along the Gila River that caused closures of FR 614 into Lower Forks Campground and FR 528 into Grapevine Campground.  Additional long duration heavy rainfall in the area forced the Gila River to rise 15 feet near the Gila Cliff Dwelling Monument with significant flooding.  Access to the monument and visitor center was closed.  All campgrounds in the region were closed, including Lower and Upper Scorpion.
Flooding along Tularosa Creek and nearby arroyos lead to flooding on Tularosa River.
Numerous roads washed out across northeastern Catron County including York Ranch Road.

State EOC Situation Report #9 detailed that the San Francisco River breached its banks and levees at Reserve, Elm, and Glenwood.  Power outages occurred in the community of Wild Horse. 18 hunters were evacuated and another 18 hunters were stranded near the San Francisco River. An elk fence was washed away and nearby fields flooded at Alma.

Rapid water rise, 5 to 8 feet,  with debris in the Middle Fork Gila River near the Gila Cliff Dwellings Visitor Center.  Observer never witnessed anything like it and was concerned flood would wipe out USGS gauge.  Bridge did not get washed out.  Search and rescue efforts initiated for 2 stranded hikers.

Mineral Creek measured a peak flow of 868 cfs (4.39 feet) at 145am on the 15th which was 7 to 8 times higher than any other flow ever observed.  US 180 closed due to water from Mineral Creek flooding roadway.  NM 159 closed east of US 180 as well.  Water in several homes in Alma.

State EOC Situation Report #10 detailed catastrophic flooding in the Glenwood area. Whitewater Creek topped the US 180 bridge at Pleasanton. The San Francisco River at Glenwood rose to its 2nd highest crest ever observed at 29,900 cfs (18.7 feet) at 2am then fell sharply around sunrise.  A flash flood emergency was posted for Glenwood.  A levee at Circle Drive in Glenwood was breached flooding 16 residences with about 3 feet of water.  A large metal barn was moved into the river bed.

The Catwalk area northeast of Glenwood was completely destroyed.  Whitewater Creek at the Catwalk measured a peak flow of 16,100 cfs (19.07 feet) at 1115pm on the 14th which was 5 to 6 times higher than any other flow ever observed.  The suspended portion of the Catwalk area within the canyon was washed out.  A 30 feet section of a concrete girder bridge was destroyed.  The campground was completely covered in silt with minor damage.  Trails within the park were destroyed.

Portions of Bursum Road to the community of Mogollon was completely destroyed by flash flooding.  All homes and business along the creek in Mogollon were flooded and damaged, many severely.  Several vehicles were carried away, destroyed, and left in the bottom of the creek bed.  The USFS delivered MREs, water, and sanitary supplies to Mogollon by foot and with 2 mules.  An 83-year old Arizona man was found dead 8 miles downstream from where his vehicle was located and destroyed in Mineral Creek.
Water and debris flooding over Interstate 25 near Algodones.
Mud and water washed into several homes in San Felipe Pueblo.
One foot of mud and rocks covered portions of the San Felipe Casino gas station parking lot.  A 2 feet section of the lot west of the casino was undermined exposing a large conduit.

Water entered several business and homes in Bernalillo. Cars were stuck in water.  NM 313 was impassible between Bernalillo and Tramway Road due to water and mud over highway.  All Sandia Pueblo holding ponds and the Bernalillo Canal were at capacity.  A water line break created a sink hole in a subdivision in Bernalillo.

Widespead heavy rainfall and flooding around Santa Rosa led to a near record crest on the Pecos River at Puerto de Luna.  The crest peaked at 35,800 cfs at 615pm on the 11th, which is the 2nd highest crest ever observed going back to 1942.  The gauge was above flood stage for several hours.

Widespread heavy rainfall led to a near record crest on the Rio Puerco at Bernardo.  The peak flow of 7,120 cfs at 1130pm on the 15th was the second highest crest ever observed dating back to 1941.  The river was above action stage for several days and was above flood stage between 7pm on the 15th and 10am on the 16th.  Flooding occurred areas along the river.  The Rio Grande at Acacia reported a 9,000 cfs at 130pm on the 16th, which was the highest crest ever observed.

The Galisteo Creek below Galisteo Dam measured its highest crest on record dating back to 1971.  The gage was above action stage between 9pm on the 15th and 3pm on the 16th with a record peak crest of 2,850 cfs.  Low lying areas along the creek were flooded.  NM 22 and Pueblo Route 85 were closed due to flooded arroyo over roadways.

Water flowing over NM 30 around mile marker 7.  Thirteen homes were flooded in Santa Clara Pueblo including a health center.  Flooding debris reported over numerous roads in the pueblo.  A public walk way and skate park damaged due to erosion.  A total of 79 structures were damaged in this multi-day event.
US 380 was closed between San Antonio and Carrizozo due to flooding.  A levee broke leading to heavy erosion along the roadway.  NM 1 was also closed between mile markers 21 and 22 due to a wash out.
Flash flood crest in the Rio Felix overtopped the Y.O. Crossing Road bridge.

Flows on the Rio Felix at the Old Highway Bridge near Hagerman indicated that flooding from the upstream area around Y.O. Crossing Road resulted in flooding in the area for at least two days after the heavy rain had ended.
The Gallinas River at Colonias was above action stage for several days and above flood stage between 330am and 1130am on the 17th.  Low lying areas around the river were flooded.

The Gallinas River at Colonias was above action stage for several days and above flood stage between 330am and 1130am on the 17th.  This flood wave surged downstream from Colonias toward Santa Rosa Lake.  Low lying areas around the river were flooded.
A mud slide up to 3 feet deep flowed into yards, homes, and a street near the Petroglyph National Monument Open Space.

State EOC Situation Report #9 indicated that N 562 Road in Fruitland was completely undermined and affected nearly 300 residences.  Area completely isolated.  A 72 inch pipe was damaged by flood water.  N 36 highway also damaged.
Numerous reports of roads flooded, washed out, and damaged along the Socorro County stretch of U.S. 380.  Emergency Manager indicated cost of damage was near 1.2 million dollars.
Numerous reports of roads flooded, washed out, and damaged in eastern portion of Socorro County.  Emergency Manager indicated cost of damage was near 1.2 million dollars.

State EOC Situation Report #12 indicated 10 businesses were flooded in Madrid.  Most significant damage done to Mine Shaft Tavern and nearby museums.  Mud and coal damage to most structures.  Gold Mine Road, Rogersville Road, and Puebla Road 76 were cleared of flooding debris.
US 84 closed due to flash flooding between mile markers 197 and 204.

Local broadcast media reported a home flooded near Chamita.  Emergency management reported that a half dozen homes were filling up with water near US 84/285 due to flooding from the Rio Chama.  A shelter was set up in Espanola.
NM 247 closed between mile markers 0 and 48 due to flooding.
Large hail reported to have caused damage to a vehicle at Napi Headquarters south of Farmington.  A funnel cloud and brief tornado also reported.
Video sent in from observer showed a well-defined gustnado that briefly spun up into a landspout tornado for a few minutes.
County EM relayed report of funnel cloud near Fort Stanton.
Nickel size hail reported at the Raton Fire Department between 1250pm and 1259pm.
Funnel cloud spotted by truck driver on Interstate 25.
Hail covered NM 197 three to six inches deep.
Broken tree limbs up to 4 inches in diameter.
Family relative reported transformer blew out and power line down.  Wind blew over grill.

A bridge was washed away northeast of Maxwell near county road A-7 with severe bank erosion along the Canadian River. Dry showers produced intense wind gusts up to 67 mph and blowing dust.
Dry showers produced intense wind gusts up to 67 mph.  Blowing dust reduced the visibility down to 2 miles.
Large 2 ft diameter tree blown over with frontal passage around 830pm local time very close to emergency managers home near San Antonio. Damage estimate for tree removal.
Strong wind gust reported with near whiteout conditions in snow as back door cold front moved through Texico.
Nickel size hail reported.
Visibilities were also reported at 1.75 SM in blowing dust.
Transwestern Pump.

events.event_narrative: A CWOP station in Quemado recorded sustained winds in the mid to upper 30's and a peak gust up to 58 mph during the afternoon hours.
A Mesonet site located northeast of Carrizozo recorded sustained winds in the lower to mid 40's with a peak gust up to 63 mph during the afternoon hours.
The Sierra Blanca AWOS recorded sustained wind speeds from 40-45 mph with gusts up to 64 mph during the afternoon hours.
The Dunken RAWS recorded a high sustained wind speed to 41 mph with gusts in the low to mid 50's during the afternoon hours.
Twitter report from KOB 4 meteorologist relaying public report that high winds had knocked down a dead tree that hit a passing van. Winds speeds estimated sustained 40 gusting to low 60's.
The Harry Mesonet at White Sands Missile Range recorded sustained wind speeds ranging from 40 - 44 mph with gusts up to 60 mph during the afternoon hours.
The Oscura Range Camp Mesonet at White Sands Missile Range recorded sustained wind speeds in the low 40's with gusts into the mid 50's.
A trained spotter reported a peak wind gust to 58 mph with some Virga in the area.
The Sulf Mesonet at White Sands Missile Range recorded sustained wind speeds ranging from 40 - 42 mph with gusts up to 60 mph.
The CSBF Transwestern Pump recorded a peak gust to 59 mph.
The Pole 616 Mesonet at White Sands Missile Range recorded sustained wind speeds in the low 40's with a peak gust to 61 mph.
The Belen AWOS recorded a high sustained wind speed up to 43 mph with gusts in the low 50's.
A CWOP station recorded a peak gust to 62 mph.
Local news station reporting tree downed by high winds in the parking lot at Alameda and Coors.

Local news media station reported on a cinder block wall at a church that got knocked over during the high wind event. The Albuquerque ASOS recorded sustained wind speeds ranging from 40 - 44 mph with a peak gust to 58 mph during this time.
The Clines Corners ASOS recorded sustained speeds in the low 40's with a peak gust to 62 mph.
The Las Vegas ASOS recorded a peak gust to 66 mph.
The Los Alamos AWOS recorded a peak gust to 59 mph.
Based off the graph produced by the Magdalena Ridge Observatory a peak gust to 110 mph was recorded.
The Fort Sumner Airport recorded a peak gust to 64 mph.
The Tucumcari ASOS recorded a peak gust to 58 mph.
Gust to 59mph reported at Clayton.
Melrose Range.
Clines Corners reported sustained winds between 41 and 44 mph for several hours and a peak wind of 63 mph.
Cannon.
Four west southwest of Tucumcari at Union Pacific Rail site.
Gust to 58 mph east southeast of Placitas.
Media reported large concrete wall toppled at church near Iliff and Artrisco.  Time and damage estimated.
The Moriarty AWOS hit 43 mph sustained during the early morning hours.

events.event_narrative: The Angel Fire AWOS hit 46 mph sustained with a peak gust to 58 mph during the early morning hours.
The Clayton ASOS hit 44 mph sustained wind speed with gusts into the low 50's.
A CWOP site located in Chaves County recorded sustained wind speeds ranging from 40 to 51 mph with gusts up to 68 mph.
The Clovis Airport AWOS recorded sustained wind speeds ranging from 40 to 47 mph with a peak gust up to 58 mph.
The CWOP station located in Milagro recorded a peak gust up to 60 mph.
The DORA Mesonet recorded high sustained wind speeds up to 40 mph with a peak gust up to 61 mph.
The Clines Corners ASOS recorded high sustained wind speeds ranging from 40 to 47 mph with a peak gust up to 66 mph.
The ASOS at Cannon AFB recorded sustained wind speeds up to 41 mph with a peak gust up to 61 mph.
The CSBF Transwestern Pump Mesonet site recorded a peak gust to 62 mph.
The Fort Sumner Airport recorded a peak gust to 66 mph.
The Tucumcari ASOS recorded high sustained wind speeds ranging from 40 to 44 mph with a peak gust up to 58 mph.
The K4MR AWOS at Melrose Gunnery Range recorded a peak gust up to 63 mph.
The CWOP site located in Milnesand recorded a peak gust up to 58 mph.
Phillips Hill.
Rerported from Las Vegas Optic indicated that part of a roof was torn off the Recreation Center in Las Vegas.  Wind gust at airport peaked at 67 pm at 214pm.
Both Harry and Stallion sites on White Sands Missile Range reported strong winds sustained near 42 mph with gusts to 58 mph.
Clines Corners peak winds likely exacerbated by some virga in the area.
Moriarty airport.  Peak winds exacerbated by virga in the area.
Sierra Blanca airport reported sustained winds of 54 mph with gusts to 67 mph ahead of cold frontal passage.
Peak wind gust due to intense convective virga shower along cold frontal boundary.
Peak wind gust due to intense convective virga shower along cold frontal boundary.
Sandia tram 61 mph around noon.  Many public reports including Tijeras and Chilili of strong winds in the 50 to 55 mph range throughout the day.
Both the Sierra Blanca airport and the Smokey Bear fire site reported peak winds up to 67 mph throughout the day.
White Sands observing sites at Stallion and Sulf reported peak winds between 61 and 62 mph.
White Sands observing sites at Phillips Hill reported 62 mph and Carrizozo weather net reported 60 mph.
Columbia Scientific instrument north northeast of Encinoso.
Pedernal estimated peak wind gust to 60 mph with some light damage to tree limbs.
Phillips Hill reported numerous gusts over 58 mph with a peak at 63 mph.

events.event_narrative: Multiple sources including Coop observers and SNOTEL sites recorded snowfall amounts ranging from 3 to 8 inches across the area.
A CoCoRaHS observer reported a snowfall amount up to 8 inches.
Travel Center.
Hail up to the size of quarters accumulated to a depth of at least 6 inches Interstate 25 resulting in at least 4 traffic accidents.
Pea to quarter size hail covered the ground.  Most hailstones were the size of a dime or penny and damage to vegetation was reported.
Anemometer on Ute Lake reported 64mph wind gust.  Report relayed via HAM radio dispatcher.
Spotter estimated 60 to 70mph wind gusts with hail and heavy rain.
Numerous reports of pea to nickel sized hail around San Jon.
Clayton.
Bottomless Lake State Park estimated wind gusts between 50 and 60mph as storm passed with pea size hail.
A 3 foot diameter tree was felled and resulted in damagd to a nearby automobile and powerlines.  No injuries were reported.

Alamogordo Creek flowed out of its banks at NM 156 with water and debris reported over the road. An Interstate 40 frontage road was closed between mile markers 311 and 321 due to flooding and high water.
Albuquerque Sunport.  Numerous reports of pea to dime size hail were also reported with this storm across the metro area.
Dime size hail accumulated 4 to 5 inches along Interstate 40 near Wagon Wheel causing significant impact to travelers.
Dunken.
Damage reported to cars and numerous windows shattered in area homes and businesses in Capitan.
Along Highway 84 near I-40 west of Santa Rosa.
A 10 inch diameter tree was snapped in half from estimated 70 to 80 mph winds.
Major street flooding was reported in Roswell.  Flood waters were up to automobile doors.  The Rio Hondo was nearly out of its banks at Sunset Avenue in Roswell.
Police and Fire Departments closed numerous roads in Roswell.

Water rescues took place in Roswell due to torrential rain and flash flooding. The Urton Bridge was washed out for the 2nd time in as many years.  The Roswell Regional Airport was inaccessible for several hours due to high water.  Several residences in Roswell required sandbags.
One mile north of Mesa.
Quarter size hail covering the ground just north of Folsom.
Reports included an overturned semi-trailer truck, downed radio tower and near complete destruction of a barn-like structure.
The CQC ASOS at Clines Corners recorded a peak wind gust to 63 MPH.
The ASOS at the Raton Crews Airport recorded a non-thunderstorm wind gust to 58 mph.
Quarter to penny size hail reported by trained spotter.
Large hail resulted in broken windows and car damage. Report received via Twitter.
A CWOP station northwest of Sumner Lake recorded a 59mph thunderstorm wind gust.
Spotter recorded a gust to 59 mph with a nearby thunderstorm. Wall cloud was also observed.
The Tucumcari ASOS recorded a 63 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
NWS employee storm chasing observed 2 inch diameter hail (hen egg size).
The ASOS located at the Cannon AFB recorded a wind gust to 79 mph. During this same time a tornado was reported in the same area. Gust is a result of thunderstorm wind/tornado winds.

Spotter observed intense hail for about 20 minutes with the largest hail up to a quarter. The majority was marble to pea size. After initial hail burst there was a mix of rain and hail with over half an inch or rain recorded.

School net site recorded a wind gust to 61 mph in association with a severe storm in the area. The same storm produced a tornado so the wind gust could have been either a thunderstorm gust or directly associated with the nearby tornado.

An estimated thunderstorm wind gust to 70 mph was reported by a trained spotter. Gusts near and higher then this had been recorded by NWS equipment 10 minutes earlier. There was a tornado in progress at this time.
Observer noted significant swirling dust and 1.25 inch hail.
Golfball sized hail mixed with nickel and quarter sized hail.
High winds from a thunderstorm bent over some trees.
Storm chasers video feed showed funnel cloud development 20 miles west of Grenville.
Storm chaser reported funnel cloud near Pasamonte.
Spotter observed funnel cloud.
A spotter positioned northwest of Ranchvale at Curry Road 22 and Highway 277 observed a funnel cloud to his southeast over Ranchvale.  Also reported 1.75 inch hail.
Emergency Manager relayed message from fire chief's son that a funnel cloud was observed near Portales.
Spotter reported 4 feet of standing water over highway 402 15 miles north of Nara Visa that made road impassable.
Trained spotter reported downed telephone pole from thunderstorm wind gusts estimated at 60mph or greater.

events.event_narrative: Storm Chaser reported finding dime to nickel size hail on the ground in Estancia.
Hail observed along Interstate 40.

Lots of reports of hail damage across the village of Corona. Numerous homes observed window, skylight, siding, and vehicle damage. Damage primarily occurred on north side of structures. Some livestock was also killed, including four chickens. Most impressive was an almost perfectly circular hole in the back pane of a home window. Back windshield of an Acura was completely shattered out. Most residents confirmed average stone size was around golf ball with larger stones of 2 to 2.75 inches in diameter.
Damage to roofs and windows and windshields and vehicles.
Hail covered the ground.

Numerous reports of hail damage just north of Pecos from significant hailstones up to hen egg size in diameter. Several homes sustained window, skylight, and roof damage, including dents to a metal roof, as well as substantial damage to at least three vehicles.
Ponderosa trees were leaning 20 degrees off center.
Golf ball or larger hail killed a cow near Highway 209 and CR21.

Tweet from STORMTRACK7, and received picture of hail with measurement.  The Agricultural Science Center for NMSU at Clovis suffered catastrophic damage to crops, vehicles, and the facility.  Windows were also broken out of a nearby home.
Second night in a row of highway flooding on highway 402 between Amistad and Nara Visa near mile marker 22 due to heavy rain from thunderstorms.
Report of funnel cloud 10 miles northwest of Corona within a rotating wall cloud.
Outflow winds from a virga shower blew over a semi-trailer truck along Interstate 25 in Los Lunas.  A small hay shed also collapsed and the sheet metal roofing blew up to 200 yards away.
Highway 248 closed due to flooding from mile marker 0 to 5.  Road remained closed beyond causative event until early in the morning on the 10th.
Meteorologist reported a supercell thunderstorm producing a tornado for 10 minutes 2 miles northwest of Dorsey Mansion State Monument.  No damage was reported.

Supercell thunderstorm spawned a tornado that touched down near Ranchvale.  NWS survey revealed the tornado occurred in an open field.  Eyewitness accounts disclosed the tornado was short-lived and narrow.
Spotter observed funnel cloud near Sedan with significant rotation in thunderstorm structure.
Spotter reported funnel cloud briefly touched ground for about 1 minute then retreated quickly back into storm 11 miles northwest of Sedan.
Supercell thunderstorm produced brief tornado touchdown with swirling dust for about 1 minute just west of Corona.

Supercell thunderstorm that produced brief tornado west of Corona a short time earlier cycled another tornado to the ground for about 2 minutes over open rangeland.  A storm survey for this storm proved difficult due to the inaccessibility of private land.  Any damage would have most likely been sustained to scrub brush and juniper trees.
Six inches of hail on Interstate 25 caused a semi-trailer truck to jack knife.  Plows were dispatched.
Chaser reported tornado on the ground for 10 minutes.  No damage was reported.

Supercell thunderstorm near Encinoso spawned a tornado along Highway 246 at Richardson Canyon Road.  The tornado traveled east-southeast down Richardson Canyon Road, snapping off the tops of trees and breaking numerous branches of Ponderosa pine. The tornado intensified as it approached 2 homes.  A single wide mobile home from the 1970s was completely destroyed as the undercarriage was moved about 20 feet and all walls separated and tossed. A double wide mobile home was tossed into a barn and destroyed.  Portions of the roof were blown 250 yards away.  At least two other homes as well as a barn and shed sustained damage.
Half dollar size hail with lots of quarter size hail as well.
In association with tornado.
Funnel cloud reported between Springer and Maxwell.
Large hail broke windows.
Nickel to quarter size hail covered the ground on Interstate 25 near Raton.
Hen egg size hail reported on US Highway 285.
Hail covered ground near Fox road and SR2.
Golfball hail covered the ground.
Pea to quarter size hail.
Supercell thunderstorm spawned a brief tornado that crossed Interstate 25 near mile marker 375.  No damage was reported.
Southern edge of multi-cellular thunderstorm complex produced a brief landspout tornado with a brown dust swirl.  No damage reported.
Motorists along Interstate 25 near Maxwell reported to the Raton police dispatch that a brief tornado touched down near the highway.  No damage reported.
House Schoolnet.
Peak gust to 60 mph with dime size hail reported in Tucumcari.
Tucumcari ASOS reported peak wind of 63mph followed by a 70mph gust a few minutes later.  No damage reported.
Amarillo NWS relayed spotter report of 60mph wind gust along Interstate 40 near Glenrio.
Cannon Air Force Base.
Ranchvale elementary schoolnet.

Multiple local news outlets reported that a wedding tent collapsed due to high winds injuring guests. The winds were outflow winds from a storm to the north of the location. Gusts estimated to be 60 + mph. The tent was a 40x80 ft tent which collapsed onto a wedding reception party during dinner service. Two women were taken to the hospital for non-life threatening injuries while 6 others sustained minor injuries.

Large outdoor event tent was toppled and destroyed at the Albuquerque Folk Festival being held at the Albuquerque Balloon Museum. There is a video of the incident on Youtube. Winds are thought to be the outflow from a storm to the north. Winds at the Albuquerque Sunport gusted to 52mph, thought to be at least 60+ where this event happened. No injuries reported.
Numerous hail stones between quarter and half dollar size indicated in photo by storm chaser.
Sierra Blanca Regional Airport.
Gallup.
Gallup.
Stanley.
Sevilleta.
Clines Corners.
Clines Corners.
Dime to quarter size hail for 12 minutes 6 miles east of Rogers.  Hail covered the ground.
Dime to quarter size hail northeast of Portales.
Ping pong to golf ball size hail along Highway 70 southeast of Clovis.
Landspout tornado just north of Interstate 40 near Moriarty on the ground for approximately 10 minutes.  No damage reported.
State police reported quarter size hail on Highway 219 south of Interstate 40.
Sumner Lake.
Near Folsom.
Quarter size hail up to 2 inches deep at State Road 551 and 456 to the northeast of Folsom.
Maxwell.
Romeroville.
Penny size hail covered ground about 1 inch deep.
Lincoln.
Lincoln.
Raton southeast side.
Cannon.
Incident management reported 14,712 acres consumed in the Chuska Mountains to the east of Crystal, New Mexico. At least 24 structures and 4 outbuildings were destroyed.
The ASOS at Clines Corners recorded gusts ranging from 49 to 58 mph during the late morning hours into the afternoon of June 27, 2014.
Semi-trailer truck blown over on Interstate 40 near Atrisco Vista from microburst wind.
Penny size hail and heavy rainfall.  Minor flooding in area arroyos.
Nickel size hail Blueberry Hill.

The City of Clovis has 3 detention ponds that are located in the upper portions of 3 small north-south oriented watersheds on the north side of the city. During Wednesday's event, the heaviest rain was anchored over and just upstream of the 3 ponds and, as a result, they quickly filled and began to spill. A lifetime resident of Clovis said it was the first time in at least 10 years that all three ponds filled, and it was the first time in recent memory that the Dennis Chavez pond spilled. The police and fire departments received about 120 calls in one hour between 6:45am and 7:45 of stalled vehicles and at least 3 vehicles that were completely submerged. Police responded to 8 water rescues from vehicles. One vehicle along 14th street was submerged in 8 feet of water. Fortunately, no injuries or major damage.  The owner of Enchanted Spirits Studios noted that up to 1 inch of water entered the business causing some carpet damage.  Fire Station #6 and one house near Dennis Chavez park (pond) were the only structures that had damage from high water and the damage estimate there was $250,000. Flooding was also reported around Green Acres Park.  Water receded very slowly through the day well after rainfall had ended.

The supercell thunderstorm that produced the tornado near Ranchvale lifted but a powerful rear flank downdraft resulted in damaging straight line winds across Clovis.  A tree was blown onto a residence at 121 East Tierra Blanca Road causing a house fire. The roof was blown off Ellison's Barber shop on the northwest corner of 21st and Thorton.
Supercell thunderstorm produced a brief gustnado along a shelf cloud advancing through Clovis.  No damage reported.
Roof blown off a house near Highway 208 and CR21.
Numerous trees blown down in Ned Houk Memorial Park.
Diego fire destroyed 4 minor structure and damaged one.  Total acres burned was near 3626.  No information was available on the structural damages.
One foot of water with mud and debris over Highway 4.
Quarters hail.
Wall of water 4.5 feet surged down Frijoles Canyon within Bandelier.

Several drainages flooded within the Paliza area of the Jemez Mountains. Water flooded Forest Road 266 before Forest Road 10 in two places. A fire engine working a wildfire in the area was trapped due to the above mentioned flooded roads, personnel had to wait out the storm.

Highway 550 and Highway 537 were impacted and the Fire Chief reported 1.5 to 2 of rain to the local Emergency Manager. There was some damage to county roads with strong flows in the arroyos. Two feet of standing water was observed on the asphalt of roads in some locations. However, no roads were closed and all debris was cleared by the following day.

Water damage was reported to the roof on two homes from heavy rain on the southern edge of town. Water ran through a couple homes and was running over dirt roads along northern portions of the area. No major damage reported from road flooding.

Local news reporting that flood waters washed away a main road on the Santo Domingo Pueblo leading to Sile. The rushing flood waters crushed the metal culverts meant to transport water underneath the roadway.
The WSMR Mesonet site located at Oscura Range Camp recorded a gust to 58 mph during the afternoon as strong thunderstorms moved through the area.
The WSMR Mesonet site located at Phillips Hill recorded a peak gust to 67 mph during the late afternoon as strong thunderstorms moved through the area.
The ABQ ASOS recorded a wind gust to 58 mph as outflow from thunderstorms to the south reached the area.
Diego fire destroyed 4 minor structure and damaged one. Total acres burned was near 3626. No information was available on the structures that were burned.
Exceptionally heavy rainfall report of 4.88 inches northwest of Espanola.
Roadway within Peralta Canyon was washed out and recently built culverts were destroyed.
Considerable debris and logs were washed down a hillside onto Highway 37.  No damage occurred to the roadway but created a significant mess and forced a temporary road closure.
Quarter size hail.
Severe winds with pea size hail and heavy downpour.  No damaged observed.
Large hail dented car on Highway 550 in Cuba.

Torrential rainfall produced significant flooding in Espanola during the overnight on the 14-15th.  The NM Emergency Operations Center and local broadcast media reported at least 8 homes suffered flood damage with numerous vehicles abandoned and flooded. At least 4 residents reported 12 to 18 inches of standing water on their properties.  North Railroad Ave and Hunter were flooded forcing city officials to run pumps to remove water. East Laguna Street around Santa Claran Casino was flooded.  Santa Clara Pueblo was also flooded during this event.
Leaves shredded off Aspen trees around Chama.

Emergency management reported 3 people were rescued from 2 vehicles in an arroyo in La Puebla.  Local broadcast media reported just down the road that a clogged culvert around the Estrella del Norte Vineyard created a flood of water, mud, and debris through the winery.  No major damage was reported to structures.

A clogged culvert led to a surge of flood waters through the Pojoaque Terrace Mobile Estates. Several homes were washed off their foundations.  A gas line break during the flood prompted the evacuation off all 60 homes.  A total of 23 units were damaged.
A water rescue occurred in El Rancho from flash flooding.
Twenty minutes of intense rainfall followed by 4 hours of moderate rainfall caused wash out of County Road 155.  A culvert beneath the road could not hold all the water and breached the roadway.
Washington impassible near Arturo Park due to strong flow over roadway.
Intersection closed at Indian School and Carlisle likely due to combination of heavy rainfall over an existing water main excavation.
Several new homes in Mesa del Sol with several inches of water inside.  Many yards with up to 6 inches of standing water.

Local media reported a vehicle that was washed off the road due to heavy rains in Rio Rancho on Northern Blvd. near 10th street. The young driver attempted to pass through fast-moving water during the early morning hours of the 15th and the vehicle was swept off the road and buried up to its wheels in mud. The road also sustained damage due to the undercutting of the water. Large chunks of asphalt were chipped off. Rain began in the area just before 10pm and did not stop until close to 7 am the following morning. Mostly light stratiform rain continued over the area with embedded heavy cells. KABX storm total precipitation estimated ranged from 2.5 to 3.2 inches.
Hail ranging from nickel to quarter size was reported on Highway 246 by a storm chaser.
The CSBF Transwestern Pump recorded a gust to 76 mph from a massive storm moving to the south.

A major footbridge was reported to have washed away on the Owl Peak Farm in La Madera. Both the Rio Ojo Caliente and the Tusas River rose to flood levels. The Rio Ojo Caliente showed a river rise from 6 cfs to 1120 cfs.

Two lightning bolts just a few seconds apart made direct hits  to the TravelCenters of America just after midnight on July 16th. The strikes caused a power surge which fried circuitry and temporarily knocked 17 fuel pumps out of service. The pumps were not restored to service until the late afternoon during that day as electricians worked to repair the damage caused by the strikes.
Intense rainfall caused a mudslide over Volcano Rd. at the Capulin Volcano National Monument. The road was closed the following day for debris removal.
NWS employee reported 1.0 inch hail on State Rd. 54 southwest of Pastura.
A large tree was blown over onto the roadway near Lake Van east of Dexter.
A large tree was blown over onto a pick-up truck east of Dexter.
A large carport collapsed onto 2 vehicles at the U.S. Wildlife fish hatchery near Dexter.
Six feet of water was reported to be flowing through the channel and over a footbridge at Bandelier National Monument. The water was out of its banks but not all the way to the parking area.
Emergency Manager reported  dangerous flows overtopped the intersection of Indian Service Route 601 and 602 on Santa Clara Pueblo. Access to the creek was blocked by authorities.
State police dispatcher reported that she received 3.05 inches of rain at her residence during the overnight hours.
Three pine trees were toppled by gusty canyon winds near San Antonio and Interstate 25.  No damage reported.

Rapid runoff from an estimated 2 to 4 inch downpour resulted in a breached levee that flooded several homes across from the Algodones fire station.  The fire department was pumping water away from Highway 313.  Water was still being pumped out of 2 homes the following morning.
Torrential rainfall dumped 3.99 inches at the Raton Crews Airport.  This was the 2nd highest 24-hour precipitation total reported at the Raton Crews Airport dating back to 1941.
Torrential rainfall produced 4.91 inches at Mosquero.
Torrential rainfall produced 4.38 inches at Mosquero.  This was the 2nd highest 24-hour precipitation total reported at Mosquero dating back to 1926.
Flash Flooding on State Highway 56 and 412 at mile markers 10 and 12.

Five to 6 feet of water from the Alamogordo Creek drainage over Highway 156. Pavement was stripped. Half a mile of fence line was tore out due to the flooding. A bunkhouse located near the water crossing took on water damage and water filled up the basement. Two water retention ponds were over-topped. Part of the Pacific Railroad tracks were left dangling because the base was washed out from the heavy rains.
Heavy rains washed out 2 roads near Navajo Dam.
Water from the Alamogordo Creeek drainage between 3 and 4 feet deep over Highway 84. Around 300 yards wide. Highway shut down by State Police.

Local broadcast media reported flooding of the Vietnam Veterans Memorial Park. Softball  players showed up to play only to find the softball fields completely underwater. Standing water was estimated at least 4 feet deep in areas.
Local broadcast media relayed a photo of a funnel cloud near Bernal.
Local media reported water up to the body frames of vehicles with multiple feet of water at 98th Street and Dennis Chavez.

Local media reported multiple feet of standing water at the intersection of Coors and Barcelona. A business owner near this intersection indicated that fast moving water ripped off a retaining berm near his business.
A mobile home was flipped and subsequently destroyed due to strong winds from a passing severe thunderstorm.
Reports of 2.5 inches of rain in just 16 minutes from severe storm in the area.
New Mexico DOT reported an overnight deluge caused ballasts under portions of the Rail Runner line within Waldo Canyon to wash out.  Service was suspended for the entire day on Saturday for repairs.
New Mexico DOT reported NM75 closed from Dixon to Penasco due to flooding.

Three cars were abandoned in 9 feet of flood water at Central Ave and the 1st Street bridge.  Drivers were rescued and swam to safety. Flood water were reported flowing through the Q Burger restaurant at 3rd and Central.  The torrent of water toppled a tree at Coal and Walter.  Four other vehicles were abandoned in flood waters at Lomas and Broadway.  A photo posted from local media showed the Vietnam Memorial park completely inundated with flood water.  A local school also reported water inside the facility.  A large sink hole developed at the intersection of MLKJ and Broadway.  The entire intersection was destroyed.  Several underground parking garages around the Convention Center were inundated with water several feet deep.
Mudslide along the access road to Interstate 25 near Mountain Rd.  Damage estimated for landscaping property loss.

Video posted to Twitter showed a torrent of water an estimated 1 foot deep flowing down Central Ave near Interstate 25.  Construction barrels were floating down the sidewalk.  Damages estimated for construction material losses.
Landscape material rockslide across 1 lane of southbound access road to Interstate 25 between Central Ave and Lomas Blvd. Two lanes closed.
Photo posted to Twitter showed a water rescue at a vehicle completely submerged in 9 feet of flood waters at Central Ave and the 1st Street bridge.
Quarter size hail and 1.2 inches of rain in 20 minutes.

Torrential rainfall observed upstream of Yeso Creek produced a significant rise near Highway 20 south of Fort Sumner.  The KFDX storm total rainfall accumulation product indicated 8+ inches over and just upstream of this location, and there was definitely evidence of high water but no major flooding found.  The NM DOT reported around 3 inches of water over the road along Yeso Creek east of Highway 20.
A trained spotter in Fort Sumner reported 4.50 inches of rainfall overnight. The Fort Sumner COOP observer reported 3.17 inches.
A trained spotter near Tolar reported 4.30 inches of rainfall overnight.
Two amateur radio operators reported 4.50 inches of rainfall.

Emergency manager indicated there was flooding in the area around Paliza however it was difficult to determine the extent of any additional damage due to the previous flash flood damage incurred from the event on July 8, 2014.  Damage value is estimated for road repairs.
Rain wrapped funnel cloud reported with the hail along Highway 246.

Emergency manager reported that heavy rainfall in the area from Cochiti south to Kewa Pueblo, San Felipe Pueblo, Algodones, and Rio Rancho resulted in numerous reports of flooding.  All arroyos around San Felipe Pueblo were reported to be running fast and full.  Residents of Sile were cut off due to flooding across a low water crossing that formed due to repeated flooding from the Las Conchas burn scar.  A low water crossing also formed by the Las Conchas flooding was reported fast and full along Tribal Road 84 near Cochiti. No extensive damage was reported but EM felt this event was flash flood worthy.  Heavy rainfall also created minor flooding around Rio Rancho. The area of Algodones the received flooding on the 23rd was also likely impacted by more heavy rainfall.  Damage is estimated for road surfaces near low water crossings and clean up.
Photo passed along from KOAT showed a wash out along an arroyo in Santa Fe.  The berm estimated to be 4 or 5 feet high was completely gone and remnant water was still flowing through the area.

Pecos River at Puerto de Luna reached 11.01 feet at 5pm pm on the 29th.  This was just barely over flood stage at this point.  Farmers and locals in the area said the areal flooding in parts of the area around the Pecos was worse than the previous flooding from September 2013.  The county was expected to assess the damage to minor farming structures along the river when the water receeded.
Owners of a large ranch south southeast of Newkirk reported an incredible 7.05 inches of rainfall from torrential rains overnight.
Trained spotter reported 3.10 inches of rainfall overnight.
One mile north of House reported 4.25 inches of rainfall and minor flooding.

Observer reported the most severe storm at this location in 15 years.  A total of 1.28 inches of rain fell in 45 minutes and the main road on their property was ripped apart and culverts destroyed.  Additionally, their garden was shredded by hail.
At least two roads were washed out near Beaverhead from heavy rainfall.  Damage estimated for repairs.
Public reported that Earthship Way road was washed out from swiftly moving water.

Local news reported that the city of Church Rock was flooded after heavy rainfall. Multiple roads were washed out with access to homes cut off. A few homes were flooded in the area and that the main water line broke under the pressure of all the rushing water. The community was still cleaning up three days after the event.
Water rose 5 to 6 feet in the Frijoles Creek at the Bandalier National Monument Visitors Center.
Three buildings had water flow into them including the dining hall, the tabernacle and the gymnasium at the Inlow Baptist youth camp.
Manager at the Inlow Baptist Youth Camp reported that they measured 4.2 inches of rain.

New Mexico DOT reported that Highway 283 was closed near San Geronimo due to flash flooding.  A CoCoRaHS observer in the area reported 2.81 inches of rainfall from this storm with strong runoff.  2.30 inches of that fell in just 30 minutes with hail.  Highway 283 was reopened the following morning around 11am.

Santa Fe police reported that a lightning strike downed a power line and started a small brush fire at 1945 Cerrillos Road in Santa Fe. The fire is shown in a YouTube video burning for nearly 10 minutes before fire officials extinguished the blaze.
Nickel size hail.
Heavy rainfall over the Little Bear burn scar produced a small rock slide that closed 1 lane of Ski Run Road.

events.event_narrative: Reports from local volunteer observers in the area reported rainfall amounts as high as 0.94 inches in less than one-half hour, with additional rainfall after the main storm. The Corrales Fire Department responded to numerous reports of flooding. Several homes and businesses were inundated with mud and water. A couple of cars were nearly half submerged by water and debris. Trees were also downed from flooding. A preliminary storm survey by local emergency management officials indicated between 15 and 20 roads were damaged and/or completely destroyed, many of which were paved. A couple residents were isolated from the village and could not travel from the area for several hours due to the flooding. Mail delivery services were temporarily suspended in some areas of Corrales because of road damage.
A 16-year-old girl and a homeless man were swept into the Embudo Arroyo channel in separate incidents. They were both rescued safely after a harrowing experience.
State police reported that a man was struck by lightning and killed while riding his motorcycle along U.S. Highway 84 just west of Cimarron at mile post 308 Friday afternoon.

SKYWARN Spotter observed partial roof damage to a structure from strong storms that struck the area. However, preexisting structural issues may have contributed to the damage. Radar estimated wind gusts to around 40 mph.
A gust to 58mph was recorded at the Clovis AWOS.
The ASOS at Cannon Air Force Base recorded a thunderstorm wind gust to 58 mph.

Local Broadcast media shared a photo of a car that was stranded due to flooding at 5th Street and St. Michaels Dr. in Santa Fe. The driver drove into deep water that had accumulated on roadways from short duration, very heavy rainfall.
Most of the hail was nickel size or smaller but for a time there were some very near quarter size to slightly larger. Some standing water also and moderate winds.
Mud and debris was reported on State Road 107 west of Bonito Lake.
HADS site located at Buck Mountain recorded 3.32 inches of rain. There was flooding reported just to the north during this same time.
Trained spotter reported that County Road 3 was impassable due to flood waters and water inundated the lobby of the post office.
Large dust devil reported in south valley area.
Residents around south valley reported tree limbs and power lines down. Yards were trashed as grills and other items were blown around.

Emergency manager reporting that people were displaced from homes in Cimarron as heavy rains led creeks to overflow. Water was also reported in some homes. The village sustained extensive damage to roads from over 5 inches of rain and creek overflowing.

Emergency Manger reported that a motorcyclist was rescued in deep water just off of Highway 285 at Lake Arthur. NM 2 was also closed for multiple hours by the State Police due to standing water on the road.
Video of a funnel cloud in Lake Arthur was posted to social media via the public.
Flooding was reported on State Road 246 at mile markers 4,27-29, and 55-56. Pavement was damaged at mile marker 29. The highway was closed from Capitan to Roswell.
COOP Observer recorded 3 inches of rain.
Schoolnet site recorded 3.60 inches of rain.
Water was reported running over Highway 285 at mile marker 137 north of Roswell. The road was closed due to high water and cleared for travel 5 hours later.

Writer from the Santa Fe newspaper reported that there was damage to E.J. Martinez Elementary School from flash flooding. It was reported that there was damage to 3 classrooms, the gym, and an office.

Local news station reporting that the body of a 58 year old man was found in the Santa Fe River after heavy rainfall and flash flooding. Reports say that he may have been sleeping in or near the river and drowned when he was swept away from rushing waters.
Schoolnet site recorded 3.64 inches of rain during the late evening hours.
Portions of NM 24 were washed out between mile markers 46 and 48 north of Dunken. The road had to be closed.
Estimated wind gust of 55 to 60 mph with outflow winds and blowing dust. This was reported from the Interstate 40 welcome center just inside the NM border.
Spotter reported broken glass and a large tree knocked over from winds and half inch size hail.
Spotter called in and reported that there was a brief funnel cloud with thunderstorms at his location.

Hail size ranged from quarter to golf ball size. Scientists working with the Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility reported damage to windows and ventilation units in several campers stationed in Fort Sumner.

Major street flooding was reported in Roswell.

Large rocks were swept onto US 380 due to intense runoff. The rocks were large enough that the highway department was called out to move them because they were disrupting traffic and preventing travel.

Safety director at the Expo New Mexico reported that the festival tent for the Rio Grande Arts and Crafts fair was destroyed due to thunderstorm wind.
Thunderstorm wind gust to 59 mph recorded at the WSMR Oscura Range Camp.

Significant damage to vehicles and skylights.

Two inches of quarter size hail on the ground.
US 84 at the railroad underpass was flooded due to heavy rain and hail. US 84 at mile marker 0.3 was under deep water through the railroad underpass due to heavy rain and hail.
Damage to culvert apron, retaining rock rip-rap, and metal fencing beneath Interstate 25 about 1 mile south of San Antonio exit. Flow was estimated to be at least 6 feet.

A tornado traveled slightly north of due east through complex terrain of the Lazy Triangle Anchor Ranch, passing less than one quarter mile north of the ranch headquarters located near the intersection of U.S. Highway 64/84. The tornado traveled through terrain ranging from 7500 feet to 9800 feet in elevation. Numerous if not hundreds of large diameter pine trees and cedars were snapped and/or twisted and subsequently uprooted along the first one to one and a half miles. An old long-standing chapel dating back to the 1940s was destroyed. A 6-ft long 4x6 beam was tossed 150 yards. The main ranch residence suffered considerable damage including complete removal of it's pitched roof that was carried 50 yards to the east northeast. A bunkhouse and other storage buildings sustained significant damage. Winds were estimtated at 110 mph, the upper end of EF-1.

COOP, CoCoRaHS, and SNOTEL sites reported between 3 and 5 feet of snowfall over the area during this extended heavy snowfall event. The storm total of 59 inches for the 8-day period was the 11th heaviest event on record dating back to 1893. The 33 inches reported by the Chama COOP observer for the 2-day period ending March 1st was the 7th heaviest snowfall on record. Several other daily records were also achieved.

events.event_narrative: CoCoRaHS, SNOTEL, and public reports averaged between 12 and 20 inches storm total snow during this extended winter storm. Arroyo Seco reported a whopping 20.5 inches of snow for the 3-day period ending February 28th.  It was the heaviest 3-day event at Pecos National Monument since 2010. The 4 inches on the 26th and the 7 inches on the 28th at Pecos set new records for those dates, respectively.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: CoCoRaHS, SNOTEL, and public reports averaged between 12 and 18 inches storm total snow during this extended winter storm. The 3-day snowfall total in Gascon was the most since 2006.

COOP and public reports averaged between 3 and 8 inches storm total snow during this extended winter storm. The bulk of the heavy snowfall ended on the 26th followed by an extended duration of light snow and bitterly cold temperatures and gusty winds through the 27th. The 2 inches that fell in Maxwell on the 26th set a new record for the date.

CoCoRaHS, trained spotters, and public reports averaged between 2 and 8 inches storm total snow during this extended winter storm. A lull in precipitation occurred during the afternoon of the 26th before another impressive round of snow moved over the area during the overnight hours. The heaviest amounts fell immediately south of Las Vegas within a very heavy snow band.

CoCoRaHS, trained spotters, and public reports averaged from 4 to 5 inches storm total snow during this extended winter storm. A lull in the precipitation during the afternoon of the 26th was followed by another intense round of heavy snowfall overnight. The heaviest amounts fell along a line from Roy to Bueyeros southward. The 2 inches of snow in Mosquero on the 27th set a new record for the day.

CoCoRaHS, trained spotters, and public reports averaged between 8 and 10 inches storm total snow during this extended winter storm. A lull in the activity developed during the afternoon of the 26th before another round of heavy snowfall moved through overnight. The heaviest amounts occurred around Mosquero.  The 3 inches that fell in Conchas Dam on the 27th set a new record for the date.
