events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: SNOTEL and public reports averaged between 9 and 17 inches storm total during this extended winter storm.
COOP reports averaged between 6 and 9 inches storm total during this extended winter storm. This ended with areas of dense freezing fog and visibilities reduced below one quarter mile.

COOP, CoCoRaHS, and SNOTEL sites reported between 12 and 18 inches of snowfall over the area during this first of several winter events to occur through early March. It was the heaviest 2-day event in Chama since 2008.  The 9 inches on the 23rd was a record snowfall for the date.
Three inches of snow was reported around Gallup. Significantly reduced visibilities and difficult travel conditions were reported.

COOP, CoCoRaHS, SNOTEL, and public reports averaged between 13 and 33 inches storm total snow during this extended winter storm. The 33 inches at Wolf Canyon was the 5th heaviest 4-day snowfall event ever reported at the site dating back to 1912. The 16 inches on the 28th also set a new record for the date.

COOP, CoCoRaHS, SNOTEL, and public reports averaged between 20 and 43 inches storm total snow during this extended winter storm. The 16 inches reported in Chama on the 28th was a record for the date and the 17 inches on the 1st was also a record for the date. The 33 inches for the 2-day period ending on the 1st was the 7th heaviest snowfall event dating back to 1893. In El Vado, the 12 inches on the 28th and the 10 inches on the 1st were a new records for the date, respectively. The 25 inches from the 27th through the 1st in El Vado set a new record for 3-day accumulations dating back to 1906.

COOP, CoCoRaHS, and SNOTEL sites reported between 13 and 33 inches storm total snow during this extended heavy snowfall event. The 33 inches at Wolf Canyon was the 5th heaviest 4-day snowfall event ever reported at the site dating back to 1912.
CoCoRaHS reports around the Espanola area averaged between 3 and 7 inches of snowfall. The bulk of the snow fell in a heavy band during the early morning hours of the 28th.

COOP, CoCoRaHS, trained spotter, and public reports average between 4 and 7 inches during this prolonged winter event. The first impulse of snow early on the 27th produced a couple inches of snow followed by a lull during the afternoon. The most intense snowfall impacted the area in a very heavy band during the predawn hours of the 28th. The roughly 6 inches of snow in Santa Fe on the 28th set a new record for the date.

An extraordinary number of reports were received during this prolonged winter event. This was the most significant event to impact the Albuquerque metro area since 2006. The Albuquerque International Sunport broke daily snowfall records on both the 27th and the 28th. It was the 9th heaviest 2-day snowfall event on record dating back to 1931. The first impulse of snow early on the 27th produced a couple inches of snow followed by a lull during the afternoon. The most intense snowfall impacted the area in a very heavy band from the evening of the 27th to sunrise on the 28th. Interstate 40 west of Albuquerque closed late on the 26th and the on-ramp from Coors Road onto Interstate 40 EB closed during the morning on the 27th due to snowl and icy conditions. This snow also caused Rio Rancho public schools to close on the 27th.  The interchange from Interstate 25 NB onto Interstate 40 WB closed late on the 27th into the 28th due to heavy snow and ice on the overpass. Both Albuquerque and Rio Rancho public schools closed on the 28th.

An extraordinary number of reports were received during this prolonged winter event. The first impulse of snow early on the 27th produced 3 to 6 inches of snow followed by a lull during the afternoon. The most intense snowfall impacted the area in a very heavy band from the evening of the 27th to sunrise on the 28th where an additional 3 to 8 inches was reported. Major impacts to travel were noted along Interstate 40 within Tijeras Canyon and around the east mountain communities.

Trained spotters reported between 2 and 6 inches of new snow from Portales to Arch and Floyd. The heaviest snowfall occurred during the overnight hours of the 26th through sunrise on the 27th.  The 1 inch of snow on the 26th and the 2.1 inches on the 27th in Portales set new records for the dates.

Trained spotters and public reported between 3 and 6 inches of new snow from Fort Sumner to Sumner Lake and Taiban. The heaviest snowfall occurred during the overnight hours of the 26th through sunrise on the 27th.  The 4 inches in Sumner Lake and the 5 inches south of Fort Sumner on the 27th each set a new record for the date.  The 1-day snowfall total in Fort Sumner was the most since 2010.
Trained spotters between 3 and 8 inches of new snow from near Picacho north to areas east of Corona. The heaviest snowfall occurred during the overnight hours of the 26th through sunrise on the 27th.

Trained spotters between 5 and 7 inches of new snow from near Corona to areas south of Mountainair. The heaviest snowfall occurred from the late evening hours of the 26th through the predawn hours of the 27th. U.S. Highway 54 closed from Carrizozo, through Corona towards Vaughn due to the weather conditions and accidents.

A large area of snowfall pushed east over the Estancia Valley during the evening of the 26th and produced around 3 to 5 inches of snowfall. The heaviest snow fell around midnight when visibilities were reduced to three-quarters of a mile at Moriarty. Impacts to travel were noted along Interstate 40.  The 3.2 inches on the 27th and the 9 inches on the 28th in Stanley, NM set new records for the date, with records dating back to 1955.  The 9 inches also was the heaviest 1-day total since 2006 and ranks as the 5th highest on record.

Strong and bitterly cold easterly upslope flow produced a heavy round of snow during the evening of the 26th through the morning of the 27th. The heaviest snow fell around Duran where 10 inches was reported. Impacts to travel were noted along Interstate 40 as well.  The 2.8 inches on the 27th in Pedernal, NM set a new record for the date, dating back to 1956.
One to 4 inches of snow fell across portions of the Sandia and Manzano Mountains. Only minor travel impacts were noted.

CoCoRaHS reports averaged between 12 and 16 inches storm total snow during this extended winter storm. Climate records indicated this was the 6th heaviest 3-day snowfall event for Taos dating back to 1892. Many folks attested they had not seen this amount of snow since 2006.

CoCoRaHS and trained spotters reported between 3 and 7 inches of snowfall around Farmington, Bloomfield, and Aztec. The first round of snow on the morning of the 27th was followed by freezing fog and flurries before the heaviest round of snow impacted the area early on the 28th. These were the heaviest 2-day snowfall amounts seen in the area since 2010.
The Navajo Whiskey SNOTEL reported a 2-day total of around 9 inches. Storm total amounts through the entire active pattern since the 24th averaged about 15 inches.
CoCoRaHS and public reports averaged between 2 and 6 inches between Navajo and points around Cedar Hill.

Public reported near 11 inches in Ojo Encino with drifts as high as 3 feet. The heaviest snow fell during the early morning hours of the 28th along the north edge of the same intense snow band that impacted the Albuquerque and Santa Fe metropolitan areas. Otis ,NM set new records for the date on the 27th and 28th, with 3.6 inches and 16.3 inches, respectively.  The 16.3 inches was the heaviest 1-day total on record, dating back to 1958. Lindrith, NM received 15 inches on the 28th, setting a new record for the date and becoming the heaviest 1-day total on record, dating back to 1972.  The 9 inches that fell near Cuba on the 28th also set a new record for the date.

CoCoRaHS, public, and amateur radio reports averaged between 4 and 5 inches around the Gallup area. Observers reported the snow was very wet and heavy. The 4 inches in the Gallup area set a new record for the date.

COOP, trained spotters, and public reports indicated between 3 and 6 inches of snow fell from Grants to Cubero and Laguna. The heaviest snowfall impacted the area as an intense band of snow moved through during the early morning hours of the 28th. Hazardous travel conditions were reported along Interstate 40.  Cubero received 6 inches of snow on the 28th, setting a new record for the date and was the most snowfall seen in 1 day since 2011.

Trained spotters reported between 3 and 6 inches of new snow from Anton Chico to Santa Rosa and Newkirk. The heaviest snowfall occurred during the overnight hours of the 26th through sunrise on the 27th. Hazardous travel conditions were reported along Interstate 40 and U.S. Highway 54 was closed from Vaughn towards Corona.  The 6.5 inches on the 26th and the 3 inches on the 27th in Dilia each set a new record for the date. It was also the heaviest 3-day accumulation in Dilia since 2005.

CoCoRaHS and trained spotters reported between 3 and 6 inches of new snow over the entire county. The heaviest snowfall occurred during the overnight hours of the 26th through sunrise on the 27th. Travel was impacted along Interstate 40.  The 2.3 inches reported on the 27th in Tucumcari, NM and the 4 inches reported on the 26th in Ragland, NM each set a new record for the respective dates.

COOP, CoCoRaHS, trained spotters, and public reports averaged between 3 and 7 inches of new snow over the entire county. The heaviest snowfall occurred along the Quay County border during the overnight hours of the 26th through sunrise on the 27th.

COOP, CoCoRaHS, trained spotters, and public reports averaged between 3 and 5 inches of new snow. The heaviest snowfall occurred during the overnight hours of the 26th through sunrise on the 27th. Severe driving conditions were reported along U.S. Highway 70 near Roswell due to black ice, which caused 1 semi-truck to jackknife early on the 27th. Travel along U.S. Highway 285 was also impacted.  The 5 inches at the Bitter Lakes Wildlife Refuge on the 27th set a new record for the date, and tied for the 14th heaviest single-day snowfall dating back to 1951.  The 3.8 inches in Roswell on the 27th also set a new record for the date.

Observers around the area reported between 2 and 3 inches of snow with blowing snow and reduced visibilities. U.S. Highway 54 was closed in Quay County and Interstate 40 was closed east of Tucumcari due to treacherous travel conditions. Areas along the Quay County border likely had even higher snowfall amounts with the intense snow band.
U.S. Highway 285 was closed for several hours beginning around 930pm on the 22nd from Artesia to Roswell and Vaughn due to light snow, freezing fog and black ice.
U.S. Highway 70 was closed for several hours beginning around 530am on the 23rd from Roswell to Hondo and Ruidoso due to light snow, freezing fog and black ice.
U.S. Highway 70 was closed for several hours beginning around 530am on the 23rd from Roswell to Hondo and Ruidoso due to light snow, freezing fog and black ice.

U.S. Highway 285 was closed for several hours beginning around 930pm on the 22nd from Roswell to Vaughn due to light snow, freezing fog and black ice. Some areas of southest Guadalupe County likely received heavier snowfall where an intense snow band crossed the area.
Light snow, freezing fog and black ice caused the closure of U.S. Highway 54 around 530am on the 27th from Carrizozo to Corona.

A rancher 6 miles northeast of Folsom indicated soil conditions have dramatically improved over the area during the winter months. They were digging post holes for a fence and noted soil moisture present down at least 18 inches.

events.event_narrative: Ski sites and SNOTELs reported between 9 and 19 inches of wet snow. Intense snowfall rates occurred with this snow event during the late afternoon and early evening hours of the 19th.
A mesonet site in the White Sands Missile Range measured a peak wind gust of 66 mph.
Storm chaser reported one to two inches of pea to quarter size hail on State Road 50.
Penny size hail.

events.event_narrative: Trained spotter and CoCoRaHS reports indicated between 10 to 18 inches of snow. Power outages caused by heavy snow were reported in Angel Fire.
Capulin National Monument shared photos of hail slightly larger than quarter size mixed in the mainly pea size hail.

According to local media reports, 65 homes in the Cannon Air Force Base area were impacted by the flooding, including roof damage, weather stripping, carpet, flooring, and sheetrock. Local officials evacuated 33 families from those homes and put them in hotel lodging. The flooding in Clovis forced the closure of U.S. Highway 60/84. Approximately 40 feet of state highway 108 between mile markers 6 and 10 was washed out. Clovis police had to use an armored vehicle to rescue 7 victims stranded by or caught in fast moving waters or flooded streets.
Trained spotter reported quarter size hail.
Trained spotter reported dime to quarter size hail covering the ground.
The public reported nickel size hail.
The public reported quarter size hail.
Trained spotter reported nickel size hail covering the ground.
Trained spotter reported penny sized hail.

Trained spotters and the public reported multiple cold-air funnels developing over the Roswell area.  Reports indicated that one cold air funnel cloud briefly made contact with the ground and damaged the roof and walls of two outbuildings. No injuries or fatalities were reported with this tornado.
Cannon Air Force Base estimated ping-pong size hail fell at their airport.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: Impressive late season snowfall amounts between 2 and 7 inches were reported over the higher terrain of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains. No significant impacts were noted.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Impressive late season snowfall of 7.2 inches was reported near Black Lake around 10,000 feet. No significant impacts were noted.
Public pictures shared on facebook show the golf ball sized hail that fell near Dora.  No reported damage due to the hail.
Trained spotter woken by penny size hail that fell during the early morning hours.
Nickel size hail stripped leaves off trees at a recreational vehicle park.
A few quarter size hailstones mixed in with predominately dime size hailstones near Pep.
Heavy rain mixed with pea to nickel size hail.
Nickel size hail accumulated around 1 inch deep at Wolf Canyon.
A total of 4 aspen trees blown over by an estimated 55 mph virga bomb north of Farmington.  One tree was 16 feet tall and another was 20 feet tall.
ASOS reported 60 mph gust ahead of a thunderstorm.
A mesonet site near Dora reported a peak wind gust of 59 mph.
Estimated quarter size hail damaged the screen doors on the west side of the house.
A 59 mph thunderstorm wind gust was measured at the Albuquerque International Sunport.
Measured at the Santa Fe airport.
A personal weather net site measured a gust of 62 mph.
Trained spotter estimated wind gusts of 60 mph that were aided by nearby convection.
A personal weather station measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 69 mph.
A mesonet site on top of North Oscura Peak measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 60 mph.
The Chupadera RAWS measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 58 mph.  Time estimated based on radar/lightning data.

Trained spotter measured 4.9 inches of rain over the course of 3 hours. This resulted in fast flowing water in their yard, with the highest watermark on the side of their house being 8 inches. No water was reported to have entered the home. The end time of the flooding and areal coverage were estimated.
Spotter noted that Yeso Creek had overflowed its banks and was also running rapidly. No further information or damage was reported.

Spotter reported several arroyos were overflowing their banks and washing out numerous roads. State Road 294 was closed due to flooding near junction with U.S. Highway 60 for several hours after causative event. Most of the flooding subsided by 3 am which allowed some roads to become passable. No damage was reported with this flooding.

Heavy rain caused all of the creeks to overflow their banks and washout a few roads. The spotter measured 3.5 inches of rain caused this flooding.  Power was out for a while before returning around 945 am.  No other damage was reported.

New Mexico Department of Transportation closed state road 108 at mile marker 14 due to flooding from the heavy rains.  While flooding may have subsided, the DOT reported that the road will remain closed through memorial day weekend. A CoCoRaHS observer near Pleasant Hill reported 3.25 inches of rain in less than 24 hours.
The New Mexico Department of Transportation closed state road 272 at mile marker 9 due to flooding.
Trained spotter estimated 60 mph wind gusts from severe storm.  The winds knocked fruit off nearby tree, but no other damage was reported.
Spotter reported marble to half dollar sized hail fell from severe storm.

Cherry picker crane carrying several individuals at Cochiti Road and Dorothy Street was toppled by an erratic outflow wind gust between 30 and 40 mph. The crane operator and one child were killed on the scene. Three others were injured. One of the injured children died several days later in the hospital.

Kalina Jinzo, a 40-year mother of three, was struck by lightning and killed while traveling from Albuquerque to Ruidoso on a motorcycle on the 15th. Her husband was also struck but his injuries were not life threatening. The woman died several days later in a Lubbock hospital around the 22nd.
At least three storms moved through Raton and each produced light accumulations of pea to dime size hail. The heaviest storm produced penny size hail.
Hail accumulated several inches deep.
Cannon Air Force Base weather staff reported copious half inch diameter hail with some stones as large as quarters.
A whopping 3.75 inches of rain was reported in a 24-hour period by the Dilia COOP observer. No flooding was reported from the heavy rain.

Widespread heavy rainfall amounts between 3 and 5 inches reported across Curry County. Significant flash flooding was observed around the Clovis area. Pleasant Hill picked up an impressive 24-hour total of 4.2 inches.
Funnel cloud spotted near rest area in Mesa.

events.event_narrative: Late season heavy snowfall of 2 to 12 inches reported from high elevation SNOTEL sites in the Sangre de Cristo Mountains. No impacts were noted due to the very high elevation and relatively warm surface temperatures.

events.event_narrative: Several more inches of wet snow in the very high elevations of the northern Sangre de Cristo Mountains tallied between 12 and 17 inches for the 2-day period around Taos Ski Valley. Impacts were limited due to the high elevation and relatively warm surface temperatures.
Quarter size hail 2 miles northeast of Portales.
Hen egg size hail for 10 minutes 1 mile east of Sedan.

Spotter reported dime to nickel size hail.
Hail stripped fruit off of trees on the property.
Numerous reports of elephant trunk tornado on the ground between Milnesand and Lingo. No damage or injuries reported.
Up to 2 feet of water on portions of Echols Avenue as well as along Cameo Street. The Dennis Chaves Park Lake was overflowing onto 14th Street which lead to several cars stalling out.
Chaser reported nickel size hail.
Spotter reported nickel sized hail.

Public reported nickel size hail.

events.event_narrative: Hail accumulated up to 3 inches deep along U.S. 64.
A schoolnet site in House reported a 1-day total rainfall of 3.4 inches.
Thunderstorms produced 3.5 inches of rainfall in less than 24 hours near Tolar. No official reports of flash flooding were received.
Numerous reports of a funnel cloud were received with a strong thunderstorm near Des Moines.
Five inch diameter tree limbs downed. Small electrical pole toppled. Some siding stripped off roof of McDonalds.

Observer noted that thunderstorm wind gusts broke a few electrical poles.

New Mexico Department of Transportation reported 1 inch of quarter size hail fell along interstate 25 between Maxwell and Raton.  Snow trucks were brought out to plow hail off the road.
Spotter passed along pictures of large tree limb blown over by thunderstorm wind gust in Roswell.
COOP Observer reported quarter size hail fell with heavy rain during the early afternoon.
New Mexico Department of Transportation reported penny size hail near Vaughn.

Trained spotter reported pea to quarter size hail in Grenville.
Trained spotter reported pea to quarter size hail fell.

Trained spotter reported that large hail and strong winds caused 4 inch diameter tree limps to snap.
Chunks of pavement removed from Big Mesa Road during heavy rainfall. High water was flowing over several portions of the roadway.
Landspout tornado on the ground for about 2 minutes near Indian Service Roads 4002 and 4017. No damage reported.
Quarter size hail in Farmington.
Half dollar size hail at San Juan College. Second hand report noted some sky lights were damaged in a couple buildings.
Photo from emergency manager showed ping pong ball size hail.

Animas River rose above bankful during the mid afternoon of the 11th and crested at minor flood stage briefly around 4pm before slowly falling through the overnight. Berg and Animas Parks experienced flooding along the riverwalk and many trails were inundated along the river for several hours. No damage to infrastructure was reported.
County road 155 washed away and culverts destroyed.
Peak wind of 59mph from thunderstorm at CSBF.
Funnel cloud spotted just west of the intersection of State Road 13 and U.S. Highway 82.
Observer reported strong wind gust seen all year. No damaged reported but lots of tumbleweeds and dirt blew around.
Nickel size hail on Isleta Pueblo.
Tennis ball size hail in Elida. No damaged reported.
Golf ball size hail in Elida.
Spotter estimated easily 60 mph wind gusts.
Several large trees limbs broken off tree in yard.
Quarter size hail.
White Sands Missile Range reported 60 mph wind gust from thunderstorm outflows.
White Sands Missile Range reported 59 mph wind gust from thunderstorm outflow.
Intersection of 17th and 18th streets with 3rd and Kilgor flooding. No damage reported.
Highway 267 closed between milemarkers 10 and 11 due to flash flooding.
A public spotter reported nickel size hail.
The ASOS at the Roswell Airport recorded a thunderstorm wind gust of 58 mph.
Hail estimated at half dollar size caused dented hoods on trucks and broke a window in a building.

USFS reported up to 2 inches of dime to quarter size hail.

Penny size hail.
Raton airport reported outflow wind of 58 mph.
Four 35 ft power poles and one 60 ft pole blown down from wet microburst along State Road 505.
Gallup airport reported a 70 mph wind gust from dry thunderstorms.
COOP Observer reported strong winds causing a large tree limp to snap and land on carport.

New Mexico Department of Transportation closed US Highway 64 as heavy rain caused debris, boulders and a mud slide to cover several miles of the road. Philmont Scout Ranch also reported major flash flooding on the Ponil Creek basin that ran through a boy scout camp site in the nearby mountains. The flooding washed away 4 boys, killing 1.
Storm chaser reported lots of hail covering the ground with the largest stone around half dollar size.
NWS Employee reported pea to nickel sized hail near Sandia Park.
Trucker reported penny size hail along interstate 40 at mile marker 178.
CoCoRaHS report of quarter size hail that lasted 6 minutes.
Twitter picture showed dime to quarter size hail that fell in the Valles Caldera National Preserve.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding south of Jemez Springs, closing state road 485 and forest service road 376. The county emergency manager reported significant damage to state road 485. Low water crossings along state road 4 between mile markers 10 and 16 were also flooded, but the road was never closed. New Mexico Department of Transportation representatives also noted that the Rio Guadalupe was out of its banks and possibly into homes.  Further information not confirmed at this time.
Twitter report indicated half dollar size hail fell along forest service road 604 near Cebollita Spring.
Emergency manager passed along report of quarter to half dollar size hail in the community of Seven Springs.
COOP observer reported up to quarter size hail fell along with over half an inch of rain.
Heavy rain caused a mudslide along NM 38, causing it to close for 2 hours.  The rain also caused a rockslide to close all but one lane of County Road 578.
Ten feet of water was rushing through a normally dry gulley on the spotters property. No damage was reported as a result of this wall of water.
COOP observer reported pea to penny sized hail along with heavy rains.

Heavy rains caused a barn and two pastures to be flooded. One lane of a two-lane gravel road was also washed out with many other roads seeing 3 feet deep ravines created by the heavy rain. Numerous roads around the Zuni Mountains were washed out and residents were trapped in their homes for several days until county officials could repair the roads. Phone services were also lost.

Heavy rain caused State Road 491 north of Gallup to close due to flooding and debris. County Emergency Manager reported flash flooding caused 4 inches of mud and 8 inches of water to enter a juvenile center on the east side of town. He also noted that a few bridges were temporarily closed due to flood waters, along with numerous county roads suffering damage. Exact location and extent of damage was unknown. Allen Joe Begay of White Cone, Arizona was swept away in flood waters while in the Rio Puerco.
A White Sands Missile Range site measured a wet microburst wind gust of 65 mph.
Large wooden doors were blown off a barn. Several trees had severe damage. A plastic roof on a greenhouse was blown off. A metal tail of a windmill was wrapped around the wheel base.

Wet microburst winds toppled a metal grain silo onto a nearby truck, resulting in 1 injury. Two other silos were also severely damaged. Numerous tree branches were broken at a nearby home. A spotter reported storm total rainfall of 3.25 inches from these storms.
A foot of water flowed over U.S. 170 between mile markers 15 and 18. NMDOT had to clean mud, rocks, and debris off the roadway.
Dime to quarter size hail in Edgewood.
A 30' x 20' metal hay barn was tossed a quarter mile and crashed into a nearby home. Flying glass injured a woman in the home. Several folks reported a brief tornado on the ground.
Rotating wall cloud and funnel reported along State Road 41 near McIntosh.

Significant flooding with estimated 6 inches of flowing water at the corner of Cerrillos and Richards. Gravel washed across the road at the corner of West Alameda and Siler. Landscaping material washed out.
Fire marshal reported a tremendous sudden burst of torrential rainfall. A fast flowing mudslide surged over highway 38 between mile markers 8 and 9. A video of the event was posted to FB.

Flash flood wave moved down Yeso Rito arroyo in less than 30 minutes, resulting in significant damage at Ghost Ranch. At least three older structures and a ropes course were completely destroyed. One newer studio structure was seriously damaged. Trees were snapped in half and mud filled several other structures. Damage has been estimated between 500,000 and 1 million dollars. No injuries were reported.
Quarter size hail north of highway 599 three miles west of highway 285.
Report of 65 mph outflow winds with torrential rainfall in San Jon.
Report of 65 mph outflow winds and over 2 inches of rainfall near Logan.
Quarter size hail along NM 6.
A significant wash out with debris near Orchard Campground west of Bonito Lake. A couple places along highway 107 were impassable due to flowing water and debris. Marthas Canyon was the hardest hit.
Spotter reported nickel to half dollar size hail southeast of Santa Fe.
Damage to roads and guard rails along canyons west of Interstate 25, particularly within Nogal Canyon.

Several foot bridges were washed away within Frijoles Canyon as the creek overflowed it's banks. Water did not make it into the parking lot at the visitor center. Rain gage reports averaged between 1 and 2 inches within the canyon.
Several rail cars toppled off the tracks of a BNSF train near Fort Sumner.
Intense rainfall from slow-moving thunderstorms dumped 4.05 inches of rainfall at the COOP observer station near Tucumcari. No major flooding was reported.

Heavy rains caused several streets to flood with between 2 to 4 feet of water in downtown Grants.  The street flooding included First and Second streets from Washington to Roosevelt as well as Fifth and Santa Fe streets. It caused one vehicle to stall due to the water height.  No business or homes were reported flooded as well as no reported injuries.
The Galisteo Creek below the Galisteo Dam reached flood stage of 9 feet for about 2 hours, cresting at 9.18 feet.

Local media reported that 100 feet of railroad track for the Rail Runner between Albuquerque and Sante Fe was washed out.  The tracks were located on north side of the bridge at the Arroyo Maria Chavez.  Rail Runner service was suspended for the rest of the weekend.

Photos showed water rushing over Red Rock Road near Madrid and making it impassable.  The report indicated that the depth of the water over the road peaked at 3 feet.  It took about an hour for the water to subside enough before safely crossing.

Public weather station reported 3.35 inches of rainfall in 1 hour near Las Campanas. Video showed flash flood waters flowing quickly over East Sunrise Road northwest of Santa Fe, making it impassable. The water depth was reported to be between 1 and 1.5 feet.
Trained spotter reported an estimated wind gust of 60 mph.
Spotter reported quarter size hail north of Santa Rosa.
State police reported thunderstorm winds causing damage to the roofs of several buildings along old route 66 in the center of town.

State police had to pull 3 vehicles out of mud on Highway 91 created by the heavy rains. Reilly Road between Highway 91 and Blue Hole was later closed as it was covered by flash flood water. These waters also went into the nearby senior center.
Spotter reported between 1 to 2 feet of flash flood waters over the Puerta de Luna Road southeast of Santa Rosa.
A lightning strike led to a fatal motorcycle crash along U.S. Highway 64 near Hopewell Lake. The victim was 37-year old Juan Trujillo.

Very heavy rainfall overnight dumped 3.20 inches at Santa Rosa. Minor flooding was observred around town and within the El Rito Creek and Pecos River drainages. Areas downstream toward Puerto de Luna saw flooding in the same area where damage occurred to Power Dam in 2013.
Very heavy rainfall overnight resulted in a whopping 4.05 inches by morning. No flooding problems were reported.

A whopping 5 inch rainfall report was received from Sumner Lake due to torrential overnight rains. Very heavy rainfall over and upstream of the reservoir resulted in an astounding 2.5 ft rise on the lake by morning. Controlled releases up to 300cfs were performed for several days following the event.

Torrential rainfall dumped 6.05 inches over Pleasant Hill within 24-hours. This resulted in the closure of State Road 108 due to high water on the roadway. The road was closed for several days in the same area earlier in the month.
A truck was found crushed by a large boulder at the base of a 30-ft deep arroyo in Superman Canyon. The body of the man operating the vehicle was discovered 3 miles downstream at White Cliff.
Six inches of rapidly flowing water over U.S. Highway 550 at mile maker 117. Nearby arroyo was raging with flash flood waters out of its banks.
U.S. Highway 60 closed due to high water at mile marker 124.
Dime to penny size hail in Tucumcari. Lightning strike also blew up a transformer.
Quarter size hail near Grenville. Light accumulations were noted.
Spotter reported overturned 18-wheeler along U.S. Highway 285 from severe thunderstorm winds. The driver was injured in the crash and transported to a local hospital.
Spotter reported a severe wind gust moved through the area with a thunderstorm on the 3rd.
Spotter reported an intense burst of wind blew over several light weight objects on the property, including lawn furniture and a dog house. The dog was not injured.
Observer reported hurricane-like wind and rainfall in the center of Clovis.
Power lines downed from high winds resulted in power outage at the Roswell Correctional Facility between Hagerman and Dexter.
Cannon Air Force Base.
Peak wind of 62 mph measured.
Penny size hail.
Nickel size hail.
Fire crews responded to lightning caused blaze at a duplex home that resulted in significant damage to the property.
Quarter size hail reported near Logan.

New Mexico Department of Transportation closed U.S. highway 54 at mile markers 124 and 170 due to heavy rain and difficult driving conditions.  This closure lasted 45 minutes and prevented traffic to drive between Corona and Carrizozo.
The Roswell airport ASOS recorded a thunderstorm wind gust of 58 mph.
Fire chief reported a 68 mph wind gust at the fire station.  This wind blew down 2 trees in a nearby alley as well as the personal weather station on site.
The Clayton municipal airport measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 62 mph.
SHAVE reported nickel size hail near Ranchvale.

Fire chief reported thunderstorm wind damage on the east side of Clayton, mainly along  U.S. highway 56.  The most notable damage was road signs being blown onto the roadways.  Heavy rain and pea size hail was also reported in this area.

The river gage along Galisteo Creek below Galisteo rose to above minor flood stage at 1 am on the 11th due to rains late on the 10th. It peaked above moderate flood stage around by 330am before dropping below moderate flood stage around 515am, and completely below minor flood stage at 730am.
Half dollar size hail fell briefly in Folsom.
Staff living near the Capulin National Monument reported hail just smaller than ping pong size with storm that hit during the evening.

Heavy rains caused a mud slide along a mile stretch of roadway that leads to the top of the Capulin National Monument.  The debris included mud and boulders that were up to 55 pounds in weight.  The road remained closed into the afternoon on the 14th as staff attempted to clear the debris.
Pea to quarter size hail fell in Maxwell while lightning knocked out power.
Pea to nickel size hail fell along with an estimated 45 mph wind gust.
The Melrose RAWS measured a peak wind gust of 60 mph.
Golf ball size hail fell along highway 285 south of Tres Piedras.
Quarter size hail north of Salman Raspberry Ranch.
Pea to quarter size hail with 50 mph estimated wind gusts.
Pea to quarter size hail along U.S. Highway 64 between Des Moines and Grenville.  Plow trucks called out to move hail off roadway.
Quarter to half dollar size hail lasted about 5 minutes.
Public reports indicate baseball size hail fell between Pastura and Vaughn along U.S. Highway 54.  EM had back windshield blown out by the hail that was falling from the same storm.
Spotter reported notable vehicle dent damage due to the golf ball size hail.
The first storm over the observer's location produced tennis ball size hail that broke 3 skylights of a house, and dented a car and broke its windows.
Quarter to half dollar size hail.
The second storm over the observer's location dropped penny size hail.
Extreme winds that observer thought would uproot the grass.
Ping pong size hail from third storm over observer's location.

Spotter passed along pictures of half a mobile home that was overturned near Dexter as it was being transported to Alto. The mobile home became completely detached from the towing truck, resulting in damage to siding and roof.  This was a high-profile vehicle traveling along U.S. Highway 285.  The other half avoided any issues.

The Blanco Arroyo overflowed its banks and, combined with heavy rain across the area, led to significant flash flooding. Firefighters rescued a few individuals from the roofs of their homes, otherwise no major injuries or fatalities were reported.  Several homes were reportedly shifted off their foundation and a propane tank at one of those homes was swept away in the flood waters.  Multiple classrooms were damaged at three area schools, causing all schools to be closed on the 27th and one school, Lydia Rippey Elementary, to be closed on the 28th.  The Aztec Municipal Golf Course at Hidden Valley was closed until further notice due to damages incurred from the flooding.  A large rock slide closed Navajo Road 36 at mile marker 28, with other smaller road closures reported around Aztec.  Measured rainfall in the area ranges from an inch to a little over an inch and a half.
Damaging winds caused multiple trees to fall over, landing on houses and power lines.  This caused power outages for portions of Aztec, Flora Vista, and Crouch Mesa.

Significant damage reported on a property near Flora Vista likely the result of intense microburst winds.  The winds downed over 100 very large cottonwood trees, including a few that were completely uprooted.  The tops of a few trees were completely snapped off, as well.  Metal roofing on a barn was torn off and horizontally displaced about 20 yards on nearby power poles.  The falling timber along with the wind itself caused damage to a barn roof, a pop up camper, a canoe, a trampoline, and a camper. Based on the EF-toolkit winds from this storm may have reached as high as 104 mph. No injuries or further damages resulted from the microburst.
Heavy rains caused state road 462 to be closed by the New Mexico DOT between mile markers 0 and 2.
Passed along a measured wind gust of 53 kts at the Fort Sumner airport.
Media member supplied pictures of trampoline that was blown on top of a power line, indicating an estimated wind speed of 55 mph.
Convectively aided wind gust.

Emergency manager reported widespread street flooding in Roswell.  Later reports and information showed road closures in the northeast portion of the city near the Anderson Museum of Contemporary Art, notably North Virginia Road and North Garden Road.  There were unconfirmed reports of swift water rescues in the area as well.  Rainfall reports from trained spotters and the CoCoRaHS network around the area showed up to 3.68 inches of rain fell, with many reports in excess of 2.5 inches.
Multiple reports via Twitter of tree damage and trees being uprooted in various portions of central and eastern Albuquerque.

Media reports indicated a man was swept away and died in fast moving water that filled the north diversion channel arroyo.  Eye witness reports noted the man was outside the arroyo before somehow ending up in it and being swept away.  Search and rescue attempts by the fire department found the body two hours later in the Rio Grande.  The only other information available at this time is that it was a male between the ages of 20 and 30 years old. The intense rainfall rates also washed lots of landscaping material, including rocks, mud, and fabric material, into streets across the metro area. A water mark near Carlisle and Comanche suggested the water was as high as 2 feet in the intersection. Road crews spent several hours cleaning up streets across the city.
Pea to half inch size hail with a few quarter size pieces of hail mixed in.
Albuquerque South Valley resident reported strong winds knocked a couple branches off a tree onto a nearby fence and car.

Three bridges were damaged from flood waters northeast of Grants. A dozen jersey barriers were washed 100 yards downstream at low water crossings along Lobo Canyon. The most significant damage occurred to the George Hannish Bridge. Bridges along county roads 19A and 19D were also impacted.
Flood damaged roads along low water crossings near Encinal and Bibo. Jersey barriers erected to protect from flood waters were washed away.
Nickel size hail near Tolar.
Fourteenth street closed near Dennis Chaves Lake.
One mile stretch of U.S. Highway 60/84 closed due to flooding.
Water up to car doors on South Avenue K.
Hail to the size of quarters accumulated several inches deep near Mount Taylor.
Peak wind gust to 66 mph at 1149pm MDT. Sustained winds peaked at 52 mph. Numerous trees and powerlines down across the east side. Unofficial site within Embudo Canyon peaked at 68 mph.
Mesonet sites across White Sands Missile Range peaked between 60 mph and 71 mph. No damage was observed.
Penny to nickel size hail covered the ground.
Picture forwarded through local media showing dime to nickel size hail.
New Mexico State road 2 closed due to flooding.  A motorist was stranded in 3 to 4 feet of water.  The road remained closed into the next day.
Pea to quarter size hail.
Observer reported damage to cars, roofs and windows.  Extent of damage unknown.
Pea to quarter size hail.
Very heavy quarter size hail and very heavy rain.
Pea to quarter size hail along US Highway 82 that covered a 4 mile stretch of highway with 1 inch deep of hail.
New Mexico State road 246 closed between mile markers 59 and 60 due to flooding over the roadway.
One inch accumulation of pea to nickel size hail.
Pea to ping pong size hail.
Pea to golf ball size hail.  Through secondhand information, observer reported a few broken windows around town.
About a two inch accumulation of pea to quarter size hail.
Twitter photo showed roughly tennis ball size hail near Taiban.  No reported damage.

Spotter reported a 24-hour rainfall total of 4.10 inches in Clovis. This was on top of roughly 2 inches of rain that fell the previous day. Other locations across the area reported intense rainfall, including 3.31 in Grady, 3.99 near Broadview, and 3.47 near Pleasant Hill.

Measured high sustained wind Dora Mesonet.

Reports from trained spotters, CoCoRaHS, SNOTELs, public, and social media indicated between 2 and 10 inches of snow. Difficult driving conditions were reported in the area, including the Gallup area. Impacts were mostly relegated to the area from Gallup southeast toward Vanderwagon. No road closures or significant delays were noted.
Large pine tree toppled at UNM Los Alamos due to strong wind gust. No damage to nearby buildings.

Interstate 25 closed from Las Vegas to Raton Pass due to blizzard conditions. Snowfall accumulations averaged 8 to 12 inches. High winds produced significantly reduced visibility and drifts between 2 and 3 feet. Severe driving conditions were also reported east of Raton to Folsom.

Interstate 25 closed from Las Vegas to Raton Pass due to blizzard conditions. Snowfall accumulations averaged 3 to 8 inches. Wind gusts as high as 64 mph at Raton airport produced drifts between 2 and 3 feet in Raton. Some snow piles ended up over 6 feet high in town.

Severe driving conditions with blizzard conditions reported from Raton east to Clayton. Snowfall accumulations averaged 3 to 12 inches with locally up to 15 inches along the Colorado border. Wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph around Union County produced drifts between 2 and 3 feet along and east of Des Moines.

Various sources reported between 5 and 10 inches of snow across the Taos area. This is one of the heaviest 24-hour snowfall accumulations for the Taos area and the greatest since 2009. Significant impacts to travel were noted.
COOP site reported 4 inches of snow around Dulce. Hazardous travel conditions were reported.
COOP and SNOTEL reports across the area indicated between 6 and 10 inches of snowfall with hazardous travel conditions in blowing snow.
COOP and SNOTEL reports across the area indicated between 10 and 18 inches of snowfall with hazardous travel conditions in blowing snow. Phone services were disrupted as well.

Various reports across the area indicated between 3 and 9 inches of snowfall with hazardous travel conditions. This was the first significant snowfall event for this winter season.
Various reports across the area indicated between 4 and 8 inches of snowfall with hazardous travel conditions. This was the first significant snowfall event for this winter season.
Various reports across the area indicated between 4 and 6 inches of snowfall with hazardous travel conditions. This was the first significant snowfall event for this winter season.

One quarter inch to one half inch of freezing rain downed power lines around the Clovis area. Near 2000 residents were without power. Widespread treacherous travel conditions were reported across the county.

One quarter inch to one half inch of freezing rain fell over northern portions of Roosevelt County from near Melrose to Tolar. Treacherous driving conditions were reported over this area for more than 24 hours.
One quarter inch of freezing rain and light accumulations of snow fell across De Baca County. Treacherous driving conditions were reported over this area for more than 24 hours.

One quarter to one half inch of freezing rain and light snow accumulations impacted the U.S. Highway 54 corridor. Treacherous driving conditions were reported from north of Carrizozo to northeast of Corona. Numerous accidents were reported, including an overturned semi truck. The highway was closed for several hours.

One half inch to one inch of freezing rain and around 1 inch of snow fell across Quay County. Treacherous driving conditions were reported along Interstate 40 and many surrounding U.S. highways. Interstate 40 was closed from Tucumcari to the Texas state line due to widespread major impacts to travel into Texas.
Near one half inch of freezing rain and around 1 inch of snow fell across Guadalupe County. Treacherous driving conditions were reported along Interstate 40 and many surrounding U.S. highways.
Light accumulations of freezing rain and around 1 to 2 inches of snowfall produced treacherous travel conditions around Clines Corners. Interstate 40 and U.S. Highway 285 were severely impacted.

Gentleman traveling through Carrizozo very early on the 28th noted much of the area was still covered in at least one half inch of ice, if not more. Broken tree branches were reported. Numerous wrecks were also reported the previous day along the highways to Capitan and Corona.

Light accumulations of freezing rain and around 1 to 2 inches of snowfall produced treacherous travel conditions around the Sacramento Mountains and Ruidoso. The combination of cold temperatures and gusty winds severely impacted all roadways around the area.

One to two tenths of an inch of freezing rain and around 1 inch of snowfall severely impacted travel around Harding County. The combination of cold temperatures and gusty winds severely impacted all roadways around the area.
One to two tenths of an inch of freezing rain, around 1 inch of snowfall, very cold temperatures, and gusty winds severely impacted travel around Harding County.
One quarter inch of freezing rain and light snow accumulations impacted the U.S. Highway 70 corridor around Arabela to Chaves County. Travel was severely impacted  toward Encinoso as well.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: Three to six inches of snowfall was reported around the high terrain. Minor impacts to travel were reported.

Trained spotters, COOP observers, highway department, and the public reported around 8 to 10 inches of snowfall around Union County, with drifts as high as 3 feet in whiteout conditions. The Clayton ASOS reported one-quarter mile visibility between 8am and 3pm with winds as high as 50 mph. U.S. Highway 64/84 and U.S. Highway 54 were closed for several hours. The webcam at Clayton showed near zero visibility.

Trained spotters, COOP observers, highway department, and the public reported around 4 to 10 inches of snowfall around northeast Colfax County near the Colorado border. Drifts as high as 2 to 3 feet covered roadways with whiteout conditions. Highway 64/84 was closed for several hours.

Four to 5 inches of snow with blowing snow and some drifting were reported from Raton south to Wagon Mound. Difficult driving conditions impacted Interstate 25. The Raton airport reported a peak wind of 60 mph with this event.
Three to 7 inches of snow and blowing snow were reported from Las Vegas to Ribera. Difficult driving conditions impacted Interstate 25.
Two to four inches of snow with blowing snow, drifts, and very low visibilities were reported from Roy to Bueyeros. Difficult driving conditions impacted nearly every roadway across Harding County.

Up to 10 inches of snow with blowing snow, drifts, and very low visibilities were reported around Bell Ranch. Difficult driving conditions impacted nearly every roadway across eastern San Miguel County.

Countywide snowfall ranged from about 8 to 10 inches of snow with the heaviest amounts falling on the caprock north of Interstate 40 from Dilia eastward. Difficult driving conditions impacted nearly every roadway across the county.

Numerous sources from across the Albuquerque Metro area reported between 2 and 7 inches with the heaviest amounts falling east of the Interstate 25 corridor. Travel conditions were difficult mainly above 5,500 feet. The 5.4 inches reported at the Sunport was a top-25 two day snowfall event.
Numerous sources from across Santa Fe south to Eldorado and Lamy reported between 3 and 9 inches. Travel conditions were difficult across the entire area.

Various sources across eastern Rio Arriba County reported between 4 and 9 inches of new snow. Blowing snow and frigid temperatures with this event led to low visibilities in the high terrain along with hazardous travel conditions.

Various sources across the Jemez Mountains reported between 5 and 10 inches of new snow. Blowing snow and frigid temperatures with this event led to low visibilities in the high terrain along with hazardous travel conditions.

Various sources across the Taos area reported between 3 and 6 inches of new snow. Blowing snow and frigid temperatures with this event led to low visibilities for a brief period along with hazardous travel conditions.
