events.event_narrative: Observer near Ute Park at Pine Ridge Store reported several gusts to 60 mph through the overnight period.
Navajo Whiskey reported 10 inches of wet snow.

Observer in Chama reported a 2-day total of 15 inches. Various SNOTEL sites across the high terrain reported between 10 and 15 inches. Snow water equivalent was high with this event thus snowfall was wet and heavy.
SNOTEL sites across the high terrain reported between 10 and 20 inches of snowfall. Liquid equivalent values were high thus snowfall was wet and heavy.

Heavy snow and high winds paralyzed the entire county through the 30th. Snowfall amounts of 8 to 12 inches were reported across the county. The 10.0 inches at the COOP site 13 miles north of Clovis tied the 3rd highest 1-day total snowfall dating back to 1949. Peak wind gusts of 70 to 80 mph were reported along and behind the cold front. The Clovis airport reported a peak wind gust of 82 mph. Drifts of 6 to 10 feet were common. Numerous motorists were stranded including rescue vehicles with the National Guard. Power outages were the most widespread across Curry County, where over 14,000 residents were without power. The Department of Agriculture reported the most widespread livestock fatalities occurred in Curry and Roosevelt counties. Nearly 12,000 adult milking cows perished with over 300 in one dairy alone. Massive losses were suffered in young livestock with between 30,000 and 50,000 deaths. Estimates did not include sheep and beef cows.

Heavy snow and high winds paralyzed the entire county through the 30th. A peak gust to 67 mph was reported at Melrose Range. Snowfall amounts of 6 to 12 inches were reported across the county. Drifts of 6 to 10 feet were common. Numerous motorists were stranded including rescue vehicles with the National Guard. Thousands of power outages were reported. The Department of Agriculture reported the most widespread livestock fatalities occurred in Curry and Roosevelt counties. Nearly 12,000 adult milking cows perished. Massive losses were suffered in young livestock with between 30,000 and 50,000 deaths. Estimates did not include sheep and beef cows.

Heavy snow and high winds paralyzed the entire county through the 31st. A peak wind gust to 60 mph was reported at Bitter Lake and Elkins. Numerous motorists were stranded including rescue vehicles with the National Guard. Snowfall amounts of 10 to 20 inches were reported across the county. The Roswell Industrial Airpark broke their all-time one day total snowfall record with 12.4 inches dating back to 1946. Drifts of 6 to 10 feet were common. Numerous power outages were reported across the county. At least four commercial roof collapses were reported, including a Diamond Shamrock gas station and a Hondo dealership. A fire was reported at Coca-Cola. The National Guard assisted with medical emergencies across the county. A 67-year old man died from a heart attack while shoveling snow in Roswell. Thousands of livestock and range land animals were expected to have perished in this storm. A state of emergency was declared for Chaves County.

Heavy snow and high winds paralyzed much of the county through the 29th. A peak wind of 69 mph was reported at the Fort Sumner airport. A shelter was opened in the county at a local church where one family was housed. Numerous motorists and emergency vehicles were stranded across the county. Snowfall amounts of 6 to 12 inches were reported with several feet drifts. The De Baca County Courthouse and Detention Center lost heat during the blizzard. Fort Sumner lost power as well.

Heavy snow and high winds paralyzed much of the county through the 29th. A peak wind gust to 70 mph blew a metal roof off of a barn in House. Snowfall amounts of 8 to 15 inches were reported with several feet drifts. The 12.0 inches at San Jon tied the 5th highest 1-day total snowfall on record dating back to 1907. The 10.0 inches 3 miles south southwest of Ragland tied the 10th highest 1-day total snowfall on record dating back to 1935. Two shelters were opened in the county. Numerous motorists and emergency vehicles were stranded across the county. One individual was reported in critical condition at a local hospital.  Interstate 40 was closed through the entire county.

Heavy snow and high winds paralyzed much of southwest Chaves County through the 30th. Snowfall amounts of 12 to 15 inches were reported along with drifts of 3 to 4 feet. The 15.0 inches at Elk was the 2nd highest 1-day total snowfall on record dating back to 1895. All roads were closed across this area.

Heavy snow and high winds paralyzed much of this area through the 30th. Numerous motorists were stranded including rescue vehicles with the National Guard. Snowfall amounts of 8 to 16 inches were reported with snow drifts of 6 to 10 feet. Nearly every roadway in this area was closed.

Heavy snow and high winds paralyzed the entire county through the 30th. Numerous motorists were stranded across the county. A shelter at Vaughn High School housed 25 people during the storm. Snowfall amounts ranged from 4 to 8 inches along Interstate 40 and around 20 inches around Vaughn. Snow drifts ranged from 4 to 9 feet. Every road in the county was closed, including Interstate 40.

Heavy snow and strong winds paralyzed the entire area through the 29th. Numerous motorists were stranded on area roadways. Snowfall amounts up to 13 inches were reported around Clines Corners. Interstate 40 was closed for the entire duration of the blizzard event.

Heavy snow and strong winds paralyzed the entire area through the 28th. Snowfall amounts averaged 12 to 15 inches with even higher drifts. The 9.0 inches 4 miles north of Estancia was the 11th highest 1-day total snowfall on record dating back to 1904. Several motorists were stranded on area roadways. Emergency shelters were opened at the Lion's Club, the Moriarty Civic Center, and Moriarty High School. A state of emergency was declared for Torrance County. Interstate 40 was closed for the entire duration of the blizzard event.

Heavy snow and strong winds paralyzed much of the county through the 28th. A peak wind gust to 51 mph was reported at Mills Canyon. Treacherous travel conditions closed nearly every road in the county. Snowfall amounts varied dramatically from north to south across the county. Areas near Union County only picked up around 2 inches while folks along the Quay County border picked up 12 to 18 inches with large snow drifts.

Heavy snow and strong winds severely impacted eastern San Miguel County through the 28th. Snowfall amounts ranged from 4 to 8 inches however snow drifts piled up as high as 4 feet near Trementina. The 8.0 inches at Conchas Dam was the 11th highest 1-day total snowfall dating back to 1938. Several motorists were stranded on area roadways. Treacherous travel conditions were reported across the entire area.

Heavy snow and strong winds severely impacted the Interstate 25 corridor around Las Vegas through the 28th. Las Vegas airport reported a peak wind gust to 54 mph. Snowfall amounts ranged from 5 to 9 inches with drifts as high as 2 feet on the Las Vegas plaza. Treacherous travel conditions were reported.

Heavy snow and strong winds severely impacted the Interstate 25 corridor within Mora County through the 28th. The heaviest snow impacted the area around Wagon Mound where 6 to 12 inches fell. Snow drifts of 3 to 5 feet were common resulting in treacherous travel conditions. Areas farther north around Raton received little impact from this event however a peak wind gust to 60 mph was reported at the airport.

Heavy snow and high winds severely impacted Union County. A peak wind gust to 71 mph was reported at Clayton. Snowfall amounts were not nearly as high as areas farther south however white out conditions occurred for several hours with blowing snow. Most locales picked up between 2 and 4 inches. The Clayton Fire Department reported visibilities below 5 feet. Despite the low snowfall amounts drifts were still reported to be several feet high.

Heavy snow and high winds severely impacted far eastern portions of Colfax and western Union counties. Snowfall amounts were not nearly as high as areas farther south in New Mexico however white out conditions occurred for several hours with blowing snow. Most locales picked up between 2 and 5 inches, particularly around Des Moines and Folsom. Snow drifts were still reported to reach 2 feet. U.S. Highway 64/87 was closed during this event.

Heavy snow and high winds paralyzed much of eastern Lincoln County through the 30th. Snowfall amounts averaged 12 to 15 inches. The NM EOC reported that a several mile stretch of State Road 246 was buried in a drift up to 15 feet. All roads were closed across this area for a couple days. A large amount of livestock and range land animals were expected to have perished in this event.

Heavy snow and strong winds paralyzed the entire area through the 29th. Snowfall amounts averaged from 20 to 30 inches with drifts between 3 and 5 feet. Interstate 40 was closed for the entire duration of the blizzard event. The 17 to 21 inches around Sandia Park falls into the top 5 heaviest 1-day snowfall events for the record period 1939 to 2009. Many long time residents said this was the most significant blizzard event they have witnessed in the area.

Snowfall amounts ranged from 4 to 16 inches along the Interstate 25 and U.S. Highway 380 corridors. The 16.0 inches at Socorro tied the all-time 1-day total snowfall record set in 1960. Travel along Interstate 25 was treacherous and U.S. Highway 380 was closed from San Antonio east to Lincoln County. Numerous accidents were reported during the event.

Heavy snowfall and strong winds produced treacherous travel and whiteout conditions at times in portions of the metro area. Snowfall amounts ranged from 2 to 6 inches, with the highest amounts in the foothills and west mesa. A snow-hole area was observed around UNM where amounts were only near one-half inch. Other parts of the city were at a standstill with over 100 accidents reported and several roads closed, including Paseo del Norte and Tramway. Winds gusted to near 40 mph during the event while temperatures fell into the teens. A homeless man was found dead at a local park as a result of exposure to the elements.

Heavy snowfall and strong winds impacted mostly areas south of Santa Fe with this event. Snowfall amounts ranged from 1 to 8 inches, with the highest amounts in the area from Lamy to Stanley. A snow-hole area was observed around Santa Fe northward where amounts were less than 1 inch. The combination of north winds gusting near 50 mph and falling snow created severe travel impacts, particularly south and east of Santa Fe.
Snowfall amounts averaged 2 to 5 inches with gusty winds and blowing snow. Severe driving conditions were reported for a few hours along Interstate 40 between Grants and Albuquerque.

The eastern slopes of the Magdalena Mountains and western Socorro County were slammed with heavy snowfall and gusty winds in this event. Snowfall amounts averaged 21 inches around Magdalena. Severe travel conditions were reported along U.S. Highway 60 west of Socorro.

Heavy snow and high winds paralyzed much of the Ruidoso area through the 28th. Snowfall amounts averaged 12 to 20 inches. A peak wind gust to 59 mph was measured at Sierra Blanca Regional airport. Many roads were closed across the area with snow drifts of 3 to 5 feet, including along U.S. Highway 70. Several roads were closed for a couple days. Ski Apache reported a whopping 41 inches from this storm.

Heavy snowfall and strong winds paralyzed travel along the U.S. Highway 54 corridor around Carrizozo. Snowfall amounts averaged 8 inches with even higher drifts. A peak wind gust of 53 mph was reported around Carrizozo.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Heavy snowfall impacted the higher terrain areas of the west slopes with up to 21 inches at the Santa Barbara SNOTEL. Other lower elevation sites picked up generally 2 to 6 inches. Difficult driving conditions were reported around the area.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: Heavy snowfall amounts around 14 inches were reported at Red River and Taos Ski Valley. Other lower elevation sites picked up generally 2 to 6 inches. Difficult driving conditions were reported around the area.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: Heavy snowfall amounts averaged 15 to 20 inches in the high mountains east of Santa Fe. Difficult driving conditions were reported around the area.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Heavy snowfall and strong winds paralyzed portions of the east slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, particularly within Mora County. Snowfall amounts averaged 12 to 24 inches from Angel Fire southward, with up to 30 inches at San Ignacio. Mora County declared a state of emergency due to the heavy snowfall and impact to roadways.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: SNOTEL and ski sites over the area picked up between 10 and 18 inches of fresh snow. The heaviest snowfall occurred during the early morning hours of the 7th.
Numerous sources across the Taos region reported 3 to 6 inches of snow, the heaviest of which occurred late on the 6th. Significant impacts to travel and some closures were noted.
COOP observers reported between 3 and 7 inches across the area from Navajo Dam to Dulce. NM DOT reported difficult travel conditions through this area.
Observers reported between 3 and 8 inches of snow in the area from Lindrith to Cuba and Torreon. NM DOT reported difficult travel conditions through this area, including U.S. Highway 550.

COOP observers reported between 1 and 6 inches across the area from Gallup to Fence Lake. Much of the area started out as rain but transitioned to snow as very cold air arrived. NM DOT reported difficult travel conditions through this area, including Interstate 40.

COOP observers and SNOTELs reported between 8 and 12 inches from near Cuba to Wolf Canyon and Pajarito Mountains. NM DOT reported difficult travel conditions through this area, including highway 4. The road from Fenton Lake to Cuba was closed following this event.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Various observers across the area reported between 6 and 10 inches of fresh snow on the morning of the 8th. NM DOT reported difficult travel conditions through the area.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: Public and COOP observers across the area reported between 4 and 14 inches of fresh snow on the morning of the 8th. NM DOT reported difficult travel conditions, including Bobcat Pass. Persistent snowfall over several days worsened the impacts to travel.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: Public observers and SNOTELs across the area reported between 10 and 15 inches of fresh snow on the morning of the 8th. NM DOT reported difficult travel conditions, including Hyde Park. Persistent snowfall over several days worsened the impacts to travel.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Intense snowfall rates of 2 to 3 inches per hour during the evening of the 25th dumped between 24 and 30 inches of snowfall in the area from Chacon to Gascon and Ledoux. Areas farther north toward Angel Fire and Black Lake also picked up between 5 and 10 inches. The observer near Ledoux noted this was the heaviest snowfall event in many years.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: SNOTEL on the east slope of the southern exposure of the Sangre de Cristos Mountains reported a whopping 18 inches. Other areas across the mountains reported 3 to 7 inches.

Intense snowfall rates of 1 to 2 inches per hour during the evening of the 25th dumped 3 to 6 inches of snowfall in the area from Las Vegas to Ribera and Villanueva. Public reported this as a heavy wet snow.
Observers reported 4 to 8 inches of snowfall in a heavy burst on the evening of the 25th before slowly tapering off early on the 26th.
Spotters around the area from Corona east along state highway 247 reported near 7 inches of snowfall with intense snowfall rates during the evening of the 25th.

An intense band of snowfall impacted western Guadalupe County with high snowfall rates. Spotters reported between 3 and 7 inches over the area from near Vaughn northward toward Pastura and around Anton Chico.
An intense band of snowfall impacted De Baca County with high snowfall rates late on the evening of the 25th. Spotters reported between 3 and 5 inches across the county, including Fort Sumner.
Measured wind gust at the Raton ASOS.
Measured wind gust at Smokey Bear RAWS.
Snowfall amounts averaged 2 to 6 inches with gusty winds and blowing snow. Difficult to severe driving conditions were reported along U.S. 550 near Cuba.

Snowfall amounts varied from 2 inches in the valley bottoms near Datil as reported by several CoCoRaHS volunteers to as much as 13 inches at the Silver Creek Divide SNOTEL. Gusty winds and blowing snow resulted in difficult to severe driving conditions along portions of U.S. 60 west of Magadalena.

Snowfall amounts generally ranged between 5 and 16 inches.  Chama received just over a foot (13.5 inches) while Dulce farther west and lower in elevation received 4 inches. Gusty winds and blowing snow resulted in difficult to severe driving conditions throughout the region.

Snowfall amounts generally ranged between 6 and 12 inches. The Los Alamos area received between 6 and 8 inches while the higher elevation Quemazon SNOTEL picked up 11 inches. Gusty winds and blowing snow resulted in difficult to severe driving conditions throughout the region.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Snowfall amounts generally ranged between 6 and 18 inches with areas near and above 8500 feet picking up at least a foot of fresh powder. Gusty winds and blowing snow resulted in difficult to severe driving conditions throughout the region.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: Snowfall amounts generally ranged between 8 and 18 inches to include a foot of new snow in Red River.  The COOP observer in Eagle Nest reported 6 inches. Gusty winds and blowing snow resulted in difficult to severe driving conditions throughout the region.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: Snowfall amounts generally ranged between 10 and 20 inches, with reports of around 22 inches at Santa Fe Ski Basin. The COOP observer in Eagle Nest reported 6 inches. Gusty winds and blowing snow resulted in difficult to severe driving conditions throughout the region.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Snowfall amounts generally ranged between 7 and 17 inches, with the highest total reported at both Angel Fire Ski area and nearby CoCoRaHS observer. Gusty winds and blowing snow resulted in difficult to severe driving conditions throughout the region.

Snowfall amounts generally ranged between 3 and 6 inches, with the highest totals reported just northeast of Questa and Arroyo Seco.  Several CoCoRaHS observers reported 4 to 5 inches in the Taos area. Gusty winds and blowing snow resulted in difficult to severe driving conditions throughout the region.

The most impactful snowfall was observed at Raton Pass extending west and southwest to the east slopes of the northern Sangre de Cristo Mountains.  Snowfall amounts generally ranged between 4 and 10 inches with 8 inches at the Shuree Ponds SNOTEL site. Gusty winds and blowing snow resulted in difficult to severe driving conditions throughout the region.
Measured wind gust at North Oscura Peak WSMR Mesonet.
Measured wind gust at Phillips Hill WSMR Mesonet site.
Measured wind gust at Melrose Bombing Range RAWS.
Measured wind gust at Dora, West Texas Mesonet.
Measured wind gust at Buck Springs northwest of Roswell.
Measured wind gust at Clovis.
Measured wind gust from APRS at Milnesand.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: Kachina Peak at Taos Ski Valley reported peak wind gusts between 50 mph and 66 mph frequently for many hours. The strongest wind gust occurred at 6 am on the 18th.
Raton Airport reported a peak wind gust to 58 mph.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Numerous reports across the east slopes indicated between 2 and 12 inches of snow. The highest amounts were above 8500 feet around Angel Fire and west of Rociada. Minor impacts to travel were noted in this area. This was the first decent shot of fresh snow in the area in a couple weeks.

Several observers along the Colorado border north and east of Raton reported between 6 and 12 inches of snow. Gusty north winds and falling snow created near blizzard conditions for several hours during the overnight period. Travel along Interstate 25 between Raton and Raton Pass was very icy with whiteout conditions. U.S. Highway 87 was also severely impacted toward Capulin.

The combination of several inches of snow along with blowing snow produced very icy travel on Interstate 25 with near whiteout conditions at times around Raton. Areas farther southeast around Abbott also picked up several inches of snow.
Trained spotters from near Gladstone to Grenville reported 3 to 6 inches of snow. Blowing snow reduced visibilities to near zero at times along U.S. Highway 87.
Areas from the Valles Caldera east to Los Alamos reported high winds.
Trained spotter shared picture of several items tossed around from gusty winds in the parking lot of a commercial retailer along 4th street in Albuquerque.

Photo showed impressive dust devil swirling through a Clovis neighborhood around 520 pm. The dust devil tore up some yards and damaged an RV as it moved east northeast through the area. A porch and yard furniture were damaged.
A peak wind gust of 58 mph was reported at 131 pm MST in Stanley, NM.
A peak wind of 59 mph was reported at Sierra Blanca Regional Airport at 155 pm MST.
Peak wind of 66 mph reported at 338pm MDT. Blowing dust reduced visibility and impacted travel along Interstate 40.
Peak wind gusts to 73 mph reported at 330am MDT at Magdalena Ridge Observatory. The remainder of the Southwest Mountains experienced gusts near 50 mph.

Public reported a peak wind gust of 67 mph from the west around 915am MDT on the 23rd. The Tower RAWS also reported a peak wind of 64 mph late on the 22nd. A large tree was toppled onto a home in Los Alamos near Aspen Elementary School.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: CWOP site measured a peak wind gust of 63 mph at 556pm MDT to the northwest of Glorieta.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: The Kachina Peak station at Taos Ski Valley reported wind gusts between 60 and 70 mph for around 18 hours. The peak gust of 71 mph was reported at 400 pm MDT on the 22nd.
The top of Sandia Peak Tramway reported a peak gust to 61 mph at 400 pm MDT on the 22nd. The tram was closed to the public due to high winds that lasted through the 23rd.
Clines Corners reported high winds for an extended duration between the 22nd and 23rd. The peak wind gust of 62 mph was reported at 138pm MDT on the 23rd.
Sierra Blanca Regional airport reported several hours of high winds. The peak gust of 62 mph occurred at 415pm MDT on the 22nd. A small wildfire broke out on a hill behind Denny's in Ruidoso.
Las Vegas airport reported a peak gust to 59 mph at 929 pm MDT.
CWOP site at Sedan measured sustained winds near 40 mph for over an hour.
Railroad site near Vaughn reported peak sustained winds to 43 mph around 350 pm MDT.
Tucumcari airport.
Cannon Air Force Base reported a peak wind gust to 64 mph at 128 pm MDT.
Dora reported peak sustained winds up to 45 mph for several hours.
Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility reported a peak wind gust to 61 mph at 800pm MDT.
CWOP site reported several hours of sustained winds above 40 mph.

Persistent wind gusts near 55 mph wreaked havoc across the Albuquerque Metro. Several roads on the west side became impassable due to tumbleweed drifts. One home had tumbleweeds pile up to the second floor. Several weakened and dead trees were also knocked down by the strong winds. Property damage was limited to fences and light weight objects.

Sources around the area from Raton to Springer reported snowfall amounts ranging from 6 to 9 inches with blowing snow and reduced visibility. The 9 inches at Springer was a record snowfall for the date.

NMDOT closed Interstate 25 between Raton Pass and Raton. Numerous reports were received of closures along U.S. Highway 64/87 east of Raton as well. Sources around the area reported between 4 and 6 inches of snowfall with strong winds and reduced visibility.
A semi was blown over 8 miles west of Fort Sumner along U.S. Highway 60. Travel was impacted as officials turned the vehicle upright and cleaned up the roadway.
Cannon Air Force Base.
Clovis airport.
Melrose Bombing Range.
Sources around Red Hill reported numerous peak wind gusts of 58 mph while the Magdalena Ridge Observatory peaked out at 66 mph.
Gallup Municipal Airport reported several wind gusts between 58 mph and 63 mph during the early afternoon.
A weather station in the upper reaches of Juan Tabo Canyon reported sustained winds of 46 mph with a peak gust of 60 mph during the early afternoon.
Clines Corners reported peak wind gusts between 58 mph and 59 mph for a couple hours.
Several White Sands Missile Range stations reported peak winds near 60 mph during the early afternoon.
Carrizozo station reported peak wind gust of 65 mph.

Several stations around the Ruidoso area reported peak wind gusts between 58 mph and 68 mph for several hours during the afternoon. A 125 acre fire burning on Moon Mountain in Ruidoso was fortunately contained during these high winds. The Ruidoso High School was closed for 2 days due to fire suppression activities.
Dunken RAWS reported a peak wind gust to 59 mph.
Tucumcari.
Penny size hail just to the northeast of Clayton.
Hail ranged from quarters to half dollar size near Seneca.
An area of very low visibility from dense fog and snow resulted in a seven car pileup with reports of several injuries. Four were transported to local hospitals with non life threatening injuries.

Various sources reported between 5 and 12 inches of snow within the Jemez Mountains. This was a very heavy, wet snow event for the area with snow water equivalent values ranging from 1 to 2 inches. The Vallecito Subdivision south of Redondo Peak at 8,000 feet picked up an impressive 12 inches of snow.

Various sources reported between 6 and 18 inches of snow within the San Juan Mountains of Rio Arriba County. This was a very heavy, wet snow event for the area with snow water equivalent values ranging from 1 to 3 inches. Power outages were reported across the area for nearly 18 hours, including Chama.
Belen airport.
Clayton airport.
Virga bomb from a dry storm at the Santa Fe Airport.
Virga bomb from a dry storm at Mills Canyon.
Gallup Airport.

The NWS captured an impressive downburst with blowing dust from a virga shower late on the afternoon of the 23rd. The nearby Albuquerque Sunport reported a peak wind to 44 mph. However, beneath the microburst wind gusts were likely in excess of 60 mph.
Gallup.
Farmington.
Damage to fence in Rio Rancho resident's yard.
Sierra Blanca.
Penny size hail in Folsom.
A peak wind of 67 mph occurred below Embudo Canyon in the Albuquerque foothills. High winds were reported at the site for several hours.
Albuquerque Sunport.
Peak wind of 65 mph in Glenwood. Cement roofing tiles blown off home.
Local media shared photos of a large, dead tree down across Silver at Dartmouth. A pergola structure also collapsed at a home near Los Altos Golf Course.
Nickel size hail at Sumner Lake.
Quarter size hail near Stanley.
Hail up to the size of quarters accumulated several inches deep.
Hail up to the size of quarters accumulated several inches deep and impacted travel along Interstate 25.
Nickel size hail near La Cueva.
Quarter size hail impacting travel along Interstate 25.
Nickel size hail in the high terrain east of Santa Fe.
Quarter size hail near Seton Village.
Pea to nickel size hail near Tesuque.
Quarter size hail on Highway 406.
Quarter size hail.
Severe hailstorm with largest at half dollar size near Moses.
Angel Fire airport.
Penny size hail in Pleasanton.
Several inches of hail accumulated on Highway 550 near Counselor. Slick travel conditions resulted in a head-on collision between two vehicles. Nine people were injured, one critically.
Pea size hail started in Portales around 508 pm MDT then grew to quarter size at 514 pm MDT.
Very brief period of quarter size hail at home in Portales.
Quarter size hail near Portales.
Penny size hail in Clovis.
Quarter size hail near Clovis.
Half dollar size hail near Pleasant Hill.
Nickel size hail near Pleasant Hill.
Quarter size hail in Tucumcari.
Funnel cloud spotted with weak thunderstorm 5 to 6 miles southeast of Datil.
Quarter size hail in Chimayo.
Quarter to golf ball size hail in Bard.
Quarter size hail along Interstate 40 at mile marker 359 near San Jon.
Quarter to golf ball size hail southeast of Bard.
Golfball size hail just west of State Road 268 and County Road 18 north of Melrose.
Penny size hail along State Road 89.
Funnel cloud spotted along State Road 89 northeast of Tolar.
Spotter reported an extreme downburst wind ahead of storm with gust near 80 mph in Bingham. No damage was incurred.
Nickel size hail with torrential rainfall in House.
State Road 252 north and east of House closed due to severe flooding over the roadway. House reported 3.18 inches of rainfall in around 2 hours.
Public weather station at State Road 528 and Northern Boulevard reported a peak wind gust to 60 mph.

Playa lakes flooding into nearby streets and intersections. Numerous roads and intersections closed across town with 2 to 3 feet of water in some areas. A CoCoRaHS station on the north side of Clovis reported 4.17 inches of rainfall.
Cannon Air Force Base reported 4.03 inches in just over 24 hours. Flooding reported in low lying areas. No damage to structures.
State Road 268 closed due to severe flooding from mile marker 0 to 18 north of Melrose.

County roads 88 and 98 washed out, exposing pipes, water and utility lines. One vehicle was partially underwater at a nearby low water crossing. Mud, water, and debris were noted over State Road 76 and U.S. Highway 285.
Pojoaque Valley Arroyo flowing rapidly out of it's banks into nearby yards. Swift water rescues took place in the area. No significant property damage sustained.
Video along Interstate 25 through Raton Pass showed three to four inches of hail. A few hail stones appeared as large as a quarter. Travel was slowed to a halt.
Golf ball size hail on Interstate 40 at Clines Corners. Torrential rainfall near 2.5 inches also fell with this storm.
Quarter to golf ball size hail, with a few up to hen egg size, accumulated 2 to 4 inches deep along U.S. Highway 285. Three vehicles had to pulled out of ditches in the area.
Golf ball size hail smashed car windows at Flying C Ranch east of Clines Corners.
Roof partially torn off roller skating rink near Interstate 40 and Juan Tabo.
Tree blown over at home in Taylor Ranch.
Wall cloud and short-lived funnel cloud spotted near Moriarty.
Dust devil destroyed fence with four inch post supports.
One house, a barn, and several outbuildings burned between the 10th and the 11th.
Ping pong ball size hail east of Wagon Mound.
Portales.

The Dog Head Fire broke out on June 14th six miles northwest of Tajique, NM. The firely quickly spread eastward down the east slopes of the Manzano Mountains and burned 12 residences and 44 other structures. The fire scorced 17,912 acres. Most of the acreage was burned in the first three to four days of the fire. Showers and thunderstorms began impacting the fire area around June 22nd and continued for several days, significantly boosting containment.
Nickel to quarter size hail in Romeroville.
Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility.

Large hail and strong winds produced heavy damage to a residence eight miles east-southeast of Solano. Golf ball size hail and 75 mph were reported. Windows were busted out of. A power pole was broken off at the base. A 12 inch diameter tree limb was snapped off the tree. The large hail piled up three to four inches deep.
Quarter size hail near Mosquero. Strong winds ahead of the storm also broke off some tree limbs.
Tree limbs broken off trees near Mosquero.
Quarter size hail in Logan.
Power pole snapped off at base and large tree limbs snapped near Mosquero.
Strong thunderstorms winds flipped over a pop-up camper at Ute Lake State Park.

Torrential rainfall created flash flooding within Bell and Kennedy canyons west of the Beaverhead Ranger Station. Roads in the area were damaged due to high flows in ditches and arroyos. Low lying areas filled up with significant amounts of standing water. The ranger station reported 1.31 inches of rainfall however much higher amounts were likely within the canyons west of the area.
Half dollar size hail in Raton. Quarter size hail occurred for several minutes.
Hail ranged from pea size to half dollar size in Raton. Most of the stones were nickel to quarter sized. Spotter reported a quick 0.71 inches of rainfall as well.
Nickel hail west of Santa Rosa.
Dime to nickel size hail on I-40 west of Santa Rosa.
Pea to quarter size hail accumulated 2 to 3 inches deep in Wagon Mound.
Quarter size hail knocked lots of leaves off trees near Romeroville.
Baseball size hail destroyed brand new pickup truck.
Santa Fe airport reported a peak wind of 58 mph.
Half dollar size hail.
Landspout spotted near Chilili.

Lomas and Carlisle intersection closed due to high water. Many yards experienced damage to landscaping from flooding over curb levels. Particularly hard hit was area around Lafayette and Mountain within Summit Park neighborhood.
Intersection of Silver and Yale flooded. Cars reported flooded out in water across several areas of Nob Hill.
Gallup airport.
Dime to nickel size hail near Ponderosa.
Penny size hail for 2 to 3 minutes near Canones.
Nickel size hail at Northern and Unser.
High water, mud, rocks, and debris flowing across highway 165 from nearby dirt roads.
Large trees toppled into Santa Cruz River assisted destruction of a small bridge downstream from Santa Cruz Lake.
Las Huertas Creek flooded out of it's banks and up to back door of one home. No damage. Sand bags were requested.
Vehicle with two occupants washed into the Santa Cruz River and tumbled downstream. Both individuals were rescued with non life threatening injuries.

Video showed a torrent of water raging through the arroyo flowing up to the base of the highway 337 bridge at Chilili. Chopper footage also showed cattle and a rancher fleeing the flood wave upstream.
Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility reported a classic heat burst event with a peak wind gust of 73 mph.

Video footage showed torrent of water flowing down arroyo through Chilili up to base of the highway 337 bridge. Water was flowing out of bank into the yard of a nearby residence but no damage was sustained. Sandbags worked great to block the water from the home.
High water forced rocks, mud, and debris over Catwalk Road near Glenwood. Mineral Creek road was washed out east of Alma.
Roadways turned to a flooded, muddy mess south of Hospah.
Low water crossings flooded in Glenwood Hills neighborhood. Many residents also reported landscaping washed into streets at several homes in the area near Menaul and Juan Tabo.
Flood waters 2 to 3 feet deep on Aztec Road between 8th and 10th streets.
Mud slide covering portion of U.S. Highway 84 near Medanales.
Highway 56 flooded between 4th and 6th streets. One to two feet of water over the roadway in low spots. Road impassable.
Fairgrounds flooded.
Oil truck washed into Large Canyon at 5 mile bridge near CR7007. Body found outside of vehicle downstream.
Penny hail in Capulin.

Serious flash flooding developed on Salt Creek Wash and created major damage to a community near Mesa Farm Road. Three to four homes were severely damaged and one home was destroyed. Several vehicles, motorcycles, recreational vehicles washed into creek and destroyed. Water rescues occurred from roof tops and amazingly no one was killed.
Las Vegas Airport.
Funnel cloud near Taos. No damage.
Water flooding over highway 53 at mile markers 14 and 17.

A lightning strike in Albuquerque at the Ladera and Unser transfer station resulted in a massive power outage across central New Mexico leaving roughly 135,000 customers without power. During this outage, a motorcyclist that was stopped at a dark traffic light in Santa Fe was rear-ended by another vehicle and killed.
Nickel size hail at the Trail's End RV Park near La Cueva.
Pea size to penny size hail accumulated up to four inches deep on Interstate 40 near San Fidel and highway 124 near McCartys. One vehicle slid off the highway.
A trained spotter and the COOP observer for Ocate reported two brief funnel clouds.
A landspout tornado touched down briefly near Ojo Encino. No damage occurred.
Brief rope tornado touched down on a distant mesa near Capulin Volcano National Monument.

Water over roadway from heavy rainfall resulted in a hydroplaning accident along U.S. Highway 550 near the National Guard Armory north of Rio Rancho. Accident resulted in drivers of both vehicles being killed.

Lightning splintered a tree at the Los Alamos Golf Course near 16 Los Alamos High School Golf Team members and four coaches. The strike occurred at around 4 pm, about 300 feet away from where the team was practicing. Several of the students reported feeling a strong static electricity sensation flow through their bodies. Fortunately, no injuries occurred.
Nickel size hail east of Seneca.
Thunderstorm outflow produced a peak wind gust to 59 mph at Clayton.
Tucumcari.
Walnut Creek overflowing banks on Spence Road, Jackson Road, and Highway 2 southwest of Lake Arthur. Roadways impassable.
Nickel size hail in Alcalde.
At least three vehicles stalled in flood waters along county road 56A.
Vehicle overturned on highway 74 near mile marker 2 due to flood waters. Women was rescued from vehicle by fire department.
Water over U.S. Highway 84 in Hernandez near highway 74.
Over one foot of water surrounding homes near La Villita.
Numerous roadways flooded and impassable around Hernandez.

Two elderly residents rescued from a mobile home that was washed off it's foundation and displaced over 50 feet downstream. Up to 30 homes inundated with water and at least 10 families displaced from flood waters. U.S. Highway 285, highway 74, and county road 57 all closed to remove mud and debris. County Road 57 washed over with mudslides from nearby mesa.
Numerous roads flooded and impassable around Alcalde.
A rancher near Arabela reported a torrential rainfall amount of 3 inches from a thunderstorm that passed over his location. No flooding was reported.
Spotters reported a long duration funnel cloud west of Roswell from a very impressive thunderstorm.
Slight hail damage to vehicle.
Funnel cloud 13 miles west of Gallup near Interstate 40.

Three to four feet of water flowing over highway 337 near Tajique. Many arroyos flowing out of banks, culverts at maximum capacity, and large areas of standing water from near Tajique north toward Chilili.
Emergency Manager relayed a report of 3 inches of rainfall at Sapello. Heavy rainfall and a clogged culvert resulted in 8 to 12 inches of water flooding over highway 266.
Half dollar size hail in Roy.
Spotter observed a well-defined wall cloud with a funnel east of Arabela.
Father and daughter killed after entering a flooded arroyo.
High water flooding over low water crossings. Roads impassable.
Pleasanton recorded 3.50 inches of rainfall from the remnants of Hurricane Newton. No significant flooding was reported in nearby creeks and streams.

NMDOT reported that a mobile home was blown off a trailer from strong cross winds while in transport along U.S. Highway 60 between Socorro and Magdalena.
Tucumcari Municipal Airport reported sustained winds between 40 and 46 mph for several hours. A peak wind gust to 59 mph was also reported.
Peak sustained winds to 44 mph at Sedan.
Peak wind gust to 64 mph at the top of Sandia Peak Tram.
Up to 15 inches of snow fell around Dulce with up to 2 feet on nearby higher peaks. This snowfall set a new daily record for the 28th. Lighter amounts around 2 inches were reported near Navajo Dam.
Snowfall amounts across the high terrain of eastern Rio Arriba County ranged from 12 to 20 inches. The 17 inches reported at Chama on the morning of the 28th set a new daily record.
Snowfall amounts as high as 16 inches were reported by the Navajo Whiskey SNOTEL and the nearby COOP observer.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Snowfall amounts along the west facing slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains ranged from 6 to 12 inches. The highest amounts were reported in the area around Shady Brook.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: Snowfall amounts over the high terrain of Taos County ranged from 12 to 24 inches. Strong winds accompanied the heavy snowfall over the Taos Ski Valley where gusts up to 69 mph were reported.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: Snowfall amounts across the southern high peaks of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains east of Santa Fe ranged from 8 to 11 inches.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Snowfall amounts ranged from 10 to 15 inches around Angel Fire and Eagle Nest. Wind gusts up to 50 mph were reported with this snowfall.
Clines Corners reported peak wind gusts up to 64 mph with sustained winds as high as 50 mph for several hours.
The Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility Transwestern Pump Station reported peak wind gusts up to 68 mph with sustained winds up to 53 mph for several hours.

Sierra Blanca Regional Airport reported peak wind gusts as high as 78 mph for several hours. An observer near Nogal reported peak wind gusts up to 61 mph. Power outages were reported across much of the area around Ruidoso.
Sierra Blanca Regional Airport reported sustained winds as high as 63 mph for several hours.
The Moriarty Airport reported peak wind gusts up to 58 mph with sustained winds as high as 48 mph for several hours.
Observer at Fence Lake reported sustained winds as high as 52 mph for a couple hours. The Magdalenda Ridge Observatory reported a peak wind gust up to 84 mph around 10,000 feet during this period.
Numerous White Sands Missile Range sites reported peak wind gusts between 58 and 63 mph for a few hours. High sustained winds as high as 44 mph were also reported around Socorro.
A public weather station north of Tecolotito reported a peak wind gust to 68 mph. The Las Vegas Municipal Airport reported sustained winds as high as 45 mph during this period.
The Chupadera RAWS reported a peak wind gust up to 59 mph.
A public weather station along U.S. Highway 54 north of Carrizozo reported a peak wind gust up to 60 mph.
The Albuquerque International Airport reported high sustained winds up to 44 mph for a couple hours. Double Eagle Airport also reported high sustained winds of 40 mph.
The Albuquerque International Airport reported a peak wind gust up to 58 mph. The helipad on top of UNMH reported a peak wind gust up to 63 mph.
The Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility at Fort Sumner reported a peak wind gust up to 70 mph. Sumner Lake reported peak wind gusts up to 58 mph.

The Buck Springs weather station near Mesa reported a peak wind gust up to 72 mph with sustained winds as high as 51 mph. The Bitterlakes Wildlife Refuge RAWS station reported a peak wind gust up to 64 mph. The Roswell Industrial Airpark reported a peak wind gust up to 58 mph. A semi-trailer was overturned and damaged in powerful crosswinds along U.S. Highway 285 north of Roswell.

The Dora mesonet site reported a peak wind gust up to 72 mph. The Melrose Bombing Range reported a peak wind gust to 67 mph. An observer in Portales reported a peak wind gust to 61 mph. Blowing dust reduced the visibility to as low as 2 miles.
A public weather station near Sedan reported peak wind gusts up to 63 mph with sustained winds as high as 49 mph. The Clayton Municipal Airport reported a peak wind gust up to 58 mph.
The Dunken RAWS reported a peak wind gust up to 66 mph with sustained winds as high as 43 mph.
The Belen Airport reported a peak wind gust up to 61 mph.
The Tucumcari Municipal Airport reported a peak wind gust up to 68 mph with sustained winds as high as 52 mph. House reported a peak wind gust up to 61 mph with sustained winds as high as 47 mph.
The Union Pacific Railroad mesonet site near Vaughn reported a peak wind gust up to 59 mph with sustained winds as high as 50 mph.

The Clovis Airport and Cannon AFB weather stations reported peak wind gusts between 60 and 67 mph with sustained winds up to 54 mph for several hours. A portion of the roof of a Sonic drive-in was torn off in Clovis with no injuries. Numerous trees and power lines were also blown down across the Clovis area.
The top of the Sandia Peak Tram reported a peak wind gust up to 70 mph. Observers around Cedar Crest reported sustained winds as high as 42 mph.
Des Moines reported a peak wind gust up to 62 mph with sustained winds as high as 45 mph.
A wildfire broke out along State Road 236 and Roosevelt Road near Portales. The fire consumed nearly 100 acres. A shed was also destroyed.

The AWOS at Los Alamos also reported a peak wind gusts of 61 mph at 650am on January 29th. The general public reported a measured peak wind gust of 60 mph in Rio Rancho at 1208am on January 29th. High winds caused roof damage in Los Alamos. A portion of a roof was blown off an old barrack style apartment building. Two pine trees fell and damaged another roof at 47th Street and Urban Avenue, while a large pine tree behind Fuller Lodge fell and damaged a rose garden. Another tree snapped and fell onto a truck's camper shell on Torreon Street in Quemazon, causing damage. Many homes in Los Alamos lost shingles and there were a number of power outages.

The top of the Sandia Peak Tram reported a peak wind gust to 61 mph. Areas along the east slopes of the Sandia Mountains from the San Pedro Creek neighborhood to Edgewood reported peak winds up to 60 mph.
The Sierra Blanca Regional Airport reported peak wind gusts between 58 and 61 mph for several hours. Sustained winds were as high as 43 mph.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: Kachina Peak at Taos Ski Valley reported peak wind gusts between 70 and 80 mph for around 12 hours.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: The RAWS station near Ute Park reported a peak wind gust to 69 mph. The Angel Fire airport also experienced high wind gusts to 62 mph for several hours.
The Raton Crews Airport reported peak wind gusts up to 60 mph for several hours.
The CSBF Transwestern Pump station reported peak wind gusts up to 58 mph for several hours.
The Los Alamos National Lab weather network reported a peak wind gust up to 72 mph. The Los Alamos airport reported a peak wind gust up to 58 mph.
The Clayton Airport reported peak wind gusts up to 60 mph for several hours. The area around Sedan also reported peak wind gusts up to 60 mph with sustained winds as high as 45 mph.
The area from Las Vegas southeastward along U.S. Highway 84 to near Tecolotito reported peak wind gusts up to 61 mph.
The area around Harvey Ranch reported peak wind gusts up to 65 mph. Clines Corners reported peak wind gusts up to 63 mph.
Moriarty reported peak wind gusts up to 60 mph.
The Tucumcari Municipal Airport reported a peak wind gust up to 61 mph.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Numerous reports of whiteout conditions with strong winds and snowfall rates near two inches per hour. Snowfall amounts ranged from 10 to 16 inches in the area from Black Lake to Angel Fire and Eagle Nest. Peak wind gusts up to 54 mph were reported at the Angel Fire airport. Power outages occurred for several hours through the morning of the 24th.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: The high terrain of Taos County experienced whiteout conditions with high winds and snowfall rates near two inches per hour. Snowfall amounts ranged from 16 to 22 inches in the area from near Questa to Red River and the Taos Ski Valley. A peak wind gust to 63 mph was reported on Kachina Peak. Power outages occurred for several hours through the morning of the 24th.

The higher terrain along the Colorado border from near Costilla to Raton Pass and Capulin experienced whiteout conditions with high winds and snowfall rates near two inches per hour. Snowfall amounts ranged from 6 to 12 inches. A peak wind gust up to 68 mph was reported with the snowfall around Des Moines. Drifts up to 3 feet were reported at Capulin. Interstate 25 was closed for several hours at Raton Pass due to blizzard conditions.

Numerous observers in the area from Taos to Questa reported 3 to 8 inches of snowfall with snowfall rates as high as two inches per hour. The 1-day total of 8 inches at Taos broke the old record of 5 inches from 1920.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Numerous observations all along the west slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains reported between 10 and 22 inches of snowfall. The area around Questa picked up nearly 2 feet of snowfall in less than 12 hours.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: The Santa Fe Ski Basin and SNOTEL sites reported between 18 and 22 inches of snowfall with rates near two inches per hour. Strong winds were also reported across the high terrain.
Snowfall ranged from 2 inches across the lower elevations of Sandoval county to 14 inches near the Colorado border.
Snowfall reports ranged from 8 and 9 inches over northern Santa Fe and southern Taos county...to around 20 inches in the high mountains.
Snowfall amounts were generally in the 2 to 5 inch range at lower elevations, while 18 inches were reported in the Chuska mountains.

The ranger station in Glenwood reported Whitewater Creek and Little Creek were out of their banks. Water over state road 174 from Glenwood to Catwalk, and was 3 feet deep in one spot. White Water and Crabapple motels were flooded.
Thunderstorm outflow winds of 72 mph at Dora.
A thunderstorm near Clovis produced heavy rainfall, pea size hail, blowing dust, and a peak wind gust up to 60 mph.
Thunderstorm outflow winds peaked at 67 mph at Cannon AFB.
Raton airport.

An extended duration of high winds was reported from Clines Corners to Harvey Ranch and Duran. A peak wind gust to 70 mph was reported at Harvey Ranch and 59 mph at Clines Corners. Sustained winds as high as 55 mph were reported near Duran.

A brief virga shower that passed over the Albuquerque Sunport enhanced strong winds in the area with a peak gust to 67 mph. The area around Placitas also reported strong winds with gusts up to 63 mph.
Dunken.

An extended period of powerful wind gusts as high as 74 mph impacted much of the Interstate 40 corridor from Montoya to Tucumcari. Sustained winds were as high as 51 mph. Fortunately no significant damage or power outages were reported.

Powerful wind gusts up to 77 mph were reported along the U.S. Highway 285 corridor from near Mesa to Roswell. Several stations reported wind gusts in the 65 to 75 mph range with sustained winds near 50 mph.
The Moriarty airport reported sustained winds as high as 46 mph while Stanley reported a peak wind gust up to 61 mph.
Sustained winds as high as 44 mph were reported for a few hours around Las Vegas. A peak wind gust to 62 mph was reported north of Tecolotito.
Clayton reported an extended period of wind gusts near 60 mph.
The CSBF Fort Sumner location reported an extended period of peak wind gusts as high as 70 mph. Sumner Lake saw wind gusts as high as 61 mph.
Strong winds developed over Curry County behind a departing line of showers and thunderstorms. Sustained winds as high as 44 mph with gusts up to 60 mph were reported for a few hours.
Strong winds developed over Roosevelt County behind a departing line of showers and thunderstorms. Sustained winds as high as 45 mph were reported for a couple hours.

Observations around Sandia Park reported peak wind gusts up to 66 mph for an extended period early on the 24th. The top of the Sandia Peak tramway reported a peak wind gust to 60 mph late on the 23rd. Light snowfall amounts accompanied the strong winds above 8,000 feet.
Socorro airport.
The CSBF Transwestern Pump station reported peak wind gusts up to 62 mph with sustained winds up to 47 mph for several hours.
Mills Canyon.
Sierra Blanca Regional Airport.
Several White Sands Missile Range sites reported high wind gusts up to 58 mph.
Dunken RAWS wind gust peaked at 59 mph.
Dora.
Roswell Industrial Airpark reported high sustained winds over 40 mph periodically for almost 10 hours. A peak wind gust of 61 mph was also reported.
Dunken.
Buck Springs reported peak wind gusts between 58 mph and 62 mph for several hours.
Harvey Ranch.
CSBF Transwestern Pump station.
Snowfall amounts ranged from 5 inches in Jemez Springs to 10 inches near Seven Springs. The Los Alamos area picked up 2 to 4 inches as well.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Snowfall amounts along the western slope of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains ranged from 6 inches near Questa to 10 inches near Shady Brook. Difficult travel conditions were reported through this region mainly in the morning hours.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: Snowfall amounts ranged from 6 to 10 inches in the area from Red River to the Shuree SNOTEL. Difficult travel was reported across this area mainly during the morning hours.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Snowfall amounts along the east slope of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains ranged from  around 5 inches in Mineral Hill to 14 inches in Angel Fire and 6 inches around Ute Park. A band of snowfall that set up during the evening hours of the 4th produced snowfall rates of 2 inches per hour. Difficult travel conditions were reported.
A solid swath of snowfall amounts near 6 inches were reported from Raton Pass to Capulin. State Road 72 and U.S. Highway 64/87 were closed for nearly 24 hours from icy travel and blowing snow.
Snowfall amounts ranged from 2 to 3 inches in Raton to as much as 8 inches around Springer. Difficult travel conditions were reported mainly during the morning hours.

Snowfall amounts ranged from 3 to 6 inches in the area from Des Moines to Clayton. U.S. Highway 64/87 was closed for nearly 24 hours due to icy travel with blowing snow. The 5.5 inches of snow at Clayton on April 4th was the largest 24-hour total of the 2016-2017 winter season and a new record for the date.

The combination of 2 to 3 inches of wet snow followed by strong winds in the Farmington area resulted in several downed tree limbs and power lines. Many utility customers were without power throughout the day on the 4th. Damages to power lines have been estimated.
A public weather station near Tecolotito reported a peak wind gust to 68 mph. The Las Vegas airport reported a peak wind gust to 60 mph.

Peak wind gusts reached 58 mph or higher between 1130 am on the 3rd through 1010 am on the 4th with gusts between 58 and 71 mph. Sustained winds of 40 mph or higher occurred between 1030 am on the 3rd through 1250 pm on the 4th with speeds between 40 and 54 mph. A tree fell on a house in Ruidoso and power lines were down across roads near the Ruidoso Downs racetrack. There were numerous reports of power surges and outages.
Largest hail stones up to the size of golf balls.
Report relayed via Twitter of hail up to the size of half dollars.
Nickel size hail.
Report relayed via Twitter of hail up to the size of half dollars along U.S. Highway 82 at the Chaves and Otero county line.
Hail up to the size of quarters at the Roswell Correctional Facility.
Nickel size hail.
Hail accumulated 10 inches deep along State Road 442. Plows were dispatched to clear the roadway.
A weak landspout tornado developed roughly one mile east of U.S. Highway 285 between mile markers 160 and 165 northwest of Mesa, NM. No damage was observed with this storm.
Pea to quarter size occurred at the Capulin National Monument.
Six to 10 inches of snow fell over much of the northwest plateau, including in Farmington.

Three to 6 inches fell across the low elevations of the northwest mountains, while 1 to 2 feet fell in the high county, with an impressive 40 inches 2 miles north of Chama, near the Colorado border. The roof collapsed at the lone grocery store in Chama (Lowes Chama Valley Supermarket).
Snow amounts of 1 to 2 feet were common in the high country.

Accumulations of 4 to 8 inches of snow fell across the lower elevations while up to 3 feet of snow fell across the Chuska Mountains.  Drifts up to 7 feet were reported at Narbona Pass due to strong and gusty winds. Snow accumulation of 8.5 inches occurred in Gallup which caused multiple road closures.
Clines Corners.
Dunken.
Fort Sumner Airport.
Clines Corners.
Albuquerque Sunport reported a peak wind gust to 66 mph. Blowing dust reduced the visibility to six miles.
SNOTEL sites across the high terrain of eastern Rio Arriba County reported a quick burst of heavy snowfall with amounts between 6 and 11 inches in just 7 hours.

Various sources across the Jemez Mountains reported snowfall accumulations of 6 to 12 inches. The Los Alamos and White Rock areas picked up 4 to 8 inches of snowfall in less than 10 hours. Ponderosa reported a whopping 13 inches. Hazardous travel conditions were also reported by NMDOT.

events.cz_name: WEST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Local broadcast media reported via Twitter that heavy snow fell along the west slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, including 8 to 16 inches around Tres Ritos. Severe driving conditions were reported through mountain passes by NMDOT.

events.cz_name: NORTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET/RED RIVER
events.event_narrative: Snowfall amounts up to one foot were reported within the high terrain of Taos County. Severe driving conditions were reported through the high terrain by NMDOT.

events.cz_name: SOUTHERN SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS ABOVE 9500 FEET
events.event_narrative: Snowfall amounts near one foot were reported within the high terrain east of Santa Fe. Severe driving conditions were reported through the high terrain by NMDOT.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES OF THE SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Spotters and COOP observers within the Moreno Valley reported 10 to 16 inches of snowfall. The 11 inches at Gascon set a new daily record for April 29th, breaking the previous record from 1953.

Various sources across the Santa Fe metro area reported very impressive snowfall amounts of 6 to 12 inches. The heaviest amounts occurred in the area from the Santa Fe Plaza to Lamy and Eldorado where near one foot of snow fell.

Various sources across the East Mountain communities within the Sandia and Manzano mountains reported snowfall amounts between 6 and 12 inches. Severe travel conditions developed in this area. A few sites set new daily records for snowfall on April 29th. Travel was severely impacted across portions of this area.

Various sources along the western portions of the Estancia reported snowfall amounts between 6 and 10 inches. The 6.7 inches of snow at Stanley set a new daily record for April 30th, breaking the previous record from 1954. Severe travel conditions developed along Interstate 40 around the Edgewood and Moriarty area.

The combination of roughly 2 to 4 inches of snowfall, strong winds, low visibility, and temperatures in the 20's produced severe travel conditions along the Interstate 40 corridor around Clines Corners.

Observers in the area from Raton Pass to Folsom and Des Moines reported generally 4 to 8 inches of snow with strong winds and low visibility. Snow drifts to 18 inches were also reported. Interstate 25 at Raton Pass and U.S. Highway 64/87 were closed for over 12 hours.
Various sources around the Las Vegas area reported between 3 and 5 inches of snowfall. NMDOT reported severe driving conditions with slick travel and low visibility.

The Clayton COOP observer reported a new daily record snowfall of 7.5 inches for April 29th. This was also the greatest 24-hour snowfall of the entire winter season. Grenville also set a new daily record snowfall amount of 5.0 inches. U.S. Highway 64/87 was closed for several hours due to extreme winter travel conditions.
The Mosquero COOP observer reported a new daily record snowfall of 8.0 inches for April 29th.

Several trees blown down along CR5173. One fell onto home with damage to roof and windows. Trees also blown down onto power lines in nearby area of Bloomfield. Power outage reported for four to five hours.
Power poles blown over onto roadway in Aztec. Minor damage reported to several vehicles.
Raton Airport.
Roswell Airport.
Nickel size hail.
Hail up to the size of ping pong balls reported in Fort Sumner.
Multiple rounds of hail with the largest stones up to quarter size a couple different times over the 20 minute period.
First round of hail with stones up to the size of quarters.
Quarter size hail.
Second round of large hail with stones up to the size of ping pong balls.
Hail up to the size of golf balls west of House.
Hail up to the size of half dollars near Roy.
Hail up to the size of golf balls in Roy.
Nickel to quarter size hail 10 miles east-southeast of Maes.
Brief tornado touchdown six miles north-northeast of Roy.
Hail up to the size of quarters.
Nickel to quarter size hail on the west side of Roswell.
Penny size hail north of Newkirk.
Quarter size hail north of Newkirk.

Radar estimated 4 to 8 inches of rainfall over a large area of the Alamogordo Creek drainage. The creek nearly reached the base of the U.S. Highway 84 bridge near Sumner Lake. Several low water crossings northeast of this area along the creek washed out.

Many residents of Santa Fe awaken by a severe storm with heavy rain and hail to the size of quarters or larger. Damage occurred to vehicles, roofs, skylights, and trees were stripped of leaves. Damages are estimated.
Dime to quarter size hail reported near Fruitland and Nenahnezad.
Thunderstorm moving over Tajique produced penny size hail.
A funnel cloud was spotted southeast of state roads 337 and 55.
Hail up to the size of pennies reported at La Cueva.
Hail up to the size of quarters reported in Moriarty.
Funnel cloud southwest of Quay moved north/northwest toward the I-40 corridor.
Quarter size hail near Corona.
Quarter size hail for five minutes southeast of Cedarvale.

A major hailstorm pummeled the area around San Felipe and Kewa pueblos and Interstate 25. Hail accumulated to several inches deep. Strong winds with the hail produced damage to roofs, windows, and several vehicles. Damage amounts are estimated.
Quarter size hail accumulated six inches deep along state highway 337 northeast of Tajique. One vehicle slid off the road into a ditch.
Emergency manager spotted a brief funnel cloud to the northeast of Carrizozo.
Quarter size hail lasted for one minute at Clines Corners.
Hail up to the size of pennies on the southwest side of Santa Fe.
Wind gusts near 65 mph snapped off a large tree limb in Santa Fe. A local horse stable sustained roof damage and a large tree was uprooted. Damages are estimated.

Storm chaser captured video of a tornado on the ground along Interstate 40 near Clines Corners. Other observers in the area reported the tornado touched down just south of Interstate 40 around 1215 pm MDT then moved north-northwest into extreme far southeast Santa Fe County over a 20 minute period. Trees were uprooted in the area.

A severe thunderstorm crossed Interstate 25 east of the Santa Fe airport then moved north along NM-599. This storm produced a brief EF-0 tornado 2.8 miles northeast of the Santa Fe airport, near NM-599 and Agua Fria, then tracked toward the north for approximately 0.3 miles. Mainly localized and minor damage was observed with this tornado event. The Santa Fe Airport tower personnel also spotted a funnel cloud north of the airport.
Nickel to quarter size hail accumulated three inches deep near Turley.
Several observers around Carrizozo reported a well developed funnel cloud near Carrizo Mountain a couple miles northeast of town.
Quarter size hail along CR-502 near El Rancho covering the roadway.
Quarter size hail in Pecos.
Hail up to the size of ping pong balls in Anton Chico.
Hail up to the size of golf balls northeast of Anton Chico.
Hail up to the size of half dollars reported along Interstate 40 at mile marker 252.
Wind gust at least 60 mph with damage to small tree limbs.
Dime to nickel size hail near NM-528 and Corrales Road.
Penny size hail in Rio Rancho.
Media crew with KRQE spotted a funnel cloud just north of Interstate 40 near U.S. Highway 84.
Storm chasers spotted a well developed tornado east of Interstate 25 a few miles northeast of Wagon Mound.
The first funnel cloud in a series spotted west-northwest of Portales.
Thunderstorm outflow crossing White Sands Missile Range produced a peak wind gust to 65 mph.
Thunderstorm outflow crossing White Sands Missile Range produced a peak wind gust to 65 mph.
Decaying thunderstorm outflow produced a peak wind gust to 62 mph near Adelino.

Decaying thunderstorms well south of Albuquerque generated a peak wind gust to 63 mph at the Sunport. Sustained winds were as high as 50 mph. Visibility fell to three miles in blowing dust at the Sunport and as low as one quarter mile in downtown Albuquerque.
Several trees, power poles, and power lines were blown down across downtown Albuquerque.
Observers at Cannon Air Force Base reported the second funnel cloud produced from a severe thunderstorm moving northeast from Roosevelt County into Curry County.
Quarter to hen egg size hail reported at a Cannon Air Force Base housing complex.
Hail up to the size of ping pong balls reported on the north side of Cannon Air Force Base.
Damaging hail storm with at least hen egg size hail. Two windows broken at residence and two windshields smashed out. Damage amounts are estimated.
Hail at least the size of half dollars fell a couple miles southeast of Tucumcari.
The third funnel cloud was spotted from a severe thunderstorm moving northeast across Curry County.
The fourth funnel cloud was reported from a severe thunderstorm moving northeast across Curry County. No touchdown was confirmed by an NWS storm survey.

The NMSU Agricultural Science Center northeast of Clovis reported major damage from a severe hail storm. Hail estimated at least to the size of hen eggs produced a major crop loss at the facility. Damage amounts are estimated.
The COOP observer north of Clovis reported half dollar size hail.
Outflow winds on the front side of an approaching thunderstorms downed several small tree limbs around Clayton. Pea size hail accumulated four inches deep.
Clayton airport.
Thunderstorm wind gusts estimated between 60 and 70 mph with dime size hail.
A weather station near Sedan reported a peak wind gust to 60 mph.
Hail began falling at nickel size on the south side of Roswell. Severe hail moved into the area after this report.
Quarter to half dollar size hail covered the ground in Roswell.
Hail up to the size of golf balls on the west side of Roswell.
Hail up to the size of nickels on the northwest side of Roswell.
Quarter size hail at Wyoming and Alameda in Roswell.
Hail up to the size of ping pong balls fell on the northwest side of Roswell.
Hail up to the size of half dollars on the north side of Roswell shredded leaves, small tree branches, and the vegetable garden.
Hail up to the size of half dollars northeast of Roswell.
A second thunderstorm moved into Roswell and produced nickel size hail.
Hail up to the size of quarters one mile south of Pep in association with a tornado warned thunderstorm.

Observer reported hail up to the size of quarters southwest of Portales.

A brief tornado touched down near NM-72 and moved northeast over rural countryside toward the Colorado border.
A funnel cloud was spotted just north of U.S. Highway 87 west of Capulin.
Hail up to the size of quarters in Hernandez.
Laguna.

Radar estimates and surface observations indicated an area of very heavy rainfall associated with a collapsing thunderstorm near House. Employees at the New Mexico Wind Energy Center observed large areas of standing water the following morning.
The Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility Transwestern Pump station reported sustained winds near 40 mph and gusts to 58 mph.
A public CWOP station in Clovis reported a peak wind gust of 60 mph. The Clovis Airport reported a peak wind gust of 61 mph.
A public CWOP station at Buck Springs reported high sustained winds for several hours with a peak speed of 47 mph.

Melrose Bombing Range.
Santa Rosa Route 66 Airport.
Tucumcari Municipal Airport.

Hail up to the size of nickels. Heavy rainfall created areas of standing water.
Two inch hail 13 miles north of Fort Sumner on U.S. Highway 84.
Hail up to the size of quarters at Sumner Lake.
Penny size hail at the NM Wind Energy Center.
Quarter size hail on Interstate 40 four miles west of Santa Rosa.

Two inch hail on State Road 20.

Hail up to two inches in diameter along U.S. Highway 70.
Golf ball size hail along U.S. Highway 380.
Half dollar size hail along U.S. Highway 380.
A funnel cloud was spotted near Las Vegas.
Farmington.

Hail up to the size of quarters northeast of Grenville.
Hail up to the size of quarters from the second storm in a row northeast of Grenville.
Hail up to the size of quarters near Seneca.
Heavy rain on January 27th caused the West Fork of the Gila River to leave its banks and severely damage a bridge on state highway 15 near the Gila cliff dwellings.
Chaser reported a tornado east/southeast of Santa Rosa on the ground for 10 minutes.

Two Forest Service employees were caught between two flooded Forest Service roads on the North Fire burn scar. Each road dipped into an arroyo where the water was bank-full.  They waited out the flood before leaving the area.

Storm chaser video showed the well-developed funnel cloud spotted by many observers near Carrizozo touched down for about one minute. An area of dust was observed swirling on the ground beneath a solid condensation funnel elevated off the ground. No damage observed.
Peak wind gust to 61 mph at Buck Springs.
Penny size hail in Farley.

A vehicle traveling northbound on Interstate 25 crashed into a divider in the center of the highway near mile marker 340. A semi truck jack knifed attempting to avoid the crash and caused a chain reaction that resulted in a 20 car pileup. Two motorists were killed in separate vehicles and numerous injures were reported. The two fatalities were identified as 52-year old Nathaniel Gerry Hurwitz of Albuquerque, New Mexico and 35-year old David Franklin Halward of Scotts Valley, California. The interstate was closed down for more than 12 hours. Damage amounts are estimated for 20 vehicles, including the contents of several semi trucks.

Severe drought conditions were declared for Curry County on January 16, 2018. Most of this area had not received measurable precipitation in nearly four months. Patchy blowing dust had already been reported with a few of the stronger wind events by late January. A wildfire that erupted near Ned Houk State Park north of Clovis rapidly grew to near 2,000 acres with strong winds on January 23, 2018.

Severe drought conditions were declared for Quay County on January 16, 2018. Most of this area had not received measurable precipitation in nearly four months. Patchy blowing dust had already been reported with a few of the stronger wind events by late January. Record high temperatures were set at the Tucumcari airport on several days in late January 2018.

Severe drought conditions were declared for Union County on January 16, 2018. Portions of this area had not received measurable precipitation in nearly four months. Patchy blowing dust had already been reported with a few of the stronger wind events by late January. A couple record high temperatures were set at the Clayton airport by mid to late January 2018.

Severe drought conditions were declared on January 2, 2018 across the San Francisco River Valley from near Reserve to Glenwood. Most of this area had not received measurable precipitation in over three months with above normal temperatures.

Severe drought conditions were declared on January 23, 2018 for the Northwest Plateau region from Shiprock to Farmington, Bloomfield, and the Navajo Reservation. Much of the area had not reported measurable precipitation in over three months with above normal temperatures. A couple quick-hitting, weak storm systems brought only very light precipitation to the area in early January.

Severe drought conditions were declared on January 23, 2018 for the Far Northwest Plateau region from Navajo Reservoir to Dulce. Precipitation was well below normal over the area during the last three months of 2017 with above normal temperatures. A couple quick-hitting, weak storm systems brought only very light precipitation to the area in early January.

Severe drought conditions were declared on January 23, 2018 for the Chuska Mountains. Precipitation was well below normal over the area during the last three months of 2017 with above normal temperatures. A couple quick-hitting, weak storm systems brought only very light precipitation to the area in early to mid January.

Severe drought conditions were declared on January 23, 2018 for the Northwest Highlands area from near Lindrith to Cuba and Torreon. Precipitation amounts were near zero over the area during the last three months of 2017 with above normal temperatures. A couple quick-hitting, weak storm systems brought only very light precipitation to the area in early to mid January.

Severe drought conditions were declared on January 23, 2018 for the West Central Mountains from near McGaffey to El Malpais and the Zuni Mountains. A landspout tornado produced a narrow swath of damage near Eagle Nest. This is the first documented tornado in the Moreno Valley since at least 1950. The landspout tornado also exhibited anti-cyclonic rotation during its entire lifecycle. It had a classically narrow condensation funnel cloud and formed in a vast open area just|west of U.S. 64 between mile markers 283 and 284 near Pepper Sauce Camp. The landspout tornado crossed U.S. 64 very near Elk Lane Rd. tracking slightly north of due east until dissipating over the northeast portion of Eagle Nest Lake. Elevations along the track ranged from approximately 8350 feet to 8175 feet. Approximately 180 feet of barbed wire/picket fence was downed and damaged. Several steel t-posts were sheared or bent nearly 90-degrees. All 10 units that comprise the Pepper Sauce Camp property suffered damage.  All but two of sixteen west-facing windows were partially or completely destroyed by flying debris. Windows and storm doors at the main building were partially or completely busted. A small car that was parked and facing east had|all but the front windshield busted out. The bed of an old truck used as a marketing sign was lifted and carried about 50 feet toward the southwest. The front windshield of an old Chevrolet C65 truck was struck no less than 75 times by flying debris but remained intact while both side windows were completely busted out. An old hay barn was collapsed and roofing material  found 300 feet away. An unoccupied fifth wheel recreational vehicle with an estimated weight of 12,000 pounds was partially lifted, shifted and rolled on its side at the Eagle Nest Campground.  Two other RVs sustained|damage to include busted windows, including a Class A diesel pusher (dry weight 32,000 pounds) that was oriented nearly perpendicular to the tornado`s path. Damage amounts have been estimated.

Just before 6 pm MDT on Tuesday, March 12, 2019, a tornado touched down in Chaves County, about 15 miles south southwest of Dexter. The tornado moved north northeast for approximately 15 minutes before dissipating about one half mile northeast of the community of Dexter. Six people suffered minor injuries, and six homes were substantially damaged or completely destroyed. An additional dozen homes and structures also sustained minor to moderate damage. This was the first March tornado documented in Chaves County since 1959, and the earliest known EF1 or stronger tornado in the state of New Mexico. The NWS surveyed damage from a strong tornado that impacted parts of southern Roosevelt County during the early evening of Sunday, May 26, 2019. The tornado lasted nearly 30 minutes and tracked about 10 miles over predominately rural ranch/farmland in southern Roosevelt County. No injuries were reported. Two known properties were impacted: one 4 miles southeast of Dora and another approximately 5 �� miles east-northeast of Dora. Additionally, considerable damage to electrical infrastructure was noted including ten consecutive power poles snapped several feet above the ground 1-2 miles east of Rogers on the north side of NM 237. Farther southwest, several high voltage power poles/structures were partially collapsed and associated lines downed 2-3 miles south-southeast of Dora. A well-built hay barn that was originally an early 20th century church was completely destroyed. A power pole was snapped 12 feet above the ground,  lofted at least 10 feet and driven into the ground 100 yards away. Partial ground scouring was noted along State Road 114 where the tornado crossed near Roosevelt County Rd. M. Based on assessed damage, wind speeds were estimated to be in the 120-130 mph range. Damage estimates are estimated for residential and infrastructure.

The Roswell airport set a new daily record maximum rainfall amount of 3.44 for October 1st, breaking the previous record of 1.54 from 1998. The entire family of seven was displaced into a hotel for several nights. Damage amounts are estimated for significant damage to the home and loss of most items inside.
