Torrential rainfall over southern Chaves County led to flash flooding and large areas of ponding water over many roadways from near Dexter south to Hagerman. An observer a few miles west of Lake Arthur along Walnut Creek reported a whopping 6.50 of rain in 24 hours. State Road 2 was closed between Darby and Orchard Park roads, State Road 267 was closed between mile markers 11 and 15, U.S. Highway 285 was closed at Chikashaw Road, and State Road 409 was closed along the entire section leading to Bottomless State Park due to falling rocks and high water. Several roads were also closed throughout the community of Dexter. At least two vehicles were inundated in flood waters and motorists had to be rescued by emergency personnel. Fortunately, no one was injured during this flooding event. Damage amounts are estimated for total losses to two vehicles.
A CoCoRaHS observer near Causey reported a whopping 6.87 of rain in just 24 hours. State Road 267 was closed due to flash flooding between mile markers 11 and 15 west of Portales.

Additional record rainfall on October 3rd led to another round of flash flooding around Roswell, Lake Arthur, and Portales. The Roswell airport set a new daily record rainfall of 0.95 for October 3rd, breaking the previous record of 0.89 set in 2015. The Bitter Lake Wildlife Refuge set a new daily record rainfall of 1.43 for October 3rd. A trailer park community along U.S. 285 was inundated with water and one home was damaged by flood waters. The area along State Road 2 and U.S. 285 between Jackson Road and Pueblo Road southwest of Lake Arthur was closed due to high water. State Road 409 was closed again due to flash flooding leading to the Bitter Lake Wildlife Refuge. Fortunately, no injuries were reported with the second round of flooding. Damage amounts are estimated for water damage to one trailer home.

The Trigo Wildfire began on the west slopes of the Manzano Mountains and was initially spread by southwest wind gusts to 35 mph. The fire reached Osha Peak during the evening of April 16th. On the 20th, the fire spread rapidly northeast due to 40 mph winds. It entered flatter terrain on the east side of the Manzanos, and by April 21st, 3750 acres were burned including nine homes, nine outbuildings and two recreational vehicles. The 4800 acre fire was 95 percent contained by April 29th, but was fanned by strong southwest winds of 40 to 50 mph on the 30th, forcing the evacuation of Sufi and Apple Mountain Campgrounds and the Sherwood Forest subdivision, west of Torreon.  Over 50 additional homes and one communications tower were damaged or destroyed, mainly in the Sherwood Forest area as the fire grew to more than 11,000 acres.  The fire continued to be uncontained into the month of May.

events.cz_name: MIDDLE RIO GRANDE VALLEY/ALBUQUERQUE METRO AREA
events.event_narrative: The Albuquerque Sunport measured damaging wind gusts between 58 mph and 71 mph for several hours as gap winds plowed through Tijeras Canyon. Dozens of large trees were toppled across the city, including; one tree along Girard just south of Gibson, one tree along Sunport Loop near the Sheraton hotel, at least one tree on the University of New Mexico campus, and other large trees at Roosevelt Park and Hyder Park. A large pine tree at Jefferson Middle School fell over power lines along Girard Blvd. Another large pine tree fell over power lines into Girard near Campus Blvd. Roofing was damaged at the city courthouse in downtown Albuquerque and another roof was damaged at a hotel near the Sunport. Thousands of PNM customers were without power for one to two days and some others were without power for three to four days. Damage amounts are a rough estimate for damage to power infrastructure, roofs, and fences.

Two observers near the Taos airport reported wind gusts between 63 mph and 71 mph as powerful gap winds surged into the Upper Rio Grande Valley. Minor damage was reported to a portal at one residence.
The Santa Fe airport reported sustained winds between 40 mph and 47 mph for several hours as gap winds pushed through the area.

events.cz_name: MIDDLE RIO GRANDE VALLEY/ALBUQUERQUE METRO AREA

Dozens of large trees were toppled across the city, including; one tree near Lomas and Eubank, one at City View park near Copper and Tramway, one tree near Central and Wyoming, and another tree along Central east of Tramway. Roof damage was reported to one home near I-40 and Eubank. A concrete wall and fence were toppled near I-40 and Louisiana. Thousands of PNM customers were without power for one to two days and some others were without power for three to four days. Damage amounts are a rough estimate for damage to power infrastructure, roofs, and fences.
A peak wind gust up to 89 mph was measured at the top of the Sandia Peak Tramway. The tram was closed for the day due to high winds.

Local media reported that fire and rescue teams evacuated around 50 campers at the Rio Chama RV park around 100 am due to falling tree branches. The weight of heavy snow on fully leafed out trees along with strong winds toppled dozens of large branches. At least one recreational vehicle was destroyed and another one was damaged. Minor injuries were reported however the extent of the injuries was not known. Damage amounts are estimated for total loss of two small RVs.

Strong southwest winds in advance of an approaching storm system downed a 30 inch diameter tree near Ruidoso. A set of power lines was also damaged as the tree fell. Damages are estimated for a short section of power lines.

The combination of strong southwest winds aloft and virga showers developing ahead of an approaching storm system resulted in high winds at the Farmington airport. Peak wind gusts between 58 mph and 71 mph occurred with several of these virga showers.
Snowfall amounts of six to 11 inches were reported in the area from Cuba to Torreon Navajo Mission. Low visibility and hazardous travel conditions occurred along U.S. Highway 550.
Snowfall amounts of four to nine inches were reported in the area around Grants. Low visibility and hazardous travel conditions occurred along Interstate 40.

Various stations within the Tusas Mountains reported snowfall amounts between 10 and 20 inches with very low visibility in heavy snow. Chama reported between five and seven inches with this storm system.

Various stations within the Jemez Mountains reported snowfall amounts of one to two feet with intense snowfall rates. The 21 inches at Wolf Canyon on October 26th set a new daily record and the storm total of 23 inches set a new monthly record snowfall for October. Records at Wolf Canyon date back to 1912.
Snowfall amounts ranged from eight to 16 inches in the area from near Glorieta to Rowe.
Various stations reported between one and two feet of snow in the area around Taos Ski Valley and Red River. The 12.6 inches reported at Red River on October 26th set a new daily record.

events.event_narrative: Various stations reported between six and 14 inches of snow in the area from Mora to Angel Fire and Eagle Nest. The 14 inches reported at Eagle Nest on October 26th set a new daily record and the storm total of 20 inches set a new monthly record snowfall for October. Records at Eagle Nest date back to 1929.
Various stations around Taos reported between eight and 14 inches of snowfall.
Various stations around Espanola reported between three and five inches of snowfall.
Various stations around Santa Fe reported between four and seven inches of snowfall.

events.cz_name: MIDDLE RIO GRANDE VALLEY/ALBUQUERQUE METRO AREA
events.event_narrative: Various stations across the Albuquerque metro area reported between four and 12 inches of snow with low visibility and severe travel conditions. Strong gap winds with gusts up to 58 mph at the Sunport resulted in a well-defined convergence band on the west side where 10 to 12 inch amounts were common. The 4.4 inches storm total snowfall at the Albuquerque Sunport set a new record snowfall for the month of October. Well over 100 motor vehicle accidents were reported and Interstate 40 was closed down at least once. Damage amounts are estimated for numerous vehicles however the extent of any injuries is unknown.
Various stations across the Socorro area reported snowfall amounts of two to five inches.
Various stations in the Sandia and Manzano mountains reported between five and 10 inches of snow with gusty winds, low visibility, and hazardous travel conditions.
Various stations in the Estancia Valley from Moriarty to near Mountainair reported between four and eight inches of snow.
Snowfall amounts of three to six inches were reported along the U.S. Highway 285 corridor from Encino to Clines Corners along with low visibility and gusty winds.
Snowfall amounts of three to six inches were reported in the area from near Mountainair to near Corona.
Various stations across the Ruidoso area reported between five and 10 inches of snow. A brief period of freezing rain was also reported toward the start of the storm.

events.cz_name: JOHNSON AND BARTLETT MESAS INCLUDING RATON PASS
events.event_narrative: Various stations reported between four and seven inches of snow from near Raton Pass to Capulin and Folsom. Areas much farther west toward Vermejo Park reported locally higher snowfall amounts in excess of 18 inches. Gusty north winds resulted in some areas of blowing and drifting snow with reduced visibility on the morning of the 28th.

Various stations reported between three and six inches of snow along the Interstate 25  corridor from Raton south to Springer. Blizzard-like conditions began on the morning of the 28th as strong north winds resulted in blowing and drifting snow.

The combination of snow and strong north winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting snow with low visibility along Interstate 25 and U.S. Highway 56 east of Springer. Snow drifts of one to four feet were reported over parts of the area. NMDOT reported severe travel along Interstate 25 and closed U.S. 56 due to impossible travel conditions.

Various stations across Union County reported between eight and 12 inches of snow. Three consecutive daily snowfall records were set at Clayton on the 26th, 27th, and 28th. The storm total snowfall of 12.2 inches set a new record snowfall for the month of October at Clayton. Blizzard-like conditions began on the morning of the 28th as strong north winds produced considerable blowing and drifting snow.

The combination of snow and strong north winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting snow with low visibility along U.S. Highway 56 west of Clayton. Snow drifts of one to four feet were reported over parts of the area. NMDOT closed U.S. 56 due to impossible travel conditions.

Various stations across Harding County reported between eight and 16 inches of snow. Blizzard-like conditions began on the morning of the 28th as strong north winds produced considerable blowing and drifting snow.

The combination of snow and strong north winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting snow with low visibility over Harding County. Snow drifts of one to three feet were reported over parts of the area.

Various stations across eastern San Miguel County reported between 10 and 20 inches of snow. Blizzard-like conditions began on the morning of the 28th as strong north winds produced considerable blowing and drifting snow. Conchas Dam and Mosquero reported two daily record snowfalls on the 27th and 28th. The 12.5 inches storm total at Conchas Dam set a new record monthly snowfall for October.

The combination of snow and strong north winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting snow with low visibility over eastern San Miguel County. Snow drifts of one to three feet were reported over parts of the area.

Various stations across Quay County reported between eight and 16 inches of snow. Blizzard-like conditions began on the morning of the 28th as strong north winds produced considerable blowing and drifting snow. Severe travel conditions were reported along Interstate 40 near Tucumcari.

The combination of snow and strong north winds resulted in considerable blowing and drifting snow with low visibility over Quay County. Snow drifts of one to three feet were reported over parts of the area. A semi-trailer rolled over off of Interstate 40 near Tucumcari. Damages are estimated for total loss of the commercial vehicle and the extent of injuries is unknown.
Snowfall amounts between four and eight inches were reported around Las Vegas.
Snowfall amounts ranged from two to four inches around Roosevelt County. Some freezing rain was reported at the onset of the storm.

Various stations within Guadalupe County reported between six and 12 inches of snowfall. Gusty north winds resulted in some blowing and drifting snow with difficult travel conditions along Interstate 40.
Various stations within De Baca County reported from eight to 12 inches of snowfall.

Snowfall amounts around Chaves County ranged from two to eight inches. The heaviest snow fell on the north side of Roswell. The 4.6 inches of snow at the Roswell airport on the 27th set a new daily record and the storm total of 4.9 inches set a new monthly record for October.

events.cz_name: MIDDLE RIO GRANDE VALLEY/ALBUQUERQUE METRO AREA
events.event_narrative: A snow squall blasted through the Albuquerque metro area with a period of moderate to heavy snow. Visibility was reduced to below one-quarter mile for around 15 minutes and winds gusted up to 30 mph. One to four inches of snow was reported as the squall moved through the city.
SNOTEL sites across the southwest mountains received an estimated 10 to 16 inches of snow with the heaviest accumulations occurring overnight on January 25th.
A trained spotter near Alma received about 4.5 inches of snow overnight on the 25th and continuing into the morning of the 26th.

The Sierra Blanca SNOTEL received an estimated 19 inches of snow during this three day event with the heaviest accumulations falling overnight on the 25th and through the day on the 26th. The heavy snow also led to severe driving conditions along New Mexico State Road 532 from Alto to Ski Apache which forced a road closure on the morning of the 26th.

The Tusas Mountains received about 4 to 8 inches of snow during this three day event although some areas observed localized heavier amounts. The Hopewell SNOTEL near Canon Plaza received about 15 inches of snow over the course of three days.

The Jemez Mountains received about 4 to 8 inches of snow during this three day event although some areas observed localized heavier amounts. The Vacas Locas SNOTEL near Cuba received about 21 inches of snow with most of that falling overnight on the 25th and through the morning of the 26th.

The northern Sangre de Cristo Mountains received about 6 to 9 inches of snow over the three day period, but some locations received locally higher amounts. A SNOTEL site near Taos received about 16 inches of snow while the Red River ski site observed about 25 inches with most of the accumulation falling overnight on the 25th and through the morning of the 26th.

The southern Sangre de Cristo Mountains received about 5 to 8 inches of snow over the three day event although some locations did observe locally higher amounts. A SNOTEL near Rociada received about 20 inches of snow with most of that falling overnight on the 25th and through the morning of the 26th.

events.event_narrative: Widespread snow impacted the Albuquerque metro area overnight on February 13th and into the morning hours of February 14th. Various sources in the area reported 2 to 4 inches of snow with the highest totals nearing 4 inches in the Rio Rancho area.

events.cz_name: MIDDLE RIO GRANDE VALLEY/ALBUQUERQUE METRO AREA
events.event_narrative: A major winter storm tracked through New Mexico through the early morning hours of February 14th. This storm brought a prolonged period of blizzard conditions to central New Mexico, including the Albuquerque metro area. Wind gusts up to 60 mph combined with heavy snow resulted in zero visibility conditions for several hours.

Various sources in the Sandia and Manzano Mountains reported 7 to 12 inches of snow. The highest amounts were found in northeastern portions of the area where a member of the public measured 12 inches of snow south of Golden on February 14th.
Various sources in the Moriarty area reported 5 to 6 inches of snow. A COOP observer in Moriarty measured 5.7 inches of snow on February 14th which set a new snowfall record for the date.
Various sources in the Central Highlands reported 4 to 6 inches of snow. A COOP observer near Encino measured 5.5 inches of snow on February 14th which set a new snowfall record for the date.

Snow as well as strong winds impacted the Tularosa Valley on the morning of February 14th. Estimated wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph resulted in four train cargo containers derailing as it traveled through Carrizozo. No injuries occurred from the train derailment, and the cargo containers were empty. Damages are estimated for the four empty cargo containers.

Various sources in the South Central Mountains reported 8 to 12 inches of snow. The highest snowfall totals were found in the Ruidoso area where a trained spotter measured 12 inches of snow during the afternoon of February 14th.
A trained spotter reported 6.5 inches of snow on the morning of February 14th.
A member of the public in Santa Rosa reported 6 inches of snow on the morning of February 14th.
A trained spotter in Clovis reported 4 inches of snow on the morning of February 14th. Strong winds resulted in snow drifts up to 4 feet.
CoCoRaHS observers in the Roswell area reported 3 to 4 inches of snow on the morning of February 14th.
A CoCoRaHS observer southwest of Arabela measured 10 inches of snow on the morning of February 14th.
A trained spotter east of Elk measured 4 inches of snow on February 14th.

A very strong arctic air mass resulted in extremely cold wind chills across east central New Mexico. The Clines Corners ASOS estimated wind chills of 25 below to 30 below zero during the morning hours of February 15th with wind speeds of about 20 mph.

A very strong arctic air mass resulted in extremely cold temperatures in Curry County. An AWOS station in Clovis estimated wind chills of about 18 below to 22 below zero during the early morning hours of February 15th.

A very strong arctic air mass resulted in extremely cold temperatures in Union County. The Clayton ASOS measured several hours of temperatures around 10 below zero. Combined with wind speeds around 10 mph, wind chills were estimated to be 25 below to 30 below zero.

A very strong arctic air mass resulted in extremely cold temperatures across northeastern New Mexico. The Raton ASOS measured several hours of temperatures around 10 below to 15 below zero. Combined with wind speeds around 10 mph, wind chills were estimated to be about 25 below zero.
Heavy snow fell across the Glorieta Mesa over the three day event. By the morning of February 18th, a CoCoRaHS observer near Pecos measured 8 inches of snow.

Heavy snow fell in the northern Sangre de Cristo Mountains over the three day event with the heaviest snow in this area falling on February 17th. The highest snow totals were found near Red River where a SNOTEL received an estimated 17 inches of snow.

Heavy snow fell in the southern Sangre de Cristo Mountains over the three day event with the heaviest snow in this area falling on February 17th. The highest snow totals were found near Llano Largo where a SNOTEL received an estimated 13 inches of snow.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: Heavy snow fell on the east slopes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains over the three day event with the heaviest snow in the area falling on February 17th. The highest snow totals were found near Eagle Nest where a SNOTEL received an estimated 14 inches of snow.

Heavy snow fell in the Sandia and Manzano Mountains over the three day event with the heaviest snow in the area observed on February 16th and 17th. By the morning of February 17th, a CoCoRaHS observer near Cedar Crest measured 6 inches of snow.

Heavy snow fell over Lincoln County and the South Central Mountains over the three day event with the heaviest snowfall in the area observed on February 16th. A member of the public near Capitan reported 11 inches of snow by the morning of February 16th. The Lincoln County emergency manager reported deteriorating road conditions across Lincoln County with areas seeing snow drifts of 3 to 4 feet.
Heavy snow fell in the Chuska Mountains over the three day event with the heaviest snow in the area observed on February 16th and 17th. A SNOTEL near Toadlena received an estimated 11 inches of snow.

Heavy snow was observed in the Santa Fe area over the three day event with the New Mexico State Capitol observing some of the highest storm total snowfall measurements across the state. The heaviest snow in the Santa Fe area was observed late February 15th through February 16th with many CoCoRaHS observers reporting 6 to 10 inches of snow by the morning of the 16th. A COOP observer near Santa Fe reported 6.9 inches of snow on February 16th which set a new snowfall record for the date.

Heavy snow fell in the Upper Rio Grande Valley over the three day event with the heaviest snowfall in the area observed on February 17th. A member of the public in Taos measured 7.5 inches of snow on the 17th.

Heavy snow fell in the Espanola Valley over the three day event with the heaviest snow in the area observed on February 16th and 17th. By the morning of February 17th, a CoCoRaHS observer near Canones measured 6.1 inches of snow.

events.cz_name: MIDDLE RIO GRANDE VALLEY/ALBUQUERQUE METRO AREA
events.event_narrative: Another round of snow impacted the Middle Rio Grande Valley and the Albuquerque metro area from February 15th through the 17th. CoCoRaHS observers around the metro area received totals ranging from 1 to 3 inches. The highest snow totals in the zone were found in Valencia County where a CoCoRaHS observer near Meadow Lake measured 5.8 inches of snow.
Heavy snow impacted northeastern New Mexico over the three day event with the heaviest snow in the area observed on February 17th and 18th. A trained spotter near Ribera measured 6.3 inches of snow.

events.event_narrative: Widespread snow impacted the Albuquerque metro area on February 14th. Various sources in the area reported 2 to 4 inches of snow with the highest totals nearing 4 inches in the Rio Rancho area.

Various sources in the Sandia and Manzano Mountains reported 7 to 12 inches of snow. The highest amounts were found in northeastern portions of the area where a member of the public measured 12 inches of snow south of Golden on February 14th.

A major winter storm tracked through New Mexico through the early morning hours of February 14th. This storm brought a prolonged period of blizzard conditions to central New Mexico, including the Sandia and Manzano Mountains. Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph combined with heavy snow resulted in zero visibility conditions for several hours.
Albuquerque's first thunderstorm of the year brought very strong winds to the metro area as well as pea size hail. A mesonet station on the northwest side of Albuquerque recorded a 62 mph wind gust.

A very strong arctic air mass resulted in extremely cold temperatures in Guadalupe County. An AWOS station in Santa Rosa estimated wind chills of about 18 below zero during the early morning hours of February 15th.

A very strong arctic air mass resulted in extremely cold temperatures across Quay County. The Tucumcari ASOS measured several hours of temperatures around 5 below to 10 below zero. Combined with wind speeds around 10 mph, wind chills were estimated to be about 18 below to 20 below zero.

A very strong arctic air mass resulted in extremely cold temperatures across Roosevelt County. An AWOS station at Melrose Air Force Range measured several hours of temperatures around 5 below zero. Combined with wind speeds around 10 mph, wind chills were estimated to be about 18 below to 20 below zero.

A very strong arctic air mass resulted in extremely cold temperatures across northeastern New Mexico. The Las Vegas ASOS measured several hours of temperatures around 10 below to 15 below zero. Combined with wind speeds around 10 mph, wind chills were estimated to be about 25 below to 28 below zero.

Heavy snow fell over the Jemez Mountains over the three day event with the heaviest snow in the area observed on February 16th and 17th. A SNOTEL southeast of Cuba received an estimated 9 inches of snow. Snow-packed and icy roads led to severe driving conditions in the area, particularly along New Mexico State Road 4 from Los Alamos to San Ysidro.

Heavy snow impacted northeastern New Mexico over the three day event with the heaviest snow in the area observed on February 17th. A trained spotter near Philmont Scout Ranch measured 4 inches of snow. Snow-packed and icy roads led to the closure of Interstate 25 near Raton.

As a result, Interstate 40 was closed into the morning hours of March 25th. Eleven people were injured, but no fatalities occurred. Damages are estimated for the multiple vehicles involved.

Nickel size hail was reported with a strong thunderstorm northwest of Roswell near the intersection of Brown Road and Relief Route.
Penny size hail from a strong thunderstorm was reported in Roswell.

A CoCoRaHS observer near Mesa reported golf ball size hail from an intense thunderstorm that tracked southeast along U.S. Highway 285. The observer reported that the hail lasted for about 30 minutes and did extensive damage to their property and livestock. The windshield on their vehicle was broken, and heavy rain washed out a fence on their property. Their sheep that were outdoors during the thunderstorm were injured from the large hail, and several baby lambs were killed. Damages are estimated for the vehicle and property damage as well as the loss of livestock.
A storm chaser near Lemitar reported nickel size hail from a strong thunderstorm.
One inch hail was reported with a severe thunderstorm located near Logan.

events.cz_name: MIDDLE RIO GRANDE VALLEY/ALBUQUERQUE METRO AREA
events.event_narrative: An ASOS station in Albuquerque measured a peak wind gust of 66 mph.

On May 2, 2021, a wildfire started near Shiprock. The wildfire spread rapidly, and within two days, it had burned 422 acres. One building was destroyed, and several other buildings were threatened before the wildfire was contained on May 4th. No information was provided on the structure that burned.

A trained spotter near Tolar estimated 60 mph wind gusts from a severe thunderstorm that tracked through the area. The severe winds broke approximately three inch diameter branches off of a tree. Damages are estimated for tree damage.
A mesonet station near Logan measured a 60 mph wind gust from a decaying thunderstorm producing a strong downburst.
A public weather station south of Belen measured 59 mph wind gusts from a dry thunderstorm and an outflow boundary.
A strong thunderstorm near Texico produced nickel size hail.
An ASOS station in Roswell measured a 69 mph thunderstorm wind gust from a severe thunderstorm.

A severe thunderstorm produced large amounts of hail at least one inch in diameter. A commuter traveling along U.S. Highway 64 west of Capulin reported that at least three inches of hail accumulation was covering the road.
A trained spotter in Portales measured 1.25 inch hail from a severe thunderstorm.
A CoCoRaHS observer reported penny size hail from a strong thunderstorm east-southeast of Tucumcari.
A trained spotter reported penny size hail from a strong thunderstorm in Portales.

Several trained spotters in Portales reported hail ranging from the size of quarters to the size of golf balls from a slow-moving severe thunderstorm. Hail accumulations of one to two inches in the area resulted in the collapse of a patio roof at one residence in Portales. Damages are estimated for the destruction of the roof.

Slow-moving thunderstorms in the Portales area produced three to four inches of rainfall in a short period of time. This led to flash flooding in the area where a trained spotter reported some roadways were under 2 feet of water. The Portales Fire Department had to perform a water rescue for a family of three which included two children after their car was swept into a drainage ditch. The family was traveling along 18th Street when their car was swept by the flooded waters and pushed into a culvert headed south along S Globe Street. Their car eventually came to a stop against a pipe that was across the culvert. The family was rescued about 45 minutes after the first 911 call, and no injuries were reported. Damages are estimated for the loss of the car as well as rough estimates for water damages to an unknown amount of structures.
An ASOS station in Tucumcari recorded a 59 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorm.
A trained spotter reported nickel size hail in Mills from a strong thunderstorm.

A microburst with estimated 70 to 90 mph winds from a severe thunderstorm caused significant damage in and around Grady as well as in far southern Quay County. North-northwest of Grady, a National Weather Service damage survey team found 17 downed electrical transmission line poles due to the microburst. A couple of the poles were snapped at the base while some were snapped halfway up the pole. Damages are estimated for the destruction of the transmission pole lines.

A microburst with estimated 70 to 90 mph winds from a severe thunderstorm caused significant damage in and around Grady as well as in far southern Quay County. In southern Quay County, a National Weather Service damage survey team estimated 70 mph winds associated with the microburst destroyed a carport. The carport along with a downed TV antenna was carried 200 yards away from their original location. A storage shed that was attached to the carport was also tipped over. Additionally, several large trees limbs were downed. Damages are estimated for the loss and damage to the carport, TV antenna, storage shed, and tree limbs.

A microburst with estimated 70 to 90 mph winds from a severe thunderstorm caused significant damage in and around Grady as well as in far southern Quay County. In Grady, a National Weather Service damage survey team estimated 70 mph winds associated with the microburst caused roof damage with metal roofs pealed back from their structures. The microburst also removed a porch cover that was attached to a house. Additionally, large trees were unrooted, and large tree limbs were downed. Damages are estimated for the roof damage as well as the tree damage.
A member of the public in Red River reported penny size hail from a strong thunderstorm.

A trained spotter measured one inch hail from a severe thunderstorm near Los Cerrillos. The severe thunderstorms also produced deep hail accumulations along Interstate 25 with multiple spotters reporting hail depths ranging from one to three inches.
A trained spotter estimated one inch hail from a severe thunderstorm in Yeso.
A trained spotter estimated nickel size hail from a strong thunderstorm near Vaughn. A travel camera indicated that hail had accumulated along U.S. Highway 285, but no impacts were reported.
A trained spotter estimated penny size hail from a strong thunderstorm near Agua Fria.

A trained spotter estimated one inch hail from a severe thunderstorm near Los Cerrillos. The spotter reported that the hail broke a skylight and also stripped leaves from their trees. Damages are estimated for the damage to the skylight.
A trained spotter estimated penny size hail from a strong thunderstorm southeast of Santa Fe.
A trained spotter reported nickel size hail from a strong thunderstorm near House.
An ASOS station in Las Vegas measured a 59 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorm.
A member of the public reported a landspout tornado near Abo, but no damage was reported.
A social media user caught video of a brief landspout from a weak thunderstorm near Bosque Farms. No damage was reported.

A member of the public reported a landspout tornado from a thunderstorm near Kewa Pueblo. The landspout developed on the southwest side of the storm and tracked northwest for approximately eight minutes. No damage was reported.
Multiple spotters reported a brief tornado north of Melrose. No damage was reported.
A supercell near Nara Visa spawned a brief tornado which tracked northwest for approximately ten minutes. No damage was reported.
A funnel cloud from a strong thunderstorm was spotted near the Santa Fe airport. The funnel cloud never touched down, and no damage was reported.
A weather station at the Portales airport measured a 74 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorms. Other trained spotters in Portales estimated wind speeds of 60 to 65 mph.
A severe thunderstorm produced penny size hail in Portales.
An ASOS station in Tucumcari measured an 81 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorm.
A school weather station in Grady measured a peak wind gust of 84 mph from a thunderstorm microburst.

A grass fire started on Road 5211 near U.S. Highway 64 between Bloomfield and Lee Acres on the evening of May 16th. The fire spread quickly and engulfed a family home with a detached garage. The residence was completely destroyed, and the three family dogs that were inside at the time tragically died. There was also reported damage to an additional outbuilding. The fire prompted an evacuation of the area, but residents were permitted to return late on May 16th. By the morning of May 17th, the fire was 5 percent contained, but no longer posed a threat to any other structures. Damages are estimated for the loss of the residence as well as damages to the outbuilding.
A CoCoRaHS observer reported one inch hail from a severe thunderstorm northeast of Santa Fe.
One inch hail was reported from a severe thunderstorm southwest of Santa Fe.
A COOP observer reported penny size hail from a strong thunderstorm moving north near Santa Fe.

Various sources in Glorieta reported quarter to ping pong size hail from a severe thunderstorm that was moving north through the area. The hail was also responsible for causing minor damage to one Glorieta resident's house by ripping holes in their gutters and tearing off pieces of stucco from their house. Damages are estimated for the house damage.
A CoCoRaHS observer near Capitan reported penny size hail from a strong thunderstorm moving northeast through the area.

events.event_narrative: An ASOS station in Albuquerque measured a peak non-thunderstorm wind gust of 60 mph.
Ping pong size hail was reported from a severe thunderstorm moving northeast through Fort Stanton.
A trained spotter reported two inch hail from a severe thunderstorm near Rociada.
A weather station near Red Hill measured a peak non-thunderstorm wind gust of 60 mph.
Various sources reported nickel to quarter size hail from a severe thunderstorm near Agua Fria.

A COOP observer near Santa Fe reported penny size hail from a strong thunderstorm. The hail reportedly caused damage and dents to a Santa Fe resident's three cars. Damages are estimated for the dent damage to the three cars.
Various sources reported penny to quarter size hail from a severe thunderstorm southwest of Santa Fe.
Half dollar size hail was reported from a severe thunderstorm near Cimarron.
A trained spotter measured a 60 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorm near Hagerman.
A weather station near Archuleta measured a 67 mph non-thunderstorm wind gust.
An ASOS station in Roswell measured a 66 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorm.

An ASOS station in Tucumcari measured a 69 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorm.
A trained spotter near Amistad reported one inch hail from a severe thunderstorm.
An ASOS station in Raton measured a peak non-thunderstorm wind gust of 59 mph.
Various sources in Clovis reported quarter to golf ball size hail from a brief severe thunderstorm.
Ping pong size hail at the Cuervo Exxon station.
The Roswell ASOS measured a 59 mph thunderstorm wind gust from a severe thunderstorm moving northeastward through the area.
An observer at 2nd and Union in Roswell measured a 65 mph thunderstorm wind gust associated with a severe thunderstorm that was moving northeastward through the area.
A mesonet station near Dora measured a 60 mph wind gust associated with a severe thunderstorm that moved northeastward through the area.
A CoCoRaHS observer near San Ysidro reported 1 inch hail from a severe thunderstorm.
A severe thunderstorm near Maxwell produced twin tornadoes. One tornado was a mesocyclonic tornado while the second tornado was a landspout. No damage was reported.

A COOP observer near Capulin reported 1 inch to 1.5 inch hail from a severe thunderstorm moving eastward through the area. The hail accumulated to about an inch at their location. The observer also reported that the glass of their greenhouse was broken and the hail tore holes in their plastic gutter. Damages are estimated for the property damage to the greenhouse and gutters.
A trained spotter near Milagro reported penny to quarter size hail from a severe thunderstorm tracking southeastward through the area.
A trained spotter southeast of Corona reported a mixture of pea size to ping pong size hail as a severe thunderstorm tracked southeastward through the area.
A trained spotter reported 1 inch hail along Interstate 40 from a severe thunderstorm that tracked southeastward over the area.
A severe thunderstorm near Maxwell produced twin tornadoes. One tornado was a mesocyclonic tornado while the second tornado was a landspout. No damage was reported.
A COOP observer near Encino reported 1 inch hail from a severe thunderstorm tracking eastward through the area.

Nickel size hail was reported from a slow-moving strong thunderstorm near Corona. The thunderstorm produced 2 inches of hail accumulation along U.S. Highway 247 east of Corona, but no impacts are known.
A trained spotter reported penny size hail from a strong thunderstorm tracking eastward near Vaughn.
A trained spotter reported 1 inch hail as they were driving along U.S. Highway 209 near Quay.
A trained spotter near Fort Sumner measured a 58 mph wind gust along the outflow boundary of a severe thunderstorm. The spotter also reported pea size hail.
A storm chaser reported a tornado moving southeast from a severe thunderstorm north-northeast of Arabela. No damage was reported.
A severe thunderstorm north of Arabela began producing 1 inch hail which grew as the thunderstorm intensified. A storm chaser reported a maximum hail size of 2 inches from the severe thunderstorm.
A storm chaser reported 1 inch hail from a severe thunderstorm near Roswell. The slow-moving thunderstorm produced sufficient hail to partially cover U.S. Highway 380, but no impacts were reported.

Storm chasers and trained spotters reported very large hail ranging from one to three inches from a severe thunderstorm near Midway. The largest hailstones reported were 3 inches along U.S. Highway 285 which broke an unknown number of vehicle windshields. The strong inflow and outflow winds from the thunderstorm also produced low visibility from dust in the area. Damages are estimated for the unknown amount of broken windshields.
One inch hail was reported from a severe thunderstorm near Roswell.

Numerous observers reported large hail ranging from 1 inch to 1.75 inches from a severe thunderstorm near Portales. The thunderstorm also produced torrential rainfall that caused minor street flooding in Portales. Damages are unknown.
A member of the public in Portales estimated 65 mph wind gusts from a severe thunderstorm moving eastward through the area.

Multiple sources reported very large hail from a severe thunderstorm in the Dexter area. The largest hailstones reported were 3 inches in diameter which broke numerous windshields along U.S. Highway 285. Damages are estimated for the unknown amount of broken windshields.

A severe thunderstorm near Dexter produced very strong winds that caused thunderstorm damage in the area. A storm chaser reported that the severe winds bent a power pole along U.S. Highway 285. Damages are estimated for the loss of the power pole.
A severe thunderstorm near Clovis produced 1 inch hail as it tracked eastward through the area.

Estimated 60 to 70 mph winds from a severe thunderstorm moving eastward through Clovis downed power lines southeast of the area. Torrential rainfall also resulted in minor street flooding which caused traffic to be diverted for a short time period during the evening. Damages are estimated for the downed power lines.
An AWOS station in Clovis measured a 66 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorm moving eastward through the area.

A trained spotter near Hagerman reported a snapped power pole along Morgan Road west of New Mexico State Road 2 as the result of a severe thunderstorm. Damages are estimated for the loss of the power pole.
An early morning severe thunderstorm near Ragland produced a mixture of quarter to golf ball size hail.

The NASA Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility southeast of Corona measured 5.77 inches of rainfall is a short period of time which caused flash flooding in the area with unpaved roadways washed out. The extent of the damages is unknown.

A trained spotter west southwest of Roy reported 1 inch hail from a severe thunderstorm moving southeast through the area. The observer also reported that their home roof was leaking as a result of hail damage. Damages are estimated for the roof damage.

A trained spotter east northeast of Bell Ranch reported hail up to 1.5 inches in diameter from a severe thunderstorm moving southeast through their area. The hail dented their vehicles and also broke three of their skylights. Damages are estimated for the vehicle damage and the broken skylights.
A trained spotter in Raton reported penny size hail from a strong thunderstorm.
A social media user reported 1.25 inch hail from a severe thunderstorm near La Cienega.
Trained spotters in Tinnie reported hail ranging from the size of nickels to the size of golf balls from a severe thunderstorm moving east through the area.
A trained spotter near Ocate reported 1 inch hail from a severe thunderstorm moving northeastward through the area.

Heavy rainfall in the Hondo area caused widespread flooding of roads and low water crossings. The Lincoln County emergency manager estimated that the Rio Ruidoso rose 4 to 6 feet quickly while Alamo Canyon Road south of U.S. Highway 70 was completely inundated. One individual was in their truck at Alamo Canyon Road and became stuck in the low water crossing when the flood waters inundated it. The individual then either tried to escape or the flood waters pulled them out of their truck. Tragically, they drowned, and their body was found the next day. Damages are estimated for the loss of the truck.
A thunderstorm near Moses produced a brief tornado as it tracked eastward. No damage was reported.
A storm chaser reported a brief tornado near the intersection of Quay Road 62 and Quay Road O. No damage was reported.
A trained spotter near Dexter reported 1.5 inch hail from a supercell thunderstorm tracking eastward through the area.
A trained spotter near Greenfield reported nickel size hail from a supercell thunderstorm that tracked eastward through the area.
A trained spotter near Milnesand reported hailstones ranging from the size of nickels to quarters from a severe thunderstorm tracking eastward through the area.

Two to four inches of rainfall in the Roswell area caused flash flooding on roadways and low water crossings. A high water rescue had to be performed at Washington and Jaffa Road in Roswell, but no injuries were reported. The extent of the damages are unknown and are roughly estimated for the unknown amount of businesses and vehicles inundated with flood waters.

Two to four inches of rainfall in a short period of time caused flash flooding in Dexter with multiple roads flooded. The extent of the damages are unknown and are roughly estimated for the unknown amount of businesses and homes inundated.

Multiple trained spotters reported flash flooding along U.S. Highway 285 near Midway with an estimated three to four feet of water over the roadway. Several people were stranded along the highway and were waiting on top of their vehicles to be rescued. Several water rescues had to be conducted at U.S. Highway 285 and Orchard Park Road. Multiple homes were inundated as well with flood waters, and one woman had to be rescued via a kayak. No injuries were reported. The extent of the damages is unknown, and damages are roughly estimated for the multiple businesses, homes, and vehicles inundated with flood waters.
A trained spotter south of U.S. Highway 380 observed a landspout near Bingham. No damage was recorded.
A spotter observed a brief landspout near Veguita. No damage was recorded.
Multiple observers near Rio Rancho reported 1 inch hail from a severe thunderstorm moving eastward through the area.
A social media user near Golf Course and Subio in northwest Albuquerque reported nickel size hail from a severe thunderstorm moving eastward through the metro area.
A trained spotter near Coors Bypass in northwest Albuquerque reported 1 inch hail from a severe thunderstorm moving eastward through the metro area.
A CoCoRaHS observer near Ellison and Golf Course in northwest Albuquerque reported penny size hail from a severe thunderstorm moving eastward through the metro area.

Thunderstorms producing heavy rain resulted in major flash flooding across southern Roswell and southern Chaves County. Heavy rainfall had fallen in the area the previous evening, and an additional 3 to 5 inches of rain during the morning of May 31st exacerbated the flash flooding. Numerous locations along U.S. Highway 285 from Lake Arthur northward into Roswell had upwards of 2 feet of water along the travel corridor while low water crossings had upwards of 4 feet of water which overfilled the banks. Multiple reports of flooding across fields, ditches, yards, and vehicles were reported. Several side roads were unpassable and had to be barricaded. A breached arroyo near the Roswell Airport also forced the closure of roads around the airport for about a week. Damages are estimated.

Heavy rain from a severe thunderstorm resulted in flash flooding on the west side of Albuquerque. An estimated six inches of water on the roadways along with three inches of hail accumulation resulted in major flash flooding along Coors Boulevard and Paseo del Norte as well as Coors Boulevard and Alameda. Numerous cars were stalled along the major travel corridor in northwest Albuquerque. Farther south near Central Avenue and 52nd Street, multiple homes and garages in the neighborhood were flooded with several inches of rain and nearly six inches of hail accumulation. Damages are estimated.

events.event_narrative: Severe drought conditions from April 2021 continued in May.
The Lincoln County Emergency Manager reported nickel size hail along New Mexico State Road 368 from a strong thunderstorm tracking eastward through the area.
A storm chaser southeast of Vaughn reported nickel size hail from a strong thunderstorm tracking southward through the area.

Multiple sources in Dilia reported nickel to quarter size hail from a severe thunderstorm tracking southward through the area. One resident of Dilia reported that the hail broke their skylight. Damages are estimated for the loss of the skylight.
A brief landspout tornado was spotted near Rainsville. No damage was reported.
Strong thunderstorm outflow produced a 67 mph wind gust at the Tucumcari airport.
A member of the public near Sapello reported golf ball size hail from a severe thunderstorm tracking southeast through the area.

An off-duty National Weather Service employee reported quarter size hail along Interstate 25 near San Antonio from a severe thunderstorm tracking southeast. The hail resulted in slick road conditions along the Interstate, but no impacts were reported.

Multiple storm chasers reported very large hail of 2 to 3 inches from a supercell tracking southeast near Las Vegas. The hail did break one storm chaser's windshield. Damage estimates are for the broken windshield.

Multiple sources reported a large cone tornado that developed from a supercell northwest of Las Vegas. The tornado was on the ground for twelve minutes and traveled about 4.5 miles towards the southeast, but was in open country. No injuries or property damage were caused by the tornado.
An ASOS station in Tucumcari measured a 61 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorm tracking eastward through the area.
A member of the public in Grady reported quarter size hail from a severe thunderstorm tracking eastward through the area.
A mesonet station in Endee measured a 65 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorm tracking eastward through the area.
A mesonet station near Dora measured a 58 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorm tracking eastward through the area.

Law enforcement reported a downed tree in Fort Sumner from strong winds associated with a severe thunderstorm. No information was provided on the diameter of the tree or if additional damage resulted. Damages are roughly estimated for the loss of the tree.

Severe winds from a thunderstorm moving southward near Santa Fe resulted in minor house damage at one residence. A trained spotter southwest of Santa Fe reported that one inch tree limbs were broken and shingles were stripped from their roof. Damages are estimated for the broken tree limbs and damaged shingles.
An AWOS station in Moriarty measured a 58 mph wind gust associated with thunderstorm outflow.
A trained spotter measured a 59 mph wind gust from a thunderstorm outflow northeast of Abo.
An ASOS station in Las Vegas measured a 71 mph wind gust from an intense thunderstorm downdraft.

An ASOS station in Clines Corners measured a 62 mph wind gust associated with a thunderstorm outflow boundary. These strong winds resulted in reduced visibility ranging from a quarter mile to 1.25 miles due to dust along Interstate 40 near Moriarty as well as U.S. Highway 285 near Encino.
An ASOS station in Las Vegas measured a peak wind gust of 71 mph associated with a decaying thunderstorm to the south.

Trained spotters and law enforcement in Logan reported estimated quarter size hail from a severe thunderstorm tracking southeast through the area. The hail tore holes in mobile home siding. This thunderstorm also produced six to twelve inches of hail accumulation across Logan, including along New Mexico State Highway 54. Damages are estimated for the hail damage to the mobile homes.

A member of the public in Logan estimated 70 mph wind gusts from a severe thunderstorm that tracked southeast through the area. The emergency manager also reported thunderstorm damage from these winds with siding and metal roofing torn from several mobile homes. A tractor trailer was also turned over on New Mexico State Highway 54, and several four feet tall mesquite bushes were snapped in half. Damages are estimated for the mobile home damage, overturned tractor trailers, and mesquite bush damage.
A strong thunderstorm moving southeast through Ragland produced nickel size hail.
An ASOS station near Cannon Air Force Base measured a peak wind speed of 61 mph as a severe thunderstorm tracked southeast through the area.
Numerous weather station in Clovis measured winds in excess of 58 mph as a severe thunderstorm tracked southeast through the area. An AWOS station in Clovis measured a peak wind gust of 61 mph.
An ASOS station in Tucumcari measured a 62 mph wind gust associated with the downdraft of a weak non-thunderstorm shower.

An ASOS station in Santa Fe measured a 59 mph wind gust associated outflow boundaries from nearby showers. Numerous observers in the Santa Fe area and along Interstate 25 reported reduced visibility less than a mile from the dust picked up by the high winds.
A RAWS station near Mountainair measured a 61 mph wind gust associated with a decaying shower.
An ASOS station in Tucumcari measured a 62 mph wind gust associated with outflow from thunderstorms south in Curry County.
An ASOS station in Clayton measured a 58 mph wind gust associated with thunderstorm outflow winds.
An ASOS station in Gallup measured a 58 mph wind gust from a shower that produced a dry microburst.
An ASOS station in Tucumcari measured a 74 mph wind gust from a shower that produced a dry microburst.
An ASOS station in Las Vegas measured a 64 mph wind gust from a shower that produced a dry microburst.
A member of the public near Cannon Air Force Base estimated a 70 mph wind gust from a shower that produced a dry microburst.

A dry microburst with estimated wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph downed a large cottonwood tree near Katherine Gallegos Elementary School. No injuries were reported. Damages are estimated for the downed tree.
A severe thunderstorm tracking southeast through Portales downed several power lines along Commercial Street and along U.S. Highway 70. Damages are estimated for the downed power lines.

Two to four inches of heavy rain that fell in a short period of time forced the closure of New Mexico State Road 2 from mile marker 6 to mile marker 9 near Lake Arthur for several hours. Damage impacts are unknown.

Heavy rain in the Picacho area in Lincoln County resulted in flooding along low water crossings across U.S. Highway 70. An individual did attempt to drive their truck into a flooded low water crossing. Fortunately, the driver was not hurt, but the truck was submerged and had to be pulled out of the water. Damages are estimated for the loss of the truck.
Heavy rain south of Yeso in De Baca County resulted in the closure of New Mexico State Road 20 from mile marker 10 to mile marker 13. There are no known impacts.

Heavy rain near Arabela forced the closure of New Mexico State Road 246 between mile marker 29 and mile marker 31.5. The Lincoln County emergency manager reported that the flood waters washed away the pavement. Damages are estimated for the loss of the road.

Heavy rain near Arabela forced the closure of New Mexico State Road 368 at mile marker 9. The Lincoln County emergency manager reported that water was flooding a substantial bridge at mile marker 9. Damages are estimated.

Heavy rain in Grenville resulted in flash flooding. Union County law enforcement reported one car that was washed into a ditch as well as a truck that was washed into a median along U.S. Highway 87. No injuries to either driver or passengers were reported. A Union County dispatcher also reported flooding at the Grenville cemetery, but it was unknown how deep the water there was. Damages are estimated for the loss of the two vehicles.

Heavy rain led to the rapid rise of the Rio Felix near Hagerman with the gauge on Wiggins Lane measuring a maximum crest of 11.4 feet. The Chaves County emergency manager reported significant flash flooding across all low water crossings near the Rio Felix. Rapidly flowing water resulted in damage to a bridge on Morgan Road. The flash flooding also forced the closure of several Hagerman roads, including Cherokee Road, Lincoln Avenue, and Shoshoni Road. Damages are estimated for the structural damage to the bridge as well as an unknown amount of damage to nearby homes and businesses along the Rio Felix.

Trained spotters near Chacon reported 30 to 45 minutes of heavy rain across the Luna burn scar resulted in significant flash flooding in the area as well as three to twelve inches of mud and debris. The rapidly moving water also displaced boulders that blocked a residential driveway. Damages are a rough estimate.
The Chaves County emergency manager reported a brief funnel cloud near Hagerman.

Heavy rain near Capitan in Lincoln County resulted in the rapid rise of the Magado Creek near the Capitan Fairgrounds. The Magado Creek rose an estimated ten feet which caused the flooding of a low water crossing in the area and temporarily trapping two unoccupied vehicles. No injuries or fatalities were reported. Damages are estimated for the damage to the two vehicles.
A strong thunderstorm near Wagon Mound produced nickel size hail as it tracked southward through the area.
An ASOS station in Tucumcari measured a 63 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorm tracking southward through the area.

A trained spotter reported small tree limbs that were generally less than 1 inch in diameter were knocked down from estimated 50 to 55 mph winds from a thunderstorm near Floyd. Damages are estimated for the downed tree limbs.
A trained spotter reported that a truck bed had been blown over from strong thunderstorm winds near Elida. Damages are estimated for the truck bed.

Rainfall totals just under one inch in a short period of time across the Luna burn scar resulted in flash flooding north of Chacon. The fast moving water and debris flow washed out large boulders and downed trees near Luna Canyon Road, and a private road to many cabins was also washed out. A CoCoRaHS observer reported that the Lujan Canyon road was impassable due to washed out culverts and large amounts of debris on the road. Damages are a rough estimate.

Heavy rain along the Rio Ruidoso caused water to overflow its banks which resulted in flash flooding alongside the river. Several bridges, such as the Main Road Bridge, Gavilan Canyon Bridge, and the Eagle Bridge were overtopped and damaged. The McDaniel Bridge in Upper Canyon was completely destroyed. The City of Ruidoso opened a community center for displaced residents and visitors. Damages are estimated for the structural damage done to the bridges. The New Mexico Governor declared a state of emergency for Lincoln County as a result of the significant flooding.
A trained spotter estimated a 60 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorm near Anton Chico.
A trained spotter estimated a 60 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorm near Sedan.
A COOP observer near Tucumcari reported nickel size hail from a strong thunderstorm tracking southwestward through the area.
Heavy rain southwest of Conchas resulted in flash flooding along New Mexico State Road 104. No damages were known.
A trained spotter reported one inch hail from a severe thunderstorm near Cuervo. The spotter also reported that the hail accumulated to about an inch deep, but impacts are known.
Heavy rain and flash flooding forced the closure of New Mexico State Road 20 from mile marker 0 to mile marker 45. No damages were known.

Heavy rain in Belen resulted in significant flash flooding across the town. Over two inches of rain breached the Belen Highline Canal which caused flooding along Main Street. An unknown amount of homes and businesses were damaged from the water. The New Mexico Governor signed an executive order declaring a State of Emergency in Valencia County due to the flooding. Damages are estimated.
Estimated penny size hail fell from a strong thunderstorm near Tererro. The hail accumulated to about 4 inches deep, but no impacts were known.
One inch hail was reported from a severe thunderstorm near Philmont Scout Ranch. The observer reported that the hail lasted about ten minutes.
One inch hail was reported from a severe thunderstorm near Maxwell.
A trained spotter near Magdalena estimated 60 mph wind gusts from a severe thunderstorm.

A lightning strike resulted in a structure fire in Edgewood during the early morning hours of July 6th. The fire destroyed a shed, a porch, and a fifth wheel RV. Damages are estimated for the loss of the property.

Very strong thunderstorms with heavy rainfall of 2 to 4 inches severely impacted the Socorro area as well as areas north of the city into the early morning hours of July 7th. The Socorro County emergency manager reported that irrigation ditches throughout Socorro County were impacted with overtopping and washing out due to the flood waters. The La Joya Acequia sustained significant damage with several feet of concrete-lined ditches lost and culverts exposed. The Sabinal Fire Station in northern Socorro County was flooded, and numerous homes in low-lying areas in the County had water surrounding them. Numerous country roads and arroyos were flooded and washed out. The BNSF Railroad was also significantly impacted as all trains had to be stopped due to silt and rock debris covering the railroad tracks that go through Socorro County. Damages are estimated.
Heavy rainfall caused an arroyo near Dilia to overflow its banks. No damages are known.
A trained spotter near Stanley reported one inch hail from a severe thunderstorm tracking southward through the area.
A public weather station near Sandia Airpark measured a 63 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorm tracking southward through the area.
A trained spotter reported a brief landspout southeast of Madrid. The landspout only lasted about a minute, and no damage was reported as it occurred over open country.

Heavy rain across the Luna burn scar resulted in major flash flooding in Luna Canyon and surrounding areas, and the force of the water altered the landscape. Water and debris destroyed one bridge and many roads became impassable. An observer reported that the water in the narrow Luna Canyon was several feet high. A CoCoRaHS observer near Chacon reported that the Luna Creek, which is usually just a few feet wide became 100 yards wide. Campsites on private land were demolished. The New Mexico Governor declared a state of emergency in Mora County for the significant flooding.

Law enforcement reported that water was flowing over County Road 84 and Reservation Road 101 around Pojoaque which forced the closure of the roadways. Water was also reported to be flowing across New Mexico State Road 503 in Nambe, but it was not closed. No damages are known.

Trained spotters near Jaconita reported flash flooding in the area from heavy rain. The spotters' truck became stuck in the flood waters and mud flow, but no injuries were reported. Damages are estimated for water damage to the truck.

A trained spotter reported golf ball size hail from a severe thunderstorm moving southwestward near Maxwell. The spotter did report that the hail caused roof damage to their home, but the extent of the damage is unknown. Damages are a rough estimate.
A Roswell resident reported golf ball size hail from a severe thunderstorm tracking northeastward through the area.
A trained spotter near Hagerman reported penny size hail from a strong thunderstorm tracking northeast through the area.

Hagerman law enforcement estimated a 60 mph wind gust from a severe thunderstorm moving northeast through the area.

A member of the public near Picacho measured 2 inch hail from a severe thunderstorm.
Multiple observers in Cuba reported nickel to quarter size hail from a severe thunderstorm.
A trained spotter near Carrizozo reported one inch hail from a severe thunderstorm. The observer also reported heavy rainfall with near zero visibility and some minor street flooding in the area.

The Carrizozo airport measured 3.95 inches of rain in a short period of time which resulted in flash flooding in the area. Extent of damages is unknown.

The Farmington Airport recorded a high temperature of 106 degrees Fahrenheit which set a new all-time record high temperature for the locations. This was also the second consecutive day of high temperatures of at least 105 degrees which met excessive heat criteria for the Northwest Plateau.

Heavy rain across eastern Quay County resulted in flash flooding along New Mexico State Road 469. Local law enforcement reported that the roadway became impassable and the road was closed. There are no known impacts.
An AWOS station at the Clovis airport measured a 58 mph wind gust associated with a severe thunderstorm.
A small tornado touched down briefly north of Gladstone.

A CoCoRaHS observer in House reported nickel size hail with a strong thunderstorm tracking southward through the area. The observer also reported some minor damage with dents in their car from the hail. Damages are estimated for the car dents.

Multiple sources reported flooding around Eldorado as an intense thunderstorm produced rain rates of about 4 to 5 inches per hour. A CoCoRaHS observer in Eldorado reported 2.03 inches of rain with 1.1 inches of that falling in just 45 minutes. The heavy rainfall flooded arroyos around Eldorado. A couple residents also reported that their yards had been flooded while another resident reported that the flood waters entered their garage. Damages are estimated for the flooded garage.

A thunderstorm producing rain rates of about 4 to 5 inches per hour caused flash flooding along New Mexico State Road 14 in the Cedar Crest area southward into Pinon Ridge. A trained spotter in Cedar Crest also reported that arroyos in the area were full and storm drains were becoming overwhelmed. Extent of damages is unknown.

A thunderstorm with heavy rain rates of 3 to 4 inches per hour resulted in flash flooding across eastern portions of Albuquerque. Several reports of flooded roadways and yards in the Albuquerque foothills was received. The rainfall also quickly filled up in city's arroyos, and three people within the arroyos were swept away. Emergency crews performed water rescues for the three individuals for several hours on July 20th, but rescue efforts were not successful. Unfortunately, emergency personnel recovered the bodies of two adult men on July 21st in the diversion channel washout area, and the body of a third adult man was recovered on July 22nd. A spokesperson for Albuquerque Fire remarked that this was the deadliest flooding event in Albuquerque in recent memory.

The Catron County emergency manager reported that heavy rain in Old Horse Springs resulted in flash flooding across the area. A local resident measured 3.5 inches of rain in just 45 minutes. This resulted in multiple barns and homes in the area flooded as well as the local fire department. The emergency manager also reported that several county roads had been washed away. Damages are estimated.
A trained spotter in Fence Lake reported that County Road 35D had been washed out due to heavy rain in the area. Damages are estimated.

A trained spotter near Corona reported baseball size hail from a severe thunderstorm tracking north-northeast through the area. The spotter reported that their front and rear windshields on their truck were broken as well as their rearview mirrors. Other reports of damage to about 100 vehicles was received although the extent of the damage is not known. A horse trailer also sustained damage while a horse lost one of its eyes due to hail injuries. Damages are estimated for extensive vehicle damage.
A large tree limb was downed at Fruit Avenue and Luna Boulevard in southwest Albuquerque as a strong thunderstorm tracked westward through the city. Damages are estimated.
A brief landspout tornado was seen near Idalia Road and Highway 528 in Rio Rancho. No damages were reported.

Heavy rain resulted in significant flash flooding near Apache Creek. The fast moving flood waters rushed through at least one home and overtopped an earthen dam. A metal tank was swept downstream, and a truck in the Apache Creek was submerged in the water. Damages are estimated.
The Lincoln County emergency manager reported that dime to nickel size hail fell from a strong thunderstorm near Alto.

Heavy rain in Jemez Springs resulted in the Jemez River to overflow its banks. People who were near the river were forced to move their cars away from their houses to prevent them from washing away. One observer noted that this was the highest they had seen the Jemez River in 25 years. No damages were known.

Video obtained by KOAT TV showed flash flooding in Angus with fast moving water rushing against a home and leaking underneath the doorway. No significant damages are known, and damages are estimated for minor home flood damage.
A trained spotter near Ute Park reported nickel size hail from a strong thunderstorm that was slowly tracking northward through the area.

Strong thunderstorms near Encinoso produced an estimated 1.5 to 2 inches of rainfall. This resulted in severe flooding along New Mexico State Road 246 which forced the closure of the roadway from mile marker 18 to mile marker 36. Damages are estimated for the washed out roadway.

A strong thunderstorm produced an estimated 1 inch of heavy rainfall in a short period of time on the Ute Park burn scar. This resulted in rapid runoff with emergency personnel reporting a six foot wall of water that flowed through Ute Park with a three foot rise of water in Cimarron. This damaged many roads in the area and trapped numerous residents within their homes. No injuries or fatalities resulted from the flash flooding. Damages are estimated.

A COOP observer reported ping pong size hail from a slow-moving thunderstorm near Duran. The observer also reported several vehicles were damaged due to broken windshields and rearview mirrors. Damages are estimated for the unknown amount of vehicles damaged.
A resident in Los Lunas reported penny to quarter size hail from a slow-moving thunderstorm along with hail accumulations of an inch.

A strong thunderstorm near Ghost Ranch produced several inches of water along U.S. Highway 84, and mud, rock, and debris were reported along the highway between mile marker 231 and mile marker 234. Several large boulders were also noted to have fallen from cliffsides onto the shoulder of the highway. Damages are estimated for along the highway.

Strong thunderstorms that moved southwest through Socorro County brought heavy rain with reports of one to two inches. This resulted in widespread flooding across central Socorro County. The La Joya area was especially impacted with additional damage to the La Joya Acequia. A large section of the concrete ditch system north of La Joya was severely damaged, and several ditches and drains were filled with silt. All of the arroyos in the La Joya area flooded which washed away several of the arroyo banks and caused additional damage. The Rio Puerco River created to 17.75 feet Friday evening which was its highest level since 2013. Homes in the Contreras area were surrounded by flood water. Damages are estimated.

An estimated 2.5 to 3.5 inches of heavy rainfall in under an hour caused flash flooding in Placitas. Several roads and drainage ditches in the Placitas area were flooded with mud and debris also covering roadways. Damages are estimated.

An estimated quarter of one inch of rain in under one hour on the Luna burn scar resulted in flash flooding in the area and areas downstream. This resulted in building damage along Luna Creek in Luna Canyon. The number of buildings damaged and to what extent is unknown. Damages are a rough estimate.

A strong thunderstorm near the Colorado and New Mexico border produced flash flooding along the La Plata River. No structures were damaged, but water did cover the roadway along New Mexico State Road 170 and nearby roadways such as Road 1788 south of La Plata. Water marks suggested that the flood waters covering the roadway were about 100 yards wide and 2 to 3 feet deep.

Heavy rain and extreme flash flooding impacted Chaco Canyon National Historical Park. Damage to roadways, including the north and south entrances to the park, was reported along with damages to the Gallo campground. One individual attempted to drive through the flooded road which prompted a successful water rescue. Due to the flooding and damages, the park was forced to close for several days. Damages are estimated.

Heavy rain in northeast Albuquerque resulted in the city's arroyos filling quickly with fast-moving water. Albuquerque Fire and Rescue reported that two people were caught in the arroyo's flood water. One person was able to escape, but rescue efforts were not successful on the second individual. A woman's body was recovered the next day in the diversion channel.
A COOP observer near Cuba reported heavy rain that resulted in flash flooding in the area with drainages overflowing along with inundation across fields. No damages are known.

A CoCoRaHS observer reported flash flooding along Luna Creek and Luna Canyon Road that resulted from heavy rain along the Luna burn scar north of Chacon. The observer also reported that some structures in the area had been damaged, but the extent or type of structures that sustained damage is unknown. Damages are a rough estimate.

A National Weather Service employee in Madrid measured 1.85 inches of rain from a thunderstorm producing heavy rain. This led to flash flooding along New Mexico State Road 14 in Madrid and south of Los Cerillos along with mud and other debris washed onto the roadway. Damages are a rough estimate.

A resident in Moriarty reported severe thunderstorm winds that resulted in damage within their neighborhood. The resident reported that the thunderstorm gusts blew their garage door off its tracks. The severe winds also overturned a 5th wheel travel trailer which landed on a mini-van. Damages are estimated for the garage door and the damage to the trailer and van.

A trained spotter near Maxwell reported quarter size hail from a brief severe thunderstorm that tracked southeast through the area.
An ASOS station in Clayton recorded a 59 mph thunderstorm wind gust.

Heavy rain near Nogal forced the closure of U.S. Highway 380 from mile marker 74 to mile marker 76. Per a trained spotter, the bridge in the area was unsafe to cross as road surfaces had been damaged from repeated rounds of heavy rain over the summer.

Heavy rain with totals of two to three inches within an hour produced flash flooding along New Mexico State Highway 272. A trained spotter reported that the highway near Fort Sumner was impassable due to water over the roadway. Damages are estimated.

Heavy rain with estimated totals of 3 to 6 inches over three consecutive days resulted in flooding along the normally dry Rio Penasco in southwest Chaves County. A river gage north of Dunken peaked at 9.89 feet around midnight August 14th. The gage initially indicated that water receded during the overnight hours, but with thunderstorms developing again early in the day, the gage rose to 11.08 feet by mid-morning. Heavy rain continued across the area throughout the day which resulted in prolonged flooding along the Rio Penasco. At its peak, the Rio Penasco, which is normally about 6 feet wide, was estimated to be 50 to 100 yards wide. The river gage north of Dunken peaked at a depth of 16.8 feet early in the afternoon while another river gage east-northeast of Dunken peaked at 14 feet by mid-afternoon. Numerous roadways, including New Mexico State Highway 24 and U.S. Highway 82, were closed as water levels rose to an estimated 5 to 15 feet. Along U.S. Highway 82, fences were reported to be washed away, and a campground was under several feet of water. The amount of damage is unknown, and damage amounts are a rough estimate.

Heavy rain in Ojo Caliente resulted in flash flooding. Flood waters reportedly entered at least one mobile home, and debris and water covered many secondary roads east of U.S. Highway 285. The extent of damage to the mobile home is unknown, and damages are a rough estimate.
Heavy rain near Aztec resulted in the flooding of an arroyo which rendered San Juan County Road 3073 unpassable as fast-moving water flowed over the roadway. Damages are estimated.
An AWOS station in Santa Rosa measured a 59 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
An ASOS station in Albuquerque measured a 66 mph thunderstorm wind gust.
Heavy rain caused Oso Creek to overfill its banks and overtop Dawson Road. The Lincoln County emergency manager reported that Dawson Road was flooded for about 20 to 30 minutes. No damages are known.

A severe thunderstorm tracking southeast across Interstate 40 near Moriarty caused thunderstorm wind damage with estimated 60 to 70 mph winds. A Moriarty resident reported that multiple trees were downed in the area with widespread power outages. Another resident's above ground cistern was also moved several feet by the strong winds. Schwebach Farms in Moriarty reported extensive damage to their entire farm crops which forced them to harvest the entire crop immediately. Damages are a rough estimate.

One to two inches of heavy rainfall caused flash flooding in Moriarty. Torrance County Dispatch reported torrential rainfall with a severe thunderstorm crossing Interstate 40 near Moriarty. Visibility was near zero which forced many travelers to pull off the road. Several Moriarty residents reported flood damage from the heavy rainfall. The water continued to flow southward through McIntosh and even caused Estancia Park Lake to overfill its banks. The extent of damages is unknown, therefore, damage amounts are a rough estimate.

One to three inches of heavy rainfall in a short period of time caused flash flooding in Roswell. The north and northeast side of the city experienced the most severe flooding where multiple cars were stranded on flooded roadways. Numerous water rescues were conducted on Atkinson, Mescalero, and Berrendo roads in northern Roswell. Flood waters entered homes on Holly Loop, and the road was barricaded due to high water rises. Damages are estimated.

Heavy rain in the Gila Cliff Dwellings flooded many creeks, canyons, and trails in the National Monument. Water overtook a bridge as debris clogged the canyon underneath which stranded visitors for a short time. Damages are estimated.

Heavy rain flooded portions of New Mexico State Road 52 which rendered the roadway impassable. The New Mexico Department of Transportation was forced to close to roadway for several hours as a result. The extent of damages is unknown.
A trained spotter near Seneca reported quarter size hail from a severe thunderstorm tracking southward through the area.
A trained spotter estimated 60 mph wind gusts associated with a severe thunderstorm.
