A thunderstorm near Luis Lopez produced estimated pea to half inch size hail which accumulated between 6 to 8 inches deep along Interstate 25. The highest accumulations were observed along Interstate 25 between mile markers 144 and 145 which resulted in multiple vehicle accidents as well as the closing of the Interstate. The hail stripped numerous trees of their leaves and also caused damage to chile plants in the Luis Lopez area. Heavy rain from the thunderstorm resulted in the minor flooding of low-water crossings along New Mexico State Road 1 between mile markers 54 and 56 which carried debris on the roadway. No injuries were reported. Damages are estimated for the unknown amount of cars involved in the multi-vehicle accident as well as the crop damage to the chile plants.
An approaching line of rain and snow showers along a strong cold front produced a brief wind gust up to 59 mph at Gallup.
The Magdalena Ridge Observatory reported peak wind gusts up to 67 mph. Areas around Red Hill peaked at 57 mph. Patchy blowing dust was also reported across the area.
The Sandia Airpark north of Edgewood reported peak wind gusts up to 60 mph.
Clines Corners reported peak wind gusts up to 63 mph.
Several White Sands Missile Range mesonet sites reported peak wind gusts between 55 and 60 mph.
A White Sands Missile Range site reported a peak wind gust up to 58 mph.

The Sierra Blanca Regional Airport reported peak wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph for several hours. Power lines were downed in Ruidoso Downs and several trees were blown over in Ruidoso. No other property damage was reported and damages are estimated for loss of power lines.
The Raton airport reported peak wind gusts up to 59 mph.
A couple public weather stations around Los Montoyas and Tecolotito reported sustained winds between 43 and 46 mph for several hours.
An area of thunderstorms moving over Tucumcari produced a brief wind gust up to 62 mph.
The Dunken RAWS site reported sustained winds of 40 mph.
Large hail defoliated trees north of Watrous.

An estimated 1.5 to 4 inches of heavy rainfall over the course of 3 hours resulted in flash flooding across the historic Picuris Pueblo. As water over topped an arroyo, flood waters rapidly entered the tribal administration building which sustained damages to the flooring. A gym, senior center, and transportation building were also hit hard by the flood waters which also all sustained various amounts of floor damage. Several grave markers in the tribal cemetery were dislodged by the flood waters. Damages to a hydrologic weir that feeds the fish hatchery pond, which houses about 5,000 fish, were also reported. No injuries or fatalities were reported, and damages are estimated.

A stationary thunderstorm dropped heavy rain over the west slopes of the Sangre De Cristo Mountains resulting in excessive runoff and flash flooding.  Water flowed across State Road 592 southeast of Chupadero.  A rural road was washed out on Tesuque Pueblo and several yards were flooded there.

The Big Springs fire consumed 5478 acres on the east slopes of the Manzano Mountains about 3 to 6 miles west northwest of Tajique.  Six homes and ten outbuildings were destroyed in the fire in the Apache Canyon area.

Snow Squall. A snow squall with associated lightning strengthened as it moved through the Farmington area. Thunderstorm wind gusts across San Juan County were in excess of 58 mph at several weather stations. The Farmington ASOS measured a peak thunderstorm wind gust of 66 mph with thunderstorms, heavy snow, and one quarter mile visibility. The combination of high winds and snow resulted in difficult driving conditions in the area.

As a snow squall with associated lightning moved through the Gallup area, it resulted in estimated 75 mph winds. Multiple reports of damage were received in the Gallup area due to the high winds. Just northeast of Gallup, a COOP observer reported that a COVID-19 drive-through building on a trailer was blown into an eighteen foot power pole which snapped the pole at its base. A resident of Zuni Pueblo reported that power had been knocked out in their area. Damages in the Gallup area are estimated.

Snow squall. The combination of high winds and snow created difficult to severe driving conditions along major roadways in western McKinley County with visibility down to one quarter mile. A crash was reported along Interstate 40 near Manuelito due to slick roads and flash freeze conditions. The extent of injuries was not known, and damages are a rough estimate.

Snow squall. High winds and snow resulted in difficult to severe driving conditions along Interstate 40 and other major roadways with visibility down to one quarter mile. Several weather stations across the Jemez Mountains measured wind gusts in excess of 58 mph. An AWOS station at Los Alamos measured a peak wind gust of 67 mph, but damages indicate wind speeds near 90 mph. These high winds resulted in numerous downed trees near Jemez Springs and Valles Caldera National Preserve which closed New Mexico State Road 4. Numerous automobile accidents were reported, and one man was even trapped in his car. Two people were transported to the hospital with non-life threatening injuries. Damages are estimated.

The weather station at Taos Ski Valley measured about twelve hours of wind speeds in excess of 58 mph with a peak wind gust of 103 mph. These high winds resulted in significant tree damage across Taos Ski Valley with numerous trees downed and splintered. A couple hundred acres of trees were completely flattened near the Wheeler Peak Condominiums. Ten to twenty acres of trees were downed at the El Funko area while another twenty acres of trees were downed near lift four at the ski resort. The Enchanted Forest Ski Site in Red River also reported numerous downed trees in their area. Taos County declared a State of Emergency due to the widespread wind damage. Damages are a rough estimate.

events.event_narrative: Strong winds in the Albuquerque area estimated at 45 to 50 mph downed trees on homes in the South Valley area. Damages are estimated.
Strong winds estimated at 45 to 50 mph snapped a transmission pole in two places at the Rio Grande crossing, resulting in a power outage at San Ildefonso Pueblo. Damages are estimated.

Snow squall. An intense line of thunderstorms with rain and snow moved quickly through Taos County early in the morning. An AWOS station in Taos measured a peak wind gust of 62 mph, but damage estimates within the city and surrounding areas indicate wind speeds of 80 to 100 mph as these high winds caused extensive damage. These thunderstorms produced a 2.9 mile long swath of damage from Blueberry Hill Road to El Prado oriented in an east-northeast direction. Six to seven homes sustained roof damage while one single wide mobile home was moved off its foundation. Numerous trees were snapped at the base with other large limbs downed, and at least two power poles were snapped at their bases. Two homes sustained significant roof damage with the aluminum roofing peeled completely off the homes. On a two story home, three-quarters of its roof was missing with part of its second story destroyed. At another home, a trampoline was found fifty feet in the air stuck in a tree. A radio tower was also downed which resulted in a power outage to the northern half of the city. Several schools in the area cancelled classes for the day while government offices were also closed. Taos County declared a State of Emergency, and COVID-19 vaccination sites were temporarily transformed into shelters for displaced people. Damages are a rough estimate.

The heavy snow resulted in snow packed and icy roads which lead to severe driving conditions in the area. Several motor vehicle accidents were reported, but one of these crashes resulted in two indirect fatalities. Two people inside of a car traveling near Sandia Crest fell nearly 100 feet down the side of the mountain. One was declared dead at the scene while the other was rescued and transported to the hospital, but they later succumbed to their injuries.

events.cz_name: EAST SLOPES SANGRE DE CRISTO MOUNTAINS
events.event_narrative: A COOP observer near Eagle Nest measured 13.2 inches of new snow. This set a new daily record for highest snowfall for the COOP site which has been reporting since 1929. Severe driving conditions were reported along U.S. Highway 64 in the Eagle Nest area.
A CoCoRaHS observer near La Madera measured 11.4 inches of snow.

Various sources across the south central mountains reported heavy snow. The highest snow totals were measured near Ruidoso where both a CoCoRaHS observer and a member of the public measured 11 inches of new snow.
A SNOTEL southwest of Rociada received an estimated 10 inches of new snow.
A CoCoRaHS observer near Glorieta measured 10 inches of new snow.

events.cz_name: MIDDLE RIO GRANDE VALLEY/ALBUQUERQUE METRO AREA
events.event_narrative: Numerous sources reported heavy snow across the Albuquerque metro area. Snow totals varied across the city with the highest totals located in the northern half of the metro where a CoCoRaHS observer in Rio Rancho measured 7.5 inches of snow. At the official climate site at the Albuquerque International Airport, the snow total for this event was 1.6 inches. This snow combined with dangerously cold temperatures resulted in treacherous road conditions. The Albuquerque Police Department responded to 51 vehicle accidents during this event with three of those involving injuries. One indirect fatality also resulted from this event. A Rio Grande High School senior was struck by an out-of-control pickup truck in Los Lunas as he was helping a woman whose car had gotten stuck in the ice and snow. The 18-year-old male was pronounced dead at the scene.
A trained spotter near San Jose measured 8.5 inches of new snow.
A CoCoRaHS observer near Ranchos de Taos measured 8.4 inches of new snow. Severe driving conditions were reported along U.S. Highway 64 from Taos to Eagle Nest.
The fire department east-southeast of Corona reported eight inches of new snow.
A trained spotter near San Fidel measured seven inches of new snow.
A COOP observer near Cuba measured seven inches of new snow. This two-day total is the second highest snowfall measurement for these days for the COOP station that has been reporting since 1946.
A trained spotter southwest of Corona estimated seven inches of new snow.
A trained spotter west-northwest of Milagro estimated 6.5 inches of new snow.

A CoCoRaHS observer north-northeast of Los Cerrillos measured 6.1 inches of new snow. Other snow totals around the Santa Fe metro area generally ranged from three to five inches. This heavy snow resulted in dangerous travel conditions. A motor vehicle accident was reported on northbound Interstate 25 near La Cienega which forced the closure of the roadway.
A CoCoRaHS observer near Moriarty measured six inches of new snow.
Several CoCoRaHS observers near Socorro measured 4 to 4.5 inches of new snow.
A COOP observer near Elk measured four inches of new snow. This set a new daily record for snowfall for the COOP site which has been reporting since 1895.
A trained spotter near Regina measured eight inches of new snow.

The combination of heavy snow and below freezing temperatures resulted in severe travel conditions. The New Mexico Department of Transportation reported severe and dangerous travel conditions along U.S. Highway 380 and U.S. Highway 54 due to snow packed and icy roads.

Various sources reported two to five inches of snow across Guadalupe County. The combination of heavy snow and below freezing temperatures resulted in dangerous travel conditions. During the morning of February 2nd, a multi-vehicle accident that involved thirteen vehicles occurred on Interstate 40 near Santa Rosa when the driver of a semi-truck collided into the rear end of another semi-truck. Eleven other commercial motor vehicles and three passenger cars then crashed into each other. All vehicles were traveling eastbound on Interstate 40, but the multi-vehicle crash forced the shutdown of the major travel corridor in both directions. One indirect fatality resulted from the accident. The 35-year-old man was driving a van carrying six other people. He was pronounced dead at the scene while the other six people had varying injuries and were transported to a hospital. Their conditions are unknown. No other injuries were reported.
